# Sutra UI: full reference

> Sutra UI (`@sutra/ui`) is a React 19 + TypeScript + Tailwind CSS v4 component library built on Radix UI: primitives, patterns, domain kits and full-page blocks, with design tokens (light, dark and a paper style), right-to-left support and CSS-first motion that respects `prefers-reduced-motion`.

Install and set up:

```
pnpm add @sutra/ui
```

```css
/* your Tailwind v4 stylesheet */
@import "@sutra/ui/styles.css";
```

Imports: everything is a flat named export of the root (`import { Button } from "@sutra/ui"`); the same names come from subpaths by domain (`@sutra/ui/overlays`, `@sutra/ui/forms`, `@sutra/ui/dataviz`, `@sutra/ui/icons` for Remix icons). Optional peers load only from their own subpaths (`@sutra/ui/editor`, `@sutra/ui/terminal`, `@sutra/ui/pdf`).

## Conventions digest

A short version of `packages/ui/CONVENTIONS.md` for people and agents who use or extend the library. When the two disagree, CONVENTIONS.md wins; re-read it when the hash above no longer matches (`node packages/ui/scripts/gen-llms.mjs --update-conventions-hash` records the new one after you update this file).

## Stack and layers
- React 19, TypeScript strict, Tailwind CSS v4, Radix UI (`radix-ui`), `class-variance-authority`, Remix icons (`@sutra/ui/icons`). Relative imports inside the package.
- Layers in `packages/ui/src`, each importing only downward: `lib` (pure functions) and `hooks`, `assets` (marks, logos, flags), `primitives` (basic controls), `patterns` (domain-neutral compositions), `kits/<domain>` (ai, agent, billing, ops, ...), `blocks` (sections and pages), `entries` (one barrel per public subpath).
- Named exports only; every export name is unique across the package (prefix sub-parts with the family: `TableRow`, `DialogContent`). `src/index.ts` and `src/entries/core.ts` are generated (`pnpm gen:index`).

## Tokens, never raw colours
- Surfaces `bg-background | card | popover | subtle | muted | accent | secondary`, `bg-inverse text-inverse-foreground`, overlay scrim `bg-overlay`, `glass`. Text `text-foreground | text-muted-foreground | text-primary`. Borders `border-border | border-border-strong | border-input`, focus `ring-ring`.
- Brand `bg-primary hover:bg-primary-hover text-primary-foreground`, `bg-primary-soft text-primary-soft-foreground`. Status `success | warning | destructive | info`, each with `-foreground`, `-soft`, `-soft-foreground`.
- Radius `rounded-control` (buttons, inputs, chips) and `rounded-box` (cards, panels, popovers); `rounded-full` only for things that are always round. Shadows `shadow-xs ... shadow-3xl`.
- Never write a palette class (`bg-zinc-500`), a hex colour or a `dark:` override: dark mode and the paper style (`data-style="paper"`) retune the tokens. Charts read `--chart-1` ... `--chart-8` (`chartColorVars`).
- Fixed on-media colours use the `white` / `black` keywords or `color-mix(white N%)`; a fixed dark surface takes the `dark` class; use `light-dark()` instead of `dark:` pairs; categorical chips use `accentClasses.chip`. Literal colours that stay (brand and store art, ANSI and syntax palettes, mask stops, Badge colour names) are listed with a reason in `test/conventions.test.ts`.
- Control heights: sm `h-8`, md `h-9`, lg `h-10` (Button also has `xs`, `xl` and `icon-*` sizes).

## Vocabulary (one spelling per concept)
- Semantic colour is `tone`: `neutral | primary | success | warning | destructive | info`. Old spellings (`brand`, `default`, `warn`, `danger`, `error`) still work but are deprecated aliases. `variant` is for structure (soft, outline, solid, ghost). Categorical colour with no meaning is `accent`.
- Lifecycle is `TaskStatus`: `pending | running | succeeded | failed | canceled` (US spelling).
- Booleans are bare adjectives: `loading`, `active`, `disabled`. Empty content is `emptyState`. Dismissal is `onDismiss`. Density is `compact | normal | relaxed`.
- Controlled state: `value` / `defaultValue` / `onValueChange(value, meta?)`; `open` / `defaultOpen` / `onOpenChange`; `checked` / `defaultChecked` / `onCheckedChange`. Every controlled prop has its `default*` partner.
- Words: "Sign in", "canceled", "..." as an ellipsis character.
- Data components take `loading` (skeletons in the real layout, `aria-busy`, no skeleton flash when data is already shown) and `emptyState`.

## Shape of a component
- `React.forwardRef` plus `displayName` for DOM components, `...props` spread on the root, `className` merged last with `cn()`. Props that can be overridden (`type`, `role`, `aria-*`, `id`, `data-*` including `data-slot`) are spread after the defaults; refs, merged class and composed handlers come last.
- `asChild` renders the child instead of the element (Radix `Slot`). Compound parts are preferred over giant prop objects; a data-driven wrapper (`items`, `options`) is welcome.
- Each exported component has a one-line JSDoc; props say what they do and when to set them. `@deprecated Use \`tone\`.` marks aliases.
- `data-slot="..."` names are the stable styling hooks (listed per component in the playground "Styling hooks" page); `*ClassName` props exist only where a part needs one.
- Floating content goes through a portal with `z-50`, `sideOffset` 6.
- Before writing a pill, list, banner, picker or formatter, check `lib/`, `hooks/` and the "Build on the existing base" table in CONVENTIONS: `StatusBadge`, `Badge`, `Spinner`, `InlineAlert`, `AlertBanner`, `EmptyState`, `Item`, `Frame`, `Card`, `Collapse`, `ToggleGroup`, `StatCard`, `Progress`, `Meter`, `CopyButton` ...

## Right to left
- Logical utilities only: `ms-/me-`, `ps-/pe-`, `start-/end-`, `text-start/end`, `border-s/e`, `rounded-s/e`. Never `ml/mr/pl/pr/left/right/text-left/text-right`.
- Anything that is direction itself gets an `rtl:` partner: `translate-x-N` with `rtl:-translate-x-N`, `origin-left` with `rtl:origin-right`, directional glyphs (chevrons, arrows) with `rtl:-scale-x-100`. Media transport, undo and enter-key glyphs are not mirrored.
- Read direction with `useDirection()` (hooks) or `directionOf(el)` / `logicalArrow(event)` (lib); never `document.dir` ad hoc. Horizontal arrow keys follow the reading order. `DirectionProvider` forces or follows the document direction (also for portalled layers).
- Charts, code viewers, maps, QR codes and the media seek bar are deliberate `dir="ltr"` islands.
- Numeric runs inside text ("0 / 500", "3 of 12", percentages, deltas) go in `<bdi dir="ltr">`. `Tooltip`, `Popover` and `HoverCard` take `side="start" | "end"`; `Sheet` takes `start` / `end` sides.

## Motion
- Motion is CSS first; there is no animation library. One ease and four speeds are tokens on `:root`: `--sutra-ease`, `--sutra-duration-fast` (150 ms), `--sutra-duration` (200), `--sutra-duration-slow` (300), `--sutra-duration-fill` (500); springs `--sutra-spring-gentle | snappy | bouncy` drive `transition-spring*` for transform properties.
- Utilities: `animate-fade-in | fade-up | pop-in`, `animate-pop`, `animate-tick`, `animate-flash`, `chevron-turn`, `animate-in/out` (tw-animate-css), `scroll-reveal`, `spotlight`, `tilt`, `magnetic`. Animate a value only when it changes (key the element on the changed value), never on first render; in lists only newly added items animate in (`AnimatedList` and `Presence` do this).
- Reduced motion has one net in `sutra.css`: decorative loops and entrances stop, transitions end in 1 ms, overlay movement is stripped, `animate-spin` stays. Do not animate dense tables, log or code viewers, live data fills or anything with its own engine. Presence (`usePresence`, `Presence`, `AnimatedList`), `useFlip`, `useDrag`, `useViewTransition` are the building blocks; gesture components always have a keyboard path.
- In-app motion switch: `<html data-motion="reduce" | "full">` (none follows the system); `prefersReducedMotion()` / `usePrefersReducedMotion()` read it, so JS and CSS agree.
- In Tailwind v4 `translate-*`, `scale-*`, `rotate-*` set individual properties: use bare `transition-transform` (or name all four in an arbitrary list).

## Accessibility
- Roles and aria attributes are part of each component; icon-only buttons need `aria-label`; controls keep at least a 24 x 24 px hit area (`hitArea` from `lib/cn`).
- Dialog, AlertDialog, Sheet and CommandDialog give focus back to the opener even when opened without a trigger.
- A visually hidden data table (`div.sr-only`) backs every chart; empty `role=listbox` is avoided (the empty state is announced in a polite live region instead).

## Layout rules
- A grid with only breakpoint columns needs a base column (`grid-cols-1 sm:grid-cols-2`). Size components by their container (`@container`, `@md:`), not the window. Flex or grid children with text need `min-w-0`; rows that cannot fit need `flex-wrap`; icons `shrink-0`; wide content scrolls in its own `overflow-x-auto` block.

## Effects and tests
- Effects survive StrictMode remounts: reset refs that cleanups flip inside the effect body, cancel async work in cleanup, share one promise for lazy imports.
- Tests live in `packages/ui/test/*.test.tsx` (Vitest, jsdom, `<StrictMode>`); `pnpm verify` runs typecheck, index check, docs checks, tests, build and the exports check.

## Components

## Accordion

> Vertically stacked set of collapsible sections.

- Import: `import { Accordion } from "@sutra/ui"` (or from `@sutra/ui/core`)
- Source: `packages/ui/src/primitives/accordion` (primitives)
- Parts: [`AccordionContent`](AccordionContent.md), [`AccordionItem`](AccordionItem.md), [`AccordionTrigger`](AccordionTrigger.md)
- Also accepts the props of HTMLAttributes, AccordionImplSingleProps, AccordionImplProps, AccordionSingleProps

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `icon` | `AccordionIcon` | `"chevron"` | Trigger indicator: rotating chevron or plus that morphs into minus. |
| `keepMounted` | `boolean` | `false` | Keep every panel in the tree while closed (hidden), so form state and iframes survive; panels can override it. |
| `variant` | `AccordionVariant` | `"default"` | default: divided list · bordered: separate bordered cards · ghost: no chrome · surface: one bordered panel with divided rows · separated: separate soft filled blocks |

### Part props

Props of `AccordionContent`, `AccordionTrigger`: see [the full page](md/Accordion.md).

### Notes

**When to use:** A vertical stack of sections that each open and close, for FAQs, settings groups and long forms. Five looks (`variant`), a chevron or plus indicator and opt-in `keepMounted` panels.

**Use instead when:**
- `Collapsible`: one standalone disclosure
- `Tabs`: one panel visible at a time and the labels always shown
- `Collapse`: show or hide a block you control with your own state

#### Keyboard

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Moves between the triggers and into open panel content |
| Enter, Space | Opens or closes the focused section (native `<button>`) |
| ArrowDown, ArrowUp | Move focus to the next or previous trigger and wrap around; disabled triggers are skipped |
| Home, End | Focus the first or last trigger |

The list is vertical, so the arrow keys do not swap in RTL. Only a root passed `orientation="horizontal"` uses ArrowLeft and ArrowRight, and those swap in RTL (the root `dir` comes from the document or the nearest `DirectionProvider`).

#### Screen readers

Each `AccordionTrigger` is a `button` with `aria-expanded` inside an `<h3>`, so sections appear in the heading outline. The panel is a `region` labelled by its trigger. A closed panel is removed from the tree (or hidden with `keepMounted`). In `type="single"` without `collapsible`, the open trigger gets `aria-disabled`. The chevron and plus are `aria-hidden`; a `leadingIcon` is not, so pass an `aria-hidden` icon.

#### Reduced motion

The panel animates its height and opacity (`animate-accordion-down` and `animate-accordion-up`) and the indicator turns with `chevron-turn`. The reduced-motion net sets the panel animations to 1 ms and ends the transitions, so sections still change state, only instantly.

#### Server rendering

Server render: part of it fills in after mount. Closed sections render only their triggers; sections open through `defaultValue` or `value` render their content in the server HTML. The root `dir` is read after mount (the server writes `ltr`), so in an RTL document the first server paint has `dir="ltr"` on the accordion until hydration settles it.

#### Gotchas

- `type` is required by Radix: `"single"` (add `collapsible` to allow closing the open item) or `"multiple"`. Without `collapsible`, the open item cannot be closed by clicking it.
- On `AccordionContent`, `className` lands on the inner padding div, not on the Radix panel; other props (`style`, `data-*`, `forceMount`) go to the panel.
- `keepMounted` on `Accordion` keeps every closed panel in the tree, hidden with `data-[state=closed]:hidden`, so inputs keep their state; `AccordionContent keepMounted` overrides it per panel, and `forceMount` wins over both.
- `AccordionTrigger icon` overrides the root indicator for one section, and `icon={false}` hides it. The `FAQ` export of this module defaults to `icon="plus"`, the root to `"chevron"`.

## AlertBanner

> Full-width announcement banner for the top of an app or page.

- Import: `import { AlertBanner } from "@sutra/ui"` (or from `@sutra/ui/core`)
- Source: `packages/ui/src/primitives/alert-banner` (primitives)
- Also accepts the props of HTMLAttributes

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `action` | `BannerAction \| React.ReactNode` |  | Inline call to action, rendered as a link (with `href`) or a button. |
| `align` | `"center" \| "start"` | `"center"` | Horizontal alignment of the message and actions. |
| `appearance` | `"solid" \| "soft"` | `"solid"` | Fill style: `solid` (full colour) or `soft` (tinted background). |
| `children` | `React.ReactNode` |  | Message content when `message` is omitted. |
| `contentKey` | `React.Key` |  | Changing it remounts the message block, replaying its enter animation (e.g. when a rotator swaps messages). |
| `contentProps` | `React.HTMLAttributes<HTMLDivElement> & { [key: `data-${string}`]: string \| number \| boolean \| undefined }` |  | Props for the message block (icon, message, action). |
| `defaultOpen` | `boolean` | `true` | Initial visibility when uncontrolled. |
| `dismissible` | `boolean` |  | Shows a close button. Controlled via `open`/`onOpenChange`, or uncontrolled. |
| `dismissLabel` | `string` | `"Dismiss banner"` | Accessible name of the dismiss button. |
| `icon` | `React.ReactNode \| false` |  | Custom icon; `false`/`null` hides it. |
| `leading` | `React.ReactNode` |  | Content before the message block (e.g. a "previous" control). |
| `message` | `React.ReactNode` |  | Main message. Children are used when `message` is omitted. |
| `onDismiss` | `() => void` |  | Called when the user dismisses the banner with the close button. |
| `onOpenChange` | `(open: boolean) => void` |  | Called with `false` when the banner is dismissed. |
| `open` | `boolean` |  | Controlled visibility. Use with `onOpenChange`. |
| `sticky` | `boolean` | `false` | Pins the banner to the top of the scroll container. |
| `tone` | `ToneInput \| "inverse"` |  | Semantic colour (default `primary`); `inverse` gives a high-contrast dark banner. |
| `trailing` | `React.ReactNode` |  | Content after the message block, before the close button (e.g. a pager). |
| `variant` | `AlertBannerVariant \| null` | `"primary"` | **Deprecated.** Use `tone` (`brand` is now `primary`). Legacy name of `tone`. |

### Variants

- `variant`: `primary`, `brand`, `neutral`, `info`, `success`, `warning`, `destructive`, `inverse` (default "primary")
- `appearance`: `solid`, `soft` (default "solid")
- `sticky`: `true`, `false` (default false)
- `align`: `center`, `start` (default "center")

### Notes

**When to use:** A full-width announcement bar for the top of an app or page, with an icon, a message, an optional action and an optional dismiss button. Solid or soft fill, optionally sticky.

**Use instead when:**
- `InlineAlert`: a notice inside a form, panel or page body
- `RotatingNoticeBar`: several notices that take turns
- `Toaster`: a transient message that leaves by itself
- `AlertDialog`: the user must answer before going on

#### Keyboard

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Moves through the `leading` and `trailing` controls, the action and the dismiss button |
| Enter | Follows the action link, or presses the action or dismiss button |
| Space | Presses the action or dismiss button (not a link) |

The banner itself is not focusable and no arrow key does anything, so RTL changes no key. In RTL the arrow glyph of an `action` object is mirrored and the dismiss button stays on the end edge, which is then the left. Dismissing does not move focus: the banner just unmounts.

#### Screen readers

- `tone` `warning` and `destructive` render `role="alert"`, which is announced when the banner is inserted. Every other tone is a `role="region"`, which is not announced on insertion, so do not rely on it for urgent news.
- Both carry `aria-label="Announcement"`. Pass your own `aria-label` to rename it. Passing `role` removes the default label, so add one yourself.
- The icon is `aria-hidden`; the arrow after an `action` label is too. The dismiss button is named by `dismissLabel` (default "Dismiss banner").
- An `action` object renders an `<a>` when it has `href`, otherwise a `<button type="button">`. Any other node you pass as `action` is rendered as is.

#### Reduced motion

Dismissing plays `animate-out` (a 200 ms fade and a small slide up). Under reduced motion the slide is removed and the fade stays; the banner unmounts on `animationend`, with a 250 ms timer as a fallback. The hover nudge of the action arrow is a transition and ends in 1 ms.

#### Server rendering

Server render: same markup as the client. An open banner renders its full markup on the server; it uses only state, and the timer starts in an effect. With `defaultOpen={false}` or `open={false}` it renders nothing on both sides.

#### Gotchas

- With `open` set, the banner is controlled: the close button calls `onOpenChange(false)` and `onDismiss`, but it stays until you pass `open={false}`. Without `open`, it hides itself.
- It stays mounted for the exit (`data-state="closed"`), so `open` going back to `true` mid-exit brings it straight back.
- `variant` is a deprecated alias of `tone` (`brand` is `primary`); `tone` wins when both are set. `inverse` is the dark high-contrast bar.
- `appearance="soft"` changes nothing for `neutral` and `inverse`. `message` wins over `children`. `icon={false}` removes the icon.

## AlertDialog

> Interrupting confirmation dialog root (no outside-click dismiss).

- Import: `import { AlertDialog } from "@sutra/ui"` (or from `@sutra/ui/overlays`)
- Source: `packages/ui/src/primitives/dialog` (primitives)
- Parts: [`AlertDialogAction`](AlertDialogAction.md), [`AlertDialogCancel`](AlertDialogCancel.md), [`AlertDialogContent`](AlertDialogContent.md), [`AlertDialogDescription`](AlertDialogDescription.md), [`AlertDialogFooter`](AlertDialogFooter.md), [`AlertDialogHeader`](AlertDialogHeader.md), [`AlertDialogTitle`](AlertDialogTitle.md), [`AlertDialogTrigger`](AlertDialogTrigger.md)
- Also accepts the props of DialogProps

### Props

No props of its own.

### Part props

Props of `AlertDialogAction`, `AlertDialogCancel`, `AlertDialogContent`, `AlertDialogFooter`, `AlertDialogHeader`: see [the full page](md/AlertDialog.md).

### Notes

**When to use:** A modal that interrupts the page for one focused task. Centred on screens from `sm` up, a bottom sheet below. `AlertDialog` and `ConfirmDialog` are the variants for confirmations that must be answered.

**Use instead when:**
- `Sheet`: a side or edge panel that keeps the page context
- `Drawer`: a touch-first bottom sheet you drag
- `Popover`: a small floating panel that does not block the page
- `DialogProvider`: ask for a confirm or a prompt from code

#### Keyboard

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Cycle focus inside the dialog (it is trapped while open) |
| Escape | Close the dialog (`AlertDialog` closes on Escape too, but not on an outside click) |
| Enter, Space | Activate the focused button, including the close button |

Focus moves into the dialog on open and returns to whatever had it before, even when the dialog was opened without a `DialogTrigger` (a hotkey, a menu item, controlled `open`). There are no arrow-key or direction-dependent keys, so RTL changes nothing.

#### Screen readers

Radix gives the panel `role="dialog"` (`alertdialog` for `AlertDialog`), `aria-labelledby` from `DialogTitle` and `aria-describedby` from `DialogDescription`, and hides the rest of the page from assistive technology while it is open. Always render a `DialogTitle` (it may be visually hidden); `ConfirmDialog` requires `title` for that reason. The built-in close button is labelled "Close". The mobile grabber bar is `aria-hidden` decoration.

#### Reduced motion

The panel fades and zooms in (from the bottom edge on mobile) with the `animate-in` utilities; under reduced motion the net removes the zoom and slide and keeps the fade.

#### Server rendering

Server render: same markup as the client. A closed dialog renders only its trigger on both server and client, so there is nothing to mismatch. The content is portalled into `<body>` after mount: a dialog that is `open` on first render appears after hydration, not in the server HTML. The portalled layer does not sit inside a subtree `data-style` or `dir`: put them on `<html>`.

#### Gotchas

- `AlertDialog` ignores outside clicks (no dismiss by clicking the backdrop), `Dialog` does not: use `AlertDialog` when the user must choose.
- `ConfirmDialog onConfirm` may return a promise: the confirm button shows a spinner and closing is blocked until it settles, and throwing keeps the dialog open.
- A dialog opened from a menu item that then unmounts cannot return focus to it (the opener is gone), and Radix's default applies; keep the opener mounted when focus matters.
- `size` only sets the maximum width from `sm` up; below that every dialog is full width.

## AppStoreBadge

> Official-style "Download on the App Store / Get it on Google Play" link badge.

- Import: `import { AppStoreBadge } from "@sutra/ui"` (or from `@sutra/ui/core`)
- Source: `packages/ui/src/primitives/app-store-badge` (primitives)
- `data-slot`: `mark`, `eyebrow`, `name`
- Also accepts the props of HTMLAttributes, AnchorHTMLAttributes

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `store` (required) | `AppStore` |  | Store the badge links to, which picks its logo and "Download on" or "Get it on" text. |
| `size` | `"sm" \| "md" \| "lg"` | `"md"` | Badge height: `sm` 40px, `md` 48px or `lg` 56px. |
| `theme` | `"dark" \| "light"` | `"dark"` | Badge colours: `dark` (black badge, for light backgrounds) or `light` (white badge). |

### Variants

- `theme`: `dark`, `light` (default "dark")
- `size`: `sm`, `md`, `lg` (default "md")

### Notes

**When to use:** A link styled as the "Download on the App Store" or "Get it on Google Play" badge. `store` picks the logo and text (`apple`, `google-play`, `microsoft`, `galaxy`), `theme` the colours and `size` the height.

**Use instead when:**
- `Button`: a normal action or a button-styled link with your own label
- `TextLink`: a plain link in running text

#### Keyboard

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Moves focus to and from the link |
| Enter | Follows the link (a native `<a>`, so Space does nothing) |

No arrow keys are used, so nothing changes in RTL.

#### Screen readers

A native `<a>` named by `aria-label`, which defaults to the badge text, for example "Download on the App Store" or "GET IT ON Google Play" (the Google Play eyebrow is written in capitals). The visible text is `aria-hidden` and the logos are decorative, so pass `aria-label` for a more specific name ("Get Sutra for iPhone"); the test pins that it replaces the default.

#### Reduced motion

On hover the badge lifts 1px with a shadow, and on press it scales to 0.98. These are transitions, which the reduced-motion net ends in 1 ms: the lift and press still happen, without the glide.

#### Server rendering

Server render: same markup as the client. Plain markup with no browser API, so server and client output match. The Galaxy mark takes a `useId` for its gradient, which is stable between server and client.

#### Slots

- `mark`: the wrapper around the store logo
- `eyebrow`: the small line above the name ("Download on the")
- `name`: the large store name

#### Gotchas

- Pass `href`. Without it the `<a>` has no link role and cannot be focused, and the type does not require it.
- The text, the four logos and the colours (`dark` black badge for light backgrounds, `light` white badge) are fixed brand art: not themed, not localized, and `size` only offers `sm` (40px), `md` (48px, default) and `lg` (56px).
- The badge is a link, not a button: for an `onClick` without navigation use `Button`.
- Extra props go on the anchor (`target`, `rel`, `onClick`), so add `rel="noopener"` yourself with `target="_blank"`.

## AspectRatio

> Box that keeps a fixed width/height ratio for media and embeds.

- Import: `import { AspectRatio } from "@sutra/ui"` (or from `@sutra/ui/core`)
- Source: `packages/ui/src/primitives/aspect-ratio` (primitives)
- Also accepts the props of HTMLAttributes, PrimitivePropsWithRef

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cover` | `boolean` | `true` | Make a direct img/video/iframe child fill the box with `object-cover`. |
| `framed` | `boolean` | `false` | Subtle muted background and border, useful as a placeholder frame. |
| `ratio` | `AspectRatioPreset \| number` | `"16/9"` | Preset like `"16/9"` or a number (width / height). Default 16/9. |
| `rounded` | `boolean` | `false` | Round the corners and clip content (`rounded-box`). |

### Notes

**When to use:** A box that keeps a fixed width-to-height ratio (a preset like `"16/9"` or a number) for images, video, embeds and placeholders, with optional rounded corners and frame.

**Use instead when:**
- `Frame`: a titled tray of rows
- `Carousel`: several slides
- `Card`: a content surface that grows with its content
- `Skeleton`: a loading placeholder with a set size

#### Keyboard

Not focusable: no keyboard interaction.

#### Screen readers

Adds no role or name: it is a plain `div` around its content. Give the image its `alt`, the video its controls and captions, and the iframe a `title`.

#### Reduced motion

Static: no animation.

#### Server rendering

Server render: same markup as the client. Plain markup with no browser API. The ratio is a padding-bottom on a wrapper (not measured in script), so the box has its final height on the first paint and the page does not jump when the media loads.

#### Gotchas

- The width comes from the parent (`w-full`); the height follows from the ratio. `ratio` is a preset (`16/9`, `4/3`, `1/1`, `21/9`, `3/4`, `9/16`) or a number as width over height, default 16/9.
- Radix renders an outer wrapper and puts your `className`, `style` and other props on the inner box, which is absolutely positioned to fill it. Size and position the box through its parent, not with `className`.
- `cover` (default true) makes a direct `img` or `video` child fill the box with `object-cover` and an `iframe` child fill it; it does not reach images nested deeper.
- `rounded` clips the content to the box radius; `framed` adds a muted background and border, which suits a placeholder before the media loads.

## Avatar

> User avatar with image, initials fallback, status dot and verified badge. The fallback is labelled with `alt` or `name`. For square tiles that stand for apps, providers or tools, use `Monogram`.

- Import: `import { Avatar } from "@sutra/ui"` (or from `@sutra/ui/core`)
- Source: `packages/ui/src/primitives/avatar` (primitives)
- Parts: [`AvatarContext`](AvatarContext.md), [`AvatarFallback`](AvatarFallback.md), [`AvatarImage`](AvatarImage.md), [`AvatarLabelGroup`](AvatarLabelGroup.md)
- Also accepts the props of HTMLAttributes

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `alt` | `string` |  | Alt text of the image and label of the initials fallback. Defaults to `name`; `""` marks the avatar decorative (use it beside a visible name). |
| `color` | `string` |  | Explicit fallback colour (any CSS colour); overrides the colour derived from `name`. |
| `colorful` | `boolean` | `true` | Colorize the initials fallback deterministically from `name` (via `colorForSeed`). Default true. |
| `fallback` | `React.ReactNode` |  | Custom fallback content (overrides auto initials). |
| `fallbackClassName` | `string` |  | Extra classes for the fallback (initials / icon) layer. |
| `frameClassName` | `string` |  | Extra classes for the inner image/fallback frame. |
| `initialsOptions` | `InitialsOptions` |  | Options for the auto initials (e.g. `{ singleWord: 2 }` → "Ma" for "Maya"). |
| `name` | `string` |  | Used to derive initials, the fallback color and the default alt text. |
| `ring` | `boolean` | `false` | Adds a ring in the background color (useful when overlapping). |
| `shape` | `AvatarShape` | `"circle"` | Outline of the avatar: round or rounded-square. |
| `size` | `AvatarSize` | `"md"` | Diameter from `xs` to `2xl`; the initials and status dot scale with it. |
| `src` | `string` |  | Image URL; the initials fallback shows while it loads or when it fails. |
| `status` | `AvatarStatus` |  | Presence dot in the bottom corner: online, offline, busy or away. |
| `variant` | `AvatarVariant` | `"soft"` | How the colour is applied to the fallback. Default `soft`. |
| `verified` | `boolean` |  | Shows a verified check badge in the corner. |

### Variants

- `size`: `xs`, `sm`, `md`, `lg`, `xl`, `2xl` (default "md")
- `shape`: `circle`, `square` (default "circle")
- `ring`: `true`, `false` (default false)

### Part props

Props of `AvatarLabelGroup`: see [the full page](md/Avatar.md).

### Notes

**When to use:** A person's picture with an initials fallback, an optional presence dot and a verified badge. `AvatarLabelGroup` adds a name and a supporting line beside it.

**Use instead when:**
- `Monogram`: a square tile for an app, provider or tool, not a person
- `AvatarGroup`: several avatars overlapping with a +N count
- `Item`: a full row with media, title and actions

#### Keyboard

Not focusable: no keyboard interaction. Wrap it in a `Button` or a link when it should be clickable.

#### Screen readers

- With `name` or `alt` the fallback is a `role="img"` whose `aria-label` is `alt` (or `name` when `alt` is not given; `alt=""` leaves it unlabelled); the loaded `<img>` gets `alt` or `name` as its alt text. With neither, the fallback is an unlabelled `RiUserLine` icon (`aria-hidden`), so a nameless avatar is silent.
- `status` renders a `role="img"` dot labelled with the status word ("online", "offline", "busy", "away"). `verified` adds a check icon (`aria-hidden`) with sr-only text "Verified".
- `AvatarLabelGroup` shows the name and supporting text as plain text, and the avatar it generates is decorative (`alt=""`), so the name is heard once; its status dot is still announced. Pass `avatarProps={{ alt: "…" }}` to name it anyway. On a plain `Avatar`, `alt=""` likewise drops the image alt and the fallback label.

#### Reduced motion

Static, apart from the loaded image fading in with `animate-fade-in`, which the reduced-motion net in `sutra.css` turns off.

#### Server rendering

Server render: part of it fills in after mount. Without `src` the initials render in the server HTML. With `src` the server output is an empty frame: Radix Avatar only renders the image after it has loaded in the browser, and `Avatar` delays the fallback by 500 ms (`delayMs`) so a fast image does not flash initials. The frame has a fixed size, so nothing shifts when the image arrives.

#### Gotchas

- Initials come from `initials(name, initialsOptions)`: first and last word by default, so "Maya" gives "M". Pass `initialsOptions={{ singleWord: 2 }}` for "MA".
- The fallback colour is derived from `name` with `colorForSeed`, so one person has one colour everywhere. `color` overrides it, `colorful={false}` turns it off, and a custom `fallback` node also skips the seed colour. `variant="solid"` fills with the full colour and sets the initials in white or dark ink, whichever contrasts more (about 4.5:1 or better; colours that are not hex keep white).
- Passing `children` replaces the built-in image and fallback entirely: compose `AvatarImage` and `AvatarFallback` yourself, then `src`, `name`, `fallback` and `color` are ignored.
- Inside an `AvatarGroup`, `size`, `shape` and `ring` come from the group, but a prop set on the avatar wins. The status dot and verified badge sit at the logical end corner, so they flip in RTL.

## AvatarGroup

> Overlapping stack of avatars with overflow count and optional add button.

- Import: `import { AvatarGroup } from "@sutra/ui"` (or from `@sutra/ui/core`)
- Source: `packages/ui/src/primitives/avatar-group` (primitives)
- Also accepts the props of HTMLAttributes

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `addLabel` | `string` | `"Add member"` | Accessible name of the add button. |
| `max` | `number` |  | Maximum avatars to show before collapsing the rest into a "+N" bubble. |
| `onAdd` | `() => void` |  | Renders a dashed "add" button at the end. |
| `shape` | `AvatarShape` | `"circle"` | Avatar shape for every avatar in the group. |
| `size` | `AvatarSize` | `"md"` | Avatar size for every avatar in the group. |
| `spacing` | `"tight" \| "normal"` | `"normal"` | How much the avatars overlap: `tight` overlaps more than `normal`. |
| `total` | `number` |  | Override the overflow count (e.g. when only a page of users is loaded). |

### Notes

**When to use:** An overlapping row of avatars that collapses extra people into a "+N" bubble and can end with a dashed add button.

**Use instead when:**
- `Avatar`: a single person
- `Item`: a list row for each person
- `Popover`: show the full list of the hidden people on click

#### Keyboard

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Moves focus to and from the add button (only rendered with `onAdd`) |
| Enter, Space | Activates the add button (native `<button>`) |

The avatars and the +N bubble are not focusable. The row is a flex row, so it mirrors in RTL; no key changes.

#### Screen readers

- The root is `role="group"`. It has no name of its own, so pass `aria-label` ("Team") when the group means something.
- The overflow bubble is a `role="img"` labelled "N more" (its text reads "+N", or "99+" above 99). The add button is labelled "Add member"; change it with `addLabel`.
- Each avatar keeps the rules of `Avatar`: labelled by `name` or `alt`, silent without either.

#### Reduced motion

Each avatar lifts 2px on hover with a 200 ms transform transition, which the reduced-motion net in `sutra.css` ends within 1 ms.

#### Server rendering

Server render: part of it fills in after mount. The group is plain markup (no browser API), so it matches on server and client. Avatars with `src` follow `Avatar`: the server HTML holds an empty frame and the picture or fallback appears after mount.

#### Gotchas

- `max` slices the children; `total` only changes the count, it does not add avatars. The bubble shows `total - visible` (or `children - visible`), so with `max={2} total={250}` and two children it reads "99+" and is labelled "248 more".
- Only React elements count as avatars: strings and `null` are dropped, and a fragment is one child.
- The group gives its avatars `size`, `shape` and a background `ring`; an avatar with its own `size` or `shape` prop keeps it, which breaks the even overlap.
- The overflow bubble is not interactive. For "click +N to see everyone" put the group in a trigger yourself.

## Badge

> Compact label for status, category or count.

- Import: `import { Badge } from "@sutra/ui"` (or from `@sutra/ui/core`)
- Source: `packages/ui/src/primitives/badge` (primitives)
- Also accepts the props of HTMLAttributes

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `color` | `"neutral" \| "primary" \| "brand" \| "success" \| "warning" \| "destructive" \| "info" \| "gray" \| "blue" \| "purple" \| "pink" \| "orange"` | `"neutral"` | Legacy colour name; prefer `tone`. Also accepts the categorical hues (gray, blue, purple, pink, orange). |
| `leadingIcon` | `React.ReactNode` |  | Icon before the label. |
| `onRemove` | `() => void` |  | Shows a small remove button. |
| `removeLabel` | `string` | `"Remove"` | Accessible name of the remove button. |
| `size` | `"sm" \| "md" \| "lg"` | `"md"` | Badge height and text size. |
| `tone` | `ToneInput` |  | Semantic colour (`neutral \| primary \| success \| warning \| destructive \| info`). Wins over `color`. |
| `trailingIcon` | `React.ReactNode` |  | Icon after the label. |
| `variant` | `"soft" \| "solid" \| "outline" \| "dot"` | `"soft"` | Fill style: `soft` (tinted), `solid` (full colour), `outline` (border only) or `dot` (neutral pill with a coloured dot). |

### Variants

- `variant`: `soft`, `solid`, `outline`, `dot` (default "soft")
- `color`: `neutral`, `primary`, `brand`, `success`, `warning`, `destructive`, `info`, `gray`, `blue`, `purple`, `pink`, `orange` (default "neutral")
- `size`: `sm`, `md`, `lg` (default "md")

### Notes

**When to use:** A compact label for a category, tag, status word or count. Four fill styles, three sizes, optional icons and a remove button.

**Use instead when:**
- `StatusBadge`: a status with a ready-made dot, icon or spinner and a default label
- `Chip`: a filter or selection token that toggles
- `Eyebrow`: a small caption above a heading

#### Keyboard

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Moves focus to the remove button, which only exists with `onRemove` |
| Enter, Space | Removes (native `<button>`) |

The badge itself is not focusable and has no direction-dependent keys, so RTL changes nothing.

#### Screen readers

- A plain `<span>`: no role, so its text is read inline. Colour carries no meaning for assistive technology, so put the meaning in the text ("Paid", not just a green badge).
- The remove button is labelled "Remove" by default. Several badges would all read the same, so pass `removeLabel` with the item ("Remove beta").
- `variant="dot"` draws its dot as an `aria-hidden` span. Icons you pass as `leadingIcon` or `trailingIcon` are not hidden for you: pass `aria-hidden` icons.

#### Reduced motion

Static. The only motion is a colour transition, which the reduced-motion net in `sutra.css` ends within 1 ms.

#### Server rendering

Server render: same markup as the client. Plain markup with no browser API, so server and client output match.

#### Gotchas

- `tone` (`neutral`, `primary`, `success`, `warning`, `destructive`, `info`, plus legacy aliases like `brand`, `danger`) wins over `color` when both are set. The categorical hues `gray`, `blue`, `purple`, `pink` and `orange` exist only on `color`.
- `variant="dot"` is always a neutral bordered pill: the colour only tints the dot, so `variant="dot" tone="success"` is not a green pill.
- Long text is truncated (`max-w-full` plus `truncate`), so give the badge a width limit from its parent rather than expecting it to wrap.
- `color` is kept for older call sites (the types say "legacy"); new code should pass `tone`.

## BatteryLevel

> Battery reading: a glyph or small bar with the percentage, toned warning when low and destructive when critical.

- Import: `import { BatteryLevel } from "@sutra/ui"` (or from `@sutra/ui/system`)
- Source: `packages/ui/src/primitives/battery-level` (primitives)
- `data-slot`: `battery-level`, `battery-level-fill`
- Also accepts the props of HTMLAttributes

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `accent` | `Accent` |  | Fill colour in the normal range (thresholds and charging still win). Default foreground. |
| `charging` | `boolean` | `false` | Shows a charging bolt and announces "charging". |
| `critical` | `number` | `10` | Critical threshold (destructive tone). Default 10. |
| `label` | `string` |  | Accessible text override. Default from `formatBatteryLevel`, e.g. "42% battery, charging". |
| `loading` | `boolean` |  | Waiting for the first reading: with no `value` the glyph or bar is an empty placeholder with no percentage. |
| `low` | `number` | `20` | Low threshold (warning tone). Default 20. |
| `showValue` | `boolean` | `true` | Show the percentage next to the glyph or bar. Default true. |
| `size` | `Size` | `"md"` | Glyph and text size. |
| `value` | `number \| null` |  | Charge 0–100. `null`/`undefined` renders an unknown reading ("—"). |
| `variant` | `BatteryLevelVariant` | `"icon"` | `icon`: battery glyph + percentage · `bar`: small horizontal bar + percentage · `text`: percentage only. Default `icon`. |

### Notes

**When to use:** A battery reading for a device: a glyph or small bar plus the percentage, warning when low, destructive when critical, with a charging bolt.

**Use instead when:**
- `Meter`: any other bounded value
- `Progress`: the progress of a task
- `StatusBadge`: a status word or dot, not a number

#### Keyboard

Not focusable: no keyboard interaction.

#### Screen readers

- The root is a `role="img"` named from `formatBatteryLevel`: "42% battery", "42% battery, charging", "18% battery, low", "7% battery, critically low", or "Battery level unknown". `label` replaces the whole sentence ("Case battery unknown"). The visible percentage sits inside the image role, so it is not read separately.
- The charging bolt is `aria-hidden`; the word "charging" comes from the label.
- `loading` with no `value` renders placeholders with `aria-busy` and sr-only text "Loading battery level…" (no image role); `loading` with a `value` keeps the reading and only adds `aria-busy="true"`.

#### Reduced motion

The fill animates its width over 500 ms and the loading placeholder pulses, both with `motion-reduce:` variants that switch them off.

#### Server rendering

Server render: same markup as the client. Plain markup computed from the props, no browser API, so server and client output match.

#### Slots

- `battery-level`: the root, with `data-state` (`ok`, `low`, `critical`, `unknown`, `loading`) and `data-charging`
- `battery-level-fill`: the filled part of the glyph or bar (its width is the percentage; the `text` variant has none)

#### Gotchas

- Thresholds are inclusive: `low` (default 20) and `critical` (default 10) are the values at or below which the tone changes, so exactly 20 reads "low" and exactly 10 reads "critically low". The value is clamped to 0 to 100.
- The fill colour is chosen in this order: critical, low, charging (success), then `accent`, then the default foreground. `accent` only applies in the normal range.
- `showValue={false}` hides the percentage for `icon` and `bar`, but the `text` variant always shows it (otherwise it would render nothing).
- A missing, `null` or `NaN` `value` is an unknown reading: a dash and an empty glyph, not 0%.

## Breadcrumb

> Breadcrumb navigation landmark.

- Import: `import { Breadcrumb } from "@sutra/ui"` (or from `@sutra/ui/navigation`)
- Source: `packages/ui/src/primitives/breadcrumbs` (primitives)
- Parts: [`BreadcrumbEllipsis`](BreadcrumbEllipsis.md), [`BreadcrumbItem`](BreadcrumbItem.md), [`BreadcrumbLink`](BreadcrumbLink.md), [`BreadcrumbList`](BreadcrumbList.md), [`BreadcrumbPage`](BreadcrumbPage.md), [`BreadcrumbSeparator`](BreadcrumbSeparator.md), [`Breadcrumbs`](Breadcrumbs.md)
- Also accepts the props of HTMLAttributes

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `separator` | `BreadcrumbSeparatorVariant` | `"chevron"` | Default separator for every `BreadcrumbSeparator` inside. |
| `size` | `"sm" \| "md"` | `"md"` | Text size of the trail. |

### Part props

Props of `BreadcrumbEllipsis`, `BreadcrumbLink`, `BreadcrumbSeparator`, `Breadcrumbs`: see [the full page](md/Breadcrumb.md).

### Notes

**When to use:** The path to the current page as a trail of links. `Breadcrumbs` takes an `items` array and can fold the middle crumbs into a menu with `maxItems`; the parts build custom trails.

**Use instead when:**
- `TabMenu`: switching between sibling views of one page
- `Steps`: progress through a fixed sequence
- `TreeView`: browsing a hierarchy rather than showing where you are

#### Keyboard

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Moves between the crumb links and the ellipsis button; the current page and separators are not focusable |
| Enter | Follows the focused link (a native `<a>` does not activate on Space) |
| Enter, Space, ArrowDown | On the ellipsis button: open the hidden-crumbs menu; ArrowUp and ArrowDown move through it, Enter follows a link, Escape closes it |

There are no left and right arrow keys, so nothing swaps in RTL. The trail itself follows the reading direction: it flows right to left in an RTL document, and the default chevron separator is mirrored (`slash` and `dot` are not).

#### Screen readers

`Breadcrumb` is a `<nav>` landmark labelled "Breadcrumb" by default (translate it with `aria-label`), holding an ordered list. The last crumb is a `<span aria-current="page">`, not a link, even when its item has an `href`. A middle crumb without an `href` is plain text with no `aria-current`. Separators are `aria-hidden` list items with `role="presentation"`. The ellipsis button is named "Show N more"; a plain ellipsis (no `items`) is hidden from assistive technology entirely.

#### Reduced motion

Static: hover colours are transitions that end in 1 ms under reduced motion. The only popup is the ellipsis menu, which keeps its fade and loses its movement like every `DropdownMenu`.

#### Server rendering

Server render: same markup as the client. Plain markup with no browser API: server and client output match. The ellipsis menu is closed, so only its button renders on the server.

#### Gotchas

- `maxItems` collapses only when `items.length > maxItems` and `maxItems` is at least 2. It keeps `itemsBeforeCollapse` (default 1) crumbs first and `itemsAfterCollapse` last (default `maxItems - itemsBeforeCollapse - 1`, at least 1); if those two cover every item, nothing collapses.
- Hidden crumbs without an `href` appear in the menu as disabled rows, because there is nowhere to go.
- For client-side routing pass `renderLink` (it receives `href`, `className` and `children`) on `Breadcrumbs`, or `BreadcrumbLink asChild` around your router link when composing the parts yourself.
- `separator` on `Breadcrumb` (`chevron`, `slash`, `dot`) sets every separator; a `variant` on one `BreadcrumbSeparator`, or children, override it. Parts need a `Breadcrumb` ancestor only for the shared `size` and `separator` defaults.

## BreakdownList

> Legend rows for a breakdown: colour dot, optional icon, label, right-aligned value and optional percent ("● Google Chrome 21.23 GB", "● postgres 312 MB 46%"). The last numeric column is muted. Rows can toggle series.

- Import: `import { BreakdownList } from "@sutra/ui"` (or from `@sutra/ui/dataviz`)
- Source: `packages/ui/src/primitives/meter` (primitives)
- `data-slot`: `breakdown-list`, `breakdown-list-marker`, `breakdown-list-icon`, `breakdown-list-label`, `breakdown-list-value`, `breakdown-list-percent`, `breakdown-list-item`
- Also accepts the props of HTMLAttributes

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `items` (required) | `BreakdownListItem[]` |  | Rows to list; each has a label, a value and a dot colour. |
| `defaultHiddenSeries` | `string[]` |  | Initially hidden row keys when uncontrolled. |
| `hiddenSeries` | `string[]` |  | Keys currently hidden (dimmed, struck through, left out of the default total). |
| `interactive` | `boolean` | `onHiddenSeriesChange !== undefined` | Rows are toggle buttons. Defaults to true when `onHiddenSeriesChange` is set. Alt-click, Alt+Enter or double-click isolates a row. |
| `marker` | `"dot" \| "square"` | `"dot"` | Swatch shape. Default "dot". |
| `onHiddenSeriesChange` | `(hidden: string[]) => void` |  | Called with the full list of hidden row keys when a row is toggled. |
| `percentFormatter` | `(share: number) => string` | `formatShare` | Formats a share (0–1). Default whole percent ("46%", "<1%"). |
| `showPercent` | `boolean` | `false` | Show the percent column. Default false. |
| `showValue` | `boolean` | `true` | Show the value column. Default true. |
| `size` | `"sm" \| "md"` | `"md"` | Row text size: "sm" (text-xs) or "md" (text-sm). Default "md". |
| `total` | `number` |  | Denominator for the default shares. Defaults to the sum of the visible values. |
| `valueFormatter` | `(value: number) => string` | `(v) => trim(v)` | Formats each row's value for display. Default is the localized number. |

### Notes

**When to use:** Legend rows for a breakdown: colour marker, optional icon, label, right-aligned value and optional percent. Rows can become toggle buttons that hide or isolate series.

**Use instead when:**
- `StackedMeter`: the bar and legend together (use `legend="list"`)
- `Item`: a general row with media, title and actions
- `KeyValue`: facts without colour markers
- `Table`: several columns per row

#### Keyboard

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Moves between the rows (only when rows are buttons, see `interactive`) |
| Enter, Space | Toggles the focused row's series hidden or shown |
| Alt+Enter, Alt+Space | Isolates the row: hides all the others, or shows everything if it is already isolated |

Alt-click and a double-click on a row isolate it too. The rows are a vertical list with no arrow keys, so RTL changes nothing.

#### Screen readers

- A `ul` of `li` rows: pass `aria-label` ("By container"), since the list has no name of its own.
- Interactive rows are `<button aria-pressed>`: pressed means the series is shown. Hidden rows are also struck through and dimmed, and their percent reads a dash.
- The colour marker and the icon are `aria-hidden`; the label names the row. Colour is never the only cue, because the label and value are text.
- The row `title` is "Click to toggle · Alt-click or double-click to isolate".

#### Reduced motion

Static; the hover background is a colour transition, which the reduced-motion net ends within 1 ms.

#### Server rendering

Server render: same markup as the client. Plain markup computed from the props with no browser API, so server and client output match.

#### Slots

- `breakdown-list`: the `ul`
- `breakdown-list-item`: each `li`, with `data-state` `visible` or `hidden`
- `breakdown-list-marker`: the colour dot or square
- `breakdown-list-icon`: the optional icon box
- `breakdown-list-label`: the label
- `breakdown-list-value`: the value column
- `breakdown-list-percent`: the percent column

#### Gotchas

- Rows are plain text unless `interactive` is true, which it is by default only when `onHiddenSeriesChange` is passed. `hiddenSeries` controls the hidden keys; `defaultHiddenSeries` starts them uncontrolled.
- `key` defaults to the label when it is a string, otherwise the row index, and hidden state is stored by key.
- Percent is `share` when given, else `value / total`, where `total` defaults to the sum of the visible rows: hiding a series changes the other rows' percentages. `valueText` replaces the formatted value.
- `color` is a token name (`primary`, `success`, `warning`, `destructive`, `info`, `muted`) or any CSS colour.

## Button

> The standard button. Extra props are spread to the `<button>` (or to the child with `asChild`); icon-only sizes need an `aria-label`.

- Import: `import { Button } from "@sutra/ui"` (or from `@sutra/ui/core`)
- Source: `packages/ui/src/primitives/button` (primitives)
- Also accepts the props of HTMLAttributes, ButtonHTMLAttributes

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `asChild` | `boolean` |  | Render as the child element (e.g. a link) while keeping button styles. |
| `fullWidth` | `boolean` |  | Stretches the button to the width of its container. |
| `leadingIcon` | `React.ReactNode` |  | Icon before the label. |
| `loading` | `boolean` |  | Shows a spinner and disables the button. |
| `size` | `"xs" \| "sm" \| "md" \| "lg" \| "xl" \| "icon-xs" \| "icon-sm" \| "icon" \| "icon-lg" \| "icon-xl"` | `"md"` | Button height and padding; `icon-*` sizes are square. |
| `spinnerProps` | `Partial<SpinnerProps>` |  | Overrides for the loading spinner (variant, size, `label`, colour via `className`); it inherits the button text colour by default. |
| `trailingIcon` | `React.ReactNode` |  | Icon after the label. |
| `variant` | `"primary" \| "secondary" \| "tertiary" \| "soft" \| "ghost" \| "outline" \| "destructive" \| "destructive-soft" \| "inverse" \| "link"` | `"primary"` | Visual style: `primary` (filled), `secondary` (bordered), `tertiary` (muted fill), `soft`, `ghost`, `outline`, `destructive`, `destructive-soft`, `inverse` or `link`. |

### Variants

- `variant`: `primary`, `secondary`, `tertiary`, `soft`, `ghost`, `outline`, `destructive`, `destructive-soft`, `inverse`, `link` (default "primary")
- `size`: `xs`, `sm`, `md`, `lg`, `xl`, `icon-xs`, `icon-sm`, `icon`, `icon-lg`, `icon-xl` (default "md")
- `fullWidth`: `true`

### Notes

**When to use:** The standard action. Ten variants and five text sizes plus five square icon sizes, with built-in loading and leading and trailing icon slots.

**Use instead when:**
- `TextLink`: the action is inline in running text or navigates
- `SplitButton`: a primary action with a menu of alternatives
- `ToggleGroup`: a set of loose on/off buttons
- `FloatingActionButton`: one pinned screen action

#### Keyboard

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Moves focus to and from the button. A `disabled` or `loading` button is not focusable |
| Enter, Space | Activates it (native `<button>` behaviour) |

With `asChild` the child element keeps its own keyboard behaviour: a link activates on Enter only, not Space. Left and Right arrows have no meaning, so nothing changes in RTL.

#### Screen readers

- A native `<button type="button">` unless you pass `type`; the name comes from its text. The `icon-*` sizes have no text, so pass `aria-label`.
- `loading` sets `aria-busy="true"` and disables the button; the spinner has its own accessible label (`spinnerProps={{ label }}` changes it, `label=""` makes it decorative).
- Icons passed as `leadingIcon` and `trailingIcon` are not hidden for you: pass `aria-hidden` icons (Remix icons are decorative when you do).
- With `asChild` and `disabled` or `loading`, the child gets `aria-disabled`, `data-disabled` and `tabIndex={-1}`, and clicks are swallowed in the capture phase.

#### Reduced motion

The press effect (`active:scale-[0.98]`) and the colour fades are transitions, which the reduced-motion net ends within 1 ms. The `loading` spinner keeps spinning, as it carries meaning.

#### Server rendering

Server render: same markup as the client. Renders plain markup with no browser API, so server and client output match. The module is a client module in the build (`"use client"`), which is only a boundary: it still renders to HTML on the first server pass.

#### Gotchas

- `loading` replaces `leadingIcon` with the spinner but keeps `trailingIcon`, and it also disables the button: do not combine it with your own `disabled` state expecting a different look.
- `type` defaults to `"button"`, not the browser's `"submit"`: pass `type="submit"` for form submit buttons.
- Use `asChild` for links (`<Button asChild><a href>`); it makes the link look and act inert while disabled or loading, but it is still an anchor, not a button.
- `variant="link"` drops the height and padding (`h-auto px-0`); size classes then only change the text. It keeps a 24px-tall hit area (an invisible `::after`), so a stand-alone link button is still a valid tap target.

## ButtonGroup

> Attached row (or column) of buttons. Pass `type="single" | "multiple"` to turn it into a toggle group whose `ButtonGroupItem`s can be pressed.

- Import: `import { ButtonGroup } from "@sutra/ui"` (or from `@sutra/ui/core`)
- Source: `packages/ui/src/primitives/button-group` (primitives)
- `data-slot`: `button-group`
- Parts: [`ButtonGroupItem`](ButtonGroupItem.md), [`ButtonGroupSeparator`](ButtonGroupSeparator.md)
- Also accepts the props of HTMLAttributes, ToggleGroupImplProps, ToggleGroupImplSingleProps, PrimitivePropsWithRef

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `attached` | `boolean` | `true` | Merge borders and radii into one segmented control. Default true. |
| `className` | `string \| string` |  | Classes for the group container. |
| `orientation` | `ButtonGroupOrientation` | `"horizontal"` | Lays the buttons out in a row or a column. |
| `size` | `Size` | `"md"` | Size applied to every `ButtonGroupItem`. |
| `type` | `undefined \| "single" \| "multiple"` |  | Leave it out for a plain attached row of buttons; `"single"` or `"multiple"` turns the group into toggle buttons. Toggle mode: at most one item is pressed (radio roles); `ButtonGroupItem` then needs a `value`. Toggle mode: any number of items can be pressed (`aria-pressed`); `ButtonGroupItem` then needs a `value`. |

### Variants

- `orientation`: `horizontal`, `vertical` (default "horizontal")
- `attached`: `true`, `false` (default true)

### Part props

Props of `ButtonGroupItem`: see [the full page](md/ButtonGroup.md).

### Notes

**When to use:** Buttons joined into one segmented row or column. Without `type` it is a set of plain actions; with `type="single"` or `type="multiple"` the items become pressable toggles.

**Use instead when:**
- `Button`: one action
- `SplitButton`: a main action plus a menu
- `ToggleGroup`: loose, spaced on/off buttons
- `SegmentedControl`: a view switch where one option must always be selected

#### Keyboard

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Plain group: each item is a tab stop. Toggle group: one tab stop for the whole group, on the active item |
| Enter, Space | Activates a plain item, or toggles a pressable one |
| ArrowRight, ArrowLeft | Toggle group, horizontal: move focus between items and wrap around |
| ArrowDown, ArrowUp | Toggle group, `orientation="vertical"`: move focus between items and wrap around |

In RTL the horizontal arrows follow the reading order: the group passes the document direction to Radix, so ArrowLeft moves to the next item. A plain group has no arrow-key handling.

#### Screen readers

- Without `type` the container is `role="group"` of native buttons; name it with `aria-label`. `aria-orientation` is not used on a group, the orientation is `data-orientation`.
- `type="single"`: the container is a radio group and each item is `role="radio"` with `aria-checked`. `type="multiple"`: items are buttons with `aria-pressed`.
- `ButtonGroupSeparator` is `role="separator"` with the opposite orientation of the group.
- An icon-only item (`iconOnly`) has no text, so pass `aria-label`.

#### Reduced motion

Only colour and shadow transitions (150 ms), which the reduced-motion net ends within 1 ms. Nothing moves.

#### Server rendering

Server render: same markup as the client. Plain markup. In toggle mode the root `dir` is written by `useRootDirection`, so the server HTML says `ltr` and an RTL document settles after hydration; the layout itself is logical and does not change.

#### Slots

- `button-group`: the container
- `button-group-item`: each item
- `button-group-separator`: the divider

#### Gotchas

- A toggle item needs `value`; without it the item falls back to the empty string, so two items without a value select together.
- `size` on the group is passed to every item, and an item's own `size` wins. Only `sm`, `md` and `lg` exist here; use `iconOnly` plus `aria-label` for a square icon item instead of Button's `icon-*` sizes.
- `attached` (default true) removes the item shadows and gives the group one shadow and joined radii; `attached={false}` spaces items with a gap and gives each its own shadow.
- `type="single"` is Radix's single toggle group: pressing the selected item again clears the value. Use `SegmentedControl` when one option must always stay selected.

## Calendar

> Date calendar built on react-day-picker v9. Supports single, multiple and range modes. The ref goes to the root element.

- Import: `import { Calendar } from "@sutra/ui"` (or from `@sutra/ui/forms`)
- Source: `packages/ui/src/primitives/calendar` (primitives)
- Also accepts the props of PropsBase, PropsMulti, PropsRange, PropsSingle

### Props

No props of its own.

### Notes

**When to use:** An inline month grid for picking one date, several dates or a range. A styled `react-day-picker` v9, so every DayPicker prop works (`mode`, `selected`, `onSelect`, `numberOfMonths`, `captionLayout`, `locale`, `weekStartsOn`).

**Use instead when:**
- `DatePicker`: one date from a field with a popover
- `DateRangePicker`: a range from a field with presets
- `DateTimePicker`: a day and a time
- `TimePicker`: only a time of day

#### Keyboard

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Moves into the grid on one day (the last focused, else the selected, else today) and out again; the other days are not tab stops |
| ArrowLeft, ArrowRight | Previous or next day |
| ArrowUp, ArrowDown | Same weekday in the previous or next week |
| Shift+ArrowLeft, Shift+ArrowRight | Previous or next month |
| Shift+ArrowUp, Shift+ArrowDown | Previous or next year |
| PageUp, PageDown | Previous or next month (Shift: year) |
| Home, End | First or last day of the week |
| Enter, Space | Select the focused day (native button) |

In RTL, ArrowLeft goes forward and ArrowRight goes back (DayPicker reads the `dir` that `Calendar` passes down), and the previous and next month chevrons mirror. Up, Down, PageUp and PageDown do not change.

#### Screen readers

- The grid is `role="grid"` named by the month and year, with `aria-multiselectable` in `multiple` and `range` mode. Days are `gridcell`s with `aria-selected`; each day button is named by its full date, prefixed "Today, " and suffixed ", selected" when they apply.
- The month label is a polite `role="status"` region, so changing month is announced. The previous and next buttons are named "Go to the Previous Month" and "Go to the Next Month" (English; pass DayPicker `labels` to translate them, and `locale` for dates and weekdays).
- With `captionLayout="dropdown"` the month and year are native `<select>`s named "Choose the Month" and "Choose the Year", laid over a visual label.
- Without `mode` and `onDayClick` the days are plain cells, not buttons.

#### Reduced motion

Day hover and selection fade with short transitions, which the reduced-motion net ends in 1 ms. Nothing else moves; DayPicker's month `animate` option is off unless you pass it.

#### Server rendering

Server render: part of it fills in after mount. The grid renders on the server. "Today" comes from the clock at render time, so a server in another time zone, or one that rendered a day earlier, can mark a different day than the client and trigger a hydration warning; pass `today` to pin it. The reading direction is `ltr` in the server HTML and settles after hydration on an RTL document. Dropdown layouts default `startMonth` and `endMonth` from the current year, so they differ across a year change.

#### Gotchas

- `captionLayout="dropdown"`, `"dropdown-months"` and `"dropdown-years"` get a default range of 100 years back and 10 years forward; pass `startMonth` and `endMonth` to change it (react-day-picker needs a range to offer year choices).
- `showOutsideDays` defaults to `true`, so the days of neighbouring months show muted; outside days are never the Tab target. Pass `showOutsideDays={false}` for blank cells.
- In `single` mode a second click on the selected day clears it unless you pass `required`; `selected` with `onSelect` is the controlled pair, and with no `onSelect` DayPicker keeps the selection itself.
- Two or more `numberOfMonths` sit side by side only while the column is wide enough; they wrap and stack in a narrow container. The ref goes to the root element, and a `dir` you pass overrides the detected direction.

## Card

> Card surface used across components and blocks; compose it with `CardHeader`, `CardContent` and `CardFooter`.

- Import: `import { Card } from "@sutra/ui"` (or from `@sutra/ui/core`)
- Source: `packages/ui/src/primitives/layout` (primitives)
- `data-slot`: `card`
- Parts: [`CardAction`](CardAction.md), [`CardContent`](CardContent.md), [`CardDescription`](CardDescription.md), [`CardFooter`](CardFooter.md), [`CardHeader`](CardHeader.md), [`CardTitle`](CardTitle.md)
- Also accepts the props of HTMLAttributes

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `as` | `CardElement` |  | Element to render, so a card can sit in the page outline as an `article`, `section` or list item. |
| `padded` | `boolean` | `false` | Adds 24px (16px at `size="sm"`) of padding on the card itself; the parts carry their own padding instead. |
| `size` | `"sm" \| "md"` | `"md"` | `sm` tightens the padding of the card and its parts. |

### Part props

Props of `CardFooter`, `CardTitle`: see [the full page](md/Card.md).

### Notes

**When to use:** The standard surface for grouped content: a bordered, raised box you compose from a header (title, description, action), a body and a footer.

**Use instead when:**
- `Frame`: a titled tray around a list of rows
- `Item`: a single row with media, title and actions
- `Dialog`: the same content in a modal
- `StatCard`: a ready-made figure with a label and trend
- `Accordion`: sections that open and close

#### Keyboard

Not focusable: no keyboard interaction. A card is not clickable by itself; put a link or button inside (`CardAction`, `CardFooter`), or make the title a link.

#### Screen readers

- `Card` has no role. `as` picks the element: `article`, `section`, `aside`, `li` or `div`. A `section` is only a named `region` landmark when it has `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`, and an `li` needs a `ul` or `ol` parent.
- `CardTitle` is a plain `div` unless `as` is `h2`, `h3` or `h4`, so it is not a heading by default. Pick the level that fits the page outline.
- `CardDescription` is a `p` and is not linked to the card: add `aria-describedby` on the card yourself if it should be read with it.

#### Reduced motion

Static: no animation.

#### Server rendering

Server render: same markup as the client. Plain markup with no browser API, so server and client output match.

#### Slots

- `card`: the root, with `data-size` set to `sm` for the small size
- `card-header`: the title row; two columns when it holds a `card-action`
- `card-title`: the title
- `card-description`: the muted line under the title
- `card-action`: the control at the end of the header
- `card-content`: the body
- `card-footer`: the footer, with `data-variant` set to `plain` or `panel`

#### Gotchas

- The parts carry the padding (from `--card-pad`): do not add `padded` to a card made of parts, or the padding doubles. `padded` is for a flat card with your own content.
- `size="sm"` shrinks the padding, gap and text through CSS variables on the card (`--card-pad`, `--card-gap` and the text sizes), so every part inside follows it.
- `CardHeader` switches to two columns with a `CardAction` through a CSS `:has()` rule; the action sits at the inline end, so it flips in RTL.
- `CardFooter variant="panel"` is a muted band with a top border flush with the card edges; the default `plain` footer is just spaced content.

## Checkbox

> Checkbox with checked, indeterminate and invalid states. Consumes `Field` context.

- Import: `import { Checkbox } from "@sutra/ui"` (or from `@sutra/ui/forms`)
- Source: `packages/ui/src/primitives/checkbox` (primitives)
- `data-slot`: `checkbox`, `checkbox-indicator`
- Parts: [`CheckboxCard`](CheckboxCard.md), [`CheckboxField`](CheckboxField.md), [`CheckboxGroup`](CheckboxGroup.md), [`CheckboxGroupItem`](CheckboxGroupItem.md), [`CheckboxGroupSelectAll`](CheckboxGroupSelectAll.md)
- Also accepts the props of HTMLAttributes, ButtonHTMLAttributes, CheckboxProps, PrimitivePropsWithRef

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `invalid` | `boolean` |  | Marks the checkbox invalid: error border and `aria-invalid`. Inherited from a surrounding `Field` when omitted. |
| `size` | `"sm" \| "md"` | `"md"` | Box size: `sm` 14px or `md` 16px. |

### Variants

- `size`: `sm`, `md` (default "md")

### Part props

Props of `CheckboxCard`, `CheckboxField`, `CheckboxGroup`, `CheckboxGroupItem`, `CheckboxGroupSelectAll`: see [the full page](md/Checkbox.md).

### Notes

**When to use:** A yes or no box with an indeterminate state. `CheckboxField` adds a label and description, `CheckboxCard` makes a whole bordered card the target, and `CheckboxGroup` binds several boxes to one `string[]` value with an optional select-all.

**Use instead when:**
- `Switch`: a setting that applies at once
- `RadioGroup`: exactly one choice
- `ToggleGroup`: loose on/off buttons
- `Combobox`: a long list of choices
- `TableCheckbox`: row selection in a table

#### Keyboard

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Moves between boxes; every box is its own tab stop, a group has no roving focus. A disabled box is skipped |
| Space | Toggles the focused box (an indeterminate box becomes checked) |

Enter does nothing: Radix cancels it, as the checkbox pattern has no Enter key. Clicking the label or, for `CheckboxCard`, anywhere on the card toggles it. No arrow keys, so RTL changes nothing.

#### Screen readers

- A `<button role="checkbox">` with `aria-checked` set to `true`, `false` or `mixed` (for `checked="indeterminate"`). `required` becomes `aria-required` and `invalid` becomes `aria-invalid`; both are inherited from a surrounding `Field` when you do not pass them.
- `CheckboxField` and `CheckboxCard` name the box through a `<label htmlFor>`; the description is added to `aria-describedby`. A bare `Checkbox`, and a `CheckboxField` with neither `label` nor `description`, has no name: pass `aria-label`.
- `CheckboxGroup` is `role="group"` named by its `label` (or `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`), described by `description` and the surrounding `Field`, and sets `aria-invalid` when `invalid`.
- The check and dash icons are `aria-hidden`.

#### Reduced motion

The tick pops in with `animate-in zoom-in-50`, and the box scales on press (`active:scale-90`) and fades its colours. Under reduced motion the net removes the zoom and ends the transitions in 1 ms; the tick still appears.

#### Server rendering

Server render: part of it fills in after mount. A single `Checkbox` renders the same on both sides, including `checked` and `defaultChecked`. In a `CheckboxGroup` the items register themselves in an effect, so on the server `CheckboxGroupSelectAll` is disabled and unchecked and takes its real state (checked, mixed, enabled) after mount. A surrounding `Field` also adds the `aria-describedby` for its description and error after mount.

#### Slots

- `checkbox`: the box, a `button role="checkbox"`
- `checkbox-indicator`: the span holding the check and dash icons, mounted only while checked or indeterminate
- `checkbox-field`: the row of box, label and description
- `checkbox-card`: the whole card label
- `checkbox-group`: the group element

#### Gotchas

- `CheckboxGroup` value is the list of checked item values, and `onValueChange` receives the whole new list; items you toggle are appended in click order. Use `name` on the group to post one entry per checked item (with each item's `value`) in a form.
- `CheckboxGroupSelectAll` acts only on enabled items, is mixed while some are checked, and is disabled when no item is enabled or registered.
- `CheckboxGroupItem` takes `value` (the group item key) and not `checked` or `onCheckedChange`; the group owns them. `disabled` on the group disables every item, and a group `invalid` is passed to each item.
- `size` is `sm` (14px) or `md` (16px); the click target stays at least 24px square through the hit area.

## Chip

> Interactive pill: toggleable filter, removable tag or selectable option.

- Import: `import { Chip } from "@sutra/ui"` (or from `@sutra/ui/core`)
- Source: `packages/ui/src/primitives/chip` (primitives)
- Parts: [`ChipGroup`](ChipGroup.md)
- Also accepts the props of HTMLAttributes, ButtonHTMLAttributes

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `avatar` | `React.ReactNode` |  | Small avatar or image at the start (sized automatically). |
| `color` | `ChipColor` | `"neutral"` | **Deprecated.** Use `tone` (`brand` is `primary`). Legacy name of `tone`. |
| `defaultSelected` | `boolean` |  | Initial toggle state when uncontrolled. |
| `leadingIcon` | `React.ReactNode` |  | Icon at the start of the chip; takes the place of the selection check mark. |
| `onRemove` | `() => void` |  | Shows a remove button; Backspace/Delete also trigger it. |
| `onSelectedChange` | `(selected: boolean) => void` |  | Called with the new state when the chip is toggled; also makes the chip a toggle button. |
| `removeLabel` | `string` | `"Remove"` | Accessible name of the remove button. |
| `selected` | `boolean` |  | Controlled toggle state (renders `aria-pressed`). |
| `showCheck` | `boolean` | `true` | Show a check mark when selected and no leading icon is set. Default true. |
| `size` | `ChipSize` | `"md"` | Chip height and text size. |
| `tone` | `ToneInput` |  | Semantic colour. Default `neutral` (`primary` inside a `ChipGroup`). |
| `value` | `string` |  | Identifies the chip inside a `ChipGroup`. |
| `variant` | `ChipVariant` | `"outline"` | Visual style: `outline` (border only), `soft` (tinted fill) or `solid` (filled). |
| `wrapperClassName` | `string` |  | Classes for the outer pill. `className` also targets the pill. |

### Variants

- `variant`: `outline`, `soft`, `solid` (default "outline")
- `color`: `neutral`, `brand`, `success`, `warning`, `destructive`, `info` (default "neutral")
- `size`: `sm`, `md`, `lg` (default "md")

### Part props

Props of `ChipGroup`: see [the full page](md/Chip.md).

### Notes

**When to use:** An interactive pill: a toggleable filter, a removable tag or a selectable option. `ChipGroup` makes single or multiple selection out of several chips.

**Use instead when:**
- `Badge`: a static label that is not clicked
- `ToggleGroup`: a bar of on/off buttons in one control
- `SegmentedControl`: two to four options that switch a view
- `Combobox`: pick many tags from a long list

#### Keyboard

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Moves between chips. The remove button is `tabIndex={-1}`, so it is skipped |
| Enter, Space | Toggles a selectable chip, or runs `onClick` (native `<button>`) |
| Backspace, Delete | With `onRemove`, removes the focused chip instead of the browser default |

There is no arrow-key roving inside a `ChipGroup`: every chip is its own tab stop. No key depends on direction, so RTL changes nothing.

#### Screen readers

- The chip is a `<button>` named by its text. A chip counts as selectable when it has `selected`, `defaultSelected`, `onSelectedChange`, or a `value` inside a `ChipGroup`; then it carries `aria-pressed`. A plain chip has no `aria-pressed`.
- `ChipGroup` is a `role="group"` with no name: pass `aria-label`. Single selection is still a set of toggle buttons (`aria-pressed`), not radios.
- The remove button is labelled "Remove" unless `removeLabel` says more ("Remove React"). The check mark is `aria-hidden`.
- Icon-only content needs an `aria-label` on the chip itself (extra props go to the inner button).

#### Reduced motion

Colour changes, the press scale and the check mark sliding open are transitions, which the reduced-motion net in `sutra.css` ends within 1 ms.

#### Server rendering

Server render: same markup as the client. Plain markup with no browser API, so server and client output match, including selected state from `defaultSelected` or `defaultValue`.

#### Gotchas

- `className` and `wrapperClassName` both style the outer pill (a span); every other prop, including `aria-*` and `onKeyDown`, goes to the inner `<button>`.
- A chip in a `ChipGroup` needs a `value`; without one it is a plain chip that ignores the group. In the group the default tone is `primary`, outside it `neutral`; a chip's own `tone` or `variant` wins over the group's.
- `type="single"` lets the selected chip be clicked off (`onValueChange(null)`); pass `allowDeselect={false}` to keep one selected. `type="multiple"` calls `onValueChange` with the whole list.
- `color` is deprecated: use `tone`. The remove button does not toggle the chip and stops the click; a disabled chip disables it too.

## CloseButton

> Icon-only "X" button for dismissing dialogs, alerts and toasts, and (`shape="pill"`) removing a chip or tag.

- Import: `import { CloseButton } from "@sutra/ui"` (or from `@sutra/ui/core`)
- Source: `packages/ui/src/primitives/close-button` (primitives)
- Also accepts the props of HTMLAttributes, ButtonHTMLAttributes

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `shape` | `"control" \| "pill"` | `"control"` | `control` (default): a standalone dismiss button with press, disabled and focus styling. `pill`: the small round remove × inside a chip, tag or badge; the pill supplies the rest. |
| `size` | `"3xs" \| "2xs" \| "xs" \| "sm" \| "md" \| "lg"` | `"md"` | Button size from `3xs` (16px) up; icons scale with it. |
| `variant` | `"ghost" \| "subtle" \| "inverse" \| "current" \| "muted"` | `"ghost"` | Look: `ghost`, `subtle` (muted fill), `inverse` (for dark surfaces), `current` (inherits the text colour, dimmed until hover) or `muted`. |

### Variants

- `shape`: `control`, `pill` (default "control")
- `variant`: `ghost`, `subtle`, `inverse`, `current`, `muted` (default "ghost")
- `size`: `3xs`, `2xs`, `xs`, `sm`, `md`, `lg` (default "md")

### Notes

**When to use:** The icon-only "X" for dismissing a dialog, alert or toast, and, with `shape="pill"`, the small round remove mark inside a chip, tag or badge.

**Use instead when:**
- `Button`: a labelled action (use an `icon-*` size for other icons)
- `Badge`: a removable label, it has `onRemove` built in
- `Chip`: a removable or selectable chip, it has `onRemove` built in
- `DialogClose`: the close part of a Dialog

#### Keyboard

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Moves focus to and from the button. A `disabled` button is skipped |
| Enter, Space | Activates it (native `<button>` behaviour) |

Left and Right arrows have no meaning, so nothing changes in RTL. The X glyph is symmetric and is not mirrored. A parent can take the button out of the tab order: `Chip` does this for its remove button.

#### Screen readers

- A native `<button>` with `type="button"` unless you pass `type`, so it never submits a form by accident.
- The accessible name is `aria-label`, which defaults to the English "Close". Pass a specific one ("Remove filter", "Close settings") when it does not close a whole dialog or when the UI is localized.
- The default X icon is `aria-hidden`. If you pass `children`, they replace the icon and you must hide a decorative icon yourself.

#### Reduced motion

The press effect (`active:scale-95`) and the colour fades are transitions, which the reduced-motion net ends within 1 ms. The `pill` shape has no press effect.

#### Server rendering

Server render: same markup as the client. Plain markup with no browser API, so the server and client output match.

#### Gotchas
