- `shape="pill"` carries no focus ring, no press effect and no `disabled` styling: it assumes the chip, tag or badge around it supplies them. Used on its own, add `focusRing` through `className`.
- `shape="control"` (the default) has a 24px hit area, 44px under a coarse pointer, even at the small sizes. `pill` keeps the 24px minimum for its 16px `3xs` size.
- `variant` only sets colours: `ghost` (default), `subtle`, `inverse` for dark surfaces, `current` (inherits the text colour, dimmed until hover) and `muted`. `current` is meant for pills.
- `size` runs from `3xs` (16px) to `lg` (36px), default `md` (32px); the icon scales with it.

## Collapse

> Height-auto open and close for a section, filter row or wizard step. The track goes from `0fr` to `1fr`, so the real content height animates with no measuring and no JS animation; closed content is `inert` (not focusable, out of the accessibility tree). Reduced motion ends the transition at once. It is controlled only: drive `open` yourself or use `Collapsible`.

- Import: `import { Collapse } from "@sutra/ui"` (or from `@sutra/ui/core`)
- Source: `packages/ui/src/primitives/collapse` (primitives)
- `data-slot`: `collapse`, `collapse-content`
- Also accepts the props of HTMLAttributes

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `open` (required) | `boolean` |  | Whether the content is shown. |
| `children` | `React.ReactNode` |  | Content that is revealed and hidden by the `open` prop. |
| `contentClassName` | `string` |  | Class names for the clipping wrapper around the children (put padding on a child inside, not here, or the closed state keeps it). |
| `fade` | `boolean` | `true` | Fade the content in and out while the height changes (default true). |
| `unmountOnExit` | `boolean` | `false` | Remove the children from the tree once the close transition has ended (and mount them again on open). |

### Notes

**When to use:** Opens and closes a block of your own content with a height animation from your own `open` state, with no measuring. For filter rows, wizard steps and expandable regions that have no built-in trigger.

**Use instead when:**
- `Collapsible`: a ready trigger, `aria-expanded` wiring and uncontrolled state
- `Accordion`: a group of sections with arrow-key navigation
- `Dialog`: content that should block the page

#### Keyboard

Not focusable: no keyboard interaction. The trigger is yours; closed content is `inert`, so Tab skips everything inside it until it opens.

#### Screen readers

`Collapse` adds no role, name or `aria-expanded`: put `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls` on your own trigger (pass an `id` to `Collapse` for it). The root carries `data-state="open"` or `"closed"`. Closed content is `inert`, which removes it from focus and the accessibility tree while it stays mounted (unless `unmountOnExit`). Nothing is announced when it opens.

#### Reduced motion

The grid track animates from `0fr` to `1fr` with an opacity fade (`fade={false}` skips the fade). The reduced-motion net ends the transition in 1 ms, so the block still changes state, just at once; `transitionend` still fires, so `unmountOnExit` unmounts as usual.

#### Server rendering

Server render: same markup as the client. Plain markup with no browser API at render. A closed `Collapse` renders its children `inert` and collapsed, or nothing at all with `unmountOnExit`; an open one renders them. The first render is not animated.

#### Slots

- `collapse`: the root grid that animates its rows
- `collapse-content`: the clipping wrapper around the children (`contentClassName`)

#### Gotchas

- It is controlled only: `open` is required and there is no `onOpenChange`; drive it from your state, or use `Collapsible` for a trigger and uncontrolled state.
- Put padding on a child, not on `contentClassName`: padding on the clipping wrapper keeps its height when closed, so the block never reaches zero.
- `unmountOnExit` removes the children after the `grid-template-rows` transition ends, with a 600 ms timer as a fallback when no `transitionend` arrives (hidden tab, `display: none` ancestor). Reopening before that cancels the removal.
- Children stay mounted while closed by default, so effects, inputs and iframes inside keep running; use `unmountOnExit` to drop them.

## Collapsible

> Show/hide section with an animated height: `Collapsible`, `CollapsibleTrigger`, `CollapsibleContent`.

- Import: `import { Collapsible } from "@sutra/ui"` (or from `@sutra/ui/core`)
- Source: `packages/ui/src/primitives/collapsible` (primitives)
- `data-slot`: `collapsible`
- Parts: [`CollapsibleContent`](CollapsibleContent.md), [`CollapsibleTrigger`](CollapsibleTrigger.md)
- Also accepts the props of HTMLAttributes

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `defaultOpen` | `boolean` | `false` | Initial open state when uncontrolled. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Disables the trigger so the panel cannot be toggled. |
| `keepMounted` | `boolean` | `false` | Keep the content in the tree while closed (the default removes it once the close animation ends). |
| `onOpenChange` | `(open: boolean) => void` |  | Called when the panel opens or closes. |
| `open` | `boolean` |  | Controlled open state. Use with `onOpenChange`. |
| `variant` | `CollapsibleVariant` | `"default"` | default: bare · surface: bordered card · ghost: soft hover and open background. |

### Part props

Props of `CollapsibleContent`, `CollapsibleTrigger`: see [the full page](md/Collapsible.md).

### Notes

**When to use:** A single show and hide section with its own trigger button and an animated height. Controlled or uncontrolled, with `default`, `surface` and `ghost` looks.

**Use instead when:**
- `Accordion`: several related sections with arrow-key navigation and one-open-at-a-time
- `Collapse`: you already have a trigger and state and only need the height animation
- `Popover`: a small floating panel instead of pushing content down

#### Keyboard

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Moves focus to and from the trigger; a disabled trigger is skipped |
| Enter, Space | Toggles the section (native `<button>`) |

The trigger is the only stop; there are no arrow keys, so RTL changes nothing. Closed content is `inert`, so Tab never lands inside it.

#### Screen readers

`CollapsibleTrigger` is a `<button type="button">` with `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls` pointing at the content wrapper. The panel has no `region` role or label of its own (unlike `AccordionContent`). The turning chevron is `aria-hidden`. Closed content is `inert`. With `asChild` the child gets the same attributes plus a click handler, so pass a real button or give your element its own role and keyboard handling.

#### Reduced motion

The height and opacity transition is the one from `Collapse`, and the chevron turns with `chevron-turn`; the reduced-motion net ends both in 1 ms.

#### Server rendering

Server render: same markup as the client. Renders the same markup on server and client with no browser API. A closed section (the default) renders no content; `defaultOpen` or `open` renders it. With `keepMounted` the closed content is in the HTML, collapsed and `inert`.

#### Slots

- `collapsible`: the root, with `data-state` and `data-disabled`
- `collapsible-content`: the animated panel (this replaces `Collapse`'s own `collapse` slot name; the inner `collapse-content` wrapper remains)

#### Gotchas

- This is not the Radix Collapsible: it is built on `Collapse` and is not a drop-in for `@radix-ui` props. `open`, `defaultOpen` and `onOpenChange` work as usual, and a controlled `open` stays put until you change it.
- `CollapsibleTrigger` and `CollapsibleContent` throw outside a `Collapsible`.
- Closed content is removed after the close animation by default; `keepMounted` on the root, or on one `CollapsibleContent` (which overrides the root), keeps it mounted and `inert`.
- `className` on `CollapsibleContent` goes to the inner padded box; other props (`id`, `style`) go to the outer `Collapse`, and overriding `id` breaks the trigger's `aria-controls`.

## Combobox

> Searchable select built on Popover + cmdk, with multi-select chips and creatable options.

- Import: `import { Combobox } from "@sutra/ui"` (or from `@sutra/ui/forms`)
- Source: `packages/ui/src/primitives/combobox` (primitives)
- `data-slot`: `combobox-announcer`, `combobox-clear`, `combobox-empty`, `combobox-loading`

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `options` (required) | `ComboboxOption[]` |  | Options to choose from; each has a `value`, a `label` and optional description, icon, group and disabled flag. |
| `aria-describedby` | `string` |  | Id(s) of the element(s) that describe the trigger (hint, error text). |
| `aria-invalid` | `boolean` |  | Overrides the invalid state announced to assistive technology; normally set `invalid` instead. |
| `aria-label` | `string` |  | Accessible name of the trigger when there is no visible label. |
| `aria-labelledby` | `string` |  | Id(s) of the element(s) that label the trigger. |
| `className` | `string` |  | Classes for the trigger button. |
| `clearable` | `boolean` | `false` | Show a clear button while something is selected; Delete also clears (Backspace too, when single). |
| `clearLabel` | `string` | `"Clear"` | Accessible name of the clear button. Default "Clear". |
| `confirmBackspace` | `boolean` | `false` | Multiple only: Backspace on the focused field first marks the last chip (announced politely) and a second press removes it, so a held key cannot empty the field. Default false: Backspace removes the last chip at once. |
| `contentClassName` | `string` |  | Classes for the popover list. |
| `creatable` | `boolean` | `false` | Offer "Create …" when the query matches no option. |
| `createLabel` | `(query: string) => React.ReactNode` | `(q) => ( <> Create <span className="font-medium text-foreground">“{q}”</span> </> )` | Builds the "Create …" row label from the current query; the default reads `Create "query"`. |
| `defaultInputValue` | `string` | `""` | Initial search text when uncontrolled. |
| `defaultOpen` | `boolean` | `false` | Initial open state when uncontrolled. |
| `defaultValue` | `string \| string[]` |  | Initially selected value when uncontrolled. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` |  | Disables the trigger so the list cannot be opened. |
| `emptyState` | `React.ReactNode` |  | Shown when the query matches nothing. Default "No results". |
| `emptyText` | `React.ReactNode` |  | **Deprecated.** Use `emptyState`. Legacy name of `emptyState`. |
| `filter` | `false \| ((option: ComboboxOption, query: string) => boolean)` |  | How options are matched against the search text. Omit for the built-in fuzzy match. `false` shows `options` exactly as given (server-side search: pass the results for the current `inputValue`). A function keeps the options it accepts. |
| `id` | `string` |  | `id` of the trigger, so a `<label htmlFor>` or `Field` can point at it. |
| `inputValue` | `string` |  | The search text, to control it (for async search). Cleared to "" when the list closes. |
| `invalid` | `boolean` |  | Marks the combobox invalid: error border and `aria-invalid`. Inherited from a surrounding `Field` when omitted. |
| `loading` | `boolean` | `false` | Options are being fetched: shows a loading row (or a spinner beside the search text while options are on screen). |
| `loadingState` | `React.ReactNode` |  | Text of the loading row. Default "Loading…". |
| `maxChips` | `number` | `3` | Max chips shown in the trigger before collapsing into "+N" (multiple only). |
| `multiple` | `false \| true` | `false` | Single-select mode (the default); `value` and `onValueChange` then work with one string. |
| `onCreate` | `(query: string) => string \| void` |  | Called with the query when the user picks "Create …". The new value is selected automatically: return a different string (e.g. a generated id) to select that instead. |
| `onInputValueChange` | `(value: string) => void` |  | Called as the search text changes. Debounce the fetch on your side (see `useDebouncedValue`). |
| `onOpenChange` | `(open: boolean) => void` |  | Called when the list opens or closes (selection, Escape, outside click). |
| `onValueChange` | `((value: string) => void) \| ((value: string[]) => void)` |  | Called with the option `value` the user picked (or the created value). |
| `open` | `boolean` |  | Controlled open state of the list. Use with `onOpenChange`. |
| `openOnFocus` | `boolean` | `false` | Open the list when the field gets keyboard focus (pointer clicks keep their normal toggle). |
| `placeholder` | `string` | `"Select…"` | Trigger text while nothing is selected. |
| `required` | `boolean` |  | Marks the combobox required. Inherited from a surrounding `Field` when omitted. |
| `searchable` | `boolean` | `true` | Hide the search input. |
| `searchPlaceholder` | `string` | `"Search…"` | Placeholder of the search input inside the list. |
| `size` | `Size` | `"md"` | Control height and text size; match the neighbouring inputs. |
| `value` | `string \| string[]` |  | Controlled selected value (an option `value`); an empty string means nothing selected. |
| `variant` | `"outline" \| "filled"` | `"outline"` | `outline` (default) is the bordered box; `filled` is a tinted surface with a hidden border. |

### Variants

- `size`: `sm`, `md`, `lg` (default "md")
- `multiple`: `true`, `false` (default false)
- `variant`: `outline`, `filled` (default "outline")

### Notes

**When to use:** A searchable select for long lists: an input-like trigger and a popover with a search box. Single or `multiple` (chips), `creatable`, async through `filter`, `inputValue` and `loading`.

**Use instead when:**
- `Select`: a short list that needs no search
- `RadioGroup`: every option should stay visible
- `TagInput`: free-form tags with no fixed list
- `SegmentedControl`: two to four options that switch a view

#### Keyboard

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| Enter, Space, ArrowDown | On the trigger: open the list and focus the search box |
| ArrowDown, ArrowUp | In the list: move the highlighted option, looping at the ends. Ctrl+N, J, P and K do the same |
| Home, End | Highlight the first or last option |
| Enter | Pick the highlighted option (or the "Create" row). Single mode closes; `multiple` stays open and toggles |
| Escape | Close and return focus to the trigger |
| Backspace | On the trigger, `multiple`: remove the last chip. With `confirmBackspace` the first press marks it and the second removes it; a held key never confirms. With `clearable` and single mode it clears the value |
| Delete | On the trigger with `clearable`: clear every selection |
| Tab | Leaves the trigger; the chip remove buttons and the clear button are not tab stops (`tabIndex` -1) |

`openOnFocus` also opens the list on keyboard focus, not on a pointer press or when focus returns. The list is vertical, so RTL swaps no keys.

#### Screen readers

- The trigger is a `div role="combobox"` with `aria-haspopup="listbox"`, `aria-expanded`, and `aria-required`, `aria-invalid` and `aria-disabled` when set. It is named by `aria-label`, `aria-labelledby` or a surrounding `FieldLabel` (a `<label htmlFor>` cannot name a div, so the wrapper points at the label id). The selected labels are its text.
- The popover is a `role="dialog"` with the same name, or the `placeholder` as a fallback. Inside, the search box is a combobox with `aria-activedescendant`, the list is a `listbox` (`aria-multiselectable` when `multiple`, `aria-busy` while `loading`) and each row is an `option`.
- Chosen options carry `aria-checked="true"` (and `data-checked`, for styling): in `multiple` mode every option is `true` or `false`, in single mode only the chosen one has it. The check icon is decoration. In cmdk `aria-selected` means highlighted, not chosen.
- The empty message sits in a polite live region next to a hidden listbox. The `confirmBackspace` prompt ("Press Backspace again to remove ...") is a polite live region on the trigger. The loading text is not a live region.
- Chip remove buttons are named "Remove" plus the label; the clear button uses `clearLabel`.

#### Reduced motion

The popover fades and zooms in with `animate-in`; the net removes the movement. A chip you just added eases in only under `motion-safe:`, so it appears at once with reduced motion. The loading spinner keeps turning.

#### Server rendering

Server render: same markup as the client. The trigger renders on the server with its selected labels or placeholder (labels come from `options`). The popover is portalled, so with `open` or `defaultOpen` the list appears after hydration.

#### Slots

- `combobox-clear`: the clear button
- `combobox-empty`: the polite region that holds the empty message
- `combobox-loading`: the loading row shown while `loading` and no option is visible
- `combobox-announcer`: the screen reader prompt, rendered only with `confirmBackspace`

#### Gotchas

- Single mode: `value` is a string and `""` means nothing selected; `multiple` takes and returns `string[]`. Picking the selected option again does not unselect it (and does not call `onValueChange`); use `clearable`.
- There is no `name` prop and no hidden input, so the value does not post with a native form: read it from `onValueChange`.
- `filter={false}` shows `options` exactly as given, for server search: drive it with `inputValue` and `onInputValueChange` (the text clears when the list closes) and debounce the fetch yourself. A selected value keeps its label after it leaves the results.
- `creatable` adds a "Create" row only when the query matches no label (case-insensitive) and `loading` is off; the string `onCreate` returns is selected instead of the typed text. `emptyText` is a deprecated alias of `emptyState`.

## ConfirmDialog

> Ready-made confirmation dialog with async-aware confirm.

- Import: `import { ConfirmDialog } from "@sutra/ui"` (or from `@sutra/ui/overlays`)
- Source: `packages/ui/src/primitives/dialog` (primitives)

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `title` (required) | `React.ReactNode` |  | Dialog heading; also its accessible name. |
| `cancelLabel` | `React.ReactNode` | `"Cancel"` | Text of the cancel button. |
| `children` | `React.ReactNode` |  | Extra content between the header and the footer. |
| `className` | `string` |  | Classes for the dialog panel. |
| `confirmLabel` | `React.ReactNode` | `"Confirm"` | Text of the confirm button. |
| `defaultOpen` | `boolean` | `false` | Initial open state when uncontrolled. |
| `description` | `React.ReactNode` |  | Supporting text under the title; also the accessible description. |
| `icon` | `React.ReactNode` |  | Featured icon shown above the title (tone-coloured). |
| `onCancel` | `() => void` |  | Called when the cancel button is clicked; the dialog closes either way. |
| `onConfirm` | `() => void \| Promise<void>` |  | May return a promise; the confirm button shows a spinner until it settles. Throw to keep the dialog open. |
| `onOpenChange` | `(open: boolean) => void` |  | Called when the dialog opens or closes (confirm, cancel, Escape; closing is blocked while a confirm is pending). |
| `open` | `boolean` |  | Controlled open state. Use with `onOpenChange`. |
| `tone` | `ToneInput` |  | `destructive` turns the icon and confirm button red. Default `neutral`. `default` is a deprecated alias of `neutral`. |
| `trigger` | `React.ReactNode` |  | Element that opens the dialog (wrapped with `asChild`). |

### Notes

**When to use:** A modal that interrupts the page for one focused task. Centred on screens from `sm` up, a bottom sheet below. `AlertDialog` and `ConfirmDialog` are the variants for confirmations that must be answered.

**Use instead when:**
- `Sheet`: a side or edge panel that keeps the page context
- `Drawer`: a touch-first bottom sheet you drag
- `Popover`: a small floating panel that does not block the page
- `DialogProvider`: ask for a confirm or a prompt from code

#### Keyboard

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Cycle focus inside the dialog (it is trapped while open) |
| Escape | Close the dialog (`AlertDialog` closes on Escape too, but not on an outside click) |
| Enter, Space | Activate the focused button, including the close button |

Focus moves into the dialog on open and returns to whatever had it before, even when the dialog was opened without a `DialogTrigger` (a hotkey, a menu item, controlled `open`). There are no arrow-key or direction-dependent keys, so RTL changes nothing.

#### Screen readers

Radix gives the panel `role="dialog"` (`alertdialog` for `AlertDialog`), `aria-labelledby` from `DialogTitle` and `aria-describedby` from `DialogDescription`, and hides the rest of the page from assistive technology while it is open. Always render a `DialogTitle` (it may be visually hidden); `ConfirmDialog` requires `title` for that reason. The built-in close button is labelled "Close". The mobile grabber bar is `aria-hidden` decoration.

#### Reduced motion

The panel fades and zooms in (from the bottom edge on mobile) with the `animate-in` utilities; under reduced motion the net removes the zoom and slide and keeps the fade.

#### Server rendering

Server render: same markup as the client. A closed dialog renders only its trigger on both server and client, so there is nothing to mismatch. The content is portalled into `<body>` after mount: a dialog that is `open` on first render appears after hydration, not in the server HTML. The portalled layer does not sit inside a subtree `data-style` or `dir`: put them on `<html>`.

#### Gotchas

- `AlertDialog` ignores outside clicks (no dismiss by clicking the backdrop), `Dialog` does not: use `AlertDialog` when the user must choose.
- `ConfirmDialog onConfirm` may return a promise: the confirm button shows a spinner and closing is blocked until it settles, and throwing keeps the dialog open.
- A dialog opened from a menu item that then unmounts cannot return focus to it (the opener is gone), and Radix's default applies; keep the opener mounted when focus matters.
- `size` only sets the maximum width from `sm` up; below that every dialog is full width.

## Container

> Centres content and caps its width (`size`), with responsive horizontal padding. Extra props are spread to the root.

- Import: `import { Container } from "@sutra/ui"` (or from `@sutra/ui/core`)
- Source: `packages/ui/src/primitives/layout` (primitives)
- Also accepts the props of HTMLAttributes

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `asChild` | `boolean` |  | Render as the child element (e.g. `<main>` or `<section>`) instead of a `<div>`, keeping the container styles. |
| `size` | `"sm" \| "md" \| "lg" \| "xl" \| "full"` | `"lg"` | Maximum content width: `sm` 48rem to `xl` 90rem, or `full` for no limit. |

### Variants

- `size`: `sm`, `md`, `lg`, `xl`, `full` (default "lg")

### Notes

**When to use:** Centres page content and caps its width, with responsive horizontal padding (16, 24 and 32 px). Sizes `sm` to `xl`, or `full` for no cap.

**Use instead when:**
- `Stack`: vertical or horizontal flow inside it
- `Grid`: a 12-column layout inside it
- `Card`: a bordered surface

#### Keyboard

Not focusable: no keyboard interaction.

#### Screen readers

A plain `div` with no role. For a landmark, pass `asChild` and a `main`, `section` or `nav` child (`<Container asChild><main>...</main></Container>`): the child keeps its own role and gets the container styles. A `section` is only a landmark when it has a name.

#### Reduced motion

Static: no animation.

#### Server rendering

Server render: same markup as the client. Plain markup with no browser API, so server and client output match.

#### Gotchas

- `size` sets `max-width`: `sm` 48rem, `md` 64rem, `lg` (default) 80rem, `xl` 90rem, `full` none. The padding is always applied, including on `full`.
- It is `mx-auto w-full` with the padding built in, so nest it once per page region; a `Container` inside another one adds its padding twice.
- `className` is merged last: a `px-0` or a `max-w-*` of yours wins over the size.

## ContentDivider

> Alias of `Separator`.

**Deprecated:** Use `Separator` (it takes a `label`).

- Import: `import { ContentDivider } from "@sutra/ui"` (or from `@sutra/ui/core`)
- Source: `packages/ui/src/primitives/separator` (primitives)
- Also accepts the props of HTMLAttributes, SeparatorProps, PrimitivePropsWithRef

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `label` | `React.ReactNode` |  | Text or content shown inside the line. `children` works too. |
| `labelPosition` | `"start" \| "center" \| "end"` | `"center"` | Where the label sits along the line. |
| `variant` | `"solid" \| "dashed"` | `"solid"` | Line style. |

### Notes

**When to use:** A horizontal or vertical rule, solid or dashed, optionally with a label in the line ("OR", "Section"). `ContentDivider` is the deprecated alias of the same component.

**Use instead when:**
- `ItemSeparator`: the hairline inside an `ItemGroup`
- `Frame`: grouped rows with a tray
- `Stack`: spacing without a line

#### Keyboard

Not focusable: no keyboard interaction.

#### Screen readers

- Decorative by default: `decorative` is `true`, so the element is `role="none"` and assistive technology skips it. This is the opposite of the Radix default. Pass `decorative={false}` for a real `role="separator"` between regions of content; a vertical one then also gets `aria-orientation="vertical"` (horizontal is the implicit default and is not written).
- A `label` (or `children`) is ordinary text and is read by screen readers whether or not the line is decorative.

#### Reduced motion

Static: no animation.

#### Server rendering

Server render: same markup as the client. Plain markup with no browser API, so server and client output match.

#### Gotchas

- A vertical separator has no height of its own: it stretches to the row it sits in (`self-stretch`), so put it in a flex row. A `className` with an `h-` or `size-` class switches it to a fixed height centred in the row instead.
- With a label, `labelPosition` is `center` (default), `start` or `end`; the short side of the line is a stub (1rem, or 0.5rem when vertical). A vertical labelled separator is at least 4rem tall.
- `variant="dashed"` only changes the line style. The line colour is the `border` token; override with a `border-*` class.
- `ContentDivider` is the same object as `Separator`; use `Separator` in new code.

## ContextMenu

> Context (right-click) menu root: Radix `ContextMenu.Root` with the reading direction filled in.

- Import: `import { ContextMenu } from "@sutra/ui"` (or from `@sutra/ui/overlays`)
- Source: `packages/ui/src/primitives/context-menu` (primitives)
- Parts: [`ContextMenuCheckboxItem`](ContextMenuCheckboxItem.md), [`ContextMenuContent`](ContextMenuContent.md), [`ContextMenuGroup`](ContextMenuGroup.md), [`ContextMenuItem`](ContextMenuItem.md), [`ContextMenuLabel`](ContextMenuLabel.md), [`ContextMenuRadioGroup`](ContextMenuRadioGroup.md), [`ContextMenuRadioItem`](ContextMenuRadioItem.md), [`ContextMenuSeparator`](ContextMenuSeparator.md), [`ContextMenuShortcut`](ContextMenuShortcut.md), [`ContextMenuSub`](ContextMenuSub.md), [`ContextMenuSubContent`](ContextMenuSubContent.md), [`ContextMenuSubTrigger`](ContextMenuSubTrigger.md), [`ContextMenuTrigger`](ContextMenuTrigger.md)
- Also accepts the props of ContextMenuProps

### Props

No props of its own.

### Part props

Props of `ContextMenuCheckboxItem`, `ContextMenuItem`, `ContextMenuLabel`, `ContextMenuSubTrigger`: see [the full page](md/ContextMenu.md).

### Notes

**When to use:** A menu of actions that opens at the pointer on right-click or touch long-press over an area, for rows, canvases, files and cards. It shares its rows and styling with `DropdownMenu`.

**Use instead when:**
- `DropdownMenu`: a visible trigger button opens the menu
- `Popover`: rich content or a form
- `Select`: choosing a value for a field

#### Keyboard

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| ArrowDown, ArrowUp | Move the highlighted row; focus stops at the ends unless you pass `loop` to `ContextMenuContent` |
| Home, End, PageUp, PageDown | Highlight the first or last row |
| A letter or digit | Typeahead: highlights the next row whose text starts with it |
| Enter, Space | Activate the highlighted row, or toggle or pick a checkbox or radio row; the menu closes |
| ArrowRight | On a sub-menu trigger: open it (Enter and Space do too) |
| ArrowLeft | Inside a sub-menu: close it and return to its trigger |
| Escape | Close the menu |
| Tab | Does nothing while the menu is open |

The trigger is a plain `<span>` with no tab stop, and Radix opens the menu only from a `contextmenu` event (right click) or a 700 ms touch or pen press. Keyboard users cannot reach it from Tab, so offer the same actions elsewhere (a `DropdownMenu` button). In RTL ArrowLeft opens a sub-menu and ArrowRight closes it.

#### Screen readers

The panel is `role="menu"`; rows are `menuitem`, `menuitemcheckbox` and `menuitemradio` with `aria-checked`, groups are `role="group"`, and a disabled row gets `aria-disabled`. The trigger area gets no role or hint, so a screen reader user is not told a context menu exists: describe it or add a visible alternative. The sub-menu trigger has `aria-haspopup="menu"` and `aria-expanded`. The check and chevron icons are `aria-hidden`; the radio dot is an empty span.

#### Reduced motion

The panel fades and zooms in from the pointer with the `animate-in` utilities; the reduced-motion net removes the slide and the scale and keeps only the fade. Rows highlight instantly.

#### Server rendering

Server render: same markup as the client. The trigger span renders on the server; the menu does not exist until a `contextmenu` event, and its panel is portalled after mount. Nothing differs between server and client.

#### Gotchas

- A touch long-press opens the menu after 700 ms and cancels if the finger moves; mouse users need the right button (the `contextmenu` event).
- `modal` defaults to true: while the menu is open, pointer events outside it are blocked and focus is trapped. Pass `modal={false}` on `ContextMenu` to keep the page interactive.
- Unlike `DropdownMenuContent`, `ContextMenuContent` has no `sideOffset` or `align` defaults: the menu opens at the cursor. `ContextMenuTrigger` renders a `<span>`: pass `asChild` to use your own element, and make it a block or give it a size so the whole area responds.
- `shortcut` is display only, `tone="destructive"` replaces the deprecated `variant`, and with `asChild` on `ContextMenuItem` the `icon`, `description` and `shortcut` props are ignored.

## CopyButton

> Copies a value to the clipboard, swaps to a check mark and announces "Copied to clipboard".

- Import: `import { CopyButton } from "@sutra/ui"` (or from `@sutra/ui/core`)
- Source: `packages/ui/src/primitives/copy-button` (primitives)
- Also accepts the props of HTMLAttributes, ButtonHTMLAttributes

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `value` (required) | `string \| (() => string)` |  | Text to copy, or a function read at click time. |
| `copiedLabel` | `string` | `"Copied"` | Shown for `timeout` ms after a successful copy. Default `"Copied"`. |
| `label` | `string` | `"Copy"` | Accessible name (icon variant) or visible text. Default `"Copy"`. |
| `onCopied` | `(text: string) => void` |  | Called with the copied text after a successful copy. |
| `size` | `CopyButtonSize` | `"sm"` | Default `"sm"`. |
| `timeout` | `number` |  | How long the copied state lasts, in ms. Default 1600. |
| `variant` | `CopyButtonVariant` | `"icon"` | `"icon"` (default, icon-only), `"button"` (bordered, icon + text) or `"ghost"` (icon + text). |

### Notes

**When to use:** Copies a value to the clipboard, swaps its icon to a check mark and announces "Copied to clipboard". `CopyField` wraps it in a read-only row for commands, ids, keys and URLs.

**Use instead when:**
- `Input`: the user types or edits the value (CopyField is read-only)
- `Button`: the action is not copying

#### Keyboard

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Moves focus to and from the copy button. A `disabled` one is skipped |
| Enter, Space | Copies (native `<button>` behaviour) |

`CopyField` itself is a `role="group"` that is not focusable: only its copy button is. No arrow keys are used, so nothing changes in RTL.

#### Screen readers

- The `icon` variant has no visible text, so `label` is its `aria-label` and `title`; after a copy both become `copiedLabel` for `timeout` ms (default 1600).
- The `button` and `ghost` variants show `label` or `copiedLabel` as text and set no `aria-label`.
- A visually hidden polite live region next to the button says "Copied to clipboard" after a successful copy. The text is fixed English and does not follow `copiedLabel`.
- `CopyField` is a `group` named by `label`, and its button is named "Copy <label>" ("Copy" without a label). The `prefix` is `aria-hidden` and is not copied.
- An `aria-label` you pass lands after the built-in one and wins, so the name stops changing to "Copied" (the live region still announces).

#### Reduced motion

The icon swap (the copy glyph shrinks away, the check grows in) is an opacity and scale transition, which the reduced-motion net ends in 1 ms, so the swap is instant. The timer for the copied state is unaffected.

#### Server rendering

Server render: same markup as the client. Plain markup with no browser API at render (`navigator.clipboard` is read in the click handler), so server and client output match.

#### Gotchas

- A failed write (permission denied, an insecure context, no `navigator.clipboard`) shows nothing: no copied state, no `onCopied`, no error. Handle the fallback yourself if the page may not be served over HTTPS.
- `value` may be a function, read at click time, so it can copy what is current. One that throws is swallowed and nothing is copied. An `onClick` that calls `preventDefault` cancels the copy.
- It renders two siblings, the button and the live-region span, so a parent with `gap` or `:last-child` rules sees both. `ref` is the button.
- `CopyField` truncates the value and puts the full text in `title` (`truncate={false}` wraps it instead), shows it in `<code>` unless `mono={false}`, and `copyButtonProps` passes props, such as `variant`, to the inner button.

## CopyField

> Read-only value with a copy button, for commands, ids, keys and URLs.

- Import: `import { CopyField } from "@sutra/ui"` (or from `@sutra/ui/core`)
- Source: `packages/ui/src/primitives/copy-button` (primitives)
- Also accepts the props of HTMLAttributes

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `value` (required) | `string` |  | The text shown and copied. |
| `copyButtonProps` | `Partial<Omit<CopyButtonProps, "value">>` |  | Props for the inner copy button. |
| `label` | `string` |  | What the value is (e.g. "API key"); names the group and the copy button ("Copy API key"). |
| `mono` | `boolean` | `true` | Monospace text. Default true. |
| `prefix` | `React.ReactNode` |  | Decorative lead-in that is not copied, e.g. `"$"` for shell commands. |
| `truncate` | `boolean` | `true` | Truncate long values with an ellipsis (full value in the tooltip). Default true. |
| `variant` | `"field" \| "chip"` | `"field"` | `"field"` (default, input-like row) or `"chip"` (compact inline pill). |

### Notes

**When to use:** Copies a value to the clipboard, swaps its icon to a check mark and announces "Copied to clipboard". `CopyField` wraps it in a read-only row for commands, ids, keys and URLs.

**Use instead when:**

- `Button`: the action is not copying

#### Keyboard

|---|---|
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Moves focus to and from the copy button. A `disabled` one is skipped |
| Enter, Space | Copies (native `<button>` behaviour) |

## DataTable

> Data-driven table with sorting, selection, loading and empty states.

- Import: `import { DataTable } from "@sutra/ui"` (or from `@sutra/ui/core`)
- Source: `packages/ui/src/primitives/table` (primitives)

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `columns` (required) | `DataTableColumn<T>[]` |  | Column definitions in display order. |
| `data` (required) | `T[]` |  | Row objects to render; each row is passed to `cell`, `sortValue` and `onRowClick`. |
| `aria-label` | `string` |  | Names the scrollable region around the table (see `caption` for the table's own title). |
| `aria-labelledby` | `string` |  | Id of the element that names the scrollable region around the table. |
| `caption` | `React.ReactNode` |  | Caption rendered under the table (`<caption>`), e.g. a source note or the table title. |
| `className` | `string` |  | Classes for the outer wrapper. |
| `defaultSelectedRowIds` | `string[]` | `[]` | Initially selected row ids when uncontrolled. |
| `defaultSort` | `DataTableSort \| null` | `null` | Initial sort when uncontrolled. |
| `density` | `TableDensity` |  | Row density. Default `normal`; `"comfortable"` is accepted as a legacy alias of `relaxed`. |
| `emptyState` | `React.ReactNode` |  | Content shown in place of the body when `data` is empty. |
| `getRowId` | `(row: T, index: number) => string` | `defaultRowId` | Stable row id. Defaults to `row.id` or the index. |
| `loading` | `boolean` |  | Shows skeleton rows instead of the data. |
| `loadingRows` | `number` | `5` | Number of skeleton rows shown while `loading`. |
| `manualSorting` | `boolean` |  | Disable built-in sorting (e.g. when sorting on the server). |
| `maxHeight` | `number \| string` |  | Maximum height of the scroll area (px number or CSS length); the body scrolls past it. |
| `onRowClick` | `(row: T, index: number) => void` |  | Called with the row and its index when a row is clicked, or activated with Enter or Space; clickable rows get a pointer cursor and are focusable. |
| `onSelectionChange` | `(ids: string[]) => void` |  | Called with the full list of selected row ids after every selection change. |
| `onSortChange` | `(sort: DataTableSort \| null) => void` |  | Called with the next sort (or `null` when sorting is cleared) when a sortable header is activated. |
| `ref` | `React.Ref<HTMLTableElement>` |  | Ref to the `<table>` element. DataTable is generic, so it takes `ref` as a plain prop (React 19) instead of going through `forwardRef`, which would erase the row type. |
| `rowLabel` | `(row: T, index: number) => string` |  | Accessible name of a row's selection checkbox (with `selectable`). Default "Select row" for every row: pass e.g. `(row) => "Select " + row.name` so the boxes can be told apart. |
| `selectable` | `boolean` |  | Adds a leading checkbox column (with select-all in the header) for row selection. |
| `selectedRowIds` | `string[]` |  | Controlled selected row ids (see `getRowId`). Use with `onSelectionChange`. |
| `sort` | `DataTableSort \| null` |  | Controlled sort (`{ key, direction }`), or `null` for unsorted. Use with `onSortChange`. |
| `stickyHeader` | `boolean` |  | Keeps the header visible while the table scrolls. Pair with `maxHeight`. |
| `striped` | `boolean` |  | Zebra-stripe the body rows. |
| `tableClassName` | `string` |  | Classes for the `<table>` element. |

### Notes

**When to use:** A table built from `columns` and `data`, with click-to-sort headers, optional row selection with select-all, skeleton loading rows and an empty state. A generic component: it is typed by your row type.

**Use instead when:**
- `Table`: compose the markup yourself or when the layout is custom
- `ItemGroup`: a list of rows with media and actions
- `KeyValue`: two-column facts about one thing

#### Keyboard

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Moves through the scroll box (only while the table overflows it), the sort buttons, clickable rows, the checkboxes and controls inside cells |
| Enter, Space | On a sortable header, cycles that column: ascending, descending, unsorted |
| Space | On a checkbox, selects or clears the row (or all rows, in the header) |
| Enter, Space | On a focused row (only with `onRowClick`): calls `onRowClick` |

With `onRowClick`, each row is a tab stop and Enter or Space on the focused row calls it (a key press on a button or link inside the row keeps its own meaning). Without `onRowClick` rows are not focusable. There is no arrow-key movement. `align` is logical (`left` is the start side), so columns flip in RTL.

#### Screen readers

- A native `table`; headers are `th scope="col"`. A sortable column (`sortable: true`) holds a button and carries `aria-sort` (`ascending`, `descending`, `none`); a column that is not sortable has neither.
- With `selectable`, the header checkbox is labelled "Select all rows" and every row checkbox is labelled "Select row" unless you pass `rowLabel`, for example `(row) => "Select " + row.name`; without it the boxes are not told apart by name. The select-all box shows the mixed state when some rows are selected.
- `loading` puts `aria-busy="true"` on the table and fills the body with `aria-hidden` skeleton rows. No "Loading" text is announced, so add your own status message.
- Empty `data` shows one full-width cell with "No results", or your `emptyState`. `caption` renders a `<caption>` under the table.

#### Reduced motion

Row hover and checkbox ticks are transitions that the reduced-motion net ends within 1 ms. The loading skeletons use a shimmer with `motion-reduce:animate-none`.

#### Server rendering

Server render: part of it fills in after mount. The table renders fully on the server, including sorted and selected rows from `defaultSort` and `defaultSelectedRowIds`. Two small things settle after mount: the mixed (indeterminate) state of the select-all box is a DOM property set in an effect, and string sorting uses the runtime's default locale, so a server and a browser with different locales can order special characters differently.

#### Gotchas

- Sorting happens in the browser and cycles asc, desc, then none (`onSortChange(null)`). Set `manualSorting` when the server sorts: the data order stays yours and the headers still report the sort. Empty values (`null`, `undefined`, "") stay last in both directions, text compares case-insensitively with numeric order ("item2" before "item10"), and ties keep the original order. `sortValue` gives a column its own sort key.
- Selection is stored by row id: `getRowId` defaults to `row.id` (string or number), else the row's index in `data`, so supply `getRowId` when data is filtered or reordered. Select-all picks every row in `data`, not only the visible page; from a partial selection it clears the rows instead.
- `onRowClick` is on the `<tr>`: clicks from buttons or links you put in a cell bubble to it unless you `stopPropagation` (the selection checkboxes already do).
- `columns[].key` must be unique and reads `row[key]` unless `cell` is given. The `ref` is a plain prop (React 19) that reaches the `<table>`; `className` styles the outer box and `tableClassName` the table.

## DatePicker

> Input-like button that opens a calendar popover to pick a single date.

- Import: `import { DatePicker } from "@sutra/ui"` (or from `@sutra/ui/forms`)
- Source: `packages/ui/src/primitives/date-picker` (primitives)

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `align` | `"start" \| "center" \| "end"` | `"start"` | Alignment of the calendar popover against the trigger. |
| `aria-describedby` | `string` |  | Id(s) of the element(s) that describe the trigger (hint, error text). |
| `aria-invalid` | `boolean` |  | Overrides the invalid state announced to assistive technology; normally set `invalid` instead. |
| `aria-label` | `string` |  | Accessible name of the trigger when there is no visible label. |
| `aria-labelledby` | `string` |  | Id(s) of the element(s) that label the trigger. |
| `captionLayout` | `"label" \| "dropdown" \| "dropdown-months" \| "dropdown-years"` |  | Show month/year dropdowns in the calendar caption. |
| `className` | `string` |  | Classes for the wrapper around the trigger button (the button itself takes no class). |
| `clearable` | `boolean` |  | Show an inline button that resets the value. |
| `contentClassName` | `string` |  | Classes for the calendar popover. |
| `defaultOpen` | `boolean` | `false` | Initial open state when uncontrolled. |
| `defaultValue` | `Date` |  | Initially selected date when uncontrolled. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` |  | Disables the trigger so the calendar cannot be opened. |
| `disabledDates` | `Matcher \| Matcher[]` |  | Dates that can't be picked (react-day-picker matchers). |
| `endMonth` | `Date` |  | Latest month the calendar can navigate to. |
| `formatDate` | `(date: Date) => string` |  | Custom formatter for the trigger text; overrides `formatOptions`. |
| `formatOptions` | `Intl.DateTimeFormatOptions` |  | Options passed to `Intl.DateTimeFormat`. Defaults to `{ dateStyle: "medium" }`. |
| `id` | `string` |  | `id` of the trigger, so a `<label htmlFor>` or `Field` can point at it. |
| `invalid` | `boolean` |  | Marks the picker invalid: error border and `aria-invalid`. Inherited from a surrounding `Field` when omitted. |
| `locale` | `string` |  | BCP 47 locale for the trigger text (`Intl.DateTimeFormat`) and the calendar's month and weekday names, digits and first weekday. |
| `name` | `string` |  | Name of the hidden input that submits the value with a surrounding form. |
| `onOpenChange` | `(open: boolean) => void` |  | Called when the popover opens or closes (selection, Escape, outside click). |
| `onValueChange` | `(value: Date \| undefined) => void` |  | Called with the picked date, or `undefined` when cleared. |
| `open` | `boolean` |  | Controlled open state of the calendar popover. Use with `onOpenChange`. |
| `placeholder` | `string` | `"Pick a date"` | Trigger text while no date is selected (each picker has its own default, e.g. "Pick a date"). |
| `required` | `boolean` |  | Marks the picker required. Inherited from a surrounding `Field` when omitted. |
| `size` | `Size` | `"md"` | Trigger height and text size; match the neighbouring inputs. |
| `startMonth` | `Date` |  | Earliest month the calendar can navigate to (days before it are not reachable). |
| `value` | `Date` |  | Selected date; `undefined` means none. Use with `onValueChange`. |
| `variant` | `"outline" \| "filled"` |  | `outline` (default) is the bordered box; `filled` is a tinted surface with a hidden border. |

### Notes

**When to use:** An input-like button that opens a calendar popover to pick one date. Picking a day sets the value and closes the popover. For a range or a date with a time, use the sibling pickers.

**Use instead when:**
- `DateRangePicker`: a from and to range with presets
- `DateTimePicker`: a day and a time
- `Calendar`: an always visible month grid
- `TimePicker`: only a time of day
- `Input`: a typed value

#### Keyboard

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Moves to the trigger, the clear button (when `clearable` and a date is set) and, while open, through the calendar |
| Enter, Space | On the trigger: open the calendar (native button) |
| Arrow keys, PageUp, PageDown, Home, End | In the calendar: move the focused day by day, week, month or year (see Calendar) |
| Enter, Space | On a day: pick it and close the popover |
| Escape | Close without changing the value; focus returns to the trigger |

The trigger is a plain button, so ArrowDown does not open it. In RTL the Left and Right arrows swap inside the calendar and the previous and next month chevrons mirror.

#### Screen readers

- The trigger is a native `<button>` that shows the formatted date, or the `placeholder`. The popover is a `role="dialog"` named by `aria-label`, falling back to the placeholder and then "Choose date"; a `FieldLabel` or `aria-labelledby` names the trigger, not the dialog.
- `required` only sets `aria-required`, `invalid` sets `aria-invalid` and a surrounding `Field` supplies `id`, `aria-describedby`, `disabled`, `required` and `invalid` when you do not pass them.
- A given name (`aria-label`, a `FieldLabel`, `aria-labelledby`) replaces the button text as its accessible name, so the chosen date is not part of that name. The clear button is named "Clear date".
- The calendar inside is a labelled grid with day buttons named by their full date (see Calendar).

#### Reduced motion

The popover fades and zooms in with `animate-in`; the reduced-motion net removes the movement and ends the transitions in 1 ms. The calendar itself only has short hover transitions.

#### Server rendering

Server render: part of it fills in after mount. The trigger renders on the server and the popover is portalled, so it appears only after mount. A trigger with a `value` or `defaultValue` is formatted with `Intl.DateTimeFormat` in the runtime's default locale and time zone unless you pass `locale` or `formatDate`, so a server and a browser that differ can print different text and trigger a hydration warning. The portalled layer does not inherit a subtree `dir` or `data-style`; set them on `<html>`.

#### Gotchas

- `locale` formats the trigger text and also sets the calendar's month and weekday names, digits and first weekday (through `Intl`); `formatOptions` only formats the trigger. The calendar's aria labels ("Go to the Next Month", the day names read by a screen reader) stay English: they are not derived from `locale`.
- `className` goes to the wrapper `div` around the trigger, not to the button; `contentClassName` styles the popover.
- Clicking the day that is already selected clears the value (`onValueChange(undefined)`) and leaves the popover open; `clearable` adds an explicit button.
- With `name` a hidden input posts the local day as `YYYY-MM-DD` (empty when none). `required` blocks nothing in a native form. `startMonth` and `endMonth` limit navigation, `disabledDates` takes react-day-picker matchers.

## DateRangePicker

> Date range picker with two months, a presets sidebar and an Apply/Cancel footer.

- Import: `import { DateRangePicker } from "@sutra/ui"` (or from `@sutra/ui/forms`)
- Source: `packages/ui/src/primitives/date-picker-range` (primitives)

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `align` | `"start" \| "center" \| "end"` | `"start"` | Alignment of the calendar popover against the trigger. |
| `applyLabel` | `string` | `"Apply"` | Text of the apply button. |
| `aria-describedby` | `string` |  | Id(s) of the element(s) that describe the trigger (hint, error text). |
| `aria-invalid` | `boolean` |  | Overrides the invalid state announced to assistive technology; normally set `invalid` instead. |
| `aria-label` | `string` |  | Accessible name of the trigger when there is no visible label. |
| `aria-labelledby` | `string` |  | Id(s) of the element(s) that label the trigger. |
| `cancelLabel` | `string` | `"Cancel"` | Text of the cancel button. |
| `className` | `string` |  | Classes for the wrapper around the trigger button (the button itself takes no class). |
| `clearable` | `boolean` |  | Show an inline button that resets the value. |
| `contentClassName` | `string` |  | Classes for the calendar popover. |
| `defaultOpen` | `boolean` | `false` | Initial open state when uncontrolled. |
| `defaultValue` | `DateRange` |  | Initial range when uncontrolled. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` |  | Disables the trigger so the calendar cannot be opened. |
| `disabledDates` | `Matcher \| Matcher[]` |  | Dates that can't be picked (react-day-picker matchers). |
| `endMonth` | `Date` |  | Latest month the calendar can navigate to. |
| `formatOptions` | `Intl.DateTimeFormatOptions` |  | Options passed to `Intl.DateTimeFormat`. Defaults to `{ dateStyle: "medium" }`. |
| `formatRange` | `(range: DateRange) => string` |  | Custom formatter for the trigger text. |
| `id` | `string` |  | `id` of the trigger, so a `<label htmlFor>` or `Field` can point at it. |
| `invalid` | `boolean` |  | Marks the picker invalid: error border and `aria-invalid`. Inherited from a surrounding `Field` when omitted. |
| `locale` | `string` |  | BCP 47 locale for the trigger text (`Intl.DateTimeFormat`) and the calendar's month and weekday names, digits and first weekday. |
| `name` | `string` |  | Name of the hidden input that submits the value with a surrounding form. |
| `numberOfMonths` | `number` | `2` | Number of months shown side by side. |
| `onOpenChange` | `(open: boolean) => void` |  | Called when the popover opens or closes (selection, Escape, outside click). |
| `onValueChange` | `(value: DateRange \| undefined) => void` |  | Called with the new range (or `undefined` when cleared); with `presets` or apply/cancel it fires on apply. |
| `open` | `boolean` |  | Controlled open state of the calendar popover. Use with `onOpenChange`. |
| `placeholder` | `string` | `"Pick a date range"` | Trigger text while no date is selected (each picker has its own default, e.g. "Pick a date"). |
| `presets` | `DateRangePreset[]` | `defaultDateRangePresets` | Sidebar presets. Pass `[]` to hide the sidebar. |
| `required` | `boolean` |  | Marks the picker required. Inherited from a surrounding `Field` when omitted. |
| `size` | `Size` | `"md"` | Trigger height and text size; match the neighbouring inputs. |
| `startMonth` | `Date` |  | Earliest month the calendar can navigate to (days before it are not reachable). |
| `value` | `DateRange` |  | Controlled range as `{ from, to }`; either may be undefined while picking. Use with `onValueChange`. |
| `variant` | `"outline" \| "filled"` |  | `outline` (default) is the bordered box; `filled` is a tinted surface with a hidden border. |

### Notes

**When to use:** An input-like button that opens a two month range calendar with a presets sidebar and an Apply and Cancel footer. The value changes only when the user applies.

**Use instead when:**
- `DatePicker`: a single date
- `DateTimePicker`: a day and a time
- `Calendar`: an always visible grid (`mode="range"`)
- `Select`: a few fixed periods with no calendar

#### Keyboard

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Through the trigger, the clear button, then (open) the presets, the calendar, Cancel and Apply |
| Enter, Space | On the trigger: open; on a preset or a day: choose it; on Cancel or Apply: run it |
| Arrow keys, PageUp, PageDown, Home, End | In the calendar: move the focused day (see Calendar) |
| Escape | Close and discard the draft; focus returns to the trigger |

The trigger is a plain button, so ArrowDown does not open it. In RTL the Left and Right arrows swap inside the calendar and the month chevrons mirror. The preset column is vertical, so it has no arrow keys.

#### Screen readers

- The trigger is a native `<button>` showing the applied range or the `placeholder`. The popover is a `role="dialog"` named by `aria-label`, then the placeholder, then "Choose date range". `required`, `invalid`, `id` and `aria-describedby` work as on `DatePicker`, including the values a surrounding `Field` supplies.
- The presets are buttons in a group named "Presets"; the one that matches the draft range has `aria-pressed="true"`.
- The footer text (the draft range, or "Select a start date") is a polite live region, so each click on a day is announced there.
- A given name (`aria-label`, a `FieldLabel`) replaces the button text as the accessible name, so the applied range is not part of it. The clear button is named "Clear date".

#### Reduced motion

The popover fades and zooms in with `animate-in`; the net removes the movement. Preset and day hovers are short transitions that end in 1 ms.

#### Server rendering

Server render: part of it fills in after mount. The trigger renders on the server and the popover is portalled, so it appears after mount. A trigger with a range is formatted with `Intl.DateTimeFormat` in the runtime's default locale and time zone unless you pass `locale` or `formatRange`, so server and browser text can differ.

#### Gotchas

- Nothing is committed until Apply: clicking days, presets or closing with Escape or an outside click leaves `value` alone, and the next open starts from the committed value. `clearable` clears at once, with no Apply.
- Apply is disabled until a start day is picked, and a range with only a start is applied as a one day range (`to` equals `from`).
- `presets` replaces the defaults (`defaultDateRangePresets`: Today, Yesterday, Last 7 days, Last 30 days, This month, Last month); `presets={[]}` hides the sidebar. Each `getRange` runs when a preset is chosen and when the popover renders, so relative ranges stay current. `numberOfMonths` defaults to 2.
- `locale` formats the trigger and footer text and sets the calendar's month and weekday names, digits and first weekday; its aria labels stay English. With `name`, two hidden inputs post `name[from]` and `name[to]` as `YYYY-MM-DD`.

## DateTimePicker

> Input-like button that opens a calendar plus a `TimePicker` to pick a local date and time. Time-zone agnostic: the value is wall-clock time in the user's zone, like `datetime-local`.

- Import: `import { DateTimePicker } from "@sutra/ui"` (or from `@sutra/ui/forms`)
- Source: `packages/ui/src/primitives/date-picker-datetime` (primitives)

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `align` | `"start" \| "center" \| "end"` | `"start"` | Alignment of the calendar popover against the trigger. |
| `aria-describedby` | `string` |  | Id(s) of the element(s) that describe the trigger (hint, error text). |
| `aria-invalid` | `boolean` |  | Overrides the invalid state announced to assistive technology; normally set `invalid` instead. |
| `aria-label` | `string` |  | Accessible name of the trigger when there is no visible label. |
| `aria-labelledby` | `string` |  | Id(s) of the element(s) that label the trigger. |
| `captionLayout` | `"label" \| "dropdown" \| "dropdown-months" \| "dropdown-years"` |  | Show month/year dropdowns in the calendar caption. |
| `className` | `string` |  | Classes for the wrapper around the trigger button (the button itself takes no class). |
| `clearable` | `boolean` |  | Show an inline button that resets the value. |
| `contentClassName` | `string` |  | Classes for the calendar popover. |
| `defaultOpen` | `boolean` | `false` | Initial open state when uncontrolled. |
| `defaultTime` | `string` | `"00:00"` | Time used when a day is picked before any time is set. Default `"00:00"`. |
| `defaultValue` | `DateTimeInput` |  | Initial date and time when uncontrolled; a `Date` or a local `"YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm"` string. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` |  | Disables the trigger so the calendar cannot be opened. |
| `disabledDates` | `Matcher \| Matcher[]` |  | Dates that can't be picked (react-day-picker matchers). |
| `doneLabel` | `string` | `"Done"` | Label of the button that closes the popover. Default "Done". |
| `endMonth` | `Date` |  | Latest month the calendar can navigate to. |
| `formatDateTime` | `(date: Date) => string` |  | Custom formatter for the trigger text; overrides `formatOptions`. |
| `formatOptions` | `Intl.DateTimeFormatOptions` |  | Options passed to `Intl.DateTimeFormat`. Defaults to `{ dateStyle: "medium", timeStyle: "short" }`. |
| `granularity` | `TimeGranularity` | `"minute"` | Add a seconds segment. Default `"minute"`. |
| `hourCycle` | `12 \| 24` |  | Force a 12- or 24-hour clock. Defaults to the locale's convention. |
| `id` | `string` |  | `id` of the trigger, so a `<label htmlFor>` or `Field` can point at it. |
| `invalid` | `boolean` |  | Marks the picker invalid: error border and `aria-invalid`. Inherited from a surrounding `Field` when omitted. |
| `locale` | `string` |  | BCP 47 locale for the trigger text (`Intl.DateTimeFormat`) and the calendar's month and weekday names, digits and first weekday. |
| `max` | `DateTimeInput` |  | Latest selectable moment. |
| `min` | `DateTimeInput` |  | Earliest selectable moment. Days before it are disabled and times are clamped. |
| `name` | `string` |  | Name of the hidden input that submits the value with a surrounding form. |
| `onOpenChange` | `(open: boolean) => void` |  | Called when the popover opens or closes (selection, Escape, outside click). |
| `onValueChange` | `(value: Date \| undefined, meta: { localValue: string }) => void` |  | Called with the new local date-time; `meta.localValue` is the same moment as `"YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm"` (`""` when cleared). |
| `open` | `boolean` |  | Controlled open state of the calendar popover. Use with `onOpenChange`. |
| `placeholder` | `string` | `"Pick a date and time"` | Trigger text while no date is selected (each picker has its own default, e.g. "Pick a date"). |
| `presets` | `DateTimePreset[]` | `[]` | Quick picks shown in a sidebar ("In 1 hour", "Tomorrow 9:00"). Choosing one sets the value and closes. |
| `required` | `boolean` |  | Marks the picker required. Inherited from a surrounding `Field` when omitted. |
| `size` | `Size` | `"md"` | Trigger height and text size; match the neighbouring inputs. |
| `startMonth` | `Date` |  | Earliest month the calendar can navigate to (days before it are not reachable). |
| `step` | `number` |  | Minutes moved by the minute segment's arrow keys. |
| `timeLabel` | `string` | `"Time"` | Label next to the time field. Default "Time". |
| `value` | `DateTimeInput` |  | A `Date`, or a local `"YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm"` string (what `<input type="datetime-local">` uses). |
| `variant` | `"outline" \| "filled"` |  | `outline` (default) is the bordered box; `filled` is a tinted surface with a hidden border. |

### Notes

**When to use:** An input-like button that opens a calendar plus a time field, to pick a local day and time together. The value is wall-clock time in the user's zone, like `datetime-local`, as a `Date` or a `"YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm"` string.

**Use instead when:**
- `DatePicker`: a day only
- `TimePicker`: a time only
- `DateRangePicker`: a from and to range
- `Input`: a native `type="datetime-local"` field

#### Keyboard

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Trigger, clear button, then (open) the presets, the calendar, the hour, minute and day period segments and Done |
| Enter, Space | On the trigger: open; on a preset: choose it and close; on a day: pick it; on Done: close |
| Arrow keys, PageUp, PageDown, Home, End | In the calendar: move the focused day (see Calendar) |
| ArrowUp, ArrowDown, digits, Backspace | In a time segment: step, type or clear it (see TimePicker) |
| Escape | Close the popover; focus returns to the trigger |

The trigger is a plain button, so ArrowDown does not open it. In RTL the calendar's Left and Right arrows swap; the time segments stay in a left to right group with fixed Left and Right.

#### Screen readers

- The trigger is a native `<button>` showing the formatted date and time, or the `placeholder`. The popover is a `role="dialog"` named by `aria-label`, then the placeholder, then "Choose date and time". `required`, `invalid`, `id` and `aria-describedby` work as on `DatePicker`.
- The time field is a group named by the visible "Time" text (`timeLabel`) with spinbutton segments for hour, minute and, with `granularity="second"`, seconds, plus an AM/PM segment on a 12-hour clock. The presets are plain buttons in a group named "Presets".
- A given name (`aria-label`, a `FieldLabel`) replaces the button text as the accessible name, so the chosen moment is not part of it. The clear button is named "Clear date".

#### Reduced motion

The popover fades and zooms in with `animate-in`; the net removes the movement and ends transitions in 1 ms. The time field has no motion of its own.

#### Server rendering

Server render: part of it fills in after mount. The trigger renders on the server and the popover is portalled, so it appears after mount. The trigger text is formatted with `Intl.DateTimeFormat` in the runtime's default locale and time zone unless you pass `locale`, `formatOptions` or `formatDateTime`, so server and browser can print different text and trigger a hydration warning. The portalled layer does not inherit a subtree `dir` or `data-style`; set them on `<html>`.

#### Gotchas

- Changes apply at once: picking a day, or stepping the time, calls `onValueChange(date, { localValue })` and the popover stays open until Done, Escape or an outside click. Picking a preset sets the value and closes. Clicking the selected day does not unselect it.
- A day picked before any time is set uses the time typed so far, else `defaultTime` (`"00:00"`). A time typed before a day exists is held until a day is picked.
- `min` and `max` disable days outside them, clamp the result, and limit the time on the boundary day; strings without a zone are read as local time.
- With `name` a hidden input posts `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm` (with `:ss` for seconds, empty when none). `locale` formats the trigger, sets the time field's clock and segment order, and sets the calendar's month and weekday names, digits and first weekday (its aria labels stay English).

## Dialog

> Modal dialog root.

- Import: `import { Dialog } from "@sutra/ui"` (or from `@sutra/ui/overlays`)
- Source: `packages/ui/src/primitives/dialog` (primitives)
- Parts: [`DialogBody`](DialogBody.md), [`DialogClose`](DialogClose.md), [`DialogContent`](DialogContent.md), [`DialogDescription`](DialogDescription.md), [`DialogFooter`](DialogFooter.md), [`DialogHeader`](DialogHeader.md), [`DialogOverlay`](DialogOverlay.md), [`DialogPortal`](DialogPortal.md), [`DialogTitle`](DialogTitle.md), [`DialogTrigger`](DialogTrigger.md)
- Also accepts the props of DialogProps

Dialog vs Sheet vs Drawer: `Dialog` is a centred modal (a bottom sheet on phones) for a focused task or decision; `Sheet` slides in from an edge for navigation, detail or filter panels; `Drawer` (`./drawer`) is a touch-first bottom sheet with drag-to-dismiss and snap points. Use `AlertDialog` / `ConfirmDialog` for interrupting confirmations.

### Props

No props of its own.

### Part props

Props of `DialogContent`, `DialogFooter`, `DialogHeader`: see [the full page](md/Dialog.md).

### Notes

**When to use:** A modal that interrupts the page for one focused task. Centred on screens from `sm` up, a bottom sheet below. `AlertDialog` and `ConfirmDialog` are the variants for confirmations that must be answered.

**Use instead when:**
- `Sheet`: a side or edge panel that keeps the page context
- `Drawer`: a touch-first bottom sheet you drag
- `Popover`: a small floating panel that does not block the page
- `DialogProvider`: ask for a confirm or a prompt from code

#### Keyboard

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Cycle focus inside the dialog (it is trapped while open) |
| Escape | Close the dialog (`AlertDialog` closes on Escape too, but not on an outside click) |
| Enter, Space | Activate the focused button, including the close button |

Focus moves into the dialog on open and returns to whatever had it before, even when the dialog was opened without a `DialogTrigger` (a hotkey, a menu item, controlled `open`). There are no arrow-key or direction-dependent keys, so RTL changes nothing.

#### Screen readers

Radix gives the panel `role="dialog"` (`alertdialog` for `AlertDialog`), `aria-labelledby` from `DialogTitle` and `aria-describedby` from `DialogDescription`, and hides the rest of the page from assistive technology while it is open. Always render a `DialogTitle` (it may be visually hidden); `ConfirmDialog` requires `title` for that reason. The built-in close button is labelled "Close". The mobile grabber bar is `aria-hidden` decoration.

#### Reduced motion

The panel fades and zooms in (from the bottom edge on mobile) with the `animate-in` utilities; under reduced motion the net removes the zoom and slide and keeps the fade.

#### Server rendering

Server render: same markup as the client. A closed dialog renders only its trigger on both server and client, so there is nothing to mismatch. The content is portalled into `<body>` after mount: a dialog that is `open` on first render appears after hydration, not in the server HTML. The portalled layer does not sit inside a subtree `data-style` or `dir`: put them on `<html>`.

#### Gotchas

- `AlertDialog` ignores outside clicks (no dismiss by clicking the backdrop), `Dialog` does not: use `AlertDialog` when the user must choose.
- `ConfirmDialog onConfirm` may return a promise: the confirm button shows a spinner and closing is blocked until it settles, and throwing keeps the dialog open.
- A dialog opened from a menu item that then unmounts cannot return focus to it (the opener is gone), and Radix's default applies; keep the opener mounted when focus matters.
- `size` only sets the maximum width from `sm` up; below that every dialog is full width.

## DialogProvider

> Mount once near the root to enable `useDialogs()`: promise-based `confirm`, `prompt` and `choose` built on `ConfirmDialog` and `Dialog`. One dialog shows at a time; later calls wait in a queue.

- Import: `import { DialogProvider } from "@sutra/ui"` (or from `@sutra/ui/overlays`)
- Source: `packages/ui/src/primitives/confirm` (primitives)

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `children` | `React.ReactNode` |  | The app subtree that can call `useDialogs()`. |

### Notes

**When to use:** Mount once near the root to ask for a confirmation, a line of text or a choice from code with promises. `useDialogs()` returns `confirm`, `prompt` and `choose`; `useConfirm()` is `confirm` alone. One dialog shows at a time and the rest queue.

**Use instead when:**
- `ConfirmDialog`: a confirmation you render in place with a `trigger` or controlled `open`
- `Dialog`: a custom form or content
- `AlertDialog`: a blocking message with your own buttons
- `Toaster`: feedback that needs no answer

#### Keyboard

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Cycle focus inside the dialog (trapped while open) |
| Escape | Cancel: `confirm` resolves `false`, `prompt` and `choose` resolve `null` |
| Enter | In `prompt`: submit the field (the form validates, then resolves the text) |
| Enter, Space | Activate the focused button |
| ArrowUp, ArrowDown, ArrowLeft, ArrowRight | In `choose`: move between the options (the radio group; Enter does not pick, Tab on to Confirm) |

`confirm` opens with focus on Cancel, so a stray Enter does not confirm; `prompt` focuses and selects the field; focus returns to whatever had it when the first dialog of a run opened, once the queue is empty. The radio group reads the document or `DirectionProvider` direction, so its left and right arrows follow reading direction in RTL.

#### Screen readers

`confirm` is a Radix `alertdialog` named by its title (default "Are you sure?") and described by `description`; `prompt` and `choose` are `dialog`s named by `title` (a `prompt` without one uses a string `label`, else "Enter a value"; `choose` falls back to "Choose an option"). The `prompt` field is named by `label`, or by the title through `aria-label` when there is no `label`; a validation message sits in `FieldError`, sets `aria-invalid` and is linked as the field's description, and focus returns to the field. `choose` is a labelled radio group. The rest is `ConfirmDialog` and `Dialog` behaviour (the page is hidden from assistive technology while open).

#### Reduced motion

The dialogs are the standard ones: a short fade and zoom (a slide from the bottom on small screens), and the reduced-motion net removes the movement and keeps the fade. The pending spinner on the confirm button keeps turning.

#### Server rendering

Server render: same markup as the client. The provider renders only its children on the server: no dialog exists until `confirm`, `prompt` or `choose` is called, which happens in handlers or effects on the client. The dialogs themselves are portalled after mount.

#### Gotchas

- `useDialogs` and `useConfirm` throw outside a `DialogProvider`. Unmounting the provider resolves every open and queued dialog as cancelled (`false` or `null`), so no `await` hangs.
- `confirm`'s `onConfirm` may be async: the button shows a spinner and the dialog cannot be dismissed meanwhile. If it throws, the dialog stays open and the error is swallowed, so show your own message from the `catch`.
- `prompt` trims and requires a value by default (`trim` and `required` default to true; `required: false` can resolve `""`). `validate` keeps the dialog open only when it returns a non-empty string (the message); returning `false` accepts the value.
- `choose` resolves the picked option's own `value` (any type) and starts on `defaultValue`, else the first enabled option; disabled options cannot be picked. Cancel resolves `null` for `prompt` and `choose`, so test for `null` before using the answer.

## DirectionProvider

> Tells Sutra and its Radix primitives which way the text runs. Put one at the app root (no `dir`: it follows `<html dir>` live) or wrap a subtree with a `dir` to force it; read it with `useDirection`.

- Import: `import { DirectionProvider } from "@sutra/ui"` (or from `@sutra/ui/core`)
- Source: `packages/ui/src/primitives/direction-provider` (primitives)
- `data-slot`: `direction-provider`
- Also accepts the props of HTMLAttributes

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `children` | `React.ReactNode` |  | The subtree that reads the direction. |
| `dir` | `Direction` |  | Force the direction of this subtree. It renders a `display: contents` element carrying `dir`, so logical utilities, `rtl:` variants and Radix keyboard handling all follow it, and nests (a chart can force `ltr` inside an RTL page). Omit it to follow the document (`<html dir>`) and render no element. |

### Notes

**When to use:** Tells Sutra and its Radix primitives which way text runs. Mount one at the app root to follow `<html dir>` live, or give it `dir` to force a subtree (a chart that stays `ltr` inside an RTL page). Read the value with `useDirection()`.

**Use instead when:**
- `useDirection`: read the direction in your own component
- `useRootDirection`: pass the direction into a wrapped Radix root

#### Keyboard

Not focusable: no keyboard interaction of its own. It decides which way horizontal arrow keys go in what sits below it: Radix primitives (Tabs, sub-menus, radio groups, a horizontal Accordion) and Sutra components such as `TabDropdown` swap ArrowLeft and ArrowRight in RTL, while vertical lists do not.

#### Screen readers

No role, name or state. With `dir` it renders one `<div dir="rtl">` (or `ltr`) with `display: contents`, so the text direction is exposed to the browser and assistive technology without adding a box. Extra HTML attributes pass through to that element, so set `lang` on it when the subtree is in another language. Without `dir` it renders nothing.

#### Reduced motion

Static: it renders no motion.

#### Server rendering

Server render: part of it fills in after mount. With `dir` the markup is the same on the server and the client: the `display: contents` element carries `dir`, and every `useDirection()` inside it reads that value. Without `dir`, `useDirection()` returns `ltr` on the server and the real `<html dir>` value after hydration, so in an RTL document the server HTML of wrappers that write a `dir` attribute (Tabs, Accordion, ScrollArea, RadioGroup) says `ltr` until hydration.

#### Slots

- `direction-provider`: the `display: contents` element, only when `dir` is set

#### Gotchas

- Without `dir` it renders no element (children only) and follows `<html dir>` live, so it does not set `<html dir>` or `lang` for you: do that on the document.
- With `dir` a `className` that needs a box (padding, background, border) has no effect, because the element is `display: contents`; put those on a child. A nested provider wins over an outer one, which is how a subtree forces `ltr` inside an RTL page.
- A forced `dir` reaches the subtree only. Dialogs, sheets, drawers, popovers, tooltips and hover cards are portalled into `<body>` outside that element, so their `rtl:` styles follow `<html dir>`; menus carry their own `dir` attribute from the provider.
- `dir` takes `"ltr"` or `"rtl"` only (no `"auto"`).

## Drawer

> Bottom sheet with drag-to-dismiss, optional snap points, scroll lock and focus return (Radix Dialog).

- Import: `import { Drawer } from "@sutra/ui"` (or from `@sutra/ui/mobile`)
- Source: `packages/ui/src/primitives/drawer` (primitives)
- Parts: [`DrawerBody`](DrawerBody.md), [`DrawerClose`](DrawerClose.md), [`DrawerContent`](DrawerContent.md), [`DrawerDescription`](DrawerDescription.md), [`DrawerFooter`](DrawerFooter.md), [`DrawerHeader`](DrawerHeader.md), [`DrawerTitle`](DrawerTitle.md), [`DrawerTrigger`](DrawerTrigger.md)

Dialog vs Sheet vs Drawer: `Dialog` is a centred modal for a focused task or decision; `Sheet` is a panel that slides in from any edge (side navigation, detail or filter panels); `Drawer` is a touch-first bottom sheet with a grabber, drag-to-dismiss and snap points. Drawer's Header, Title, Description, Body and Footer are the Sheet parts with drawer spacing.

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `children` | `React.ReactNode` |  | The drawer parts: a `DrawerTrigger` and a `DrawerContent`. |
| `defaultOpen` | `boolean` | `false` | Initial open state when uncontrolled. |
| `defaultSnapPoint` | `number` |  | Initially active snap point when uncontrolled; one of `snapPoints`. |
| `dismissible` | `boolean` | `true` | Allow closing by drag, Escape and scrim click. Default true. |
| `modal` | `boolean` | `true` | Modal (scroll lock, focus trap, inert page). Default true. |
| `onOpenChange` | `(open: boolean) => void` |  | Called when the drawer opens or closes (drag, Escape, scrim click, a close button). |
| `onSnapPointChange` | `(snap: number) => void` |  | Called with the snap point the sheet settled on after a drag. |
| `open` | `boolean` |  | Controlled open state. Use with `onOpenChange`. |
| `snapPoint` | `number` |  | Active snap point (one of `snapPoints`). |
| `snapPoints` | `number[]` |  | Heights as fractions of the viewport, e.g. `[0.5, 1]`. Omit for a content-sized sheet. |

### Part props

Props of `DrawerContent`: see [the full page](md/Drawer.md).

### Notes

**When to use:** A touch-first bottom sheet with a grabber, drag-to-dismiss and optional snap points (`snapPoints` as fractions of the viewport height). Modal, with scroll lock and focus return. Header, title, body and footer are the Sheet parts with drawer spacing.

**Use instead when:**
- `Sheet`: a panel from any edge that is not dragged
- `Dialog`: a centred modal for one decision or task
- `Popover`: a small floating panel that does not block the page

#### Keyboard

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Cycle focus inside the drawer (trapped while it is modal) |
| Escape | Close the drawer; ignored with `dismissible={false}` |
| Enter, Space | On the handle button (only with two or more `snapPoints`): go to the next snap point and wrap to the smallest |
| Enter, Space | Activate the focused button, including `DrawerClose` and the close button from `showClose` |

Dragging is pointer-only. Without snap points the handle is a decorative `aria-hidden` bar, so keyboard users close with Escape or a `DrawerClose` button. There are no direction-dependent keys, so RTL changes nothing. Focus returns to the `DrawerTrigger` on close (Radix), and for a drawer opened without a trigger (a hotkey, controlled `open`) to the element that had focus when it opened, as `SheetContent` does; a `preventDefault()` in your `onCloseAutoFocus` still wins.

#### Screen readers

Radix gives the panel `role="dialog"` with `aria-labelledby` from `DrawerTitle` and `aria-describedby` from `DrawerDescription`, and hides the rest of the page while it is open.
