Always render a `DrawerTitle` (it may be visually hidden). The handle button with snap points is named "Expand sheet" or "Collapse sheet" depending on the current snap point; the grabber bar itself is `aria-hidden`. The close button from `showClose` is labelled "Close".

#### Reduced motion

The sheet slides up from the bottom with `animate-in` and the drag release settles with a 320 ms translate transition. The reduced-motion net removes the slide, keeps the fade and ends the settle transition in 1 ms. Dragging follows the pointer and is not affected.

#### Server rendering

Server render: same markup as the client. Only the trigger renders on the server. The sheet is portalled into `<body>` after mount, so a drawer that is `open` on first render appears after hydration. The viewport height used for snap points is read only inside the portalled content.

#### Slots

- `drawer-content`: the sheet panel (`data-dragging` while dragged, `data-snap` with snap points)
- `drawer-handle`: the grabber, a button with two or more snap points, else a decorative bar
- `drawer-header`: the pinned header; it is draggable
- `drawer-body`: the scrollable content area
- `drawer-footer`: the pinned action row

#### Gotchas

- A release past 80 px of drag, or a fast flick down (above 500 px/s), dismisses the drawer; with snap points a flick moves one snap point and only the smallest one dismisses. A drag never starts on text fields, sliders, `[data-drawer-no-drag]` elements, or inside a scroll area that is scrolled down.
- `dismissible={false}` disables Escape, scrim clicks and drag-to-dismiss, but `DrawerClose` and a controlled `open` still close it. It stays draggable between snap points if there are two or more.
- `snapPoints` are clamped to 0.05 through 1 and sorted. The panel is as tall as the largest one, and an uncontrolled drawer reopens at `defaultSnapPoint` or the smallest. `snapPoint` makes it controlled with `onSnapPointChange`.
- Drawer parts must be inside `<Drawer>` (they throw otherwise). `showHandle` is on and `showClose` off by default, and the panel is at most `max-w-2xl`, centred, on wide screens.

## DropdownMenu

> Dropdown menu root: Radix `DropdownMenu.Root` with the reading direction filled in.

- Import: `import { DropdownMenu } from "@sutra/ui"` (or from `@sutra/ui/overlays`)
- Source: `packages/ui/src/primitives/dropdown-menu` (primitives)
- Parts: [`DropdownMenuCheckboxItem`](DropdownMenuCheckboxItem.md), [`DropdownMenuContent`](DropdownMenuContent.md), [`DropdownMenuGroup`](DropdownMenuGroup.md), [`DropdownMenuItem`](DropdownMenuItem.md), [`DropdownMenuLabel`](DropdownMenuLabel.md), [`DropdownMenuPortal`](DropdownMenuPortal.md), [`DropdownMenuRadioGroup`](DropdownMenuRadioGroup.md), [`DropdownMenuRadioItem`](DropdownMenuRadioItem.md), [`DropdownMenuSeparator`](DropdownMenuSeparator.md), [`DropdownMenuShortcut`](DropdownMenuShortcut.md), [`DropdownMenuSub`](DropdownMenuSub.md), [`DropdownMenuSubContent`](DropdownMenuSubContent.md), [`DropdownMenuSubTrigger`](DropdownMenuSubTrigger.md), [`DropdownMenuTrigger`](DropdownMenuTrigger.md)
- Also accepts the props of DropdownMenuProps

### Props

No props of its own.

### Part props

Props of `DropdownMenuCheckboxItem`, `DropdownMenuItem`, `DropdownMenuLabel`, `DropdownMenuSubTrigger`: see [the full page](md/DropdownMenu.md).

### Notes

**When to use:** A menu of actions that opens from a trigger button. Rows take an `icon`, `description`, display-only `shortcut` and `tone="destructive"`, plus checkbox and radio rows and nested sub-menus.

**Use instead when:**
- `Select`: the menu chooses a value for a form field
- `ContextMenu`: the menu opens from a right-click on an area
- `SplitButton`: a primary action with a menu of alternatives
- `Popover`: rich content or a form rather than a list of actions

#### Keyboard

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| Enter, Space, ArrowDown | On the trigger: Enter and Space toggle the menu, ArrowDown opens it (a left click opens it too) |
| ArrowDown, ArrowUp | Move the highlighted row; focus stops at the ends unless you pass `loop` to `DropdownMenuContent` |
| Home, End, PageUp, PageDown | Highlight the first or last row |
| A letter or digit | Typeahead: highlights the next row whose text starts with it |
| Enter, Space | Activate the highlighted row; a checkbox or radio row toggles or picks, and the menu closes |
| ArrowRight | On a sub-menu trigger: open it (Enter and Space do too) |
| ArrowLeft | Inside a sub-menu: close it and return to its trigger |
| Escape | Close the menu |
| Tab | Does nothing while the menu is open (Radix blocks it) |

In RTL the sub-menu keys swap: ArrowLeft opens a sub-menu and ArrowRight closes it, and the sub-menu opens to the left. `DropdownMenu` passes the document or `DirectionProvider` direction to Radix (an explicit `dir` prop wins). Focus returns to the trigger when the menu closes.

#### Screen readers

The trigger gets `aria-haspopup="menu"`, `aria-expanded` and, while open, `aria-controls`. The panel is `role="menu"` labelled by the trigger; rows are `menuitem`, `menuitemcheckbox` and `menuitemradio` (with `aria-checked`), groups are `role="group"` and the separator is `separator`. `DropdownMenuLabel` is a plain text div that is not linked to its group, so give `DropdownMenuGroup` an `aria-label` to name it. A disabled row gets `aria-disabled`. Icons and the sub-menu chevron are decoration (the chevron is `aria-hidden`; an `icon` you pass is not hidden for you). The `shortcut` text is read as part of the row name. An icon-only trigger needs `aria-label`.

#### Reduced motion

The panel fades and zooms in from the trigger with the `animate-in` utilities and slides slightly from its side; the reduced-motion net removes the slide and the scale and keeps only the fade. Row highlight changes are instant by design.

#### Server rendering

Server render: same markup as the client. A closed menu renders only its trigger on both server and client, so nothing can mismatch. The panel is portalled into `<body>` after mount, so a menu with `defaultOpen` or `open` on first render appears after hydration. The panel carries its own `dir` (the document or `DirectionProvider` direction), but it is portalled outside a subtree `data-style`: set that on `<html>`.

#### Gotchas

- `shortcut` is only a label: it does not bind any key. Wire the real shortcut yourself.
- `DropdownMenuItem` closes the menu on select; call `event.preventDefault()` in `onSelect` to keep it open (use `onSelect`, not `onClick`, for keyboard and pointer alike).
- `tone="destructive"` replaces the deprecated `variant="destructive"` (`tone` wins when both are set). With `asChild` the row styling applies but `icon`, `description` and `shortcut` are ignored: you render the content.
- `DropdownMenuContent` already wraps itself in a portal (`sideOffset` 6, `align="start"`), so `DropdownMenuPortal` is only for custom compositions. Radix `loop` defaults to off.

## Dropzone

> Drag-and-drop file area that also opens the file picker on click, Enter or Space.

- Import: `import { Dropzone } from "@sutra/ui"` (or from `@sutra/ui/forms`)
- Source: `packages/ui/src/primitives/dropzone` (primitives)
- Also accepts the props of HTMLAttributes

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `accept` | `string` |  | Accepted types, as for `<input accept>`: extensions (".pdf") and/or MIME types ("image/*"), comma separated. Others are rejected. |
| `compact` | `boolean` |  | **Deprecated.** Use `density="compact"`. Legacy form of `density="compact"`. |
| `currentCount` | `number` | `0` | Files already selected elsewhere, counted against `maxFiles`. |
| `density` | `Density` |  | `compact` is a single-row layout for tight spaces. Default `normal`. |
| `directory` | `boolean` | `false` | Upload whole folders: clicking opens a folder picker (`webkitdirectory`) and dropped folders are walked recursively. Every file is validated on its own and carries its `relativePath` (see `getFileRelativePath`). Where the browser can't pick folders, clicking falls back to the file picker and the hint says why. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Disables dropping and picking. |
| `hint` | `React.ReactNode` |  | Defaults to a description of `accept` / `maxSize`. |
| `icon` | `React.ReactNode` |  | Icon above the title. Defaults to an upload icon. |
| `inputRef` | `React.Ref<HTMLInputElement>` |  | Ref to the hidden `<input type="file">`, e.g. to open the picker from your own button. |
| `maxFiles` | `number` |  | Most files accepted per drop or pick (counted with `currentCount`); extra files are rejected. |
| `maxSize` | `number` |  | Largest accepted file in bytes; larger files are rejected. |
| `multiple` | `boolean` | `true` | Accept more than one file per drop or pick. |
| `name` | `string` |  | Name for the underlying file input. With it, the accepted files stay on the input so a native form post sends them. |
| `onDrop` | `(files: File[], rejections: FileRejection[]) => void` |  | Called with accepted files and rejections after a drop or pick. |
| `title` | `React.ReactNode` |  | Headline of the drop target. Defaults to a prompt to drop or choose files. |

### Notes

**When to use:** A drag-and-drop area that also opens the file picker on click, Enter or Space. It checks type, size and count and calls `onDrop(accepted, rejections)`; with `directory` it takes whole folders. It only collects files: you upload them.

**Use instead when:**
- `FileUpload`: a compound uploader that owns the file list and validation (put FileUploadDropzone in it)
- `FileUploadTrigger`: a button that opens the picker, with no drop area
- `Input`: a plain form field

#### Keyboard

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Focuses the zone (one tab stop; a `disabled` zone is skipped) |
| Enter, Space | Open the file picker (a folder picker with `directory`) |

Only a key pressed on the zone itself counts: keys from a `children` control inside it do not open the picker. There are no arrow keys, so RTL changes nothing. Dragging has no keyboard path; the picker is the keyboard way to add files.

#### Screen readers

- The zone is a `div role="button"` named by its visible prompt ("Click to upload or drag and drop") or by `aria-label` if you pass one. The hint (for example "Images, PDF · up to 10 MB") is added to `aria-describedby` next to any `aria-describedby` you pass. `disabled` sets `aria-disabled`.
- The real `<input type="file">` is a sibling that is `aria-hidden`, off the tab order and visually hidden, so it is never a second control; `name` and `inputRef` go to it.
- While a dropped folder is being read the zone has `aria-busy`. During a drag the prompt text is swapped for "Drop to upload" or "Some files aren't supported"; that swap is not a live region.
- Rejections are reported only through `onDrop`: nothing is announced for you, so show the messages (each rejection carries `errors[].message`) in your own status or list.
- Where `directory` cannot work, the reason ("This browser can't choose folders. Choose files instead.") is shown and added to the description.

#### Reduced motion

The icon lifts and the border, background and ring change with transitions on drag, which the reduced-motion net ends in 1 ms. Nothing loops.

#### Server rendering

Server render: part of it fills in after mount. Without `directory` the zone renders the same on both sides. With `directory` the server (and the hydration pass) assumes folders are unsupported, so the HTML says "Click to upload" and shows the "can't choose folders" reason; after hydration a supporting browser switches to "Click to choose a folder" and drops the reason.

#### Gotchas

- `onDrop` is `(accepted, rejections)` and runs for every drop or pick, also when everything was rejected or `accepted` is empty. A rejection is `{ file, errors: [{ code, message }] }` with codes `file-invalid-type`, `file-too-large` and `too-many-files`. It does not run while `disabled`.
- The red drag state only reflects what the browser reveals mid-drag: MIME types (and `multiple={false}` with several files). Extension rules such as `accept=".pdf"` and `maxSize` are checked at drop. `multiple={false}` keeps the first file and rejects the rest.
- `currentCount` counts files you already hold against `maxFiles`. Without `name` the picker input is cleared after each pick, so the same file can be chosen again. With `name` the accepted files stay on the input through `DataTransfer` (picks and drops; a rejected pick is not kept), so a native form post sends them: the earlier ones are kept while `currentCount` is above 0 and the input is emptied when it returns to 0. Where `input.files` cannot be set it is cleared as before.
- `directory` walks dropped folders and sets each file's `relativePath` (read it with `getFileRelativePath`); every file is validated on its own and counts toward `maxFiles`. `compact` is a deprecated alias of `density="compact"`. The helpers `validateFiles`, `isFileAccepted` and `describeFileConstraints` are exported for your own checks.

## EmptyState

> Placeholder for an empty list, search or first-run screen. `variant="welcome"` is the large greeting at the start of a conversation or workspace (see `ChatEmptyState`).

- Import: `import { EmptyState } from "@sutra/ui"` (or from `@sutra/ui/identity`)
- Source: `packages/ui/src/primitives/empty-state` (primitives)
- `data-slot`: `empty-state`
- Also accepts the props of HTMLAttributes

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `actions` | `React.ReactNode` |  | Buttons or links under the text. |
| `description` | `React.ReactNode` |  | Supporting text under the title. |
| `icon` | `React.ReactNode` |  | Icon shown in a ringed featured circle (default: inbox). Ignored when `illustration` is set. In the `welcome` variant it sits in a card tile and has no default. |
| `illustration` | `EmptyStateIllustrationVariant \| React.ReactNode` |  | An `EmptyStateIllustration` variant name, or any custom node. |
| `size` | `Size` | `"md"` | Spacing and type scale of the empty state. |
| `title` | `React.ReactNode` |  | Heading. Optional only for the `welcome` variant. |
| `variant` | `EmptyStateVariant` | `"default"` | `dashed` draws a dashed bordered drop-area style box; `welcome` is the large first-run greeting (`ChatEmptyState`). |

### Notes

**When to use:** The placeholder for an empty list, search result or first-run screen: an icon or illustration, a title, a description and actions. `variant="welcome"` is the large greeting at the start of a chat or workspace.

**Use instead when:**
- `Note`: a quiet one-line message inside a screen that is working or empty
- `InlineAlert`: a notice about something that needs attention
- `Skeleton`: content that is still loading
- `ChatEmptyState`: the welcome variant preconfigured for chat

#### Keyboard

Not focusable itself: no keyboard interaction. The `actions` you pass (buttons, links) are ordinary tab stops.

#### Screen readers

- The root is a `<section>` labelled by the title (`aria-labelledby`), so with a title it is a named `region` landmark. Without a title (only possible in practice for `welcome`) it has no name and is not a landmark.
- The title is a real heading: `h3` by default and `h2` for `variant="welcome"`. The level is not configurable, so check it fits your outline.
- Built-in illustrations (`search`, `inbox`, `files`, `error`, `success`, `cloud`) are `aria-hidden`, and so is the default inbox icon. A custom `illustration` node or `icon` is used as you pass it: hide decoration with `aria-hidden`.

#### Reduced motion

The block rises in with `animate-fade-up`, which the reduced-motion net in `sutra.css` removes.

#### Server rendering

Server render: same markup as the client. Plain markup with a `useId` for the heading, so server and client output match. The entrance animation starts when the page paints.

#### Slots

- `empty-state`: the root `section`, with `data-variant` set to `default`, `dashed` or `welcome`

#### Gotchas

- `icon` is ignored when `illustration` is set. In the `default` and `dashed` variants an empty `icon` falls back to an inbox glyph; in `welcome` there is no default icon and a given one sits in a small card tile.
- `illustration` takes one of the six variant names or any node: an unknown string is rendered as text, not looked up.
- `actions` sit in a wrapping row under the text; `children` follow them (inside a full-width box in `welcome`).
- `size` (`sm`, `md`, `lg`) sets spacing and type scale for the non-welcome variants only; `welcome` has its own fixed layout.

## Eyebrow

> Small all-caps label above headings.

- Import: `import { Eyebrow } from "@sutra/ui"` (or from `@sutra/ui/core`)
- Source: `packages/ui/src/primitives/typography` (primitives)
- Also accepts the props of HTMLAttributes

### Props

No props of its own.

### Notes

**When to use:** Body text with size, tone and weight steps, plus the small typographic pieces: `Eyebrow` (an all-caps label above a heading), `Kbd` (a key hint) and `InlineCode`.

**Use instead when:**
- `Heading`: a heading with the display scale
- `ShortcutKeys`: a whole key combination from a shortcut string
- `CodeBlock`: multi-line code
- `Badge`: a short status label

#### Keyboard

Not focusable: no keyboard interaction. `Kbd` only shows a key; it does not listen for it.

#### Screen readers

- `Text` renders a `p` by default; `as` takes `p`, `span`, `div`, `small`, `strong` or `em`, and `asChild` styles your own element. Use `span` inside a line of text so you do not nest paragraphs.
- `Eyebrow` is a plain `p`, not a heading: it is read as a paragraph in front of the heading it labels.
- `Kbd` renders a native `<kbd>`, which screen readers read as its text. A symbol such as the command key may be read as nothing or as a name, so for combinations that matter use `ShortcutKeys` (it carries spoken text) or add visually hidden words.
- `InlineCode` renders a native `<code>`.

#### Reduced motion

Static: no animation.

#### Server rendering

Server render: same markup as the client. Plain markup with no browser API, so server and client output match.

#### Gotchas

- `tone` is `default` (foreground), `neutral`, `primary`, `success`, `warning`, `destructive` or `info`; `muted` is the old name of `neutral`. `neutral` is the muted grey, so it is quieter than `default`; `warning` uses the darker readable shade.
- `size` is `xs` to `xl` with `md` being `text-base`; `Text` sets no line-height or margin, so spacing comes from the parent (a `Stack`) and line-height from the surrounding styles.
- `Eyebrow` is always `text-primary`, uppercase and tracked; override with `className`. `Kbd` and `InlineCode` take only the HTML props of their element plus `className`; they have no size or tone variants.

## Favicon

> Site icon for a domain: explicit `src`, provider-resolved URL, or a local monogram.

- Import: `import { Favicon } from "@sutra/ui"` (or from `@sutra/ui/ai`)
- Source: `packages/ui/src/primitives/favicon` (primitives)
- Parts: [`FaviconProvider`](FaviconProvider.md)
- Also accepts the props of HTMLAttributes

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `domain` (required) | `string` |  | Domain of the site, e.g. "github.com"; it feeds the resolver and the monogram fallback. |
| `shape` | `"circle" \| "square"` | `"circle"` | Outline of the icon. |
| `src` | `string` |  | Explicit icon URL; overrides the provider. |

### Part props

Props of `FaviconProvider`: see [the full page](md/Favicon.md).

### Notes

**When to use:** The small icon of a website: an explicit `src`, an icon your `FaviconProvider` resolves for the domain, or a local letter tile. By default it makes no network request.

**Use instead when:**
- `Monogram`: a letter tile for an app or tool you name yourself
- `Avatar`: a person
- `Item`: a row that holds a logo, title and description

#### Keyboard

Not focusable: no keyboard interaction.

#### Screen readers

Always decorative: the `img` has `alt=""` and the letter tile is `aria-hidden`. The site name must be visible text next to it (a link label, a source title); a favicon alone tells a screen reader nothing.

#### Reduced motion

Static: no animation.

#### Server rendering

Server render: same markup as the client. The same markup on server and client for the same props: the letter tile, or an `img` when a `src` or resolver gives a URL. The tile letter and colour are pure functions of `domain`. An image that fails to load switches to the tile through its `onError` handler, which runs in the browser.

#### Gotchas

- Without a `FaviconProvider` and without `src`, `Favicon` renders the local tile: no request leaves the page. `FaviconProvider resolve` opts in, and `googleFaviconResolver` sends every rendered domain to Google, so prefer your own resolver for private data. A resolver that returns `undefined` falls back to the tile.
- `src` wins over the provider. A failed `img` (`onError`) falls back to the tile and tries again when the URL changes.
- There is no default size: set it with `className` (`size-4`, `size-5`). `shape` is `circle` (default) or `square`.
- The tile letter is the first letter or digit of `domain` as given, so pass a bare host: `"www.example.com"` gives W. `domainOf(url)` returns a clean host to pass in.

## Field

> Groups a label, control, description and error, and wires their ids together.

- Import: `import { Field } from "@sutra/ui"` (or from `@sutra/ui/forms`)
- Source: `packages/ui/src/primitives/field` (primitives)
- `data-slot`: `field`
- Parts: [`FieldContent`](FieldContent.md), [`FieldContext`](FieldContext.md), [`FieldDescription`](FieldDescription.md), [`FieldError`](FieldError.md), [`FieldGroup`](FieldGroup.md), [`FieldHint`](FieldHint.md), [`FieldLabel`](FieldLabel.md), [`FieldLegend`](FieldLegend.md), [`Fieldset`](Fieldset.md)
- Also accepts the props of HTMLAttributes

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Disables the control. |
| `id` | `string` |  | Id applied to the control. Generated when omitted. |
| `invalid` | `boolean` | `false` | Marks the control invalid; the control and the error text pick it up. |
| `orientation` | `"vertical" \| "horizontal"` | `"vertical"` | Places the label above the control (`vertical`) or beside it (`horizontal`). |
| `required` | `boolean` | `false` | Marks the control required; the label shows the required indicator. |

### Part props

Props of `FieldError`, `FieldHint`, `FieldLabel`, `FieldLegend`: see [the full page](md/Field.md).

### Notes

**When to use:** Wires one form control to its label, description, hint and error: shared id, `aria-describedby`, `aria-invalid`, `disabled` and `required`. Controls that call `useField` (Input, Textarea, Select, Checkbox, Switch, the pickers and others) pick it up with no props.

**Use instead when:**
- `Label`: a standalone label with no shared state
- `Fieldset`: group related fields under a legend
- `RadioGroup`: a set of radios has its own group label
- `FieldGroup`: only vertical spacing between fields

#### Keyboard

Not focusable: `Field` renders layout and text only, so there is no keyboard interaction. Tab goes to the control inside it, and clicking the `FieldLabel` focuses that control.

#### Screen readers

- `FieldLabel` is a `<label htmlFor>` pointing at the field `id` (generated, or the `id` you pass to `Field`), and carries a label id that widgets which are not labelable elements use as `aria-labelledby` (Combobox, TimePicker). Its asterisk follows `required` but is `aria-hidden`.
- The control gets `aria-describedby` listing the description, hint and error parts that are mounted, in that order, plus any ids you pass yourself; a part with a custom `id` is listed under that id. `invalid` becomes `aria-invalid` on the control.
- `FieldError` is `role="alert"`, so it is announced when it appears, and renders nothing when it has no content. Pass `errors` (strings or `{ message }` objects from a form library) instead of children: one message is plain text, several become a list.
- `Fieldset` is a native `<fieldset>` and `FieldLegend` a `<legend>`; a `disabled` fieldset disables the controls inside it natively.

#### Reduced motion

`FieldError` fades and slides in with `animate-in slide-in-from-top-1`; the reduced-motion net removes the slide and ends the rest in 1 ms.

#### Server rendering

Server render: part of it fills in after mount. The label, control and parts render on the server, but each description, hint and error registers itself in an effect, so the control's `aria-describedby` is missing from the server HTML and appears after hydration. The id comes from `useId`, so it matches on both sides.

#### Slots

- `field`: the wrapper; carries `data-orientation`, `data-invalid` and `data-disabled`
- `field-content`: stacks label, description and error beside a control in a `horizontal` field
- `field-description`, `field-hint`, `field-error`: the text parts
- `field-group`: a vertical stack of fields
- `fieldset`, `field-legend`: the native group and its title (`data-variant` is `legend` or `label`)

#### Gotchas

- Explicit props on the control win: `useField` takes the control's own `id`, `disabled`, `required` and `invalid` (a true `aria-invalid` also counts) before the field's, and joins `aria-describedby` instead of replacing it.
- Showing a `FieldError` does not mark the control invalid: set `invalid` on `Field` (or on the control) for `aria-invalid` and the red border.
- `Field` gives one `id` to one control. For a group of controls (radios, checkboxes) use `Fieldset` with `FieldLegend`, or the group's own `label`.
- Read the state yourself with `useFieldContext()` (it returns `null` outside a `Field`), or wire a custom control with `useField`.

## FloatingActionButton

> Floating primary action, optionally expanding into a speed-dial menu.

- Import: `import { FloatingActionButton } from "@sutra/ui"` (or from `@sutra/ui/core`)
- Source: `packages/ui/src/primitives/fab` (primitives)
- `data-slot`: `fab`
- Also accepts the props of HTMLAttributes, ButtonHTMLAttributes

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `label` (required) | `string` |  | Accessible name; also the visible text when `extended`. |
| `actions` | `FabAction[]` |  | Speed-dial actions that fan out on click. |
| `containerClassName` | `string` |  | Classes for the positioned wrapper (`className` styles the button). |
| `defaultOpen` | `boolean` | `false` | Initial open state of the speed dial when uncontrolled. |
| `extended` | `boolean` | `false` | Show the label next to the icon. |
| `icon` | `React.ReactNode` |  | Icon inside the button; the only content unless `extended`. |
| `onOpenChange` | `(open: boolean) => void` |  | Called when the speed dial opens or closes. |
| `open` | `boolean` |  | Controlled open state of the speed dial. Use with `onOpenChange`. |
| `position` | `FabPosition` | `"bottom-right"` | Corner or edge of the container the button sits in. |
| `shape` | `"circle" \| "rounded"` | `"circle"` | Outline: fully round, or rounded square. |
| `size` | `"sm" \| "md" \| "lg"` | `"md"` | Button size: 48, 56 or 64 px (`sm`, `md`, `lg`). |
| `strategy` | `"fixed" \| "absolute" \| "static"` | `"fixed"` | `fixed` to the viewport (default), `absolute` within a relative parent, or `static` inline. |
| `variant` | `"primary" \| "secondary" \| "inverse"` | `"primary"` | Fill style: `primary`, `secondary` (outlined) or `inverse`. |

### Variants

- `variant`: `primary`, `secondary`, `inverse` (default "primary")
- `size`: `sm`, `md`, `lg` (default "md")
- `shape`: `circle`, `rounded` (default "circle")
- `extended`: `true`, `false` (default false)

### Notes

**When to use:** One pinned primary action for a screen, round or rounded-square, icon-only or extended with a label. Pass `actions` and it becomes a speed dial that fans a menu of small actions out of the button.

**Use instead when:**
- `Button`: an ordinary action in the page flow
- `DropdownMenu`: a menu of actions from an ordinary trigger
- `FanMenu`: a radial menu of icons
- `Dialog`: the action needs a form or a decision

#### Keyboard

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| Enter, Space | On the button: runs `onClick`, and toggles the dial when it has `actions` |
| ArrowUp | With `actions`, on a bottom position: opens the dial and focuses the action nearest the button (already open: focuses it) |
| ArrowDown | The same for a `top-*` position |
| ArrowUp, ArrowDown | In the open dial: the key that points away from the button moves to the next action, the other moves back; both wrap and skip disabled actions |
| Home, End | Focus the first (nearest) or last action |
| Enter, Space | On an action: runs its `onClick`, then closes the dial. A link action (`href`) follows on Enter only |
| Escape | While the dial is open: closes it and returns focus to the button, wherever focus is |
| Tab | Moves through the open actions one by one (they are not roving) and does not close the dial |

The dial is vertical, so no arrow key swaps in RTL. The `position` names are physical (`bottom-right` stays at the right edge in RTL).

#### Screen readers

- Without `actions` it is a plain `<button type="button">` named by `label` (`aria-label`); with `extended`, the visible `label` is the name and `aria-label` is dropped. The icon is `aria-hidden`.
- With `actions` the button gets `aria-haspopup="menu"`, `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`; the list is a `role="menu"` named by `label`, with `menuitem` buttons (links when an action has `href`) wrapped in `role="none"` items.
- A closed dial is `inert`, so its actions are neither focusable nor in the accessibility tree. A disabled action is `disabled` (a link gets `aria-disabled`, no `href` and `tabindex="-1"`).
- On `*-center` positions the action labels are visually hidden but still read; elsewhere each label shows beside its round icon.

#### Reduced motion

The fan-out (each item fades, scales and slides with a 30 ms stagger), the 45 degree turn of the default plus icon, the hover lift and the press scale are all transitions. The reduced-motion net ends them in 1 ms and removes the delays, so the dial opens at once and the lift and press are instant.

#### Server rendering

Server render: same markup as the client. No browser API at render: the document listeners attach in an effect and `useId` names the menu. A `defaultOpen` or `open` dial is already open in the server HTML.

#### Slots

- `fab`: the positioned wrapper that holds the dial and the button (`containerClassName` styles it; `className` styles the button)

#### Gotchas

- `strategy` defaults to `fixed`, pinned to the viewport corner with `z-50`. In a card, a demo or any container use `absolute` (inside a `relative` parent) or `static`, which ignores `position` offsets.
- `label` is required and is not shown unless `extended`; there is no tooltip. Default icon is a plus; it turns only when you pass `actions` and no `icon`.
- Your `onClick` runs first, and `preventDefault()` in it stops the toggle. `open` and the actions do nothing without a non-empty `actions` array.
- Running an action closes the dial and, when focus is still on the action (its handler did not move it), puts focus back on the button, as Escape does; clicking elsewhere closes it and leaves focus where you clicked.

## Frame

> A titled tray around a panel of rows: `FrameHeader` (title, description, action), `FramePanel`, `FrameFooter`.

- Import: `import { Frame } from "@sutra/ui"` (or from `@sutra/ui/core`)
- Source: `packages/ui/src/primitives/frame` (primitives)
- `data-slot`: `frame`
- Parts: [`FrameAction`](FrameAction.md), [`FrameDescription`](FrameDescription.md), [`FrameFooter`](FrameFooter.md), [`FrameHeader`](FrameHeader.md), [`FramePanel`](FramePanel.md), [`FrameTitle`](FrameTitle.md)
- Also accepts the props of HTMLAttributes

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `variant` | `"default" \| "band" \| "inset" \| "plain"` | `"default"` | Container look: `default` (tray with a raised panel), `band` (one card with header and footer bands), `inset` (soft tray, roomy panel) or `plain` (no tray). |

### Variants

- `variant`: `default`, `band`, `inset`, `plain` (default "default")

### Part props

Props of `FramePanel`, `FrameTitle`: see [the full page](md/Frame.md).

### Notes

**When to use:** A titled tray around a panel of rows: a header with title, description and action, a panel that holds the rows, and a footer. Four looks, with loading and empty states in the panel.

**Use instead when:**
- `Item`: the row itself (put `Item`s in the panel)
- `Card`: a free-form content container
- `Accordion`: rows that open and close
- `Table`: comparable columns

#### Keyboard

Not focusable itself: no keyboard interaction. The action in `FrameAction` and the rows in the panel are ordinary tab stops.

#### Screen readers

- `FrameTitle` renders an `h3` by default; `as` picks `h2` to `h6`, `p` or `div`, so set it to fit your heading outline.
- `FramePanel` is a `role="list"` and needs an `aria-label`. `Item` rows inside it become list items by themselves. Any other row must carry `role="listitem"` itself, or the list has no valid children.
- `loading` shows `aria-busy` with sr-only "Loading…" and `aria-hidden` placeholder rows (an icon box and two lines). `emptyState` is wrapped in a `listitem`.
- `Frame`, `FrameHeader` and `FrameFooter` add no roles, so the header is not linked to the panel: label the panel yourself.

#### Reduced motion

Static: no animation of its own. The loading placeholders are `Skeleton`s and follow the net in `sutra.css`.

#### Server rendering

Server render: same markup as the client. Plain markup with no browser API, so server and client output match. The variant styles come from CSS (`group-data-[variant=...]`), so they apply on the first paint.

#### Slots

- `frame`: the root, with `data-variant`
- `frame-header`: title, description and action; wraps on narrow widths
- `frame-title`: the heading
- `frame-description`: a line under or beside the title
- `frame-action`: a control at the end of the header
- `frame-panel`: the raised surface that holds the rows
- `frame-footer`: a count, hint or action

#### Gotchas

- `variant` is `default` (a tray with a raised panel, corners kept concentric), `band` (one card with tinted header and footer bands), `inset` (a soft tray with a roomy, borderless panel) or `plain` (no tray). The header, footer and panel read the variant from the root, so they must sit inside `Frame`.
- `FramePanel` draws hairlines between rows by default; pass `divided={false}` for none.
- `emptyState` shows only when the panel has no children and `loading` is off. `loadingRows` defaults to 3.
- `FrameDescription` is full width, so inside a wrapping header it falls onto its own line under the title and action.

## GlyphSpinner

> Text-glyph spinner (braille dots, arcs, …): a preset of `<Spinner variant="glyph">`. Holds a static frame under reduced motion.

- Import: `import { GlyphSpinner } from "@sutra/ui"` (or from `@sutra/ui/core`)
- Source: `packages/ui/src/primitives/glyph-spinner` (primitives)
- Also accepts the props of HTMLAttributes

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `frames` | `readonly string[]` |  | Custom frames (overrides `variant`). |
| `interval` | `number` |  | Milliseconds per frame. Default 80. |
| `label` | `string` |  | Screen reader label. Default "Loading". |
| `paused` | `boolean` |  | Pause on the current frame. |
| `size` | `NonNullable<SpinnerProps["size"]>` |  | Glyph size as on `Spinner`: `xs` to `xl` sets the font size. Leave it out to inherit the parent's font size. |
| `variant` | `GlyphSpinnerVariant` | `"dots"` | Which glyph animation to play (a key of the spinner glyph frame sets). |

### Notes

**When to use:** A loading indicator made of a cycling text character (braille dots, arcs, a rotating line), for terminals, agent status lines and anywhere a monospace look fits. A preset of `Spinner` with `variant="glyph"`.

**Use instead when:**
- `Spinner`: a ring, dots, bars or pulse that scales with `size`
- `Skeleton`: a placeholder in the shape of content that is loading
- `Progress`: the amount done is known

#### Keyboard

Not focusable: no keyboard interaction.

#### Screen readers

A `role="status"` span with visually hidden text, "Loading" unless `label` says otherwise. The glyph itself is `aria-hidden`, so screen readers do not hear each frame. `label=""` makes it decorative (`aria-hidden`, no role). Name what is loading when several are on the page.

#### Reduced motion

It reads `usePrefersReducedMotion` and holds its current frame (frame 0 on first render) instead of cycling. This is the component's own check, not a CSS rule.

#### Server rendering

Server render: same markup as the client. Always renders frame 0 first: the preference hook reads `false` on the server and the interval starts after mount, so the server and client markup match.

#### Gotchas

- `frames` overrides `variant` when it is not empty; an empty array falls back to `variant`. `variant` is one of `dots` (default), `line`, `arc`, `circle`, `bounce`, `star` or `pulse`, the same sets as `glyphSpinnerFrames`.
- `size` (`xs` to `xl`, as on `Spinner`) sets the font size; without it the glyph takes the font size and colour of its parent, so a `text-*` class on `className` or a wrapper also works.
- `interval` is milliseconds per frame (default 80) and is clamped to at least 16; `paused` holds the current frame, as does a single-frame `frames` array.
- The glyph sits in a `min-w-[1ch]` monospace box, so a custom frame set should use characters of similar width to avoid jitter.

## Grid

> 12-column responsive grid (4 → 8 → 12 columns). Use `GridItem span` to size children.

- Import: `import { Grid } from "@sutra/ui"` (or from `@sutra/ui/core`)
- Source: `packages/ui/src/primitives/layout` (primitives)
- Parts: [`GridItem`](GridItem.md)
- Also accepts the props of HTMLAttributes

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `gap` | `"sm" \| "md" \| "lg"` | `"md"` | Space between the cells: `sm` 12px, `md` 16px (24px from the tablet width up) or `lg` 24px (32px from the tablet width up). |

### Part props

Props of `GridItem`: see [the full page](md/Grid.md).

### Notes

**When to use:** A responsive 12-column page grid that is 4 columns on mobile, 8 on tablet and 12 on desktop. `GridItem` sets how many columns a child spans at each size.

**Use instead when:**
- `Stack`: a one-dimensional flex layout
- `Container`: centre content and cap its width
- `Card`: a bordered surface to place in a cell

#### Keyboard

Not focusable: no keyboard interaction.

#### Screen readers

Plain `div`s with no role. The reading order is the DOM order, whatever the spans do visually, so keep the source order meaningful.

#### Reduced motion

Static: no animation.

#### Server rendering

Server render: same markup as the client. Plain markup; the column counts come from CSS breakpoints (`md`, `lg`), so there is no script and no mismatch.

#### Gotchas

- `GridItem span` counts columns of the 4-column mobile grid and defaults to `"full"`: an item with only `lg={4}` is full width on mobile and tablet too. Give `md` when the tablet layout should differ.
- `span` above 4 on mobile makes implicit columns; use `md` (of 8) and `lg` (of 12) for larger spans.
- `md` is typed 1 to 8 or `"full"` because the tablet grid has 8 columns (a larger value used to compile and do nothing); `span` and `lg` accept 1 to 12 and `"full"`.
- `gap` is `sm`, `md` (default, wider from `md` up) or `lg`.

## Heading

> Heading with the display type scale (`size`); the element level (`as`) is independent of the look. Extra props are spread to the heading.

- Import: `import { Heading } from "@sutra/ui"` (or from `@sutra/ui/core`)
- Source: `packages/ui/src/primitives/typography` (primitives)
- Also accepts the props of HTMLAttributes

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `as` | `HeadingLevel` | `"h2"` | Heading element to render (`h1` to `h6`), independent of the visual `size`. |
| `asChild` | `boolean` |  | Render as the child element instead of the heading tag, keeping the heading styles. |
| `size` | `"display-3xl" \| "display-2xl" \| "display-xl" \| "display-lg" \| "display-md" \| "display-sm" \| "display-xs" \| "xl" \| "lg" \| "md" \| "sm"` | `"display-sm"` | Type scale step, from `display-xs` to `display-3xl`; large steps shrink on small screens. |

### Variants

- `size`: `display-3xl`, `display-2xl`, `display-xl`, `display-lg`, `display-md`, `display-sm`, `display-xs`, `xl`, `lg`, `md`, `sm` (default "display-sm")

### Notes

**When to use:** A heading on the display type scale. The element level (`as`) is independent of the look (`size`), so the outline and the design can differ.

**Use instead when:**
- `Text`: body copy
- `Eyebrow`: a small caps label above a heading
- `CardTitle`: the title inside a Card
- `SectionHeader`: a section heading with eyebrow, description and actions

#### Keyboard

Not focusable: no keyboard interaction.

#### Screen readers

- Renders the element named by `as` (`h1` to `h6`), and the default is `h2`, not `h1`. Pass `as="h1"` once per page; pick levels by document outline, never by size.
- `asChild` renders your child element with the heading styles instead; the child then decides the semantics (a `div` child is not a heading unless it has `role="heading"` and `aria-level`).
- The text is balanced (`text-balance`) for wrapping only, which has no effect on what is read.

#### Reduced motion

Static: no animation.

#### Server rendering

Server render: same markup as the client. Plain markup with no browser API, so server and client output match. The size steps change at CSS breakpoints, not in script.

#### Gotchas

- `size` runs from `display-3xl` down to `display-xs` and then `xl`, `lg`, `md`, `sm`; the default is `display-sm`. The large display steps shrink on small screens (`display-3xl` is `display-lg` on mobile).
- `as` only takes `h1` to `h6`; use `asChild` for anything else, including a link inside the heading.
- The weight is always semibold and the colour foreground; override with `className` (merged last).

## HoverCard

> Hover card root (preview on hover, e.g. user cards and link previews).

- Import: `import { HoverCard } from "@sutra/ui"` (or from `@sutra/ui/overlays`)
- Source: `packages/ui/src/primitives/popover` (primitives)
- Parts: [`HoverCardContent`](HoverCardContent.md), [`HoverCardTrigger`](HoverCardTrigger.md)
- Also accepts the props of HoverCardProps

### Props

No props of its own.

### Part props

Props of `HoverCardContent`: see [the full page](md/HoverCard.md).

### Notes

**When to use:** A rich preview that appears when the pointer rests on a link or when it gains focus, for user cards and link previews. Opens after 300 ms and closes after 150 ms by default. The content is supplementary, not interactive.

**Use instead when:**
- `Tooltip`: a short plain-text label
- `Popover`: content the user must be able to click, type in or reach by keyboard
- `InfoTooltip`: a help icon with a short explanation

#### Keyboard

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Focusing the trigger opens the card after `openDelay`; moving focus away closes it after `closeDelay` |
| Escape | Close the card |

The trigger is an `<a>`, so it is a tab stop only when it has an `href` (or `tabIndex`). Radix sets `tabindex="-1"` on every focusable element inside the card, so keyboard users cannot reach links or buttons in it. There are no arrow keys, so RTL changes nothing for keys. In RTL, `side="start"` and `side="end"` swap left and right (read through `useDirection()`: a `DirectionProvider` with a `dir`, else `<html dir>`; a plain `dir` attribute on a container is not seen); the default is `bottom`, `left` and `right` stay physical, and Radix still flips the card on a collision.

#### Screen readers

The card has no role, no label and no `aria-describedby` link to its trigger, and it is portalled to the end of `<body>`: a screen reader user may not find it, and it does not announce when it opens. Treat its content as a duplicate of something reachable elsewhere (the linked page, a profile), never as the only place for information or actions.

#### Reduced motion

The card fades and zooms in from its trigger and slides slightly from its side; the reduced-motion net removes the slide and the scale and keeps only the fade. The open and close delays are timers and stay.

#### Server rendering

Server render: same markup as the client. Only the trigger renders on the server; the card is portalled after mount and only opens from pointer hover or focus. A `defaultOpen` card appears after hydration.

#### Gotchas

- Touch never opens it: Radix ignores touch pointers and prevents default on `touchstart`, so a touch user taps the link and navigates. Do not rely on it for mobile.
- `HoverCard` sets `openDelay` 300 and `closeDelay` 150, shorter than Radix's own 700 and 300; pass your own values to change them.
- Pressing the pointer on the card, or having text selected inside it, stops it from closing when the pointer leaves.
- `HoverCardContent` shares `size` (`md`, 18rem), `padded` and `arrow` with `PopoverContent` but has no `disablePortal`.

## HStack

> Horizontal `Stack` (`direction="row"`). Takes the other `Stack` props.

- Import: `import { HStack } from "@sutra/ui"` (or from `@sutra/ui/core`)
- Source: `packages/ui/src/primitives/layout` (primitives)
- Also accepts the props of HTMLAttributes

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `align` | `"center" \| "end" \| "start" \| "stretch" \| "baseline" \| null` |  | Cross-axis alignment of the children (`align-items`). |
| `asChild` | `boolean` |  | Render as the child element instead of a `<div>`, keeping the stack styles. |
| `gap` | `0 \| 1 \| 3 \| 6 \| 2 \| 8 \| 10 \| 5 \| 4 \| 12 \| null` | `4` | Space between children, in Tailwind spacing steps (4 = 1rem). |
| `justify` | `"center" \| "end" \| "start" \| "between" \| null` |  | Main-axis distribution of the children (`justify-content`). |
| `wrap` | `boolean \| null` |  | Lets children wrap onto new lines when they overflow. |

### Notes

**When to use:** A flex layout on the spacing scale: a column by default, with gap, alignment, justify and wrap props. `HStack` is the same in a row, centred on the cross axis.

**Use instead when:**
- `Grid`: a responsive 12-column layout
- `Container`: centre content and cap its width
- `ButtonGroup`: attached buttons
- `ItemGroup`: a list of rows

#### Keyboard

Not focusable: no keyboard interaction.

#### Screen readers

A plain `div` with no role, so it is invisible to assistive technology and the DOM order is the reading order. `direction="row"` and `justify` change only the layout, not the order, so keep the source order meaningful. With `asChild` the child element (a `ul`, `nav`, `section`) keeps its own semantics.

#### Reduced motion

Static: no animation.

#### Server rendering

Server render: same markup as the client. Plain markup with no browser API, so server and client output match.

#### Gotchas

- `gap` takes the steps 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10 and 12 (4 is 1rem) and defaults to 4: other numbers have no class. `direction` defaults to `column`.
- `HStack` is `direction="row"` with `align="center"` as default; pass `align` to change that. It takes every other `Stack` prop except `direction`.
- Row direction and `justify` follow the writing direction, so a row flips in RTL without changes.
- `wrap` is only the flex-wrap flag. Children of a column that should not stretch need `align="start"`, because the cross-axis default is the browser's stretch.

## InfoTooltip

> Small (i) / (?) icon button that reveals a title + description tooltip.

- Import: `import { InfoTooltip } from "@sutra/ui"` (or from `@sutra/ui/overlays`)
- Source: `packages/ui/src/primitives/info-tooltip` (primitives)
- Also accepts the props of HTMLAttributes, ButtonHTMLAttributes

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `align` | `TooltipContentProps["align"]` |  | Alignment of the tooltip along that side. |
| `contentClassName` | `string` |  | Classes for the tooltip bubble. |
| `description` | `React.ReactNode` |  | Body text. |
| `icon` | `"info" \| "help"` | `"info"` | Trigger icon: an info "i" or a help "?". |
| `label` | `string` |  | Accessible label for the trigger. |
| `side` | `TooltipContentProps["side"]` | `"top"` | Side of the trigger the tooltip opens on. |
| `size` | `Size` | `"md"` | Icon size. |
| `title` | `React.ReactNode` |  | Bold first line. |
| `variant` | `TooltipContentProps["variant"]` |  | Look of the bubble: `inverse` (dark) or `light`. |

### Notes

**When to use:** A small (i) or (?) icon button that reveals a bold title and a description in a tooltip, placed next to a label or field to explain it.

**Use instead when:**
- `Tooltip`: a label on an existing control
- `Popover`: longer help with links or interactive content
- `HoverCard`: a rich preview of a linked thing
- `FieldDescription`: help text that should always be visible

#### Keyboard

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Focusing the button opens the tooltip after the delay; moving focus away closes it |
| Escape | Close the tooltip |
| Enter, Space | Activate the button (native `<button type="button">`), which closes the tooltip |

There are no arrow keys, so RTL changes nothing; the bubble text uses `text-start`.

#### Screen readers

The trigger is a `<button>` named by `label`, else by `title` when it is a string, else `"Help"` (icon `help`) or `"More information"`. While open, the tooltip (`role="tooltip"`) is linked to the button by `aria-describedby`, so a `title` that is also the name is read twice. The icon is `aria-hidden`. `children` are rendered inside the bubble after the description.

#### Reduced motion

The bubble fades and zooms in from the button and slides slightly from its side; the reduced-motion net removes the slide and the scale and keeps only the fade. The icon colour change is a transition and ends in 1 ms.

#### Server rendering

Server render: same markup as the client. Only the button renders on the server; the bubble is portalled after mount and only opens from hover or focus. Nothing differs between server and client.

#### Gotchas

- Touch does not open it (Radix tooltips ignore touch pointers and a tap closes them): do not put the only copy of important help in an `InfoTooltip`.
- It uses `Tooltip`, so it follows the nearest `TooltipProvider`'s delay (200 ms by default); there is no `delayDuration` prop, so set the delay on the provider.
- Extra props and `className` go to the button, `contentClassName` to the bubble; `side`, `align` and `variant` position and style the bubble.
- `size` (`sm`, `md`, `lg`) changes the icon and the button box; the pointer target is enlarged to at least 24 px by `hitArea`.

## InlineAlert

> Contextual message placed inline with content (forms, panels, settings). `layout="strip"` turns it into an edge-to-edge bar with only a bottom border, for the top of a page or panel.

- Import: `import { InlineAlert } from "@sutra/ui"` (or from `@sutra/ui/core`)
- Source: `packages/ui/src/primitives/inline-alert` (primitives)
- `data-slot`: `inline-alert-icon`, `inline-alert-action`
- Parts: [`InlineAlertActions`](InlineAlertActions.md), [`InlineAlertDescription`](InlineAlertDescription.md), [`InlineAlertTitle`](InlineAlertTitle.md)
- Also accepts the props of HTMLAttributes

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `action` | `React.ReactNode` |  | Trailing control(s) beside the message, before the close button (e.g. a CTA). Use `InlineAlertActions` for a row under the text. |
| `appearance` | `"soft" \| "outline" \| "accent"` | `"soft"` | Surface style: `soft` (tinted), `outline` (bordered) or `accent` (soft with a coloured start edge). |
| `dismissLabel` | `string` | `"Dismiss"` | Accessible name of the dismiss button. |
| `icon` | `React.ReactNode \| false` |  | Custom icon; pass `false` or `null` to hide the default per-variant icon. |
| `layout` | `"box" \| "strip"` | `"box"` | Shape: `box` is a rounded block, `strip` is a full-width bar with only a bottom border. |
| `onDismiss` | `() => void` |  | Shows a close button that calls this handler. |
| `tone` | `InlineAlertTone \| null` |  | Semantic colour. Default `info`. |
| `variant` | `InlineAlertVariant \| InlineAlertTone \| null` | `"info"` | **Deprecated.** Use `tone` (`brand` → `primary`). Legacy name of `tone`. |

### Variants

- `variant`: `info`, `success`, `warning`, `destructive`, `neutral`, `brand` (default "info")
- `appearance`: `soft`, `outline`, `accent` (default "soft")
- `layout`: `box`, `strip` (default "box")

### Notes

**When to use:** A contextual message that sits inside content (a form, a panel, a settings page), with an icon, a title and description, an optional action and an optional dismiss button. `layout="strip"` makes it an edge-to-edge bar.

**Use instead when:**
- `AlertBanner`: a page-level announcement at the top of the app
- `Toaster`: a transient message that goes away by itself
- `AlertDialog`: the user must answer before going on
- `StatusBadge`: a small state label

#### Keyboard

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Reaches the controls you put in `action`, in `InlineAlertActions` or in the text, then the dismiss button |
| Enter, Space | Presses the focused button (Enter follows a link) |

The alert itself is not focusable and has no arrow-key behaviour, so nothing changes in RTL. The dismiss button is on the end edge, and the `accent` appearance puts its coloured edge on the start side (`border-s`), so both flip with `dir`.

#### Screen readers

- The root is `role="alert"` for `warning` and `destructive` (announced at once, interrupting) and `role="status"` for every other tone (a polite live region). Pass `role` to override: the strip layout in the tests uses `role="status"` on a warning.
- The icon is `aria-hidden`; the colour alone does not carry the meaning, so put the severity in the text.
- The dismiss button is named by `dismissLabel` (default "Dismiss"). Give it a more specific label when several alerts are on screen.
- `InlineAlertTitle` is a `<p>`, not a heading, so it adds nothing to the heading outline.

#### Reduced motion

Static: nothing enters or animates. Only the close button's hover fade, which the reduced-motion net ends in 1 ms.

#### Server rendering

Server render: same markup as the client. Plain markup with no browser API, so the server and client output match.

#### Slots

- `inline-alert-icon`: the wrapper around the icon (not rendered when `icon={false}`)
- `inline-alert-action`: the box that holds the `action` node, placed before the dismiss button

#### Gotchas

- There is no open state. `onDismiss` only reports the click and the dismiss button appears only when you pass it: unmount the alert yourself (the tests do it with `useState`). `AlertBanner` is the one that hides itself.
- `action` sits beside the message, vertically centred; `InlineAlertActions` is the row of buttons under the description. Do not use both for the same buttons.
- `variant` is a deprecated alias of `tone` (`brand` is `primary`); `tone` wins when both are set. The default tone is `info`.
- `appearance` is `soft` (tinted), `outline` (bordered, on the page background) or `accent` (soft with a 3px coloured start edge); `layout="strip"` also drops the radius and all borders but the bottom one.

## InlineCode

> Inline code.

- Import: `import { InlineCode } from "@sutra/ui"` (or from `@sutra/ui/core`)
- Source: `packages/ui/src/primitives/typography` (primitives)
- Also accepts the props of HTMLAttributes

### Props

No props of its own.

### Notes

**When to use:** Body text with size, tone and weight steps, plus the small typographic pieces: `Eyebrow` (an all-caps label above a heading), `Kbd` (a key hint) and `InlineCode`.

**Use instead when:**
- `Heading`: a heading with the display scale
- `ShortcutKeys`: a whole key combination from a shortcut string
- `CodeBlock`: multi-line code
- `Badge`: a short status label

#### Keyboard

Not focusable: no keyboard interaction. `Kbd` only shows a key; it does not listen for it.

#### Screen readers

- `Text` renders a `p` by default; `as` takes `p`, `span`, `div`, `small`, `strong` or `em`, and `asChild` styles your own element. Use `span` inside a line of text so you do not nest paragraphs.
- `Eyebrow` is a plain `p`, not a heading: it is read as a paragraph in front of the heading it labels.
- `Kbd` renders a native `<kbd>`, which screen readers read as its text. A symbol such as the command key may be read as nothing or as a name, so for combinations that matter use `ShortcutKeys` (it carries spoken text) or add visually hidden words.
- `InlineCode` renders a native `<code>`.

#### Reduced motion

Static: no animation.

#### Server rendering

Server render: same markup as the client. Plain markup with no browser API, so server and client output match.

#### Gotchas

- `tone` is `default` (foreground), `neutral`, `primary`, `success`, `warning`, `destructive` or `info`; `muted` is the old name of `neutral`. `neutral` is the muted grey, so it is quieter than `default`; `warning` uses the darker readable shade.
- `size` is `xs` to `xl` with `md` being `text-base`; `Text` sets no line-height or margin, so spacing comes from the parent (a `Stack`) and line-height from the surrounding styles.
- `Eyebrow` is always `text-primary`, uppercase and tracked; override with `className`. `Kbd` and `InlineCode` take only the HTML props of their element plus `className`; they have no size or tone variants.

## InlineEditText

> Single-line inline editor for renaming things in place: Enter or blur commits, Escape cancels, and key presses never reach the surrounding row's shortcuts.

- Import: `import { InlineEditText } from "@sutra/ui"` (or from `@sutra/ui/ai`)
- Source: `packages/ui/src/primitives/inline-edit-text` (primitives)
- Also accepts the props of HTMLAttributes, InputHTMLAttributes

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `autoFocus` | `boolean` | `true` | Focus the field and select its text when it mounts. Default true. |
| `defaultValue` | `string` |  | Initial draft text (uncontrolled). Also the value a commit is compared against. |
| `label` | `string` | `"Edit text"` | Accessible name. Default "Edit text". `aria-label` wins when both are set. |
| `onCancel` | `() => void` |  | Called on Escape, and on Enter / blur when there is nothing to commit (empty or unchanged). |
| `onCommit` | `(value: string) => void` |  | Called with the trimmed text on Enter or blur, when it is non-empty and differs from the starting value. |
| `onValueChange` | `(value: string) => void` |  | Called on every keystroke with the raw draft. |
| `value` | `string` |  | Draft text (controlled). |

### Notes

**When to use:** A single-line field that appears in place of a title or name so the user can rename it: it focuses and selects on mount, Enter or blur commits the trimmed text, Escape cancels. Mount it when editing starts and unmount it on `onCommit` or `onCancel`.

**Use instead when:**
- `Input`: a field that is always visible in a form
- `Textarea`: several lines
- `SearchInput`: a query field

#### Keyboard

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| Enter | Commit: `onCommit` gets the trimmed text when it is non-empty and differs from the starting value; otherwise `onCancel` runs |
| Escape | Cancel: restore the starting text (uncontrolled) and call `onCancel` |
| Tab or a click elsewhere | Blur commits, the same as Enter |
| Any other key | Typed into the field as usual |

Every key press and click on the field stops propagating, so the surrounding row's shortcuts (a list's arrow keys, a hotkey, a row click) do not fire while editing. Enter and Escape are ignored during IME composition. No arrow-key handling of its own, so RTL changes nothing.

#### Screen readers

- A native `<input type="text">` named by `aria-label`, else `label` (default "Edit text"). Pass a specific name such as "Rename Quarterly report" when several rows can be edited.
- It takes focus and selects its text on mount, so the screen reader moves to the field when editing starts. After `onCommit` or `onCancel` you are responsible for returning focus to the row or button that opened it.
- There is no announcement of the commit or the cancel; show your own status if the change needs one.

#### Reduced motion

Static: no animation or transition beyond the focus ring.

#### Server rendering

Server render: same markup as the client. Renders a plain input from `value` or `defaultValue`. The focus and select happen in an effect after mount, so the server HTML is the same as the client's and nothing is focused until hydration.

#### Gotchas

- Blur commits, it does not cancel. Clicking away, or moving focus to a button, saves the text; use Escape to discard. An empty or unchanged draft counts as a cancel, so `onCancel` also runs on those.
- The starting value is read once, on mount: later edits are compared with it, and a committed draft is not treated as the new starting text. Unmount the field after `onCommit` instead of keeping it open.
- `onValueChange` receives the raw draft on every keystroke; `onCommit` receives the trimmed text. The native `onChange` is removed from the type. With controlled `value` the field does not reset itself on Escape: restore your state in `onCancel`.
- `autoFocus` defaults to true and is handled by the component (focus and select on mount); pass `autoFocus={false}` to skip it. A commit or cancel runs once even though Enter is followed by a blur.

## Input

> Text input with optional icons, text addons and a clear button. Consumes `Field` context.

- Import: `import { Input } from "@sutra/ui"` (or from `@sutra/ui/forms`)
- Source: `packages/ui/src/primitives/input` (primitives)
- `data-slot`: `input`, `input-wrapper`
- Also accepts the props of HTMLAttributes, InputHTMLAttributes

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `className` | `string` |  | Classes for the element that renders. Without addons that is the `<input>` itself (the root). With addons (`leadingIcon`, `trailingIcon`, `prefix`, `suffix`, `clearable`) it lands on the **inner** `<input>`, not the outer wrapper, so layout classes (`w-48`, `flex-1`, margins) have no visible effect there; use `wrapperClassName` for those. |
| `clearable` | `boolean` |  | Shows a clear button while the field has a value. |
| `invalid` | `boolean` |  | Marks the field invalid: error border and `aria-invalid`. Inherited from a surrounding `Field` when omitted. |
| `leadingIcon` | `React.ReactNode` |  | Icon rendered inside the field before the text. |
| `onClear` | `() => void` |  | Called after the clear button empties the field. |
| `prefix` | `React.ReactNode` |  | Text addon before the field, e.g. "https://". |
| `size` | `"sm" \| "md" \| "lg"` | `"md"` | Field height and text size. |
| `suffix` | `React.ReactNode` |  | Text addon after the field, e.g. ".com". |
| `trailingIcon` | `React.ReactNode` |  | Icon or small action rendered inside the field after the text. |
| `variant` | `"outline" \| "filled" \| null` | `"outline"` | `outline` (default) is the bordered box; `filled` is a tinted surface with a hidden border. |
| `wrapperClassName` | `string` |  | Classes for the outer wrapper `<div>`, which is only rendered when addons are present. Put layout/sizing classes here when the input has addons. |

### Variants

- `size`: `sm`, `md`, `lg` (default "md")
- `variant`: `outline`, `filled` (default "outline")

### Notes

**When to use:** The single-line text field. It takes every native `<input>` prop and adds `leadingIcon`, `trailingIcon`, `prefix`, `suffix` and `clearable`. `PasswordInput` adds a show and hide toggle, `SearchInput` a search icon, a clear button and an optional focus hotkey.

**Use instead when:**
- `Textarea`: several lines
- `NumberInput`: numbers with steppers and locale formatting
- `InputGroup`: addons that are real buttons, selects or other controls
- `InputOTP`: a one-time code split into slots
- `Combobox`: a choice from a list
- `TagInput`: several free-form tags

#### Keyboard

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Moves to and from the field and the `PasswordInput` toggle. The `clearable` button is not a tab stop (`tabIndex` -1) |
| Enter, Space | On the `PasswordInput` toggle: show or hide the text |
| Escape | In a `SearchInput` that has text and `clearable`: empty it and call `onClear` |
| `hotkey` (for example `/` or `mod+k`) | Anywhere on the page: focus and select the `SearchInput`. A plain key typed into another field stays text; a chord with Ctrl or Meta still fires |

Typing is native. There are no arrow-key handlers, and the icons and addons use logical padding, so RTL only mirrors the layout.

#### Screen readers

- A native `<input>` named by a `<label>`, `aria-label` or a surrounding `FieldLabel`; a field with no visible label needs `aria-label`. `invalid` sets `aria-invalid`, and `Field` adds `id`, `aria-describedby`, `disabled` and `required` unless you pass them.
- `SearchInput` is `type="search"` (role `searchbox`), sets `aria-keyshortcuts` from `hotkey`, and hides the key hint (`aria-hidden`).
- The clear button is named "Clear" (not translatable through a prop). The `PasswordInput` toggle is named "Show password" or "Hide password" and also carries `aria-pressed`. Icons are `aria-hidden`; `leadingIcon`, `trailingIcon`, `prefix` and `suffix` content that you pass is not hidden for you.

#### Reduced motion

The clear button pops in with `animate-in fade-in-0 zoom-in-75`, and the border and ring fade with a short transition; the reduced-motion net removes the zoom and ends the transitions in 1 ms.

#### Server rendering

Server render: part of it fills in after mount. `Input` and `PasswordInput` render the same markup on both sides, including the clear button when a `value` or `defaultValue` is set. `SearchInput` reads its key hint after mount (`hotkey` is turned into key labels in an effect), so the hint chips are not in the server HTML and appear on hydration.

#### Slots

- `input`: the `<input>` element (the root when there are no addons)
- `input-wrapper`: the outer `div`, rendered only when an icon, addon or `clearable` is present

#### Gotchas

- `className` lands on the inner `<input>` once any addon is present, so layout classes (`w-48`, `flex-1`) do nothing there; put them in `wrapperClassName`. Without addons `className` is the root.
- `PasswordInput` defaults to `autoComplete="current-password"` (pass `"new-password"` when setting one), turns off `spellCheck`, and does not accept `type` or `trailingIcon`.
- `clearable` fires a real `input` event, so `onChange` runs with an empty value, then `onClear`. `SearchInput` is `clearable` by default.
- Pass `prefix` and `suffix` as text addons; for interactive addons use `InputGroup`.

## InputGroup

> A container that looks like a single input and hosts addons around a control.

- Import: `import { InputGroup } from "@sutra/ui"` (or from `@sutra/ui/forms`)
- Source: `packages/ui/src/primitives/input-group` (primitives)
- `data-slot`: `input-group`
- Parts: [`InputGroupAddon`](InputGroupAddon.md), [`InputGroupButton`](InputGroupButton.md), [`InputGroupInput`](InputGroupInput.md), [`InputGroupText`](InputGroupText.md), [`InputGroupTextarea`](InputGroupTextarea.md)
- Also accepts the props of HTMLAttributes

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `size` | `"sm" \| "md" \| "lg"` | `"md"` | Group height and text size. |
| `variant` | `"outline" \| "filled"` | `"outline"` | `outline` (default) is the bordered box; `filled` is a tinted surface with a hidden border (the surface returns to normal on focus). |

### Variants

- `size`: `sm`, `md`, `lg` (default "md")
- `variant`: `outline`, `filled` (default "outline")

### Part props

Props of `InputGroupAddon`, `InputGroupButton`, `InputGroupInput`, `InputGroupTextarea`: see [the full page](md/InputGroup.md).

### Notes

**When to use:** One input-like box that hosts a control with addons around it: text, icons, buttons or keys at the start or end, or in a row above or below. `InputGroupInput` or `InputGroupTextarea` is the control; the box takes its focus, invalid and disabled styling from it.

**Use instead when:**
- `Input`: a field whose addons are only an icon, a text prefix or suffix, or a clear button
- `Textarea`: several lines with no addons
- `ButtonGroup`: attached buttons with no text field
- `SearchInput`: a ready-made search field

#### Keyboard

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Follows DOM order through the control and any addon buttons, links or inputs |
| Enter, Space | Activates a focused `InputGroupButton` (native button) |

The group adds no key handling. Clicking padding or an `InputGroupText` addon focuses the control (a click on a button, link or other control inside an addon is left alone). Visual order comes from `align` through CSS `order`, but tab and reading order come from where you put the parts in the markup, so write them in the order users should reach them. RTL only mirrors the layout: `inline-start` and `inline-end` follow the reading direction.

#### Screen readers

- The group and every addon are `role="group"` without a name. Give the `InputGroup` an `aria-label` when its parts need announcing as a unit; the control still needs its own name from a `<label>`, `aria-label` or a surrounding `FieldLabel`.
- `InputGroupInput` and `InputGroupTextarea` are native controls that read `id`, `disabled`, `required`, `aria-describedby` and `invalid` (as `aria-invalid`) from a surrounding `Field`. Put `invalid`, `disabled` and `required` on the control, not on `InputGroup`; the box restyles through `has-[...]` on the control.
- An icon-only `InputGroupButton` needs `aria-label`. Text that sits in an addon (`https://`, `USD`) is read as plain text before or after the field, so repeat it in the control's label if it matters.

#### Reduced motion

Static apart from the border and ring fade on focus, which the reduced-motion net ends in 1 ms.

#### Server rendering

Server render: same markup as the client. Plain markup with no browser API or mount state, so server and client output match.

#### Slots

- `input-group`: the box
- `input-group-addon`: an addon; `data-align` is `inline-start`, `inline-end`, `block-start` or `block-end`
- `input-group-text`: muted inline text inside an addon
- `input-group-button`: a compact button
- `input-group-control`: the input or textarea that drives the box styling

#### Gotchas

- `InputGroup` `size` (`sm`, `md`, `lg`) sets the height and `variant` the look; it does not size the control. Pass `size` to `InputGroupInput` too when you change the padding.
- `block-start` and `block-end` addons stack above or below the control and make the box auto-height; with a textarea the box also becomes auto-height.
- `InputGroupButton` is a `Button`: `variant` defaults to `ghost`, `size` to `xs` (`xs`, `sm`, `icon-xs`, `icon-sm`), and `type` to `button`.
- Only the control gets focus styling; a focused addon button does not light the box.

## InputOTP

> One-time code input built on `input-otp`. Compose with `InputOTPGroup` and `InputOTPSlot`.

- Import: `import { InputOTP } from "@sutra/ui"` (or from `@sutra/ui/forms`)
- Source: `packages/ui/src/primitives/input-otp` (primitives)
- `data-slot`: `input-otp`
- Parts: [`InputOTPGroup`](InputOTPGroup.md), [`InputOTPSeparator`](InputOTPSeparator.md), [`InputOTPSlot`](InputOTPSlot.md)
- Also accepts the props of HTMLAttributes, InputHTMLAttributes, OTPInputBaseProps, OTPInputProps

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `invalid` | `boolean` |  | Marks the field invalid: error ring on the slots and `aria-invalid`. Inherited from a surrounding `Field` when omitted. |
| `size` | `Size` | `"md"` | Slot size. |

### Part props

Props of `InputOTPSlot`: see [the full page](md/InputOTP.md).

### Notes

**When to use:** A one-time code or PIN field drawn as separate character slots over one real input (the `input-otp` library). Compose `InputOTPGroup`, `InputOTPSlot` and `InputOTPSeparator` yourself, or use `OTPField` for a ready-made row of slots.

**Use instead when:**
- `Input`: free text of any length
- `NumberInput`: a number with steppers
- `PasswordInput`: a secret typed in full
- `TagInput`: several free-form tags

#### Keyboard

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Focuses the single underlying input (the slots are not tab stops) |
| Digits, or any character `pattern` allows | Fill the next slot; a character that fails `pattern` is rejected |
| Backspace, Delete | Remove characters, as in a normal text input |
| Arrow keys, Home, End | Move the native caret, which highlights the matching slot |
| Ctrl+V, Cmd+V | Paste a code; `pasteTransformer` can clean it first |

Everything is native text input behaviour: one `<input>` sits over the slots with transparent text. `onComplete` fires when the value reaches `maxLength` (`length` for `OTPField`). Slots are a flex row, so in an RTL document they run right to left; wrap the field in `dir="ltr"` if a code should read left to right.

#### Screen readers

- The real input carries the whole value and is what assistive technology reads. Give it a name with `aria-label`, `aria-labelledby` or a surrounding `FieldLabel`; `invalid` sets `aria-invalid`, and `Field` supplies `id`, `aria-describedby`, `disabled` and `required`.
- The input defaults to `autoComplete="one-time-code"` (so the browser can offer an SMS code), `inputMode="numeric"` and `spellCheck` off. `OTPField` sets `inputMode` to `text` when you give it a non-digit `pattern`.
- Slots are plain `div`s with no role or `aria-hidden`, and the fake caret is `aria-hidden`. `InputOTPSeparator` is a `role="separator"`, so each one is announced when a reader walks the content.

#### Reduced motion

A character pops in with `animate-in zoom-in-90`, which the reduced-motion net strips of its movement. The fake caret blinks with `animate-caret-blink`, which the net turns off, so it stays solid.

#### Server rendering

Server render: same markup as the client. The input and the slots render on the server from `value` or `defaultValue`; the active slot, the fake caret and the library's autofill style rules appear only after mount, because they depend on focus and `document.head`.

#### Slots

- `input-otp`: the underlying input
- `input-otp-group`: a run of slots
- `input-otp-slot`: one character cell; `data-active` while it holds the caret, `data-filled` when it has a character
- `input-otp-separator`: the divider between groups

#### Gotchas

- `OTPField` is digits only by default (`pattern` is `REGEXP_ONLY_DIGITS`); pass `pattern` to allow letters, and `groupSize` and `separator` to split the slots (3 and 3 for a six digit code).
- `InputOTP` needs `maxLength` and one `InputOTPSlot index` per character; a missing index leaves a character with nothing to show it. `OTPField` takes `length` instead.
- `onChange` receives the string value, not an event. `defaultValue` works because the wrapper owns the uncontrolled state; pass `value` to control it.
- `size` is `sm`, `md` or `lg` and applies to every slot through context; `invalid` turns the slot borders red.

## Item

> One row: `ItemMedia`, `ItemContent` (`ItemTitle` and `ItemDescription`) and `ItemActions`. Static, or a link or button.

- Import: `import { Item } from "@sutra/ui"` (or from `@sutra/ui/core`)
- Source: `packages/ui/src/primitives/item` (primitives)
- `data-slot`: `item`
- Parts: [`ItemActions`](ItemActions.md), [`ItemContent`](ItemContent.md), [`ItemDescription`](ItemDescription.md), [`ItemGroup`](ItemGroup.md), [`ItemMedia`](ItemMedia.md), [`ItemSeparator`](ItemSeparator.md), [`ItemTitle`](ItemTitle.md)
- Also accepts the props of HTMLAttributes

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `asChild` | `boolean` |  | Render the child element as the row (a router link, say) instead of a `div`. |
| `chevron` | `boolean` |  | Show a trailing chevron on a link, button or `asChild` row (added after the child's own content). |
| `disabled` | `boolean` |  | A link or button row that cannot be used (`aria-disabled`, dimmed). |
| `href` | `string` |  | Make the row one link. Put no buttons inside it (a link cannot hold interactive content). |
| `onClick` | `React.MouseEventHandler<HTMLElement>` |  | Make the row one button. Put no buttons inside it. |
| `orientation` | `"horizontal" \| "vertical"` | `"horizontal"` | Lays the media, content and actions out in a row or stacks them. |
| `rel` | `string` |  | Link `rel` when `href` is set. Defaults to `noreferrer noopener` for `target="_blank"`. |
| `size` | `"default" \| "sm" \| "xs"` | `"default"` | Row padding and gap: `default`, `sm` or `xs`. |
| `target` | `string` |  | Link `target` when `href` is set. |
| `variant` | `"plain" \| "outline" \| "muted"` | `"plain"` | Surface of the row: plain, outlined card or muted panel. |

### Variants

- `variant`: `plain`, `outline`, `muted` (default "plain")
- `size`: `default`, `sm`, `xs` (default "default")
- `orientation`: `horizontal`, `vertical` (default "horizontal")

### Part props

Props of `ItemDescription`, `ItemGroup`, `ItemMedia`: see [the full page](md/Item.md).

### Notes

**When to use:** One list row: media, a title with a description, and trailing actions. Static, or one link or button for the whole row. `ItemGroup` lists rows with placeholders for loading and empty states.

**Use instead when:**
- `Frame`: a titled tray with a header and footer around a panel of rows
- `Table`: rows with several comparable columns
- `KeyValue`: name and value facts
- `Card`: a free-form container
- `DropdownMenu`: commands in a popup

#### Keyboard

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Moves to a row that is a link or a button, and to controls inside a static row's `ItemActions` |
| Enter | Follows the link, or runs the button's `onClick` |
| Space | Runs the button's `onClick` (not for a link row) |

A static row is not focusable. With `asChild` the child keeps its own keyboard behaviour. No key depends on direction, but the `chevron` mirrors in RTL.

#### Screen readers

- `ItemGroup` is a `role="list"` (it cannot be changed) and needs an `aria-label`. A static `Item` inside it has `role="listitem"`; a link or button row keeps its own role and is wrapped in a `listitem` box. Outside a group, a static `Item` is a plain `div`.
- A `disabled` link loses its `href` and gets `aria-disabled`; a disabled button row is natively disabled. The `chevron` is `aria-hidden`.
- `loading` renders `aria-busy` with sr-only "Loading…"; the placeholder rows are `aria-hidden`.
- `ItemTitle` and `ItemDescription` set a `title` tooltip from their text when it is a plain string, because they truncate.
- `ItemSeparator` is `role="presentation"`.

#### Reduced motion

Static; the hover background and the chevron nudge are transitions, which the reduced-motion net in `sutra.css` ends within 1 ms.

#### Server rendering

Server render: same markup as the client. Plain markup with no browser API, so server and client output match.

#### Slots

- `item-group`: the list, with `data-variant`
- `item-media`: the leading visual, with `data-variant` (`plain`, `icon`, `image`, `avatar`)
- `item-content`: the text column
- `item-title`: the single truncated line
