- `item-description`: the secondary text
- `item-actions`: the trailing controls
- `item-separator`: a hairline for a group that is not `divided`

#### Gotchas

- The element follows the props: `href` gives an `<a>`, `onClick` (without `href`) a `<button type="button">`, `asChild` renders your child (a router link) as the row, and nothing gives a `div`. With `href` and `onClick`, the link still gets the `onClick`.
- A link or button row must hold no other buttons or links (nested interactive content). Put the actions in a static row instead.
- `chevron` only shows on an interactive row (link, button or `asChild`), never on a static one; with `asChild` it is appended after the child's own content.
- `ItemDescription` truncates to one line by default; pass `lines={2}` or `lines="none"`. `ItemGroup` `divided` draws hairlines, and `emptyState` shows only when there are no children and `loading` is off.

## Kbd

> Keyboard key hint.

- Import: `import { Kbd } from "@sutra/ui"` (or from `@sutra/ui/core`)
- Source: `packages/ui/src/primitives/typography` (primitives)
- Also accepts the props of HTMLAttributes

### Props

No props of its own.

### Notes

**When to use:** Body text with size, tone and weight steps, plus the small typographic pieces: `Eyebrow` (an all-caps label above a heading), `Kbd` (a key hint) and `InlineCode`.

**Use instead when:**
- `Heading`: a heading with the display scale
- `ShortcutKeys`: a whole key combination from a shortcut string
- `CodeBlock`: multi-line code
- `Badge`: a short status label

#### Keyboard

Not focusable: no keyboard interaction. `Kbd` only shows a key; it does not listen for it.

#### Screen readers

- `Text` renders a `p` by default; `as` takes `p`, `span`, `div`, `small`, `strong` or `em`, and `asChild` styles your own element. Use `span` inside a line of text so you do not nest paragraphs.
- `Eyebrow` is a plain `p`, not a heading: it is read as a paragraph in front of the heading it labels.
- `Kbd` renders a native `<kbd>`, which screen readers read as its text. A symbol such as the command key may be read as nothing or as a name, so for combinations that matter use `ShortcutKeys` (it carries spoken text) or add visually hidden words.
- `InlineCode` renders a native `<code>`.

#### Reduced motion

Static: no animation.

#### Server rendering

Server render: same markup as the client. Plain markup with no browser API, so server and client output match.

#### Gotchas

- `tone` is `default` (foreground), `neutral`, `primary`, `success`, `warning`, `destructive` or `info`; `muted` is the old name of `neutral`. `neutral` is the muted grey, so it is quieter than `default`; `warning` uses the darker readable shade.
- `size` is `xs` to `xl` with `md` being `text-base`; `Text` sets no line-height or margin, so spacing comes from the parent (a `Stack`) and line-height from the surrounding styles.
- `Eyebrow` is always `text-primary`, uppercase and tracked; override with `className`. `Kbd` and `InlineCode` take only the HTML props of their element plus `className`; they have no size or tone variants.

## KeyValue

> One fact in a `KeyValueList`, optionally copyable.

- Import: `import { KeyValue } from "@sutra/ui"` (or from `@sutra/ui/identity`)
- Source: `packages/ui/src/primitives/key-value` (primitives)
- `data-slot`: `key-value`
- Parts: [`KeyValueList`](KeyValueList.md)
- Also accepts the props of HTMLAttributes

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `label` (required) | `React.ReactNode` |  | Name of the entry, shown as the row's label. |
| `children` | `React.ReactNode` |  | The value, when `value` is not set. |
| `copyable` | `boolean \| string` |  | Adds a copy button; `true` copies the value text, a string copies that text instead. |
| `mono` | `boolean` |  | Shows this value in the monospace face. |
| `truncate` | `boolean` |  | Single-line with ellipsis; the full text is in the `title` tooltip. Default true in `rows`. |
| `value` | `React.ReactNode` |  | The value; `children` work too. Empty values render the list's placeholder. |

### Part props

Props of `KeyValueList`: see [the full page](md/KeyValue.md).

### Notes

**When to use:** A description list of facts, a name on one side and a value on the other, in rows, stacked or grid layouts, with an optional copy button per value.

**Use instead when:**
- `Table`: several columns of records to compare or sort
- `Item`: a row with media, title and actions
- `MetricReadout`: one number with a label and a trend

#### Keyboard

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Moves focus to the copy buttons (only on entries with `copyable`) |
| Enter, Space | Copies the value (native `<button>`) |

The list and its text are not focusable. No key depends on direction.

#### Screen readers

- `KeyValueList` is a real `<dl>`; each `KeyValue` is a `<div>` holding a `<dt>` (the label) and a `<dd>` (the value), so assistive technology announces them as term and definition pairs. Do not put `KeyValue` outside a list.
- The copy button is named "Copy <label>" when `label` is a string, and "Copy value" when it is a node. `CopyButton` announces the copied state itself.
- A missing value shows the `empty` placeholder ("—" by default) as plain text.

#### Reduced motion

Static: no animation. The copy button's own feedback follows `CopyButton`.

#### Server rendering

Server render: same markup as the client. Plain markup from the props, with no browser API, so server and client output match. The copy button renders a normal button on the server.

#### Slots

- `key-value-list`: the `<dl>`, with `data-layout` set to `rows`, `stacked` or `grid`
- `key-value`: one entry

#### Gotchas

- `layout="rows"` (default) truncates the value on one line with the full text in `title`; `stacked` and `grid` wrap instead. `truncate` on a single `KeyValue` overrides either way. The `title` is only set for string or number values.
- `copyable` copies the value only when it is a string or number: with a node value, pass a string (`copyable="sk_live_123_full"`) to say what to copy. An empty value shows no copy button.
- Use either `items` (data) or `KeyValue` children: when `items` is set the children are ignored. `columns` only applies to `layout="grid"` and `dividers` only to `rows` and `stacked`.
- `mono` on the list sets the monospace face for every value; an entry's own `mono` wins, including `mono={false}`.

## Label

> Form label with an optional required asterisk and `hint`; use it with `htmlFor` or let `Field` wire it. Extra props are spread to the `<label>`.

- Import: `import { Label } from "@sutra/ui"` (or from `@sutra/ui/forms`)
- Source: `packages/ui/src/primitives/label` (primitives)
- Also accepts the props of HTMLAttributes, LabelHTMLAttributes, PrimitivePropsWithRef

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `hint` | `React.ReactNode` |  | Muted helper shown after the label text, e.g. "(optional)". |
| `required` | `boolean` |  | Appends a red asterisk (hidden from assistive technology); set `required` on the control itself for validation. |

### Notes

**When to use:** A form label for any control: a Radix label with an optional required asterisk and a muted `hint`. Point it at a control with `htmlFor`, or let `FieldLabel` do it inside a `Field`.

**Use instead when:**
- `FieldLabel`: a label inside a `Field` that wires itself to the control
- `FieldLegend`: the title of a `Fieldset` of related controls
- `Badge`: a categorical tag, not a form label

#### Keyboard

Not focusable: no keyboard interaction. Clicking the label forwards focus (and a click, for a checkbox or switch) to the control it names.

#### Screen readers

- It renders a native `<label>`, so `htmlFor` (or wrapping the control) gives the control its accessible name. The `hint` text is inside the label, so it is part of the name (for example "Email (work)").
- The required asterisk is `aria-hidden`: `required` on `Label` is only the visual mark. Set `required` on the control (or on `Field`) to expose `required` to assistive technology and to validation.
- A label does not name custom widgets that are not labelable elements (a `div role="combobox"`); those take `aria-labelledby` pointing at the label id, which `FieldLabel` and `Combobox` do for you.

#### Reduced motion

Static: no animation or transition.

#### Server rendering

Server render: same markup as the client. Plain markup with no browser API or mount state, so server and client output match.

#### Gotchas

- Radix cancels text selection on a double click on the label (so a quick double click on a checkbox label does not highlight it), except when the target is a button, input, select or textarea inside it.
- The disabled look comes from `peer-disabled:` (the control must be a preceding sibling with the `peer` class, as `Checkbox` is) or from a `group` ancestor with `data-disabled="true"`; otherwise pass your own classes. `FieldLabel` dims itself from the surrounding `Field`.
- Extra props go to the `<label>`; `className` merges after the defaults.

## MeshGradient

> Decorative animated gradient background; children render above it.

- Import: `import { MeshGradient } from "@sutra/ui"` (or from `@sutra/ui/core`)
- Source: `packages/ui/src/primitives/mesh-gradient` (primitives)
- Also accepts the props of HTMLAttributes

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `animated` | `boolean` | `true` | Slowly drifts the colour blobs; the motion stops under `prefers-reduced-motion`. |
| `blur` | `number` | `64` | Blur radius in px. |
| `colors` | `string[]` | `defaultColors` | Up to 5 CSS colors. Defaults to the brand palette. |
| `grain` | `boolean` | `false` | Film-grain noise overlay. |
| `grainOpacity` | `number` | `0.18` | Opacity of the grain overlay, 0 to 1 (needs `grain`). |
| `intensity` | `number` | `0.7` | Blob opacity, 0–1. |
| `layerClassName` | `string` |  | Classes for the decorative background layer. |
| `speed` | `number` | `1` | Animation speed multiplier (1 = 18s loop). |

### Notes

**When to use:** A decorative background of blurred, slowly drifting colour blobs, with optional film grain. Children render above it, so it works as a hero or panel backdrop.

**Use instead when:**
- `Card`: a plain bordered surface
- `Frame`: a tray around rows
- `Skeleton`: a loading placeholder

#### Keyboard

Not focusable: no keyboard interaction. The background layer is `pointer-events-none`, so it never blocks clicks on the content above it.

#### Screen readers

The blob layer and the grain are `aria-hidden` decoration; only your `children` are exposed. The gradient adds no contrast guarantee: check that the text you put on it passes against every colour in `colors`.

#### Reduced motion

Under `prefers-reduced-motion` the blobs stand still (`motion-reduce:animate-none`, and the `animate-mesh` rule in `sutra.css` stops it too), leaving the static gradient. `animated={false}` does the same on demand.

#### Server rendering

Server render: same markup as the client. Plain markup with inline styles and no browser API, so server and client output match. The motion is CSS only.

#### Gotchas

- At most five colours are used (one per blob); fewer repeat, and an empty array falls back to the default palette (three brand shades plus the `--chart-2` cyan and `--chart-6` violet, so a style such as paper retunes it). `colors` take any CSS colour, including `var(--color-brand-500)`.
- `speed` multiplies the loop (1 is about 18 s, and each blob runs a little slower), `blur` is in px, `intensity` is blob opacity from 0 to 1 (default 0.7), and `grain` with `grainOpacity` adds the noise overlay.
- The root is `relative isolate overflow-hidden`, and the layer sits at `-z-10` inside it: give the root a size (`className="h-64"`) and your own padding, since the layer is absolute. `layerClassName` styles the layer.
- Large blurred areas cost paint time on low-end devices: a big `blur` over a full screen is the expensive combination.

## Meter

> Labeled usage meter with threshold coloring (role="meter"): a level read against thresholds. For task completion use `Progress`.

- Import: `import { Meter } from "@sutra/ui"` (or from `@sutra/ui/dataviz`)
- Source: `packages/ui/src/primitives/meter` (primitives)
- `data-slot`: `meter-value-skeleton`, `meter-value`, `meter-track`, `meter-segment`, `meter-fill`
- Parts: [`MeterGroup`](MeterGroup.md)
- Also accepts the props of HTMLAttributes

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `value` (required) | `number \| null` |  | Current value; `null` renders an empty "no data" meter. |
| `accent` | `Accent` |  | Categorical fill colour (a provider or metric colour). Colour order: the warning/danger threshold colours, then `tone`/`color`, then `accent`, then primary. Sets `--sutra-accent` on the root. |
| `ariaValueText` | `string` |  | Screen-reader value text override. |
| `barClassName` | `string` |  | Classes for the bar track (`className` styles the whole meter). |
| `caption` | `React.ReactNode` |  | Secondary line under the bar, e.g. "resets in 2h". |
| `color` | `MeterColor \| ToneInput` |  | **Deprecated.** Use `tone`. Legacy name of `tone`. |
| `label` | `React.ReactNode` |  | Text shown above the bar; also the accessible name of the meter. |
| `loading` | `boolean` |  | Waiting for the first reading: with no `value` the bar is a muted track with no fill and a placeholder value. |
| `max` | `number` | `100` | Default 100. |
| `min` | `number` | `0` | Value that counts as empty (the start of the scale). |
| `segments` | `number` |  | Render as n discrete blocks instead of a continuous bar. |
| `showValue` | `boolean` | `true` | Show the value text next to the label. Default true. |
| `size` | `"sm" \| "md" \| "lg"` | `"md"` | Bar height. |
| `thresholds` | `MeterThresholds \| false` | `defaultMeterThresholds` | Percent thresholds for automatic warning/danger color, or false to disable. |
| `tone` | `ToneInput` |  | Base fill tone when below thresholds (or always, if thresholds are off). Default `primary`. |
| `unit` | `string` |  | Unit appended to the default value text: "62.1 / 80 GB". Without it the text is a percentage. |
| `valueText` | `React.ReactNode \| ((value: number, max: number, percent: number) => React.ReactNode)` |  | Custom value text, or a formatter. Strings are also used as aria-valuetext. |

### Part props

Props of `MeterGroup`: see [the full page](md/Meter.md).

### Notes

**When to use:** A labelled usage bar for a level read against limits (CPU, memory, quota), turning warning and destructive past thresholds. Continuous or in discrete segments, with a caption. `MeterGroup` stacks or grids several.

**Use instead when:**
- `Progress`: how far a task has got (a determinate bar with start and end)
- `StackedMeter`: one bar split into labelled parts
- `BreakdownList`: the legend rows of such a split
- `RingMeter`: a round gauge
- `BatteryLevel`: a battery reading
- `MetricReadout`: a compact text reading

#### Keyboard

Not focusable: no keyboard interaction.

#### Screen readers

- The bar is a `role="meter"` with `aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuemin` (`min`), `aria-valuemax` (`max`) and `aria-valuetext`. It is named by `label` (`aria-labelledby`), or just "Usage" when there is no label, so give every meter a `label`. An `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` passed to `Meter` goes on the bar (replacing the label as its name), not on the outer div.
- The value text is "62.1 / 80 GB" with `unit`, otherwise a rounded percentage ("62%"). A string from `valueText` (or its function) becomes `aria-valuetext` too; `ariaValueText` overrides it, and a non-text `valueText` falls back to the percentage. `value={null}` reads "No data".
- `loading` with no value drops the meter role and shows sr-only "Loading CPU…" (or "Loading usage…" without a string label); `loading` with a value keeps the meter and only sets `aria-busy`.
- `MeterGroup` is a `role="group"`; pass `aria-label` ("Node").

#### Reduced motion

The fill width transition (500 ms), the segment colour fade and the loading pulse all carry `motion-reduce:` variants that turn them off.

#### Server rendering

Server render: same markup as the client. Plain markup computed from the props (the label id uses `useId`), so server and client output match.

#### Slots

- `meter-fill`: the continuous fill, with an inline `width` percentage
- `meter-segment`: one block in `segments` mode, `data-state` `on` or `off`
- `meter-value`: the value text beside the label
- `meter-track`: the muted placeholder track while `loading`
- `meter-value-skeleton`: the value placeholder while `loading`
- `meter-group`: the `MeterGroup` root

#### Gotchas

- Thresholds are percentages of the range, higher is worse, and default to warn 75 and danger 90; `thresholds={false}` turns them off. `data-level` on the root is `ok`, `warn` or `danger`.
- Fill colour order: the threshold colour when strained, then `tone` (or the deprecated `color`), then `accent`, then primary. With `thresholds={false}` and no tone you get primary.
- `min` and `max` set the scale and the fill is clamped to 0 to 100%, and `aria-valuenow` is clamped to the same range, while the visible and `aria-valuetext` text keep the real value ("130 / 100 GB").
- `segments={n}` fills `round(percent * n)` blocks, so small values can show none. For task completion use `Progress`, which has the progressbar role.

## MetricReadout

> Compact menu-bar style reading ("CPU 92%"): optional icon, label, tabular value with unit and a tiny trend slot. It turns warning or destructive under strain (from `thresholds` or `tone`), and its accessible text reads "CPU 92%, high".

- Import: `import { MetricReadout } from "@sutra/ui"` (or from `@sutra/ui/system`)
- Source: `packages/ui/src/primitives/metric-readout` (primitives)
- `data-slot`: `metric-readout`, `metric-readout-icon`, `metric-readout-label`, `metric-readout-value-skeleton`, `metric-readout-value`, `metric-readout-trend`
- Parts: [`MetricReadoutGroup`](MetricReadoutGroup.md)
- Also accepts the props of HTMLAttributes

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `value` (required) | `number \| string \| null \| undefined` |  | Numeric readings are formatted and classified by `thresholds`; strings are shown as given; `null` shows "—". |
| `accent` | `Accent` |  | Icon colour while the reading is normal. Default: muted. |
| `formatValue` | `(value: number) => string` |  | Formats a numeric value. Default: whole numbers in the locale ("2,400"). |
| `icon` | `React.ReactNode` |  | Leading icon (decorative). |
| `label` | `React.ReactNode` |  | Short name before the value ("CPU", "GPU", "Fan"). |
| `labelText` | `string` |  | Plain-text label for the accessible text when `label` is not a string. |
| `loading` | `boolean` |  | Waiting for the first reading: with no `value` the label stays and the value is a short placeholder. |
| `locale` | `string` |  | BCP 47 locale used by the default number formatter. |
| `size` | `"xs" \| "sm"` | `"sm"` | Default `sm`. |
| `statusLabels` | `ReadoutStatusLabels` |  | Words added to the accessible text when strained. |
| `statusText` | `string \| false` |  | Replaces the status word ("throttling"), or `false` for none. |
| `thresholds` | `ReadoutThresholds \| false` |  | Absolute thresholds for the strain colour. |
| `tone` | `ToneInput` |  | Explicit semantic colour; wins over `thresholds`. |
| `trend` | `React.ReactNode` |  | Tiny trailing chart, e.g. `<SparkBar data={…} width={24} height={12} />` (decorative here; the text names the reading). |
| `unit` | `string` |  | "%", "°C", "rpm", "MB/s" … |
| `variant` | `"plain" \| "pill"` | `"plain"` | `plain` (menu-bar text) or `pill` (a filled chip that turns soft warning / destructive under strain). Default `plain`. |

### Part props

Props of `MetricReadoutGroup`: see [the full page](md/MetricReadout.md).

### Notes

**When to use:** A compact menu-bar style reading ("CPU 92%") with an optional icon and tiny trend, turning warning or destructive when the value crosses thresholds. `MetricReadoutGroup` lines several up with separators.

**Use instead when:**
- `Meter`: a value shown against a bounded bar
- `BatteryLevel`: a battery with a glyph and charging state
- `KeyValue`: a fact in a list
- `StatCard`: a large headline figure with a trend

#### Keyboard

Not focusable: no keyboard interaction.

#### Screen readers

- The visible parts (icon, label, value, unit, trend) sit in an `aria-hidden` wrapper, and a single sr-only sentence is read instead: "CPU 92%, high", "Fan 2,400 rpm", "GPU no data". The status word is appended under strain: "high" for warning and "critical" for danger. `statusLabels` renames them and `statusText` replaces the word (or `false` for none).
- A `label` that is not a string or number needs `labelText`, or the sentence has no name.
- `loading` with no value keeps the label, shows a placeholder, sets `aria-busy="true"` and reads "Loading CPU…".
- `MetricReadoutGroup` is a `role="group"`; give it `label` ("System readings"). Its separators are `aria-hidden`.

#### Reduced motion

Static: no animation of its own (the loading placeholder is a `Skeleton`, which follows the net in `sutra.css`).

#### Server rendering

Server render: part of it fills in after mount. Plain markup, but numbers go through `Intl.NumberFormat` in the default locale, so a value of 1,000 or more can print "2,400" on a server and "2.400" in a browser, and hydration warns. Pass `locale` (or `formatValue`) when you server-render such values. Nothing else waits for mount.

#### Slots

- `metric-readout`: the root, with `data-level` (`normal`, `warning`, `danger`) and `data-tone`
- `metric-readout-icon`: the leading icon
- `metric-readout-label`: the name before the value
- `metric-readout-value`: the number with its unit
- `metric-readout-trend`: the trailing trend slot
- `metric-readout-value-skeleton`: the placeholder shown while `loading`
- `metric-readout-group`: the strip
- `metric-readout-separator`: a divider between two readouts

#### Gotchas

- `thresholds` direction comes from the numbers: when `danger >= warning` higher is worse (CPU 70 and 90), otherwise lower is worse (battery 20 and 10). Only numeric values are classified, and `false` turns it off.
- `tone` wins over `thresholds`, but only `destructive` and `warning` count as strain (they add the status word); other tones just colour the reading.
- A string `statusText` is appended even when the reading is normal. A string `value` is shown as given and never classified; `null`, `undefined` and `""` show a dash and read "no data".
- `variant="pill"` fills the chip (muted, or soft warning or destructive under strain); `plain` only colours the text. The `trend` slot is decorative, so the text must carry the meaning.

## Monogram

> Square letter tile for things that are not people: apps, providers, tools, workspaces. Same initials and seed colour as `Avatar`; use `Avatar` for users.

- Import: `import { Monogram } from "@sutra/ui"` (or from `@sutra/ui/agent-admin`)
- Source: `packages/ui/src/primitives/monogram` (primitives)
- `data-slot`: `monogram`
- Also accepts the props of HTMLAttributes

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` (required) | `string` |  | Name the letters and the seed colour are derived from. |
| `color` | `string` |  | Tile colour (any CSS colour); defaults to `colorForSeed(name)`. Ignored by the `brand` variant. |
| `initialsOptions` | `InitialsOptions` |  | Options for the generated letters. |
| `label` | `string` |  | Accessible name. Without it the tile is decorative (`aria-hidden`), which suits a tile next to a visible name. |
| `letters` | `string` |  | Override the generated letters (1–2 characters). |
| `size` | `MonogramSize` | `"md"` | Tile size from `xs` to `xl`. |
| `variant` | `MonogramVariant` | `"solid"` | Look: `solid` (tinted tile, white letters), `soft` (light tile) or `brand` (brand-colour tile). |

### Variants

- `size`: `xs`, `sm`, `md`, `lg`, `xl` (default "md")
- `variant`: `solid`, `soft`, `brand` (default "solid")

### Notes

**When to use:** A square letter tile for things that are not people: apps, providers, tools and workspaces. The letters and the colour come from the name, so the same name always looks the same.

**Use instead when:**
- `Avatar`: a person, with image, status and verified badge
- `Favicon`: a site's real icon with a fallback
- `Badge`: a text label, not a tile

#### Keyboard

Not focusable: no keyboard interaction.

#### Screen readers

Decorative by default: with no `label` the tile is `aria-hidden`, which suits a tile that sits next to the name as visible text. Pass `label` ("Calendar") to make it a `role="img"` with that name, for example when the tile stands alone.

#### Reduced motion

Static: no animation.

#### Server rendering

Server render: same markup as the client. Plain markup computed from the props, with no browser API. The seed colour is a pure function of `name`, so server and client output match.

#### Slots

- `monogram`: the tile

#### Gotchas

- Letters come from `monogramInitials(name)`: words split on anything that is not a letter or digit, the first letter of the first two words ("Nimbus AI" gives NA, "github-mcp" gives GM), two letters from a single word ("corvid" gives CO), and "?" for an empty name. `letters` or `children` replace them; `initialsOptions` tunes them.
- `name` is required even with `letters`, because it seeds the colour. `color` overrides it, and the `brand` variant ignores both and uses the brand gradient.
- `variant` is `solid` (seed colour, white letters; the default), `soft` (a light tint with coloured letters) or `brand`. `size` runs `xs` to `xl` and defaults to `md`.
- `ProviderLogo` and `CapabilityMonogram` are presets built on it; use `Avatar` for a user.

## Note

> The quiet line a screen says while working or when there is nothing here: small, grey, unalarming.

- Import: `import { Note } from "@sutra/ui"` (or from `@sutra/ui/identity`)
- Source: `packages/ui/src/primitives/empty-state` (primitives)
- `data-slot`: `note`
- Also accepts the props of HTMLAttributes

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `align` | `"center" \| "start"` | `"center"` | Aligns the icon and text to the centre or the start. |
| `busy` | `boolean` |  | **Deprecated.** Use `loading`. Legacy name of `loading`. |
| `icon` | `React.ReactNode` |  | Icon shown before the text. |
| `loading` | `boolean` |  | Shows a spinner and marks the note `aria-busy`. |
| `tone` | `NoteTone` |  | `neutral` (default) or `destructive`. Legacy `default` / `error` are accepted; `busy` is the same as `loading`. |

### Notes

**When to use:** The quiet line a screen says while working or when there is nothing here: small, grey, optionally with a spinner or an icon, or in the destructive tone for a failure.

**Use instead when:**
- `EmptyState`: a full placeholder with title and actions
- `InlineAlert`: a boxed notice with an action
- `Spinner`: only a loading indicator
- `Toaster`: a transient message

#### Keyboard

Not focusable: no keyboard interaction.

#### Screen readers

- A neutral or loading `Note` is `role="status"` (a polite live region); the destructive tone is `role="alert"` (assertive), so use it only for a real failure the user needs to hear.
- `loading` adds `aria-busy="true"`. The spinner in it is hidden from assistive technology, so the text must say what is happening ("Loading results…").
- Changing the text of a mounted `Note` is what a live region announces. Icons you pass as `icon` are not hidden for you: pass `aria-hidden` icons.

#### Reduced motion

While `loading`, the text breathes with a slow `animate-pulse` that has `motion-reduce:animate-none`, and the net in `sutra.css` stops it too. The ring spinner keeps spinning, as it carries meaning.

#### Server rendering

Server render: same markup as the client. Plain markup with no browser API, so server and client output match.

#### Slots

- `note`: the root, with `data-tone` (`neutral` or `destructive`) and `data-loading`

#### Gotchas

- `loading` wins over the tone: a loading `Note` is never `alert`, whatever `tone` says, and it replaces `icon` with the spinner.
- `tone` is `neutral` or `destructive`. The older `default`, `error` and `busy` still work (`busy` as a tone or a prop equals `loading`), but are deprecated.
- `align` is `center` by default; `start` left-aligns the icon and text (it follows the writing direction, so it flips in RTL).

## NumberInput

> Numeric stepper with keyboard support, press-and-hold repeat and locale-aware formatting.

- Import: `import { NumberInput } from "@sutra/ui"` (or from `@sutra/ui/forms`)
- Source: `packages/ui/src/primitives/number-input` (primitives)
- `data-slot`: `number-input`, `number-input-field`
- Also accepts the props of HTMLAttributes, InputHTMLAttributes

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clampOnBlur` | `boolean` | `true` | Clamp typed values to min/max on blur. |
| `decrementLabel` | `string` | `"Decrease"` | Accessible name of the decrement button. |
| `defaultValue` | `number \| null` | `null` | Initial number when uncontrolled; `null` starts empty. |
| `formatOptions` | `Intl.NumberFormatOptions` |  | Display formatting, e.g. `{ style: "currency", currency: "USD" }`. |
| `incrementLabel` | `string` | `"Increase"` | Accessible name of the increment button. |
| `invalid` | `boolean` |  | Marks the field invalid: error border and `aria-invalid`. Inherited from a surrounding `Field` when omitted. |
| `largeStep` | `number` |  | Step used by PageUp / PageDown and Shift+Arrow. Defaults to `step * 10`. |
| `layout` | `"split" \| "stacked"` | `"split"` | `split` renders − value +, `stacked` renders chevrons on the right. |
| `locale` | `string` |  | BCP 47 locale for number formatting and parsing (decimal and group separators). Defaults to the user's locale. |
| `max` | `number` |  | Largest allowed value; stepping and blur clamp to it. |
| `min` | `number` |  | Smallest allowed value; stepping and blur clamp to it. |
| `onValueChange` | `(value: number \| null) => void` |  | Called with the parsed number (or `null` when emptied) when a typed entry is committed (blur or Enter) and on each step, Home or End; not on every keystroke. |
| `precision` | `number` |  | Fixed number of decimals; values are rounded to it. |
| `size` | `Size` | `"md"` | Field height and text size. |
| `step` | `number` | `1` | Amount added or removed by the buttons and the arrow keys. |
| `value` | `number \| null` |  | Controlled number; `null` is an empty field. Use with `onValueChange`. |
| `variant` | `"outline" \| "filled"` |  | `outline` (default) is the bordered box; `filled` is a tinted surface with a hidden border. |
| `wrapperClassName` | `string` |  | Class for the outer group. |

### Notes

**When to use:** A numeric field with step buttons, arrow-key stepping, press-and-hold repeat, min and max, and locale-aware formatting and parsing (currency, percent, units). The value is a `number` or `null`, never a string.

**Use instead when:**
- `Input`: free text, or a native `type="number"` where the browser spinner is enough
- `Slider`: a coarse value on a range
- `TimePicker`: a time of day
- `InputOTP`: a fixed length code

#### Keyboard

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Moves to and from the field; the step buttons are not tab stops (`tabIndex` -1) |
| ArrowUp, ArrowDown | Add or subtract `step`, clamped to `min` and `max` |
| Shift+ArrowUp, Shift+ArrowDown, PageUp, PageDown | Add or subtract `largeStep` (default `step * 10`) |
| Home, End | Jump to `min` or `max`; with no bound set they move the caret as usual |
| Enter | Commit what was typed |

Pressing a step button with a pointer steps once, then repeats every 60 ms after 400 ms until release or a bound. Nothing here reads the Left and Right arrows, so RTL changes only the layout. Keys do nothing while the field is `disabled` or `readOnly`.

#### Screen readers

- The field is a text input with `role="spinbutton"` and `aria-valuemin`, `aria-valuemax`, `aria-valuenow` and `aria-valuetext` (the formatted value, such as "$1,234.50"). They follow the committed value, not text still being typed.
- The step buttons are named "Increase" and "Decrease" (`incrementLabel`, `decrementLabel`) and point at the field with `aria-controls`; use the arrow keys instead of tabbing to them. Icons are `aria-hidden`.
- Name the field with a `<label>`, `aria-label` or a surrounding `FieldLabel`. `invalid`, `required`, `disabled` and `aria-describedby` are inherited from a surrounding `Field` unless you pass them.

#### Reduced motion

Static apart from colour transitions on the step buttons and the border, which the reduced-motion net ends in 1 ms.

#### Server rendering

Server render: part of it fills in after mount. The field renders on the server, but the display text is formatted with `Intl.NumberFormat` in the runtime's default locale unless you pass `locale`, so a server and a browser with different locales can show "1,234.5" against "1.234,5" and trigger a hydration warning. Pass `locale` to make both sides agree.

#### Slots

- `number-input`: the outer group; `data-layout` is `split` or `stacked`
- `number-input-field`: the text input

#### Gotchas

- `onValueChange` fires when a typed entry is committed (blur or Enter), and on each step, Home or End; it does not fire per keystroke. The native `onChange` prop is removed from the type.
- `clampOnBlur` is on by default: a typed 42 with `max={10}` becomes 10 on blur. Turn it off to keep out-of-range text; stepping still clamps. Clearing the text commits `null`.
- `precision` fixes the number of decimals shown and rounds values to it; without it up to three decimals show (more if `step` has more), and stepping rounds to the step's own decimals, so `0.1` plus `0.2` gives `0.3`.
- Typed text is parsed with the locale's separators, native digits (Arabic-Indic, Persian) and currency or percent signs; a `percent` style stores a fraction (50 % is 0.5). `name` posts the raw number, not the formatted text.

## OTPField

> Ready-made OTP input that renders its slots automatically. Digits only by default.

- Import: `import { OTPField } from "@sutra/ui"` (or from `@sutra/ui/forms`)
- Source: `packages/ui/src/primitives/input-otp` (primitives)
- Also accepts the props of HTMLAttributes, InputHTMLAttributes, OTPInputBaseProps

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `groupSize` | `number` |  | Split slots into groups of this size with a separator between them. |
| `invalid` | `boolean` |  | Marks the field invalid: error ring on the slots and `aria-invalid`. Inherited from a surrounding `Field` when omitted. |
| `length` | `number` | `6` | Number of characters. |
| `separator` | `React.ReactNode` |  | Custom separator node. |
| `size` | `Size` |  | Slot size. |
| `slotClassName` | `string` |  | Classes for every slot. |

### Notes

**When to use:** A one-time code or PIN field drawn as separate character slots over one real input (the `input-otp` library). Compose `InputOTPGroup`, `InputOTPSlot` and `InputOTPSeparator` yourself, or use `OTPField` for a ready-made row of slots.

**Use instead when:**
- `Input`: free text of any length
- `NumberInput`: a number with steppers
- `PasswordInput`: a secret typed in full
- `TagInput`: several free-form tags

#### Keyboard

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Focuses the single underlying input (the slots are not tab stops) |
| Digits, or any character `pattern` allows | Fill the next slot; a character that fails `pattern` is rejected |
| Backspace, Delete | Remove characters, as in a normal text input |
| Arrow keys, Home, End | Move the native caret, which highlights the matching slot |
| Ctrl+V, Cmd+V | Paste a code; `pasteTransformer` can clean it first |

Everything is native text input behaviour: one `<input>` sits over the slots with transparent text. `onComplete` fires when the value reaches `maxLength` (`length` for `OTPField`). Slots are a flex row, so in an RTL document they run right to left; wrap the field in `dir="ltr"` if a code should read left to right.

#### Screen readers

- The real input carries the whole value and is what assistive technology reads. Give it a name with `aria-label`, `aria-labelledby` or a surrounding `FieldLabel`; `invalid` sets `aria-invalid`, and `Field` supplies `id`, `aria-describedby`, `disabled` and `required`.
- The input defaults to `autoComplete="one-time-code"` (so the browser can offer an SMS code), `inputMode="numeric"` and `spellCheck` off. `OTPField` sets `inputMode` to `text` when you give it a non-digit `pattern`.
- Slots are plain `div`s with no role or `aria-hidden`, and the fake caret is `aria-hidden`. `InputOTPSeparator` is a `role="separator"`, so each one is announced when a reader walks the content.

#### Reduced motion

A character pops in with `animate-in zoom-in-90`, which the reduced-motion net strips of its movement. The fake caret blinks with `animate-caret-blink`, which the net turns off, so it stays solid.

#### Server rendering

Server render: same markup as the client. The input and the slots render on the server from `value` or `defaultValue`; the active slot, the fake caret and the library's autofill style rules appear only after mount, because they depend on focus and `document.head`.

#### Slots

- `input-otp`: the underlying input
- `input-otp-group`: a run of slots
- `input-otp-slot`: one character cell; `data-active` while it holds the caret, `data-filled` when it has a character
- `input-otp-separator`: the divider between groups

#### Gotchas

- `OTPField` is digits only by default (`pattern` is `REGEXP_ONLY_DIGITS`); pass `pattern` to allow letters, and `groupSize` and `separator` to split the slots (3 and 3 for a six digit code).
- `InputOTP` needs `maxLength` and one `InputOTPSlot index` per character; a missing index leaves a character with nothing to show it. `OTPField` takes `length` instead.
- `onChange` receives the string value, not an event. `defaultValue` works because the wrapper owns the uncontrolled state; pass `value` to control it.
- `size` is `sm`, `md` or `lg` and applies to every slot through context; `invalid` turns the slot borders red.

## Pagination

> Page navigation: numbered, simple, dots or load-more, with an optional page-size selector.

- Import: `import { Pagination } from "@sutra/ui"` (or from `@sutra/ui/navigation`)
- Source: `packages/ui/src/primitives/pagination` (primitives)
- `data-slot`: `pagination-jump`
- Parts: [`PaginationEllipsis`](PaginationEllipsis.md), [`PaginationItem`](PaginationItem.md), [`PaginationNext`](PaginationNext.md), [`PaginationPrev`](PaginationPrev.md), [`PaginationStatus`](PaginationStatus.md)
- Also accepts the props of HTMLAttributes

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `totalPages` (required) | `number` |  | Total number of pages (not rows); drives which page buttons are shown. |
| `boundaryCount` | `number` | `1` | Pages always shown at the start and end of the range. |
| `defaultPage` | `number` | `1` | Initial page (1-based) when uncontrolled. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` |  | Disables every control. |
| `loading` | `boolean` |  | load-more: spinner on the button. |
| `loadMoreLabel` | `React.ReactNode` | `"Load more"` | Text of the load-more button. |
| `onPageChange` | `(page: number) => void` |  | Called with the new 1-based page when the user changes page. |
| `onPageSizeChange` | `(pageSize: number) => void` |  | Called with the chosen rows-per-page count; update `pageSize` and usually reset the page. |
| `page` | `number` |  | Current page (1-based). |
| `pageJump` | `boolean` | `false` | numbered: activating an ellipsis turns it into a page field (Enter jumps to that page, Escape cancels), so a long range can be crossed in one step. Opt-in; the page list is shown from the `@lg` container width up. |
| `pageSize` | `number` |  | Rows per page; enables the page size selector together with `pageSizeOptions`. |
| `pageSizeLabel` | `React.ReactNode` | `"Rows per page"` | Label of the page size selector. |
| `pageSizeOptions` | `number[]` |  | Choices for the page size selector (needs `pageSize`); each is a rows-per-page count. |
| `siblingCount` | `number` | `1` | Pages shown on each side of the current page before collapsing into an ellipsis. |
| `size` | `Size` | `"md"` | Control height and text size. |
| `variant` | `"numbered" \| "simple" \| "dots" \| "load-more"` | `"numbered"` | Layout: numbered page buttons, prev/next only, a dot indicator, or a "load more" button. |

### Part props

Props of `PaginationEllipsis`, `PaginationItem`, `PaginationNext`, `PaginationPrev`, `PaginationStatus`: see [the full page](md/Pagination.md).

### Notes

**When to use:** Page navigation for a list or table. Four layouts (`numbered`, `simple`, `dots`, `load-more`), an optional rows-per-page select, an opt-in `pageJump` field in the ellipsis and `PaginationStatus` for the "1–10 of 245" line.

**Use instead when:**
- `Steps`: a fixed sequence of steps with progress
- `Carousel`: paging through slides
- `Breadcrumbs`: showing where the user is in a hierarchy

#### Keyboard

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Moves through previous, the page buttons, next and the rows-per-page select; disabled buttons are skipped |
| Enter, Space | Activate the focused button: go to that page, or previous or next |
| Enter | In the jump field (`pageJump`): go to the typed page |
| Escape | In the jump field: cancel and return focus to the ellipsis; leaving the field cancels too |

There are no arrow-key shortcuts, so keys do not swap in RTL; the row flows in reading order and the previous and next arrows are mirrored. After a jump, focus moves to the button of the page it landed on. A disabled previous or next button is a real `disabled` button, so it leaves the tab order.

#### Screen readers

The root is a `<nav>` labelled "Pagination" (override with `aria-label`). Page buttons are named "Page 3" and the current one has `aria-current="page"`; previous and next are named "Previous page" and "Next page" whatever their visible text (pass your own `aria-label` if you change `children`). A plain ellipsis is `aria-hidden`; with `onJump` it is a button named "Jump to a page" (`jumpLabel`), and the field it opens is named "Go to page, 1 to N". In narrow containers the page list is replaced by "Page x of y" in an `aria-live="polite"` region. `PaginationStatus` is a polite live region too (`aria-busy` while `loading`, with an sr-only "Loading…" placeholder), so it announces the new row window after a page change.

#### Reduced motion

Mostly static. The `dots` indicator (each dot has a 24px hit area; neighbours are 14px apart, so the boxes overlap and the later dot wins the overlap) grows with a width transition and the button states fade; both end in 1 ms under reduced motion. The `loading` spinner on the load-more button keeps turning.

#### Server rendering

Server render: part of it fills in after mount. The pager renders plain markup on the server. Whether the page list or the "Page x of y" label shows depends on a container query (`@lg`) in CSS, not on JavaScript. `PaginationStatus` formats numbers with `Intl.NumberFormat`: without `locale` the server and the browser may use different default locales and print "1,245" and "1.245", so pass `locale` when rendering on a server.

#### Slots

- `pagination-ellipsis`: the span wrapping a clickable ellipsis (only with `onJump` or `pageJump`)
- `pagination-jump`: the page field that replaces the ellipsis
- `pagination-status`: the row window line of `PaginationStatus`

#### Gotchas

- `totalPages` is a page count, not a row count; `page` is 1-based and is clamped to `1..totalPages`, and `onPageChange` is not called for the current page. Controlled use needs `page` and `onPageChange` together; otherwise it starts at `defaultPage`.
- The page list is hidden below the `@lg` container width (32rem) and replaced by the "Page x of y" label, so narrow cards do not show page buttons. The `simple` variant always shows the label.
- The rows-per-page select appears only with `pageSize` and a non-empty `pageSizeOptions`; `onPageSizeChange` just reports the choice, so update `pageSize` and usually reset `page` yourself.
- `PaginationItem isActive` is a deprecated alias of `active`. In `load-more`, `page` is the number of pages loaded: the button advances `page` by one and is disabled on the last page.

## PasswordInput

> Password field with a show/hide toggle.

- Import: `import { PasswordInput } from "@sutra/ui"` (or from `@sutra/ui/forms`)
- Source: `packages/ui/src/primitives/input` (primitives)
- Also accepts the props of HTMLAttributes, InputHTMLAttributes

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `className` | `string` |  | Classes for the element that renders. Without addons that is the `<input>` itself (the root). With addons (`leadingIcon`, `trailingIcon`, `prefix`, `suffix`, `clearable`) it lands on the **inner** `<input>`, not the outer wrapper, so layout classes (`w-48`, `flex-1`, margins) have no visible effect there; use `wrapperClassName` for those. |
| `clearable` | `boolean` |  | Shows a clear button while the field has a value. |
| `defaultVisible` | `boolean` | `false` | Initial visibility of the password. |
| `invalid` | `boolean` |  | Marks the field invalid: error border and `aria-invalid`. Inherited from a surrounding `Field` when omitted. |
| `leadingIcon` | `React.ReactNode` |  | Icon rendered inside the field before the text. |
| `onClear` | `() => void` |  | Called after the clear button empties the field. |
| `prefix` | `React.ReactNode` |  | Text addon before the field, e.g. "https://". |
| `size` | `"sm" \| "md" \| "lg" \| null` | `"md"` | Field height and text size. |
| `suffix` | `React.ReactNode` |  | Text addon after the field, e.g. ".com". |
| `variant` | `"outline" \| "filled" \| null` |  | `outline` (default) is the bordered box; `filled` is a tinted surface with a hidden border. |
| `wrapperClassName` | `string` |  | Classes for the outer wrapper `<div>`, which is only rendered when addons are present. Put layout/sizing classes here when the input has addons. |

### Notes

**When to use:** The single-line text field. It takes every native `<input>` prop and adds `leadingIcon`, `trailingIcon`, `prefix`, `suffix` and `clearable`. `PasswordInput` adds a show and hide toggle, `SearchInput` a search icon, a clear button and an optional focus hotkey.

**Use instead when:**
- `Textarea`: several lines
- `NumberInput`: numbers with steppers and locale formatting
- `InputGroup`: addons that are real buttons, selects or other controls
- `InputOTP`: a one-time code split into slots
- `Combobox`: a choice from a list
- `TagInput`: several free-form tags

#### Keyboard

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Moves to and from the field and the `PasswordInput` toggle. The `clearable` button is not a tab stop (`tabIndex` -1) |
| Enter, Space | On the `PasswordInput` toggle: show or hide the text |
| Escape | In a `SearchInput` that has text and `clearable`: empty it and call `onClear` |
| `hotkey` (for example `/` or `mod+k`) | Anywhere on the page: focus and select the `SearchInput`. A plain key typed into another field stays text; a chord with Ctrl or Meta still fires |

Typing is native. There are no arrow-key handlers, and the icons and addons use logical padding, so RTL only mirrors the layout.

#### Screen readers

- A native `<input>` named by a `<label>`, `aria-label` or a surrounding `FieldLabel`; a field with no visible label needs `aria-label`. `invalid` sets `aria-invalid`, and `Field` adds `id`, `aria-describedby`, `disabled` and `required` unless you pass them.
- `SearchInput` is `type="search"` (role `searchbox`), sets `aria-keyshortcuts` from `hotkey`, and hides the key hint (`aria-hidden`).
- The clear button is named "Clear" (not translatable through a prop). The `PasswordInput` toggle is named "Show password" or "Hide password" and also carries `aria-pressed`. Icons are `aria-hidden`; `leadingIcon`, `trailingIcon`, `prefix` and `suffix` content that you pass is not hidden for you.

#### Reduced motion

The clear button pops in with `animate-in fade-in-0 zoom-in-75`, and the border and ring fade with a short transition; the reduced-motion net removes the zoom and ends the transitions in 1 ms.

#### Server rendering

Server render: part of it fills in after mount. `Input` and `PasswordInput` render the same markup on both sides, including the clear button when a `value` or `defaultValue` is set. `SearchInput` reads its key hint after mount (`hotkey` is turned into key labels in an effect), so the hint chips are not in the server HTML and appear on hydration.

#### Slots

- `input`: the `<input>` element (the root when there are no addons)
- `input-wrapper`: the outer `div`, rendered only when an icon, addon or `clearable` is present

#### Gotchas

- `className` lands on the inner `<input>` once any addon is present, so layout classes (`w-48`, `flex-1`) do nothing there; put them in `wrapperClassName`. Without addons `className` is the root.
- `PasswordInput` defaults to `autoComplete="current-password"` (pass `"new-password"` when setting one), turns off `spellCheck`, and does not accept `type` or `trailingIcon`.
- `clearable` fires a real `input` event, so `onChange` runs with an empty value, then `onClear`. `SearchInput` is `clearable` by default.
- Pass `prefix` and `suffix` as text addons; for interactive addons use `InputGroup`.

## Popover

> Popover root.

- Import: `import { Popover } from "@sutra/ui"` (or from `@sutra/ui/overlays`)
- Source: `packages/ui/src/primitives/popover` (primitives)
- Parts: [`PopoverAnchor`](PopoverAnchor.md), [`PopoverBody`](PopoverBody.md), [`PopoverClose`](PopoverClose.md), [`PopoverContent`](PopoverContent.md), [`PopoverDescription`](PopoverDescription.md), [`PopoverFooter`](PopoverFooter.md), [`PopoverHeader`](PopoverHeader.md), [`PopoverTitle`](PopoverTitle.md), [`PopoverTrigger`](PopoverTrigger.md)
- Also accepts the props of PopoverProps

### Props

No props of its own.

### Part props

Props of `PopoverContent`: see [the full page](md/Popover.md).

### Notes

**When to use:** A small floating panel anchored to a trigger, for filters, quick forms, pickers and rich details. It does not block the page. `PopoverContent` takes `size`, `padded` and `arrow`.

**Use instead when:**
- `DropdownMenu`: a list of actions
- `Tooltip`: a short non-interactive label
- `HoverCard`: a preview on hover or focus
- `Dialog`: the user must finish a task before going on
- `Select`: a single choice for a form field

#### Keyboard

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| Enter, Space | On the trigger (a native button): toggle the popover |
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Move through the panel; focus is not trapped, and moving it outside the panel closes it |
| Escape | Close and return focus to the trigger |

Focus moves into the panel when it opens and goes back to the trigger on close (not after a click outside). There are no arrow-key or direction-dependent keys, so RTL changes nothing. In RTL, `side="start"` and `side="end"` swap left and right (read through `useDirection()`: a `DirectionProvider` with a `dir`, else `<html dir>`; a plain `dir` attribute on a container is not seen); the default is `bottom`, `left` and `right` stay physical, and Radix still flips the panel on a collision.

#### Screen readers

The trigger gets `aria-haspopup="dialog"`, `aria-expanded` and, while open, `aria-controls`. The panel is `role="dialog"`. `PopoverTitle` and `PopoverDescription` (an `h3` and a `p`) name and describe the dialog: inside `PopoverContent` they get ids and the content sets `aria-labelledby` / `aria-describedby` while they are mounted. An `aria-label`, `aria-labelledby` or `aria-describedby` you pass to `PopoverContent` wins, and a popover without a title stays unnamed, so give it an `aria-label`. The arrow is decoration. An icon-only trigger needs `aria-label`.

#### Reduced motion

The panel fades and zooms in from its trigger and slides slightly from its side; the reduced-motion net removes the slide and the scale and keeps only the fade.

#### Server rendering

Server render: same markup as the client. A closed popover renders only its trigger on server and client. The panel is portalled into `<body>` after mount, so a popover that is `open` or `defaultOpen` on first render appears after hydration. The portalled panel is outside a subtree `dir` or `data-style`: set them on `<html>`, or pass `disablePortal` to keep it inside the subtree.

#### Gotchas

- It is non-modal by default (`modal` on `Popover` is false): the page stays interactive, outside clicks close it, and there is no focus trap. Pass `modal` for a trapped, `aria-hidden`-backed panel, but then consider a `Dialog`.
- `size` defaults to `md` (18rem), `padded` to true (`p-4`). `PopoverHeader`, `PopoverBody` and `PopoverFooter` bring their own padding, so set `padded={false}` when you compose them.
- Use `PopoverAnchor` to position against another element than the trigger; `PopoverClose asChild` closes from inside the panel.
- `PopoverContent disablePortal` renders in place, which suits a popover inside a `Dialog` or `Sheet` with its own stacking; the default portal puts it in `<body>` at `z-50`.

## PortBadge

> Small monospaced chip for a network port, optionally linking to it on localhost.

- Import: `import { PortBadge } from "@sutra/ui"` (or from `@sutra/ui/system`)
- Source: `packages/ui/src/primitives/port-badge` (primitives)
- `data-slot`: `port-badge`
- Parts: [`PortBadgeList`](PortBadgeList.md)
- Also accepts the props of HTMLAttributes

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `port` (required) | `number \| string` |  | Port number; a leading colon is stripped when a string is given. |
| `accent` | `Accent` |  | Categorical colour. Without `accent` or `tone` the badge follows the inherited accent (or primary). |
| `colon` | `boolean` | `false` | Show a leading colon (":3000"). Default false. |
| `host` | `string` |  | Host for `href={true}`. Default "localhost". |
| `href` | `string \| boolean` |  | Makes the badge a link: `true` opens `localhost:<port>` (see `host`), a string is used as is. |
| `size` | `"sm" \| "md" \| "lg"` | `"sm"` | Badge height and text size. |
| `target` | `string` | `"_blank"` | Link target. Default "_blank" (with `rel="noopener noreferrer"`). |
| `tone` | `ToneInput` |  | Semantic colour; wins over the accent. |

### Part props

Props of `PortBadgeList`: see [the full page](md/PortBadge.md).

### Notes

**When to use:** A small monospaced chip for a network port, optionally a link that opens it on localhost. `PortBadgeList` shows a row of them with a "+N" overflow.

**Use instead when:**
- `Badge`: any other short label
- `KeyValue`: a port as one fact among others
- `CopyButton`: copy the port or URL

#### Keyboard

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Moves focus to the link, only when `href` is set (a plain badge is not focusable) |
| Enter | Follows the link (native `<a>`) |

No key depends on direction, so RTL changes nothing.

#### Screen readers

- A linked badge is an `<a>` whose `aria-label` is "Open localhost:3000" (the URL without `http://`), which replaces the visible "3000" as its name. A plain badge is a `<span>` read as its text.
- `PortBadgeList` is a `ul` with `aria-label` "Ports" (change it with `label`) and one `li` per badge. The "+N" chip is `aria-hidden`; a visually hidden "N more: 9001, 15672" is read instead, and the same ports are in its `title`.

#### Reduced motion

Static, apart from the hover fade on a linked badge, which the reduced-motion net in `sutra.css` ends within 1 ms.

#### Server rendering

Server render: same markup as the client. Plain markup built from the props, with no browser API, so server and client output match.

#### Slots

- `port-badge`: the badge, which is the `<a>` for a linked badge and the `<span>` otherwise
- `port-badge-list`: the list
- `port-badge-overflow`: the "+N" chip

#### Gotchas

- `href` is `true` for `http://localhost:<port>` (change the machine with `host`), or a string used as is. The link is plain HTTP and opens in a new tab (`target="_blank"` with `rel="noopener noreferrer"`); `rel` is dropped if you change `target`.
- A string `href` that fails `isSafeHref` (such as `javascript:`) is dropped silently and you get a plain, unlinked badge.
- `tone` wins over `accent`; with neither, the badge follows the inherited accent or primary. `PortBadgeList` takes `accent` once on the list (a CSS variable that the badges inherit), `tone` on every badge.
- `PortBadgeList` renders nothing for an empty `ports` array, and `max={0}` shows only the "+N" chip. A string port such as `":8080"` loses its leading colon, and `colon` adds one back to the text.

## Progress

> Linear progress bar, determinate or indeterminate (role="progressbar"): how far a task has got. For a level read against thresholds (disk usage, context window) use `Meter` instead. Restyle the track with `className` (e.g. `rounded-none bg-transparent` for an edge strip) and the fill with `indicatorClassName`.

- Import: `import { Progress } from "@sutra/ui"` (or from `@sutra/ui/core`)
- Source: `packages/ui/src/primitives/progress` (primitives)
- Parts: [`ProgressCircle`](ProgressCircle.md), [`ProgressRingSvg`](ProgressRingSvg.md), [`ProgressSegments`](ProgressSegments.md)
- Also accepts the props of HTMLAttributes, ProgressProps, PrimitivePropsWithRef

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `color` | `ProgressColor` |  | **Deprecated.** Use `tone`. Legacy name of `tone`. |
| `formatValue` | `(value: number, max: number) => React.ReactNode` |  | Formats the displayed value; receives the value and `max`. Default is the rounded percentage, e.g. "40%". A text or number result is also used as `aria-valuetext`. |
| `indeterminate` | `boolean` |  | Forces the looping animation regardless of `value` (also used when `value` is null). |
| `indicatorClassName` | `string` |  | Classes for the filled indicator bar (`className` styles the track). |
| `label` | `React.ReactNode` |  | Text shown above the bar; it also becomes the accessible name. |
| `showValue` | `boolean \| "right" \| "top"` |  | Show the percentage on the right of the bar or above it, next to the label. |
| `size` | `"2xs" \| "xs" \| "sm" \| "md" \| "lg"` | `"md"` | Track height: 2xs 2px (hairline loading strips), xs 4px, sm 6px, md 8px, lg 12px. Default "md". |
| `tone` | `ToneInput` |  | Semantic colour of the filled part. Default "primary". |
| `value` | `number \| null` |  | Completed amount from 0 to `max`; `null` or `undefined` renders the indeterminate animation. |

### Part props

Props of `ProgressCircle`, `ProgressRingSvg`, `ProgressSegments`: see [the full page](md/Progress.md).

### Notes

**When to use:** How far a task has got: a linear bar (determinate or indeterminate) with optional label and value, plus a ring (`ProgressCircle`) and a stepped bar (`ProgressSegments`).

**Use instead when:**
- `Meter`: a level read against thresholds (disk, memory, quota)
- `Spinner`: work of unknown length with no bar
- `Skeleton`: a placeholder for content that is loading
- `Steps`: named stages with their own state
- `RingMeter`: a round level gauge

#### Keyboard

Not focusable: no keyboard interaction.

#### Screen readers

- `Progress` is Radix's `role="progressbar"` with `aria-valuemin` 0, `aria-valuemax` and `aria-valuenow`, plus `aria-valuetext` of the rounded percentage ("40%"). `label` names it through `aria-labelledby`; without a visible `label`, pass `aria-label` (it reaches the bar itself).
- With no `value` (or `indeterminate`) there is no `aria-valuenow` and `data-state="indeterminate"`; announce what is happening in the name or nearby text, since no number is exposed.
- `ProgressCircle` and `ProgressSegments` are `role="progressbar"` divs with `aria-valuemin`, `aria-valuemax`, `aria-valuenow` (clamped) and `aria-label` from `label`. They have no `aria-valuetext`, so a ring reads its raw value against `max`. `ProgressSegments role="meter"` makes it a level (password strength); add `aria-valuetext` then.
- `ProgressRingSvg` is `aria-hidden`; the wrapper that uses it carries the role.

#### Reduced motion

The determinate fill slides with a 500 ms transform, the ring arc with a stroke transition, and the segments fade with staggered delays; the first two have `motion-reduce:transition-none` and the net ends transitions in 1 ms. The indeterminate bar does not stop: the net slows its loop to 3 s because it carries meaning.

#### Server rendering

Server render: part of it fills in after mount. Renders on the server, but direction is read from the page after mount: the server paints left-to-right (the fill is hidden by a negative `translateX`), so on an RTL page the fill flips to the right side after hydration. `ProgressCircle` and `ProgressSegments` have no direction logic and match exactly.

#### Gotchas

- `value` is clamped to 0 to `max`; an out-of-range value never reaches Radix's console error. `max <= 0` reads as an empty bar. `showValue` is `true` (above next to the label, else on the right), `"top"` or `"right"`.
- `formatValue` also sets `aria-valuetext` when it returns text or a number ("3 / 8 GB"), so the bar reads what it shows; a JSX result cannot be spoken, so the default percentage stays. Radix's `getValueLabel` or an explicit `aria-valuetext` overrides it.
- When there is a `label` or a shown value, the bar sits in a wrapper: `className` then styles the wrapper, not the track (use `indicatorClassName` for the fill).
- `ProgressCircle` has no indeterminate state; use `Spinner` for that. Its centre text is `children`, or the percentage unless `showValue={false}`.

## RadioCard

> Bordered, selectable card variant of a radio item.

- Import: `import { RadioCard } from "@sutra/ui"` (or from `@sutra/ui/forms`)
- Source: `packages/ui/src/primitives/radio` (primitives)
- `data-slot`: `radio-card`
- Also accepts the props of HTMLAttributes, ButtonHTMLAttributes, RadioProps$1, PrimitivePropsWithRef

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `label` (required) | `React.ReactNode` |  | Primary text of the card (the whole card is the label and click target). |
| `description` | `React.ReactNode` |  | Supporting text under the label. |
| `icon` | `React.ReactNode` |  | Icon shown at the start of the card. |
| `indicatorPosition` | `"start" \| "end"` | `"end"` | Which side of the card the radio dot sits on. |
| `radioClassName` | `string` |  | Class for the radio control (`className` styles the card). |
| `size` | `"sm" \| "md"` | `"md"` | Radio size: `sm` 14px or `md` 16px. |

### Variants

- `size`: `sm`, `md` (default "md")

### Notes

**When to use:** Exactly one choice from a few options that should all stay visible. Compose `RadioGroupItem`, `RadioField` (with label and description) and `RadioCard` (a selectable card) inside `RadioGroup`, or pass `options` to `RadioGroupField`.

**Use instead when:**
- `Select`: the list is long or space is tight
- `SegmentedControl`: two to four options that switch a view
- `CheckboxGroup`: several choices at once
- `ToggleGroup`: loose on/off buttons
- `Combobox`: a long searchable list

#### Keyboard

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Enters the group on the checked radio (the first one when none is checked) and leaves it; the other radios are skipped |
| ArrowDown, ArrowUp | `orientation="vertical"` (the default): move to the next or previous radio, loop at the ends, and select it |
| ArrowRight, ArrowLeft | `orientation="horizontal"`: the same; the other axis does nothing |
| Home, PageUp, End, PageDown | First or last radio |
| Space | Select the focused radio |

Enter does nothing (Radix cancels it). Disabled radios are skipped. In RTL with `orientation="horizontal"`, ArrowLeft goes to the next radio and ArrowRight to the previous; vertical groups do not change. The group reads the direction from its parent, so a `DirectionProvider`, a `dir` container or `<html dir>` all work.

#### Screen readers

- The group is `role="radiogroup"` with `aria-orientation` and `aria-required` from `required`; each item is a `<button role="radio">` with `aria-checked`. `invalid` sets `aria-invalid` on the group, and a surrounding `Field` supplies `id`, `aria-describedby`, `disabled` and `required`.
- The group has no name of its own. `RadioGroupField` names it from `label` through `aria-labelledby` and links `description` with `aria-describedby`; for a bare `RadioGroup` pass `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`.
- `RadioField` and `RadioCard` name each radio through `<label htmlFor>` and announce the description through `aria-describedby`. A bare `RadioGroupItem` needs `aria-label`.

#### Reduced motion

The dot scales in with a spring transition (`ease-spring`) and the item scales on press; the reduced-motion net ends both in 1 ms, so the dot appears at once.

#### Server rendering

Server render: same markup as the client. Items and the group render on the server, including `value` and `defaultValue`. The group writes a `dir` attribute that is `ltr` in the server HTML and settles to the page direction after hydration, which only shows on an RTL page.

#### Slots

- `radio-group`: the group; `radio-group-field`: the wrapper around label, description and group
- `radio-group-item`: the radio button; `radio-dot`: its dot
- `radio-field`: the row of radio, label and description
- `radio-card`: the whole card label

#### Gotchas

- Arrow keys select as well as move focus; there is no "focus without selecting". Use `value` and `onValueChange` (a string) to control it, and `name` on the group so a native form posts it.
- `RadioGroupField` renders `variant="card"` with auto-fit columns when horizontal; the default variant is a plain list. Both take `size` (`sm` or `md`) for every option.
- Each `RadioGroupItem` needs a `value`; an item with no label has no name unless you pass `aria-label`.
- `RadioCard` moves the focus ring from the dot to the whole card. `disabled` on the group disables every item.

## RadioField

> Radio item with a label and optional description.

- Import: `import { RadioField } from "@sutra/ui"` (or from `@sutra/ui/forms`)
- Source: `packages/ui/src/primitives/radio` (primitives)
- `data-slot`: `radio-field`
- Also accepts the props of HTMLAttributes, ButtonHTMLAttributes, RadioProps$1, PrimitivePropsWithRef

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `description` | `React.ReactNode` |  | Secondary text under the label, announced as the item description. |

| `labelClassName` | `string` |  | Classes for the `<label>` element. |

## RadioGroup
