## RangeSlider

> `Slider` preset with two thumbs (defaults to the full min–max range).

- Import: `import { RangeSlider } from "@sutra/ui"` (or from `@sutra/ui/forms`)
- Source: `packages/ui/src/primitives/slider` (primitives)
- Also accepts the props of HTMLAttributes, SliderProps, PrimitivePropsWithRef

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `accent` | `Accent` |  | Categorical colour for the range, thumb border and active marks. Default primary. |
| `formatValue` | `(value: number) => React.ReactNode` |  | Formats the number shown in the value bubble (see `showValue`). Default shows the raw value. |
| `getValueText` | `(value: number, index: number) => string` |  | Accessible value text per thumb (`aria-valuetext`), e.g. `(v) => v + "%"`. |
| `invalid` | `boolean` |  | Marks the slider invalid: error styling on the range and `aria-invalid`. Inherited from a surrounding `Field` when omitted. |
| `marks` | `(number \| SliderMark)[]` |  | Tick marks under the track; numbers or `{ value, label }`. |
| `showValue` | `boolean \| "always"` |  | Show a value bubble above the thumb on hover, focus and drag. `"always"` keeps it visible. |
| `size` | `Size` |  | Track and thumb size. |
| `thumbLabels` | `string[]` |  | Accessible labels per thumb, e.g. `["Volume"]` or `["Minimum", "Maximum"]`. Without it a single thumb is named by `aria-label` / `aria-labelledby` (or the surrounding `FieldLabel`); two thumbs are "Minimum" and "Maximum". |
| `tone` | `ToneInput` |  | Semantic colour (`success`, `warning`, …). Takes precedence over `accent`. |

### Notes

**When to use:** Pick a number, or a range with two thumbs, by dragging along a track. The value is always an array (`[40]`, or `[10, 80]` for `RangeSlider`). It has an optional value bubble, tick marks, `accent` and `tone` colours, and a vertical orientation.

**Use instead when:**
- `NumberInput`: an exact number is typed or stepped
- `VolumeSlider`: a slider with a mute toggle and level readout
- `Progress`: a level the user cannot change
- `Rating`: a few discrete stars
- `SegmentedControl`: a few labelled steps

#### Keyboard

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Each thumb is a tab stop |
| ArrowRight, ArrowUp | Raise the focused thumb by one `step` |
| ArrowLeft, ArrowDown | Lower it by one `step` |
| Shift+Arrow, PageUp, PageDown | Move ten steps (PageUp raises, PageDown lowers) |
| Home, End | Set the first thumb to `min` and the last thumb to `max`, whichever thumb has focus |

In RTL on a horizontal slider ArrowLeft raises and ArrowRight lowers, and the track fills from the right; Up and Down do not change. The direction is read from the parent (a `DirectionProvider`, a `dir` container or `<html dir>`), and a `dir` you pass wins. Thumbs keep a minimum gap of `minStepsBetweenThumbs` steps (1 for `RangeSlider`).

#### Screen readers

- Each thumb is a `role="slider"` with `aria-valuemin`, `aria-valuemax`, `aria-valuenow` and `aria-orientation`. A single thumb is named by `thumbLabels` (such as `["Volume"]`), else by `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` on the `Slider`, else by a surrounding `FieldLabel`; two thumbs are named "Minimum" and "Maximum" by default (an `aria-label` on the `Slider` then becomes a `role="group"` around them), more are "Value 1 of 3" and so on. `getValueText` sets `aria-valuetext` per thumb, for example `(v) => v + "%"`.
- `id` stays on the Radix root `span` (which has no role), so a `FieldLabel` click does not focus a thumb. The slider reads `Field`: its id, `disabled`, invalid state and description, hint and error ids (`aria-describedby`, also on every thumb); an explicit prop wins.
- The value bubble and the tick marks and their labels are `aria-hidden`; put what matters in `getValueText`. `invalid` (or an invalid `Field`) sets `aria-invalid` on the root and on each thumb and turns the range red.

#### Reduced motion

The thumb ring, press scale and value bubble use short transitions, which the reduced-motion net ends in 1 ms.

#### Server rendering

Server render: part of it fills in after mount. The track and range render on the server from `value` or `defaultValue`, but each thumb is `display: none` until Radix has mounted and located it, so the thumbs appear after hydration. The direction is `ltr` in the server HTML and settles after hydration on an RTL page.

#### Gotchas

- `value` and `defaultValue` are arrays, and `onValueChange` receives the whole array. `onValueCommit` fires when a drag or key press ends.
- `ref` and `className` go to the outer wrapper (which also holds the marks); every other prop, including `disabled`, `step`, `name` and `orientation`, goes to the Radix root inside it. `name` posts one hidden input per thumb (named `name[]` for a range) inside a form.
- `showValue` shows the bubble on hover, focus and drag; `"always"` keeps it. `marks` take numbers or `{ value, label }` and only mark; they do not snap the value (use `step`).
- A given `tone` beats `accent`, and `invalid` beats both.

## Rating

> Star rating input with hover preview, half steps and radiogroup keyboard support.

- Import: `import { Rating } from "@sutra/ui"` (or from `@sutra/ui/forms`)
- Source: `packages/ui/src/primitives/rating` (primitives)
- Parts: [`RatingSummary`](RatingSummary.md)
- Also accepts the props of HTMLAttributes

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `activeClassName` | `string` | `"text-warning"` | Class applied to the filled part of each icon (defaults to an amber fill). |
| `allowClear` | `boolean` | `true` | Let the user take the rating back to 0: click the selected star again, press Delete, Backspace or 0, or arrow below the first step. `false` keeps a given rating at one star or more. Default true. |
| `allowHalf` | `boolean` | `false` | Allow half-star values (0.5 steps). |
| `defaultValue` | `number` | `0` | Initial rating when uncontrolled. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Disables the control: dimmed and not focusable. |
| `getLabel` | `(value: number, max: number) => string` | `defaultGetLabel` | Builds the accessible label for each option. |
| `icon` | `React.ComponentType<{ className?: string }>` | `RiStarFill` | Icon component used for every star; receives `className`. |
| `inactiveClassName` | `string` | `"text-border-strong"` | Class applied to the empty part of each icon. |
| `max` | `number` | `5` | Number of stars. |
| `name` | `string` |  | Name for a hidden input, for native form submission. |
| `onValueChange` | `(value: number) => void` |  | Called with the new rating when the user picks, clears or steps it. |
| `readOnly` | `boolean` | `false` | Displays the rating without letting the user change it (still announced as a rating). |
| `size` | `Size` | `"md"` | Star size. |
| `value` | `number` |  | Controlled rating, from 0 to `max` (halves when `allowHalf`). Use with `onValueChange`. |

### Part props

Props of `RatingSummary`: see [the full page](md/Rating.md).

### Notes

**When to use:** A star rating input from 0 to `max` with hover preview, optional half steps and radiogroup keyboard support. With `readOnly` or `disabled` it is a static display of a score; `RatingSummary` adds the average, the count and a 5 to 1 distribution.

**Use instead when:**
- `Slider`: a value on a continuous range
- `SegmentedControl`: a few labelled choices
- `RadioGroup`: named options that need labels
- `Meter`: a level measured against thresholds

#### Keyboard

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab / Shift+Tab | One tab stop: the checked star (the first star when there is no rating) |
| ArrowRight, ArrowUp | Add one star (half a star with `allowHalf`) |
| ArrowLeft, ArrowDown | Remove one star; below the first step it goes to 0, or stops at one step with `allowClear={false}` |
| Home, End | One step, or `max` |
| 0 to 9 | Set that rating, up to `max` (0 only with `allowClear`) |
| Delete, Backspace | Clear to 0 (only with `allowClear`) |

Every key sets the value at once and moves focus to the matching star. Space and Enter do nothing. In RTL the stars run right to left, so ArrowLeft adds and ArrowRight removes (the key towards the inline end always adds); Up and Down do not change. A `readOnly` or `disabled` rating is not focusable.

#### Screen readers

- Interactive: a `role="radiogroup"` of `role="radio"` stars with `aria-checked`, each named "N stars out of M" (`getLabel` changes the wording; with `allowHalf` the checked star carries the half value, such as "2.5 stars out of 5"). The group has no name of its own: pass `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`.
- `readOnly` and `disabled`: a single `role="img"` named "Rated N out of M" (a given `aria-label` replaces it), with `aria-disabled` when disabled. The star icons are `aria-hidden`.
- `RatingSummary` shows the average as text, a read-only `Rating` rounded to the nearest half, and a list named "Rating distribution" whose rows are `role="meter"` named "5 star" to "1 star" with the percentage as the value.

#### Reduced motion

The star under the pointer scales up (`hover:scale-110`), presses down, and the fill width eases over 150 ms; the distribution bars ease over 500 ms. All are transitions, which the reduced-motion net ends in 1 ms.

#### Server rendering

Server render: same markup as the client. Plain markup with no browser API at render time: the fill comes from `value` or `defaultValue`, the hover preview exists only after a pointer move, and the direction is read from the DOM when a key or click happens. Server and client output match.

#### Gotchas

- `allowClear` is on by default: clicking the selected star again sets 0, and so do Delete, Backspace and `0`. With `allowClear={false}` a rating of one or more cannot go back to 0; an unrated control can still be rated.
- With `allowHalf`, a click on the half of a star nearer the inline start sets the half value, and that half flips in RTL.
- `onValueChange` receives a number (0 for cleared). `name` posts the number through a hidden input; `value` and `defaultValue` are numbers up to `max`.
- `icon` swaps the star glyph, and `activeClassName` and `inactiveClassName` replace the amber fill and grey outline colours instead of adding to them.

## ScrollArea

> Custom-styled scroll container with thin overlay scrollbars and optional edge fades. The viewport is focusable while it overflows; `aria-label` / `aria-labelledby` name it as a `region`.

- Import: `import { ScrollArea } from "@sutra/ui"` (or from `@sutra/ui/core`)
- Source: `packages/ui/src/primitives/scroll-area` (primitives)
- Also accepts the props of HTMLAttributes, ScrollAreaProps, PrimitivePropsWithRef

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fadeEdges` | `FadeEdges` | `false` | Fade content into gradient masks at the edges that can still scroll. |
| `orientation` | `"vertical" \| "horizontal" \| "both"` | `"vertical"` | Which scrollbars to render. Default "vertical". |
| `viewportClassName` | `string` |  | Classes for the inner viewport (e.g. a max height). |
| `viewportRef` | `React.Ref<HTMLDivElement>` |  | Ref to the scrolling viewport element (for `scrollTo` or scroll listeners). |

### Notes

**When to use:** A scrolling region with thin overlay scrollbars that match the theme, optional edge fades and a ref to the viewport. Scrolling stays native (wheel, touch, keyboard). A plain `overflow-auto scrollbar-thin` element is enough when only a thin native scrollbar is needed.

**Use instead when:**
- `Carousel`: paged or snapping content that moves in steps

#### Keyboard

No keys of its own: the viewport is the real scroller, so the browser's scrolling keys work whenever focus is inside it (on a focusable child, or on the viewport itself), and the viewport gets `tabindex="0"` while its content overflows (measured after mount and on resize), so a keyboard user can focus it and scroll; content that fits adds no tab stop. The custom scrollbars and thumbs are for the pointer only and are not focusable. Nothing swaps in RTL.

#### Screen readers

Adds no state: the content reads in its normal order and the scrollbars are not exposed. Pass `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` when the region needs a name: they go on the viewport, which then has `role="region"` (without a name it has no role). The edge fades are a visual mask only.

#### Reduced motion

The scrollbar fades in and out (`animate-in` and `animate-out` fades) and the thumb colour is a transition; the reduced-motion net ends the transitions in 1 ms and the fade stays. Scrolling itself is native and not affected. The scrollbar hides after Radix's `scrollHideDelay` of 600 ms, a timer.

#### Server rendering

Server render: part of it fills in after mount. The server renders the root and the viewport with the content. With the default `type="hover"` the scrollbars do not exist until the pointer enters after mount, `fadeEdges` shows no fades until the edges are measured in an effect, and the root `dir` is read after mount (the server writes `ltr`), so the first server paint of an RTL page has `dir="ltr"` on the area.

#### Gotchas

- Give it a bounded size: the root is `overflow-hidden`, so without a height (`className="h-64"`) or a `max-h` (`viewportClassName`) it grows with its content and nothing scrolls.
- `orientation` decides which axes scroll at all: Radix sets `overflow: hidden` on the axis without a scrollbar, so `orientation="vertical"` (the default) clips horizontal overflow and `"horizontal"` clips vertical overflow. Use `"both"` for two-way scrolling.
- Radix wraps the children in a `display: table; min-width: 100%` div, so long unbroken text or wide content widens the area (that is what makes horizontal scrolling work) instead of wrapping or truncating.
- `type` is a Radix prop (default `"hover"`; also `auto`, `always`, `scroll`). `viewportRef` is the element to `scrollTo` or attach scroll listeners to; the root `ref` is not the scroller. `fadeEdges` takes `true`, `"vertical"` or `"horizontal"` and fades only the edges that still have content beyond them.

## ScrollBar

> Thin scrollbar track + thumb; rendered automatically by `ScrollArea`.

- Import: `import { ScrollBar } from "@sutra/ui"` (or from `@sutra/ui/core`)
- Source: `packages/ui/src/primitives/scroll-area` (primitives)
- Also accepts the props of HTMLAttributes, PrimitivePropsWithRef, ScrollAreaScrollbarProps, ScrollAreaScrollbarVisibleProps

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `thumbClassName` | `string` |  | Classes for the draggable thumb. |

### Notes

**When to use:** A scrolling region with thin overlay scrollbars that match the theme, optional edge fades and a ref to the viewport. Scrolling stays native (wheel, touch, keyboard). A plain `overflow-auto scrollbar-thin` element is enough when only a thin native scrollbar is needed.

**Use instead when:**
- `Carousel`: paged or snapping content that moves in steps

#### Keyboard

The custom scrollbars and thumbs are for the pointer only and are not focusable. Nothing swaps in RTL.

#### Screen readers

Adds no state: the content reads in its normal order and the scrollbars are not exposed. Pass `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` when the region needs a name: they go on the viewport, which then has `role="region"` (without a name it has no role). The edge fades are a visual mask only.

#### Reduced motion

With the default `type="hover"` the scrollbars do not exist until the pointer enters after mount, `fadeEdges` shows no fades until the edges are measured in an effect, and the root `dir` is read after mount (the server writes `ltr`), so the first server paint of an RTL page has `dir="ltr"` on the area.

#### Gotchas

- Give it a bounded size: the root is `overflow-hidden`, so without a height (`className="h-64"`) or a `max-h` (`viewportClassName`) it grows with its content and nothing scrolls.
- `orientation` decides which axes scroll at all: Radix sets `overflow: hidden` on the axis without a scrollbar, so `orientation="vertical"` (the default) clips horizontal overflow and `"horizontal"` clips vertical overflow. Use `"both"` for two-way scrolling.
- Radix wraps the children in a `display: table; min-width: 100%` div, so long unbroken text or wide content widens the area (that is what makes horizontal scrolling work) instead of wrapping or truncating.
- `type` is a Radix prop (default `"hover"`; also `auto`, `always`, `scroll`). `viewportRef` is the element to `scrollTo` or attach scroll listeners to; the root `ref` is not the scroller. `fadeEdges` takes `true`, `"vertical"` or `"horizontal"` and fades only the edges that still have content beyond them.

## SearchInput

> Search field with an icon, a keyboard shortcut hint and a clear button.

- Import: `import { SearchInput } from "@sutra/ui"` (or from `@sutra/ui/forms`)
- Source: `packages/ui/src/primitives/input` (primitives)
- Also accepts the props of HTMLAttributes, InputHTMLAttributes

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `className` | `string` |  | Classes for the element that renders. Without addons that is the `<input>` itself (the root). With addons (`leadingIcon`, `trailingIcon`, `prefix`, `suffix`, `clearable`) it lands on the **inner** `<input>`, not the outer wrapper, so layout classes (`w-48`, `flex-1`, margins) have no visible effect there; use `wrapperClassName` for those. |
| `clearable` | `boolean` | `true` | Shows a clear button while the field has a value. |
| `hotkey` | `string` |  | Global shortcut that focuses the field, e.g. "/" or "mod+k" (⌘ on macOS, Ctrl elsewhere). Also rendered as a key hint unless `shortcut` is provided. |
| `invalid` | `boolean` |  | Marks the field invalid: error border and `aria-invalid`. Inherited from a surrounding `Field` when omitted. |
| `onClear` | `() => void` |  | Called after the clear button empties the field. |
| `prefix` | `React.ReactNode` |  | Text addon before the field, e.g. "https://". |
| `shortcut` | `React.ReactNode \| string[]` |  | Custom key hint shown while the field is empty (strings render as `Kbd`). |
| `size` | `"sm" \| "md" \| "lg" \| null` | `"md"` | Field height and text size. |
| `suffix` | `React.ReactNode` |  | Text addon after the field, e.g. ".com". |
| `trailingIcon` | `React.ReactNode` |  | Icon or small action rendered inside the field after the text. |
| `variant` | `"outline" \| "filled" \| null` |  | `outline` (default) is the bordered box; `filled` is a tinted surface with a hidden border. |
| `wrapperClassName` | `string` |  | Classes for the outer wrapper `<div>`, which is only rendered when addons are present. Put layout/sizing classes here when the input has addons. |

### Notes

**When to use:** The single-line text field. It takes every native `<input>` prop and adds `leadingIcon`, `trailingIcon`, `prefix`, `suffix` and `clearable`. `PasswordInput` adds a show and hide toggle, `SearchInput` a search icon, a clear button and an optional focus hotkey.

**Use instead when:**
- `Textarea`: several lines
- `NumberInput`: numbers with steppers and locale formatting
- `InputGroup`: addons that are real buttons, selects or other controls
- `InputOTP`: a one-time code split into slots
- `Combobox`: a choice from a list
- `TagInput`: several free-form tags

#### Keyboard

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Moves to and from the field and the `PasswordInput` toggle. The `clearable` button is not a tab stop (`tabIndex` -1) |
| Enter, Space | On the `PasswordInput` toggle: show or hide the text |
| Escape | In a `SearchInput` that has text and `clearable`: empty it and call `onClear` |
| `hotkey` (for example `/` or `mod+k`) | Anywhere on the page: focus and select the `SearchInput`. A plain key typed into another field stays text; a chord with Ctrl or Meta still fires |

Typing is native. There are no arrow-key handlers, and the icons and addons use logical padding, so RTL only mirrors the layout.

#### Screen readers

- A native `<input>` named by a `<label>`, `aria-label` or a surrounding `FieldLabel`; a field with no visible label needs `aria-label`. `invalid` sets `aria-invalid`, and `Field` adds `id`, `aria-describedby`, `disabled` and `required` unless you pass them.
- `SearchInput` is `type="search"` (role `searchbox`), sets `aria-keyshortcuts` from `hotkey`, and hides the key hint (`aria-hidden`).
- The clear button is named "Clear" (not translatable through a prop). The `PasswordInput` toggle is named "Show password" or "Hide password" and also carries `aria-pressed`. Icons are `aria-hidden`; `leadingIcon`, `trailingIcon`, `prefix` and `suffix` content that you pass is not hidden for you.

#### Reduced motion

The clear button pops in with `animate-in fade-in-0 zoom-in-75`, and the border and ring fade with a short transition; the reduced-motion net removes the zoom and ends the transitions in 1 ms.

#### Server rendering

Server render: part of it fills in after mount. `Input` and `PasswordInput` render the same markup on both sides, including the clear button when a `value` or `defaultValue` is set. `SearchInput` reads its key hint after mount (`hotkey` is turned into key labels in an effect), so the hint chips are not in the server HTML and appear on hydration.

#### Slots

- `input`: the `<input>` element (the root when there are no addons)
- `input-wrapper`: the outer `div`, rendered only when an icon, addon or `clearable` is present

#### Gotchas

- `className` lands on the inner `<input>` once any addon is present, so layout classes (`w-48`, `flex-1`) do nothing there; put them in `wrapperClassName`. Without addons `className` is the root.
- `PasswordInput` defaults to `autoComplete="current-password"` (pass `"new-password"` when setting one), turns off `spellCheck`, and does not accept `type` or `trailingIcon`.
- `clearable` fires a real `input` event, so `onChange` runs with an empty value, then `onClear`. `SearchInput` is `clearable` by default.
- Pass `prefix` and `suffix` as text addons; for interactive addons use `InputGroup`.

## SegmentedControl

> Single-choice segmented control with an animated sliding thumb.

- Import: `import { SegmentedControl } from "@sutra/ui"` (or from `@sutra/ui/forms`)
- Source: `packages/ui/src/primitives/segmented-control` (primitives)
- Parts: [`SegmentedControlItem`](SegmentedControlItem.md)
- Also accepts the props of HTMLAttributes, ToggleGroupImplProps, PrimitivePropsWithRef

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `defaultValue` | `string` |  | Initially selected item value when uncontrolled. |
| `fullWidth` | `boolean` | `false` | Stretch to the container and split segments evenly. |
| `onValueChange` | `(value: string) => void` |  | Called with the value of the segment the user picked. |
| `options` | `SegmentedControlOption[]` |  | Data-driven alternative to `SegmentedControlItem` children. |
| `size` | `Size` | `"md"` | Control height and text size. |
| `value` | `string` |  | Controlled selected item value. Use with `onValueChange`. |

### Variants

- `size`: `sm`, `md`, `lg` (default "md")
- `fullWidth`: `true` (default false)

### Part props

Props of `SegmentedControlItem`: see [the full page](md/SegmentedControl.md).

### Notes

**When to use:** One choice from two to four short options that switch a view or a mode, drawn as a pill with a sliding thumb. Pass `options`, or compose `SegmentedControlItem` children; icon-only segments are square.

**Use instead when:**
- `RadioGroup`: options need descriptions or must read as a form field
- `Select`: more than a handful of options
- `Tabs`: the choice swaps panels of content
- `ToggleGroup`: loose on/off buttons that can all be off
- `ButtonGroup`: attached action buttons

#### Keyboard

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab / Shift+Tab | One tab stop: the selected segment (the first one when none is selected) |
| ArrowRight, ArrowLeft, ArrowDown, ArrowUp | Move focus to the next or previous enabled segment, looping at the ends |
| Home, End | Focus the first or last segment |
| Enter, Space | Select the focused segment |

Arrow keys move focus only; selecting needs Enter or Space. In RTL the horizontal arrows swap (ArrowLeft goes to the next segment), because Radix roving focus reads the `dir` that the control passes down: a `DirectionProvider`, a `dir` container or `<html dir>`, or a `dir` you set yourself.

#### Screen readers

- The root is `role="radiogroup"` and each segment is a `role="radio"` button with `aria-checked`. The group has no name of its own: pass `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`.
- A segment is named by its label text. An icon-only segment has no text, so give it `aria-label` (an `options` entry takes `"aria-label"`). The sliding thumb is `aria-hidden`.
- Disabled segments are skipped by focus.

#### Reduced motion

The thumb slides with a 300 ms transform transition and the label colours fade in 200 ms; the reduced-motion net ends both in 1 ms, so the thumb jumps. The thumb never animates on the first frame, it appears in place.

#### Server rendering

Server render: part of it fills in after mount. The segments render on the server with the selected one marked, but the thumb behind it is measured after mount, so the server HTML shows the selection by text colour only and the pill appears on hydration. The group's `dir` is `ltr` in the server HTML and settles after hydration on an RTL page.

#### Gotchas

- It is a single-select that never deselects: clicking the selected segment keeps it, and `onValueChange` does not fire for it (it receives a string, never an empty one).
- With `options` and no `value` or `defaultValue` the first option is selected; with `SegmentedControlItem` children and no `defaultValue` nothing is selected until the user picks.
- The root has `overflow-x-auto` and `max-w-full`, so many options scroll sideways in a narrow column instead of overflowing. `fullWidth` stretches the root and splits the segments evenly.
- Extra props (including `dir`, `disabled`, `loop`) go to the Radix root; a `dir` you pass overrides the detected direction.

## Select

> Root of a select: Radix `Select.Root` with the reading direction filled in.

- Import: `import { Select } from "@sutra/ui"` (or from `@sutra/ui/forms`)
- Source: `packages/ui/src/primitives/select` (primitives)
- Parts: [`SelectContent`](SelectContent.md), [`SelectGroup`](SelectGroup.md), [`SelectItem`](SelectItem.md), [`SelectLabel`](SelectLabel.md), [`SelectScrollDownButton`](SelectScrollDownButton.md), [`SelectScrollUpButton`](SelectScrollUpButton.md), [`SelectSeparator`](SelectSeparator.md), [`SelectTrigger`](SelectTrigger.md), [`SelectValue`](SelectValue.md)
- Also accepts the props of SelectSharedProps, SelectProps

### Props

No props of its own.

### Part props

Props of `SelectItem`, `SelectTrigger`: see [the full page](md/Select.md).

### Notes

**When to use:** A single choice from a short list, shown as an input-like trigger and a floating listbox. `SimpleSelect` takes an `options` array, the compound parts give full control.

**Use instead when:**
- `Combobox`: the list is long, searchable or loaded from a server
- `RadioGroup`: every option should stay visible
- `SegmentedControl`: two to four options that switch a view
- `WheelPicker`: a touch-first scrolling picker

#### Keyboard

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| Enter, Space, ArrowDown, ArrowUp | On the trigger: open the list |
| A letter or digit | On the closed trigger, selects the next matching option; in the open list, moves to it |
| ArrowDown, ArrowUp | Move the highlighted option |
| Home, End | Highlight the first or last option |
| Enter, Space | Pick the highlighted option and close |
| Escape | Close without changing the value |
| Tab | Does nothing while the list is open (Radix blocks it), so close first |

The list is vertical, so the arrow keys do not swap in RTL. The `dir` of the root follows the document or the nearest `DirectionProvider`, so the popover opens on the correct side.

#### Screen readers

The trigger is a `combobox` with `aria-expanded`; the list is a `listbox` of `option`s with the selected one marked. `SelectGroup` plus `SelectLabel` announce the group name. `SimpleSelect` forwards `aria-label`, `aria-labelledby` and `aria-describedby` to the trigger and reads `invalid`, `disabled`, `required` and `id` from a surrounding `Field`, which also sets `aria-invalid` and `aria-required`. A select with no visible label needs an `aria-label`.

#### Reduced motion

The popover fades and zooms in from the trigger with the `animate-in` utilities and the chevron turns with `chevron-turn`; under reduced motion the net removes the zoom and slide (the fade stays) and the chevron turn ends in 1 ms.

#### Server rendering

Server render: part of it fills in after mount. The trigger renders on the server, but the option list lives in a fragment created after mount, so a select that starts with a `value` or `defaultValue` shows an empty trigger (or the placeholder) in the server HTML and the selected label appears after hydration. Reserve the trigger width with `className` to avoid a jump.

#### Gotchas

- Radix Select needs a non-empty string for every item `value`; an empty string is reserved for clearing back to the placeholder.
- `SelectContent` uses `position="popper"`, `sideOffset` 6 and the trigger width by default; pass `position="item-aligned"` for the native-style overlap, which then ignores `sideOffset`.
- `SelectItem description` shows only in the list: the trigger shows the item's own text (and `icon`).
- Inside a `<form>`, give the root a `name` so Radix renders its hidden native `<select>`; `required` and `disabled` go on the root or on `Field`.

## Separator

> Horizontal or vertical rule, optionally with a centered label.

- Import: `import { Separator } from "@sutra/ui"` (or from `@sutra/ui/core`)
- Source: `packages/ui/src/primitives/separator` (primitives)
- Also accepts the props of HTMLAttributes, SeparatorProps, PrimitivePropsWithRef

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `label` | `React.ReactNode` |  | Text or content shown inside the line. `children` works too. |
| `labelPosition` | `"start" \| "center" \| "end"` | `"center"` | Where the label sits along the line. |
| `variant` | `"solid" \| "dashed"` | `"solid"` | Line style. |

### Notes

**When to use:** A horizontal or vertical rule, solid or dashed, optionally with a label in the line ("OR", "Section"). `ContentDivider` is the deprecated alias of the same component.

**Use instead when:**
- `ItemSeparator`: the hairline inside an `ItemGroup`
- `Frame`: grouped rows with a tray
- `Stack`: spacing without a line

#### Keyboard

Not focusable: no keyboard interaction.

#### Screen readers

- Decorative by default: `decorative` is `true`, so the element is `role="none"` and assistive technology skips it. This is the opposite of the Radix default. Pass `decorative={false}` for a real `role="separator"` between regions of content; a vertical one then also gets `aria-orientation="vertical"` (horizontal is the implicit default and is not written).
- A `label` (or `children`) is ordinary text and is read by screen readers whether or not the line is decorative.

#### Reduced motion

Static: no animation.

#### Server rendering

Server render: same markup as the client. Plain markup with no browser API, so server and client output match.

#### Gotchas

- A vertical separator has no height of its own: it stretches to the row it sits in (`self-stretch`), so put it in a flex row. A `className` with an `h-` or `size-` class switches it to a fixed height centred in the row instead.
- With a label, `labelPosition` is `center` (default), `start` or `end`; the short side of the line is a stub (1rem, or 0.5rem when vertical). A vertical labelled separator is at least 4rem tall.
- `variant="dashed"` only changes the line style. The line colour is the `border` token; override with a `border-*` class.
- `ContentDivider` is the same object as `Separator`; use `Separator` in new code.

## Sheet

> Edge-anchored panel root (a Dialog).

- Import: `import { Sheet } from "@sutra/ui"` (or from `@sutra/ui/overlays`)
- Source: `packages/ui/src/primitives/dialog` (primitives)
- Parts: [`SheetBody`](SheetBody.md), [`SheetClose`](SheetClose.md), [`SheetContent`](SheetContent.md), [`SheetDescription`](SheetDescription.md), [`SheetFooter`](SheetFooter.md), [`SheetHeader`](SheetHeader.md), [`SheetTitle`](SheetTitle.md), [`SheetTrigger`](SheetTrigger.md)
- Also accepts the props of DialogProps

Dialog vs Sheet vs Drawer: `Sheet` slides in from `side` (left, right, top, bottom) and stays put; `Dialog` is a centred modal; `Drawer` is a touch-first bottom sheet with a grabber, drag-to-dismiss and snap points, built on the Sheet parts below.

### Props

No props of its own.

### Part props

Props of `SheetContent`: see [the full page](md/Sheet.md).

### Notes

**When to use:** A modal panel that slides in from an edge (right by default) and keeps the page visible behind a scrim, for detail, filter, settings and navigation panels. Sizes, `detached` and `blur` looks, logical `start` and `end` sides, and stacked nested sheets.

**Use instead when:**
- `Dialog`: a centred modal for one decision or task
- `Drawer`: a touch-first bottom sheet you drag with snap points
- `Popover`: a small panel that does not block the page
- `Collapsible`: content that expands in the page instead of overlaying it

#### Keyboard

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Cycle focus inside the sheet (trapped while open) |
| Escape | Close the sheet; ignored with `dismissible={false}` |
| Enter, Space | Activate the focused button, including the close button |

Focus moves into the sheet on open and returns to whatever had it before, even when it was opened without a `SheetTrigger` (a hotkey, controlled `open`). There are no arrow keys, so RTL changes nothing. With stacked sheets Escape closes only the topmost.

#### Screen readers

The panel is a Radix dialog: `role="dialog"` with `aria-labelledby` from `SheetTitle` and `aria-describedby` from `SheetDescription`, and the page behind is hidden from assistive technology while it is open. Always render a `SheetTitle` (it may be visually hidden). The built-in close button is labelled "Close" and appears when `dismissible` is true (or with `showClose`).

#### Reduced motion

The panel slides in from its edge and the sheet underneath a nested one scales down and fades; the reduced-motion net removes the slide, keeps the fade and ends the scale and opacity transition in 1 ms.

#### Server rendering

Server render: same markup as the client. A closed sheet renders only its trigger on the server and the client. The panel is portalled into `<body>` after mount, so a sheet that is `open` on first render appears after hydration. Being portalled, it does not sit inside a subtree `dir` or `data-style`: the `start` and `end` sides and the `rtl:` flips read `<html dir>`, so set it there.

#### Slots

- `sheet-content`: the panel (`data-side`, plus `data-detached` and `data-nested` when set)

#### Gotchas

- `side` accepts `left`, `right`, `top`, `bottom` (fixed edges) and `start`, `end` (follow the document direction, so `start` is the right edge in RTL). Prefer `start` and `end` for side navigation.
- `size` is a width for side sheets and a height for `top` and `bottom` (`auto`, `sm`, `md`, `lg`, `half`, `full`); without it a side sheet is 24rem wide (up to 85vw) and a top or bottom sheet is as tall as its content. `className` still wins over it.
- `dismissible={false}` ignores Escape and outside clicks and hides the close button, so give users another way out (`showClose` brings the button back; a `SheetClose` or controlled `open` also closes it).
- Nested sheets stack only when the inner `Sheet` is rendered inside the outer `SheetContent`; the one underneath gets `data-nested`. `Sheet` is the Radix Dialog root, so `open`, `defaultOpen`, `onOpenChange` and `modal` work as in `Dialog`.

## ShortcutKeys

> Renders a keys spec as platform-aware Kbd chips, with "then" between sequence steps.

- Import: `import { ShortcutKeys } from "@sutra/ui"` (or from `@sutra/ui/suite`)
- Source: `packages/ui/src/primitives/shortcut-keys` (primitives)
- Also accepts the props of HTMLAttributes

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `keys` (required) | `string` |  | Keys spec: "mod+k", "shift+?", "g t". |
| `kbdClassName` | `string` |  | Classes for each Kbd chip. |
| `platform` | `ShortcutPlatform` |  | Platform whose key glyphs are shown (`mac` shows ⌘ and ⌥). Defaults to the detected or provided platform. |
| `size` | `"sm" \| "md"` | `"sm"` | Key chip size. |

### Notes

**When to use:** Renders a key spec ("mod+k", "shift+?", "g t") as platform-aware key chips, with "then" between the steps of a sequence. It is display only.

**Use instead when:**
- `Kbd`: a single key chip you write yourself
- `ShortcutProvider`: actually register and handle shortcuts
- `ShortcutsDialog`: a help sheet listing the live shortcuts
- `CommandShortcut`: the hint at the end of a command item

#### Keyboard

Not focusable, and it does not listen for the keys it shows: pair it with `useShortcut` or `ShortcutProvider` to make the shortcut work.

#### Screen readers

The chips are `aria-hidden` and a visually hidden sentence is read instead, spelled out per platform: "Shift Command K" for `mod+shift+k` on a Mac, and a sequence reads "G then T". The glyphs (command, shift, option) are therefore never read aloud. The root is a plain `span` with `data-shortcut` set to the spec.

#### Reduced motion

Static: no animation.

#### Server rendering

Server render: part of it fills in after mount. The server has no `navigator` and uses the non-Mac labels ("Ctrl", "Shift"). The hydrating client render uses the same default, so the markup matches, and a Mac browser switches to the glyphs (command, option) right after hydration, before paint. A client-only render detects the platform at once. Pass `platform` (or set it on a `ShortcutProvider`, which `ShortcutKeys` reads) to make the first render already right.

#### Gotchas

- `keys` is a spec, not display text: `mod` means Command on a Mac and Ctrl elsewhere, a space separates the steps of a sequence ("g t"), and `+` joins keys that are held together. A string of ready-made glyphs ("⌘K") is not a spec; render it in `Kbd` yourself.
- `platform` is `mac` or `other`; without it the platform comes from the nearest `ShortcutProvider`, else from the browser. `size` is `sm` or `md`, and `kbdClassName` styles each chip.
- Each chip is a `Kbd`, so it renders a real `<kbd>` element; it is hidden from assistive technology here only because the spoken sentence replaces it.

## SimpleSelect

> Data-driven select: pass `options` and get a styled trigger + list.

- Import: `import { SimpleSelect } from "@sutra/ui"` (or from `@sutra/ui/forms`)
- Source: `packages/ui/src/primitives/select` (primitives)
- Also accepts the props of SelectSharedProps, SelectProps

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `options` (required) | `SelectOption[]` |  | Options to render, in order; each has a `value`, a `label` and optional description, icon and disabled flag. |
| `aria-describedby` | `string` |  | Id(s) of the element(s) that describe the trigger (hint, error text). |
| `aria-invalid` | `boolean` |  | Overrides the invalid state announced to assistive technology; normally set `invalid` instead. |
| `aria-label` | `string` |  | Accessible name of the trigger when there is no visible label. |
| `aria-labelledby` | `string` |  | Id(s) of the element(s) that label the trigger. |
| `className` | `string` |  | Classes for the trigger. |
| `contentClassName` | `string` |  | Classes for the popover list. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` |  | Disables the select. Inherited from a surrounding `Field` when omitted. |
| `id` | `string` |  | `id` of the trigger, so a `<label htmlFor>` or `Field` can point at it. |
| `invalid` | `boolean` |  | Marks the select invalid: error border and `aria-invalid`. Inherited from a surrounding `Field` when omitted. |
| `leadingIcon` | `React.ReactNode` |  | Icon shown at the start of the trigger. |
| `placeholder` | `React.ReactNode` | `"Select…"` | Trigger text while nothing is selected. |
| `required` | `boolean` |  | Marks the select required. Inherited from a surrounding `Field` when omitted. |
| `size` | `"sm" \| "md" \| "lg"` | `"md"` | Trigger height and text size. |

### Variants

- `size`: `sm`, `md`, `lg` (default "md")

### Notes

**When to use:** A single choice from a short list, shown as an input-like trigger and a floating listbox. `SimpleSelect` takes an `options` array, the compound parts give full control.

**Use instead when:**
- `Combobox`: the list is long, searchable or loaded from a server
- `RadioGroup`: every option should stay visible
- `SegmentedControl`: two to four options that switch a view
- `WheelPicker`: a touch-first scrolling picker

#### Keyboard

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| Enter, Space, ArrowDown, ArrowUp | On the trigger: open the list |
| A letter or digit | On the closed trigger, selects the next matching option; in the open list, moves to it |
| ArrowDown, ArrowUp | Move the highlighted option |
| Home, End | Highlight the first or last option |
| Enter, Space | Pick the highlighted option and close |
| Escape | Close without changing the value |
| Tab | Does nothing while the list is open (Radix blocks it), so close first |

The list is vertical, so the arrow keys do not swap in RTL. The `dir` of the root follows the document or the nearest `DirectionProvider`, so the popover opens on the correct side.

#### Screen readers

The trigger is a `combobox` with `aria-expanded`; the list is a `listbox` of `option`s with the selected one marked. `SelectGroup` plus `SelectLabel` announce the group name. `SimpleSelect` forwards `aria-label`, `aria-labelledby` and `aria-describedby` to the trigger and reads `invalid`, `disabled`, `required` and `id` from a surrounding `Field`, which also sets `aria-invalid` and `aria-required`. A select with no visible label needs an `aria-label`.

#### Reduced motion

The popover fades and zooms in from the trigger with the `animate-in` utilities and the chevron turns with `chevron-turn`; under reduced motion the net removes the zoom and slide (the fade stays) and the chevron turn ends in 1 ms.

#### Server rendering

Server render: part of it fills in after mount. The trigger renders on the server, but the option list lives in a fragment created after mount, so a select that starts with a `value` or `defaultValue` shows an empty trigger (or the placeholder) in the server HTML and the selected label appears after hydration. Reserve the trigger width with `className` to avoid a jump.

#### Gotchas

- Radix Select needs a non-empty string for every item `value`; an empty string is reserved for clearing back to the placeholder.
- `SelectContent` uses `position="popper"`, `sideOffset` 6 and the trigger width by default; pass `position="item-aligned"` for the native-style overlap, which then ignores `sideOffset`.
- `SelectItem description` shows only in the list: the trigger shows the item's own text (and `icon`).
- Inside a `<form>`, give the root a `name` so Radix renders its hidden native `<select>`; `required` and `disabled` go on the root or on `Field`.

## SimpleTooltip

> One-line tooltip wrapper: `<SimpleTooltip content="Save" shortcut="⌘S"><Button/></SimpleTooltip>`.

- Import: `import { SimpleTooltip } from "@sutra/ui"` (or from `@sutra/ui/overlays`)
- Source: `packages/ui/src/primitives/tooltip` (primitives)
- Also accepts the props of TooltipProps

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `children` (required) | `React.ReactNode` |  | The element the tooltip describes; it must accept a ref and focus. |
| `content` (required) | `React.ReactNode` |  | Tooltip content. |
| `align` | `TooltipContentProps["align"]` |  | Alignment of the tooltip along that side. |
| `contentClassName` | `string` |  | Classes for the tooltip bubble. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` |  | Skip the tooltip entirely (renders children only). |
| `shortcut` | `string \| string[]` |  | Keyboard shortcut. A keys spec ("mod+k", "g t") renders platform-aware chips; a glyph string ("⌘K") or an array (["⌘", "K"]) renders one Kbd per entry. |
| `side` | `TooltipContentProps["side"]` | `"top"` | Side of the trigger the tooltip opens on; it flips when there is no room. |
| `variant` | `TooltipContentProps["variant"]` | `"inverse"` | Look of the bubble: `inverse` (dark) or `light` (bordered popover surface). |

### Variants

- `variant`: `inverse`, `light` (default "inverse")

### Notes

**When to use:** A short text label that appears when an element is hovered or focused, for icon buttons and truncated text. `SimpleTooltip` is the one-line form with an optional keyboard `shortcut` chip.

**Use instead when:**
- `Popover`: interactive or rich content the user can click into
- `HoverCard`: a rich preview on hover
- `InfoTooltip`: a help icon with a title and description
- `Dialog`: anything the user must read or act on

#### Keyboard

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Focusing the trigger opens the tooltip after the delay; moving focus away closes it |
| Escape | Close the tooltip while its trigger has focus |

The tooltip has no focusable content and the trigger keeps its own keyboard behaviour. There are no arrow keys, so RTL changes nothing. In RTL, `side="start"` and `side="end"` swap left and right (read through `useDirection()`: a `DirectionProvider` with a `dir`, else `<html dir>`; a plain `dir` attribute on a container is not seen); the default is `top`, `left` and `right` stay physical, and Radix still flips the bubble on a collision. Pressing the trigger (click, Enter or Space) also closes the tooltip.

#### Screen readers

The content is `role="tooltip"` and, while open, the trigger gets `aria-describedby` pointing at it, so it is read as the trigger's description, not its name. Give icon-only triggers an `aria-label`: the tooltip alone does not name them. If you pass `aria-label` to `TooltipContent`, Radix hides the visual content from assistive technology and exposes that label in a visually hidden `role="tooltip"` copy. The arrow is decoration. Keep tooltip text short and plain; no links or buttons.

#### Reduced motion

The bubble fades and zooms in from its trigger and slides slightly from its side; the reduced-motion net removes the slide and the scale and keeps only the fade. The open delay is a timer and stays.

#### Server rendering

Server render: same markup as the client. Only the trigger renders on the server; the bubble is portalled after mount and only opens from pointer hover or focus. Nothing differs between server and client.

#### Gotchas

- The default open delay is 200 ms (`TooltipProvider` and a provider-less `Tooltip` both fall back to 200, not Radix's 700), and `skipDelayDuration` is 300 ms. Mount one `TooltipProvider` near the root so moving between tooltips skips the delay; without one each `Tooltip` makes its own provider.
- Touch does not open it: Radix ignores touch pointers and a tap closes it, so never keep essential information only in a tooltip.
- `SimpleTooltip` wraps `children` in `TooltipTrigger asChild`, so the child must accept a ref and forward props to a focusable element. It renders just the children when `disabled`, or when `content` is `null`, `undefined` or `false`.
- `SimpleTooltip shortcut` is display only: a spec like `"mod+k"` renders platform-aware chips, a glyph string or an array renders one `Kbd` per entry. Nothing is bound to the keys.

## Skeleton

> Loading placeholder with a shimmer.

- Import: `import { Skeleton } from "@sutra/ui"` (or from `@sutra/ui/core`)
- Source: `packages/ui/src/primitives/progress` (primitives)
- Also accepts the props of HTMLAttributes

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `height` | `number \| string` |  | Height of the placeholder (px number or CSS length); a circle without a height is as tall as it is wide. |
| `lines` | `number` | `1` | Number of text lines (shape "text" only). The last line is shorter. |
| `shape` | `"text" \| "circle" \| "rect"` | `"rect"` | What the placeholder looks like: text lines, a circle (avatar) or a rectangle. |
| `shimmer` | `boolean` | `true` | Shimmer sweep instead of a pulse. Default true. |
| `width` | `number \| string` |  | Width of the placeholder (px number or CSS length); defaults to the full width. |

### Notes

**When to use:** A loading placeholder shaped like the content to come: text lines, a circle or a rectangle, with a shimmer sweep or a pulse.

**Use instead when:**
- `Spinner`: a short wait with no content shape
- `Progress`: a known amount of work
- `Meter`: a level that is not loading

#### Keyboard

Not focusable: no keyboard interaction.

#### Screen readers

Every skeleton is `aria-hidden`, so it is invisible to assistive technology. Announce the wait yourself: set `aria-busy="true"` on the region being loaded, and add visually hidden text ("Loading profile…") or a status message, as the loading states of `Meter` and `BatteryLevel` do.

#### Reduced motion

The shimmer (`animate-shimmer`) and the pulse both carry `motion-reduce:animate-none`, so a skeleton is a still muted block.

#### Server rendering

Server render: same markup as the client. Plain `div` markup with no browser API, so server and client output match, which makes skeletons the right fallback for streamed content.

#### Gotchas

- `shape` defaults to `"rect"` (96 px tall, full width). `"circle"` is 40 px unless you pass `width` (the height follows the width); `"text"` is one line high.
- `lines` only applies to `shape="text"` and makes a stack with a shorter last line (60 percent wide); the wrapper takes `width`, the lines take `height`.
- `shimmer={false}` swaps the sweep for `animate-pulse`.
- `width` and `height` accept a number (px) or any CSS length, and they win over `className` sizes because they are inline styles.

## Slider

> Range input with one or more thumbs, optional value bubble and labeled marks. `ref` and `className` land on the outer wrapper (which also holds the marks); the other props go to the Radix slider root inside it.

- Import: `import { Slider } from "@sutra/ui"` (or from `@sutra/ui/forms`)
- Source: `packages/ui/src/primitives/slider` (primitives)
- Also accepts the props of HTMLAttributes, SliderProps, PrimitivePropsWithRef

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `accent` | `Accent` |  | Categorical colour for the range, thumb border and active marks. Default primary. |
| `formatValue` | `(value: number) => React.ReactNode` | `(v) => v` | Formats the number shown in the value bubble (see `showValue`). Default shows the raw value. |
| `getValueText` | `(value: number, index: number) => string` |  | Accessible value text per thumb (`aria-valuetext`), e.g. `(v) => v + "%"`. |
| `invalid` | `boolean` |  | Marks the slider invalid: error styling on the range and `aria-invalid`. Inherited from a surrounding `Field` when omitted. |
| `marks` | `(number \| SliderMark)[]` |  | Tick marks under the track; numbers or `{ value, label }`. |
| `showValue` | `boolean \| "always"` | `false` | Show a value bubble above the thumb on hover, focus and drag. `"always"` keeps it visible. |
| `size` | `Size` | `"md"` | Track and thumb size. |
| `thumbLabels` | `string[]` |  | Accessible labels per thumb, e.g. `["Volume"]` or `["Minimum", "Maximum"]`. Without it a single thumb is named by `aria-label` / `aria-labelledby` (or the surrounding `FieldLabel`); two thumbs are "Minimum" and "Maximum". |
| `tone` | `ToneInput` |  | Semantic colour (`success`, `warning`, …). Takes precedence over `accent`. |

### Notes

**When to use:** Pick a number, or a range with two thumbs, by dragging along a track. The value is always an array (`[40]`, or `[10, 80]` for `RangeSlider`). It has an optional value bubble, tick marks, `accent` and `tone` colours, and a vertical orientation.

**Use instead when:**
- `NumberInput`: an exact number is typed or stepped
- `VolumeSlider`: a slider with a mute toggle and level readout
- `Progress`: a level the user cannot change
- `Rating`: a few discrete stars
- `SegmentedControl`: a few labelled steps

#### Keyboard

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Each thumb is a tab stop |
| ArrowRight, ArrowUp | Raise the focused thumb by one `step` |
| ArrowLeft, ArrowDown | Lower it by one `step` |
| Shift+Arrow, PageUp, PageDown | Move ten steps (PageUp raises, PageDown lowers) |
| Home, End | Set the first thumb to `min` and the last thumb to `max`, whichever thumb has focus |

In RTL on a horizontal slider ArrowLeft raises and ArrowRight lowers, and the track fills from the right; Up and Down do not change. The direction is read from the parent (a `DirectionProvider`, a `dir` container or `<html dir>`), and a `dir` you pass wins. Thumbs keep a minimum gap of `minStepsBetweenThumbs` steps (1 for `RangeSlider`).

#### Screen readers

- Each thumb is a `role="slider"` with `aria-valuemin`, `aria-valuemax`, `aria-valuenow` and `aria-orientation`. A single thumb is named by `thumbLabels` (such as `["Volume"]`), else by `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` on the `Slider`, else by a surrounding `FieldLabel`; two thumbs are named "Minimum" and "Maximum" by default (an `aria-label` on the `Slider` then becomes a `role="group"` around them), more are "Value 1 of 3" and so on. `getValueText` sets `aria-valuetext` per thumb, for example `(v) => v + "%"`.
- `id` stays on the Radix root `span` (which has no role), so a `FieldLabel` click does not focus a thumb. The slider reads `Field`: its id, `disabled`, invalid state and description, hint and error ids (`aria-describedby`, also on every thumb); an explicit prop wins.
- The value bubble and the tick marks and their labels are `aria-hidden`; put what matters in `getValueText`. `invalid` (or an invalid `Field`) sets `aria-invalid` on the root and on each thumb and turns the range red.

#### Reduced motion

The thumb ring, press scale and value bubble use short transitions, which the reduced-motion net ends in 1 ms.

#### Server rendering

Server render: part of it fills in after mount. The track and range render on the server from `value` or `defaultValue`, but each thumb is `display: none` until Radix has mounted and located it, so the thumbs appear after hydration. The direction is `ltr` in the server HTML and settles after hydration on an RTL page.

#### Gotchas

- `value` and `defaultValue` are arrays, and `onValueChange` receives the whole array. `onValueCommit` fires when a drag or key press ends.
- `ref` and `className` go to the outer wrapper (which also holds the marks); every other prop, including `disabled`, `step`, `name` and `orientation`, goes to the Radix root inside it. `name` posts one hidden input per thumb (named `name[]` for a range) inside a form.
- `showValue` shows the bubble on hover, focus and drag; `"always"` keeps it. `marks` take numbers or `{ value, label }` and only mark; they do not snap the value (use `step`).
- A given `tone` beats `accent`, and `invalid` beats both.

## SlideToConfirm

> Confirm an irreversible action by sliding the thumb along the track. It is a `role="slider"` (value 0 to 100, arrow keys step, Home resets, End and Enter and Space confirm), the offset follows the finger without React state (`useDrag`), a release short of 90% springs back, and under reduced motion the release is instant. `onConfirm` may return a promise: the control stays busy until it settles and slides back if it rejects.

- Import: `import { SlideToConfirm } from "@sutra/ui"` (or from `@sutra/ui/core`)
- Source: `packages/ui/src/primitives/slide-to-confirm` (primitives)
- `data-slot`: `slide-to-confirm`, `slide-to-confirm-fill`, `slide-to-confirm-label`, `slide-to-confirm-thumb`
- Also accepts the props of HTMLAttributes

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `confirmed` | `boolean` |  | The thumb is at the end. Pass `false` to slide it back after a confirmation. |
| `confirmedLabel` | `string` | `"Confirmed"` | Hint shown once the thumb reaches the end. |
| `defaultConfirmed` | `boolean` | `false` | Initial confirmed state when uncontrolled. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Disables dragging and the keyboard. |
| `icon` | `React.ReactNode` |  | Icon on the thumb. Default a chevron. |
| `label` | `string` | `"Slide to confirm"` | Visible hint, also the slider's accessible name. Default "Slide to confirm". |
| `loading` | `boolean` | `false` | Thumb at the end with a spinner while the action runs (a promise from `onConfirm` does the same by itself). |
| `loadingLabel` | `string` | `"Confirming…"` | Shown while the action runs. Default "Confirming…". |
| `onConfirm` | `() => void \| Promise<unknown>` |  | Runs once the thumb reaches the end (or Enter, Space or End is pressed). A returned promise keeps the control busy; a rejection slides it back. |
| `onConfirmedChange` | `(confirmed: boolean) => void` |  | Called when the control reaches or leaves the confirmed state. |
| `size` | `"sm" \| "md" \| "lg"` | `"md"` | Control height and thumb size. |
| `step` | `number` | `10` | Arrow key step in percent of the track. Default 10. |
| `tone` | `ToneInput` | `"primary"` | Colour of the thumb and the filled track. |

### Notes

**When to use:** Confirms an irreversible or deliberate action by sliding a thumb along a track. A `role="slider"` with arrow, Home, End, Enter and Space keys, a drag that follows the finger, and a spring back when released early.

**Use instead when:**
- `UndoAction`: the action can be reversed for a few seconds
- `ConfirmDialog`: a plain yes or no in a dialog
- `Button`: the action is not dangerous

#### Keyboard

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Focuses the thumb (the slider). It is skipped when `disabled` |
| ArrowRight, ArrowUp | Move forward by `step` percent (default 10); reaching 100 confirms |
| ArrowLeft, ArrowDown | Move back by `step` percent, down to 0 |
| Home | Back to 0 |
| End, Enter, Space | Confirm at once |

Keys with Alt, Ctrl or Meta held are ignored, and so are all keys once the control is `disabled`, `loading`, busy or confirmed. In RTL the thumb starts at the right and travels left, and ArrowLeft is the forward key and ArrowRight the back key (the test pins it); ArrowUp and ArrowDown do not swap.

#### Screen readers

- The thumb is the `role="slider"` (`aria-valuemin` 0, `aria-valuemax` 100, `aria-valuenow`, `aria-orientation="horizontal"`), named through `aria-labelledby` by the visible hint, "Slide to confirm" unless `label` changes it. The hint text switches to `loadingLabel` and then `confirmedLabel`, so the name follows the state.
- At the end it sets `aria-valuetext` to `confirmedLabel` or `loadingLabel`. The root gets `aria-busy` while loading and `aria-disabled` when disabled.
- A visually hidden `role="status"` says `confirmedLabel` once the control is confirmed and no longer busy.
- The fill and the thumb icon are `aria-hidden`; the spinner in the thumb is decorative.

#### Reduced motion

There are no CSS transitions: the thumb and the fill follow a CSS variable that the drag writes, and the settle after a release or a key press is a spring from `useDrag`. Under `prefers-reduced-motion` that spring is skipped and the thumb snaps straight to its place.

#### Server rendering

Server render: part of it fills in after mount. The server renders the track and the thumb at the start edge, because the width is measured after mount and the position is applied in an effect. `defaultConfirmed` or `confirmed` marks it confirmed in the markup (value 100, check icon) while the thumb jumps to the end after hydration. Direction is read as `ltr` on the server.

#### Slots

- `slide-to-confirm`: the track (the root element)
- `slide-to-confirm-fill`: the tinted fill behind the thumb
- `slide-to-confirm-label`: the hint text, which fades as the thumb moves
- `slide-to-confirm-thumb`: the draggable `slider` element

#### Gotchas

- Only the thumb starts a drag; pressing on the track does nothing. A release confirms from 90 percent of the travel, and speed alone never confirms. Vertical scrolling is left to the browser (`touch-action` is set for you).
- `onConfirm` may return a promise: the control stays busy until it settles and slides back if it rejects. A synchronous throw also slides it back and then rethrows. A resolved promise leaves it confirmed.
- Once confirmed it is locked at the end (keys and drags are ignored) until you pass `confirmed={false}`; `onConfirmedChange` reports both changes. `loading` shows the end position and a spinner without calling `onConfirm`.
- With a controlled `confirmed` that stays `false`, `onConfirm` still runs on a confirm gesture and then the thumb slides back home.

## Snackbar

> Compact dark (inverse) notification bar with an optional action, Material-style.

- Import: `import { Snackbar } from "@sutra/ui"` (or from `@sutra/ui/core`)
- Source: `packages/ui/src/primitives/toast` (primitives)
- Also accepts the props of HTMLAttributes

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `message` (required) | `React.ReactNode` |  | Notification text. |
| `action` | `SnackbarAction` |  | Optional action button on the right (`label` and `onClick`), e.g. Undo. |
| `closeLabel` | `string` | `"Dismiss"` | Accessible name of the dismiss button. |
| `icon` | `React.ReactNode` |  | Icon shown before the message. |
| `onClose` | `() => void` |  | **Deprecated.** Use `onDismiss`. Legacy name of `onDismiss`. |
| `onDismiss` | `() => void` |  | Shows a dismiss button when provided. |

### Notes

**When to use:** Transient notifications through sonner. Mount `Toaster` once, then call `toast()` or `toast.success`, `toast.error`, `toast.promise` from anywhere. `snackbar()` shows the compact dark `Snackbar`; `Snackbar` also works as a plain inline bar.

**Use instead when:**
- `InlineAlert`: a message that stays next to the content it concerns
- `AlertBanner`: a page-level notice that persists
- `ConfirmDialog`: something the user must answer
- `DialogProvider`: ask from code and wait for the answer

#### Keyboard

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| Alt+T | Anywhere on the page: expand the stack and move focus to the notifications region (sonner's default `hotkey`, changeable with `hotkey`) |
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Moves through the focusable toasts and their action, cancel and close buttons once the region is focused |
| Enter, Space | Activate the focused button |
| Escape | While focus is inside the region: collapse the stack (it does not dismiss a toast) |

The region is not in the normal tab order (`tabindex="-1"`), so keyboard users reach it only through the hotkey. Toasts can also be swiped away with a pointer. The hotkey has no arrow keys. Sonner reads the document direction (`dir="auto"`) and mirrors its buttons and icons, but `position` is physical: `bottom-right` stays on the right in RTL.

#### Screen readers

The Toaster renders a `<section aria-label="Notifications alt+T" aria-live="polite" aria-relevant="additions text" aria-atomic="false">` on first render, so new toasts are announced politely without moving focus (`containerAriaLabel` and `customAriaLabel` rename it). Toasts are focusable list items with no role of their own; the close button is named "Close toast" (`closeButtonAriaLabel`). The success, info, warning and error icons are `aria-hidden`. `Snackbar` is `role="status"` with `aria-live="polite"` (pass `role="alert"` for errors), its dismiss button is named "Dismiss" (`closeLabel`), and its `icon` sits in an `aria-hidden` span. A snackbar shown through `snackbar()` sits inside the Toaster's live region and carries its own `status`.

#### Reduced motion

Sonner's own stylesheet turns off the toast transitions and animations under `prefers-reduced-motion`, so toasts appear and leave without sliding or stacking motion. The loading icon is Sutra's `Spinner`. Auto-dismiss timers are not affected.

#### Server rendering

Server render: same markup as the client. The server renders the empty live-region `<section>` only: toasts exist only after `toast()` is called on the client. The colour theme is read from `<html>` in an effect (light first), which cannot show before a toast appears.

#### Gotchas

- `toast()` is sonner's own function (re-exported from this module), callable outside React, and shows nothing until a `Toaster` is mounted. Mount exactly one near the root.
- Toasts last 4 seconds, pause while hovered, focused or expanded, and have no close button unless you pass `closeButton` to `Toaster`. Without it a keyboard user can only wait or press the hotkey; give actionable toasts `duration: Infinity` and a close button.
- `Toaster` follows `.dark` or `data-theme="dark"` on `<html>` unless you set `theme`; it defaults to `position="bottom-right"` and `gap={10}`, shows `visibleToasts` (3) at once, and applies Sutra classes with `unstyled` on. `toastOptions.classNames` are merged with the Sutra ones.
- `snackbar(message, options)` returns the toast id and closes after its action runs; `closable` (default true) shows a dismiss button whose `onClose` fires only for that button, so use sonner's `onDismiss` to catch timeouts and swipes. `Snackbar onClose` is a deprecated alias of `onDismiss`.

## SocialButton

> OAuth sign-in button with the provider's logo. Defaults to "Continue with {Provider}".

- Import: `import { SocialButton } from "@sutra/ui"` (or from `@sutra/ui/core`)
- Source: `packages/ui/src/primitives/social-button` (primitives)
- Also accepts the props of HTMLAttributes, ButtonHTMLAttributes

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `provider` (required) | `SocialProvider` |  | Identity provider; sets the logo and the default label ("Continue with Google"). |
| `asChild` | `boolean` |  | Render as the child element (e.g. a link) while keeping the button styles. |
| `fullWidth` | `boolean` |  | Stretches the button to the width of its container. |
| `loading` | `boolean` |  | Shows a spinner and disables the button (with `asChild`: `aria-disabled`, no tab stop, clicks swallowed, `aria-busy`). |
| `size` | `"sm" \| "md" \| "lg"` | `"md"` | Button height and text size. |
| `variant` | `"default" \| "brand" \| "icon"` | `"default"` | Look: `default` (outlined), `brand` (provider colours) or `icon` (square, icon only; set an `aria-label`). |

### Variants

- `variant`: `default`, `brand`, `icon` (default "default")
- `size`: `sm`, `md`, `lg` (default "md")
- `fullWidth`: `true`

### Notes

**When to use:** A sign-in button with the logo of an identity provider. `provider` picks one of eleven (google, apple, github, microsoft, x, facebook, linkedin, discord, slack, figma, gitlab) and the label defaults to "Continue with <Provider>".

**Use instead when:**
- `Button`: a normal action with your own label and icon
- `KunjiButton`: sign in with kunji, which has its own brand rules
- `TextLink`: the sign-in is a link in running text

#### Keyboard

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Moves focus to and from the button. A `disabled` or `loading` button is not focusable |
| Enter, Space | Activates it (native `<button>` behaviour) |

With `asChild` the child keeps its own keyboard behaviour: a link activates on Enter only. No arrow keys are used, so nothing changes in RTL.

#### Screen readers

- A native `<button>` with `type="button"` unless you pass `type`; the name is its text, "Continue with GitHub" by default, or your `children`.
- `variant="icon"` shows only the logo and ignores `children`: its `aria-label` defaults to "Continue with <Provider>" and you can pass your own.
- The provider logos are `aria-hidden`.
- `loading` sets `aria-busy="true"` and disables the button. The spinner keeps its own default "Loading" status label.

#### Reduced motion

The press effect (`active:scale-[0.98]`) and the colour fades are transitions, which the reduced-motion net ends within 1 ms. The `loading` spinner keeps turning, as a progress indicator does.

#### Server rendering

Server render: same markup as the client. Plain markup with no browser API, so server and client output match. The logos are inline SVG or icon components.

#### Gotchas

- With `asChild`, `disabled` and `loading` cannot set the native `disabled` on the child (often a link), so, like `Button asChild`, the child gets `aria-disabled="true"`, `data-disabled`, `tabindex="-1"` and its clicks are swallowed in the capture phase; `loading` also sets `aria-busy` and swaps the logo for a spinner.
- `variant="brand"` paints the provider's own colours as fixed values (white for Google, black for Apple, and so on), so it does not follow the theme or `data-style`; the `default` (outlined) and `icon` variants do. `fullWidth` is ignored for `variant="icon"`.
- `children` replaces the whole label, including the provider name: the default text is only used when there are no `children`. The label is English unless you pass `children`.
- The element carries `data-provider` with the provider key, which is handy for tests and analytics.

## Spinner

> Loading indicator. Uses `currentColor`, so set a text color to recolor it.

- Import: `import { Spinner } from "@sutra/ui"` (or from `@sutra/ui/core`)
- Source: `packages/ui/src/primitives/spinner` (primitives)
- Also accepts the props of HTMLAttributes

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `frames` | `SpinnerGlyphFrameSet \| readonly string[]` |  | glyph only: a built-in frame set or custom frames. Default "dots". |
| `interval` | `number` |  | glyph only: milliseconds per frame. Default 80. |
| `label` | `string` | `"Loading"` | Accessible label. Default "Loading". Pass `""` to make the spinner decorative (hidden from assistive tech). |
| `paused` | `boolean` |  | glyph only: hold the current frame. |
| `size` | `"xs" \| "sm" \| "md" \| "lg" \| "xl"` | `"md"` | Spinner diameter: `xs` 12px, `sm` 16px, `md` 20px, `lg` 24px or `xl` 32px. |
| `variant` | `SpinnerVariant` | `"ring"` | ring: arc spinner · dots: three bouncing dots · bars: equalizer · pulse: breathing dot · glyph: cycling text glyphs (braille dots, arcs, …; inherits font size and colour unless `size` is set). The box variants scale with their box, so `className="h-1.5 w-6"` gives a compact row of dots. |

### Variants

- `size`: `xs`, `sm`, `md`, `lg`, `xl` (default "md")

### Notes

**When to use:** The loading indicator. Five looks (`ring`, `dots`, `bars`, `pulse` and `glyph`, a cycling text character) in five sizes, drawn in the current text colour.

**Use instead when:**
- `Skeleton`: a placeholder in the shape of content that is loading
- `Progress`: the amount done is known
- `GlyphSpinner`: the text-glyph look as a component of its own, with `variant` instead of `frames` names
- `Button`: a button with built-in `loading`

#### Keyboard

Not focusable: no keyboard interaction.

#### Screen readers

- Every variant is a `role="status"` named "Loading" (`label` changes it). The `ring`, `dots`, `bars` and `pulse` variants put it in `aria-label`; `glyph` renders the label as visually hidden text and hides the changing character with `aria-hidden`, so the frames are never read out.
- `label=""` makes the spinner decorative: no role and `aria-hidden`. Do that when the surrounding text already says what is loading (a Button with `loading` does it with its own label).
- Several spinners on one page are several `status` regions with the same name: label them by what is loading.

#### Reduced motion

`ring` keeps spinning, because it carries meaning (the net in `sutra.css` keeps `animate-spin`). `dots`, `bars` and the halo of `pulse` use looping utilities that the net stops, leaving a still row of dots, a still row of full-height bars, or a still disc with a dot in it. `glyph` checks `usePrefersReducedMotion` and holds its current frame.

#### Server rendering

Server render: same markup as the client. Plain markup, and the glyph variant always starts on frame 0 (the reduced-motion hook reads `false` on the server), so server and client output match and the cycling starts after mount.

#### Gotchas

- The box variants are `text-primary` by default (they use `currentColor`): recolour with a `text-*` class. The `glyph` variant has no colour class and inherits it, and takes its font size from the parent unless you pass `size`.
- `size` is `xs` 12px, `sm` 16px, `md` 20px (default), `lg` 24px or `xl` 32px for the box variants; they scale with their box, so `className="h-1.5 w-6"` gives a compact row of dots.
- `frames` (glyph only) takes a set name (`dots`, `line`, `arc`, `circle`, `bounce`, `star`, `pulse`) or your own array of strings; an empty array or an unknown name falls back to `dots`. `interval` is clamped to at least 16 ms, and `paused` holds the frame.
- `frames`, `interval` and `paused` are ignored by the other variants.

## SplitButton

> A primary action fused with a chevron that opens a menu of secondary actions.

- Import: `import { SplitButton } from "@sutra/ui"` (or from `@sutra/ui/core`)
- Source: `packages/ui/src/primitives/split-button` (primitives)
- Also accepts the props of HTMLAttributes, ButtonHTMLAttributes

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `actions` | `SplitButtonAction[]` | `[]` | Secondary actions listed in the chevron menu. |
| `align` | `"start" \| "center" \| "end"` | `"end"` | Alignment of the menu against the button. |
| `asChild` | `boolean` |  | Render as the child element (e.g. a link) while keeping button styles. |
| `fullWidth` | `boolean \| null` |  | Stretches the button to the width of its container. |
| `groupClassName` | `string` |  | Class for the outer group. |
| `leadingIcon` | `React.ReactNode` |  | Icon before the label. |
| `loading` | `boolean` |  | Shows a spinner and disables the button. |
| `menuContent` | `React.ReactNode` |  | Custom menu content (rendered after `actions`). |
| `menuHeading` | `React.ReactNode` |  | Optional heading inside the menu. |
| `menuLabel` | `string` | `"More options"` | Accessible name of the chevron button. Default "More options". |
| `size` | `SplitButtonSize` | `"md"` | Button's text-size scale; the chevron uses the matching icon size. Default "md". |
| `spinnerProps` | `Partial<SpinnerProps>` |  | Overrides for the loading spinner (variant, size, `label`, colour via `className`); it inherits the button text colour by default. |
| `trailingIcon` | `React.ReactNode` |  | Icon after the label. |
| `variant` | `"link" \| "ghost" \| "primary" \| "destructive" \| "soft" \| "outline" \| "inverse" \| "secondary" \| "tertiary" \| "destructive-soft" \| null` | `"primary"` | Visual style: `primary` (filled), `secondary` (bordered), `tertiary` (muted fill), `soft`, `ghost`, `outline`, `destructive`, `destructive-soft`, `inverse` or `link`. |

### Notes

**When to use:** A primary action fused with a chevron button that opens a menu of secondary actions, such as Save with Save as draft or Publish with Schedule. Takes Button's `variant` and `size`, an `actions` array and optional custom `menuContent`.

**Use instead when:**
- `Button`: one action with no alternatives
- `DropdownMenu`: a menu with its own trigger and no default action
- `ButtonGroup`: several equal, always visible buttons
- `Select`: choosing a value rather than running an action

#### Keyboard

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Moves to the main button, then to the chevron button; a disabled or `loading` half is skipped |
| Enter, Space | On the main button: run the primary action |
| Enter, Space, ArrowDown | On the chevron button: open the menu |
| ArrowDown, ArrowUp | In the menu: move the highlighted action |
| Home, End | Highlight the first or last action |
| Enter, Space | Run the highlighted action and close the menu |
| Escape | Close the menu and return focus to the chevron |

Menu rows are vertical, so no arrow keys swap in RTL. The two halves use logical corners, so in an RTL page the chevron sits on the left of the main button.

#### Screen readers

The pair is wrapped in a `role="group"` with no name; pass `aria-label` to name the main button (extra props go to it, not to the group). The chevron is a `<button>` named "More options" (`menuLabel`, also used as its `title`) with `aria-haspopup="menu"`, `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls` while open, and its arrow icon is `aria-hidden`. The menu is the `DropdownMenu`: `role="menu"` with `menuitem` rows, the optional `menuHeading` as a label, and `aria-disabled` rows.

#### Reduced motion

The press scale is switched off on both halves (`active:scale-100`) so they stay visually joined. Colour fades end in 1 ms under reduced motion and the menu loses its movement and keeps its fade. The `loading` spinner on the main button keeps turning.

#### Server rendering

Server render: same markup as the client. Plain markup with no browser API at render. The menu is closed, so only the two buttons render on the server; the menu is portalled after mount.

#### Gotchas

- The chevron and the menu only exist when there are `actions` or `menuContent`; with neither, the component is a plain `Button` in a group.
- `disabled` and `loading` disable both halves (the chevron is disabled while `loading`), and `loading` shows the spinner on the main button only. `onClick` and other button props belong to the main button.
- Each action needs `id`, `label` and `onSelect`; the menu closes after `onSelect` runs. An action's `variant: "destructive"` colours the row red, and `shortcut` is a display-only hint that binds nothing.
- `menuContent` renders after `actions` and should be `DropdownMenuItem` or other menu parts; `align` defaults to `end`, so the menu lines up with the chevron end of the button. `size` follows Button's scale (`xs` to `xl`) and `variant` any Button variant, with a matching divider between the halves.

## Stack

> Flex stack on the 4px spacing grid.

- Import: `import { Stack } from "@sutra/ui"` (or from `@sutra/ui/core`)
- Source: `packages/ui/src/primitives/layout` (primitives)
- Also accepts the props of HTMLAttributes

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `align` | `"start" \| "center" \| "end" \| "stretch" \| "baseline"` |  | Cross-axis alignment of the children (`align-items`). |
| `asChild` | `boolean` |  | Render as the child element instead of a `<div>`, keeping the stack styles. |
| `direction` | `"row" \| "column"` | `"column"` | Main axis of the flex layout: `column` stacks, `row` lines up. |
| `gap` | `0 \| 1 \| 2 \| 3 \| 4 \| 5 \| 6 \| 8 \| 10 \| 12` | `4` | Space between children, in Tailwind spacing steps (4 = 1rem). |
| `justify` | `"start" \| "center" \| "end" \| "between"` |  | Main-axis distribution of the children (`justify-content`). |
| `wrap` | `boolean` |  | Lets children wrap onto new lines when they overflow. |

### Variants

- `direction`: `row`, `column` (default "column")
- `gap`: `0`, `1`, `2`, `3`, `4`, `5`, `6`, `8`, `10`, `12` (default 4)
- `align`: `start`, `center`, `end`, `stretch`, `baseline`
- `justify`: `start`, `center`, `end`, `between`
- `wrap`: `true`

### Notes

**When to use:** A flex layout on the spacing scale: a column by default, with gap, alignment, justify and wrap props. `HStack` is the same in a row, centred on the cross axis.

**Use instead when:**
- `Grid`: a responsive 12-column layout
- `Container`: centre content and cap its width
- `ButtonGroup`: attached buttons
- `ItemGroup`: a list of rows

#### Keyboard

Not focusable: no keyboard interaction.

#### Screen readers
