A plain `div` with no role, so it is invisible to assistive technology and the DOM order is the reading order. `direction="row"` and `justify` change only the layout, not the order, so keep the source order meaningful. With `asChild` the child element (a `ul`, `nav`, `section`) keeps its own semantics.

#### Reduced motion

Static: no animation.

#### Server rendering

Server render: same markup as the client. Plain markup with no browser API, so server and client output match.

#### Gotchas

- `gap` takes the steps 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10 and 12 (4 is 1rem) and defaults to 4: other numbers have no class. `direction` defaults to `column`.
- `HStack` is `direction="row"` with `align="center"` as default; pass `align` to change that. It takes every other `Stack` prop except `direction`.
- Row direction and `justify` follow the writing direction, so a row flips in RTL without changes.
- `wrap` is only the flex-wrap flag. Children of a column that should not stretch need `align="start"`, because the cross-axis default is the browser's stretch.

## StackedMeter

> One bar split into colored parts with a legend (storage breakdown, wait vs. generate…).

- Import: `import { StackedMeter } from "@sutra/ui"` (or from `@sutra/ui/dataviz`)
- Source: `packages/ui/src/primitives/meter` (primitives)
- `data-slot`: `stacked-meter-track`, `stacked-meter-legend-skeleton`, `stacked-meter-part`
- Also accepts the props of HTMLAttributes

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `parts` (required) | `StackedMeterPart[]` |  | Segments of the bar in order; each has a label, a value and an optional colour. |
| `caption` | `React.ReactNode` |  | Secondary line under the bar, e.g. "resets in 2h". |
| `label` | `React.ReactNode` |  | Text shown above the bar; also the accessible name of the meter. |
| `legend` | `boolean \| "inline" \| "list"` | `true` | Legend under the bar. `true` / `"inline"` (default): wrapping chips. `"list"`: one `BreakdownList` row per part with the value right-aligned and a percent column. `false` hides it. |
| `loading` | `boolean` |  | Waiting for the first breakdown: with no `parts` the bar is a muted track and the legend shows placeholders. |
| `max` | `number` |  | Capacity. Defaults to the sum of parts (bar is full). |
| `partSlot` | `string` | `"stacked-meter-part"` | `data-slot` of each part. Default "stacked-meter-part". |
| `showPercent` | `boolean` |  | Show each part's percentage (of `max`, else of the total) in the legend. Default false inline, true for `"list"`. |
| `showValue` | `boolean` | `true` | Show the label / value header. Default true. |
| `size` | `"sm" \| "md" \| "lg"` | `"md"` | Bar height. |
| `trackProps` | `React.HTMLAttributes<HTMLDivElement> & Record<`data-${string}`, string \| undefined>` |  | Props for the bar itself. By default it is `role="img"` named by a parts summary; pass `{ role: "meter", "aria-valuenow": … }` when the bar is a level against `max` (see `ContextUsageBreakdown`). |
| `valueFormatter` | `(value: number) => string` | `(v) => trim(v)` | Formats the values shown in the legend. Default is the localized number. |
| `valueText` | `React.ReactNode` |  | Text beside the label. Defaults to "used / max" when `max` is set. |

### Notes

**When to use:** One bar split into coloured parts with a legend, for a breakdown against a capacity (storage by kind, time by phase). The legend is inline chips or a `BreakdownList` with values and percentages.

**Use instead when:**
- `Meter`: a single level against thresholds
- `BreakdownList`: only the legend rows, next to a chart you draw yourself
- `Progress`: task completion
- `DonutChart`: a round breakdown

#### Keyboard

Not focusable: no keyboard interaction. The `legend="list"` rows are static here (they are not toggle buttons); use `BreakdownList` directly for a legend that hides series.

#### Screen readers

- The root is a `role="group"` named by `label` (through `aria-labelledby`); without `label` the group has no name, so pass `aria-label`.
- The bar is a `role="img"` whose label summarises the parts: "Models 50 GB, Datasets 20 GB of 100 GB". Override it, or turn the bar into a real meter, with `trackProps` (for example `role: "meter"` plus the `aria-value*` attributes).
- The legend is a real list of the parts with their values; the colour swatches are `aria-hidden`.
- `loading` with no `parts` replaces the bar and legend with `aria-hidden` placeholders and an sr-only "Loading Storage…"; with parts it only sets `aria-busy`.

#### Reduced motion

Part widths animate over 500 ms, and the loading track pulses; both have `motion-reduce:` variants that switch them off.

#### Server rendering

Server render: same markup as the client. Plain markup computed from the props (the label id uses `useId`), so server and client output match.

#### Gotchas

- `max` is the capacity: without it the bar is the sum of the parts and always full. The header text defaults to "used / max" (or just the sum); `valueText` replaces it and `showValue={false}` hides the header.
- Parts without `color` take the chart palette in order; a `color` is a token name (`primary`, `success`, ...) or any CSS colour. Parts with a value of 0 or less draw nothing but still appear in the legend. Each drawn part has `data-slot="stacked-meter-part"` (change it with `partSlot`) and a `title` tooltip.
- `legend` is `true` or `"inline"` for chips, `"list"` for rows with a percent column (`showPercent` defaults to true for the list, false for chips), or `false` for none. Percentages are of `max`, otherwise of the total.
- Keep `key` stable: it defaults to `label`, so two parts with the same label collide.

## StatusBadge

> Status pill with a colored dot (or a spinner / icon).

- Import: `import { StatusBadge } from "@sutra/ui"` (or from `@sutra/ui/core`)
- Source: `packages/ui/src/primitives/status-badge` (primitives)
- Also accepts the props of HTMLAttributes

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `icon` | `StatusIndicatorIcon` | `"dot"` | Leading indicator: `"dot"` (default), `"spinner"`, any icon node, or `null` for none. Always decorative. |
| `label` | `React.ReactNode` |  | Custom text; defaults to the status name. |
| `pulse` | `boolean` |  | Animated halo around the dot; defaults to on for the `processing` status. |
| `size` | `"sm" \| "md" \| "lg"` | `"md"` | Badge height and text size. |
| `status` | `StatusBadgeStatus` |  | Preset status (sets colour and default label). Optional when `tone` is given. |
| `tone` | `ToneInput` |  | Open semantic colour; overrides the preset status colour. |
| `variant` | `"soft" \| "outline" \| "plain"` | `"soft"` | soft: tinted pill · outline: bordered pill · plain: dot + text only |

### Notes

**When to use:** A status pill with a coloured dot, spinner or icon and a label, from 13 preset statuses or any `tone`. `StatusDot` is the same indicator on its own.

**Use instead when:**
- `Badge`: a category or tag with no status meaning
- `Chip`: a clickable filter or tag
- `Spinner`: only a loading indicator
- `Meter`: a measured value

#### Keyboard

Not focusable: no keyboard interaction.

#### Screen readers

- `StatusBadge` is a plain `<span>`. The label is visible text (the status name, `label`, or `children`), and the indicator inside it is always `aria-hidden`: the text carries the meaning, so never pass an empty label with a coloured dot.
- `StatusDot` on its own is a `role="img"` named by `label`, which defaults to the status name ("Busy"). With only `tone` and no `status` or `label` it is `aria-hidden`, so a bare dot is silent. `label=""` hides it on purpose.
- `icon="spinner"` renders a `Spinner` with an empty label (decorative); the node you pass as `icon` is wrapped in `aria-hidden`.

#### Reduced motion

The `pulse` halo uses `motion-safe:animate-ping`, so it never runs under `prefers-reduced-motion`. The pop of a changed custom icon (`animate-pop`) is stopped by the net in `sutra.css`, and the colour fade ends in 1 ms. The `spinner` icon keeps spinning, as it carries meaning.

#### Server rendering

Server render: same markup as the client. Plain markup with no browser API, so server and client output match. The icon pop is skipped on the first render and only plays when the status changes later.

#### Gotchas

- `tone` wins over the colour of `status`, and `status` still supplies the default label. Statuses: online, offline, busy, away, active, inactive, pending, success, error, warning, info, draft, processing (`processing` is primary and pulses by default).
- `pulse` only affects the dot: it does nothing with `icon="spinner"` or a custom icon node. In `StatusBadge`, `variant` is the pill style (`soft`, `outline`, `plain`); the dot's own fill (`solid`, `hollow`, `dashed`) exists only on `StatusDot`.
- `icon={null}` or `false` removes the indicator on `StatusBadge`; on `StatusDot` any `null` or boolean icon draws the plain dot.
- `children` replace the default label, and `label` is ignored when `children` are present.

## StatusDot

> Small colored dot (or round status glyph) indicating a status.

- Import: `import { StatusDot } from "@sutra/ui"` (or from `@sutra/ui/core`)
- Source: `packages/ui/src/primitives/status-badge` (primitives)
- Also accepts the props of HTMLAttributes

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `icon` | `StatusIndicatorIcon` | `"dot"` | `"dot"` (default), or `"spinner"` / an icon to render a small round status glyph instead of a dot. |
| `label` | `string` |  | Accessible label; defaults to the status name. Set to "" to hide from assistive tech. |
| `pulse` | `boolean` |  | Animated halo. Defaults to true for `processing`. |
| `size` | `"sm" \| "md" \| "lg"` | `"md"` | Dot size. |
| `status` | `StatusBadgeStatus` |  | Preset status (sets colour and default label). Optional when `tone` is given. |
| `tone` | `ToneInput` |  | Open semantic colour; overrides the preset status colour. |
| `variant` | `StatusDotVariant` | `"solid"` | Fill style. Default `solid`. |

### Notes

**When to use:** A status pill with a coloured dot, spinner or icon and a label, from 13 preset statuses or any `tone`. `StatusDot` is the same indicator on its own.

**Use instead when:**
- `Badge`: a category or tag with no status meaning
- `Chip`: a clickable filter or tag
- `Spinner`: only a loading indicator
- `Meter`: a measured value

#### Keyboard

Not focusable: no keyboard interaction.

#### Screen readers

- `StatusBadge` is a plain `<span>`. The label is visible text (the status name, `label`, or `children`), and the indicator inside it is always `aria-hidden`: the text carries the meaning, so never pass an empty label with a coloured dot.
- `StatusDot` on its own is a `role="img"` named by `label`, which defaults to the status name ("Busy"). With only `tone` and no `status` or `label` it is `aria-hidden`, so a bare dot is silent. `label=""` hides it on purpose.
- `icon="spinner"` renders a `Spinner` with an empty label (decorative); the node you pass as `icon` is wrapped in `aria-hidden`.

#### Reduced motion

The `pulse` halo uses `motion-safe:animate-ping`, so it never runs under `prefers-reduced-motion`. The pop of a changed custom icon (`animate-pop`) is stopped by the net in `sutra.css`, and the colour fade ends in 1 ms. The `spinner` icon keeps spinning, as it carries meaning.

#### Server rendering

Server render: same markup as the client. Plain markup with no browser API, so server and client output match. The icon pop is skipped on the first render and only plays when the status changes later.

#### Gotchas

- `tone` wins over the colour of `status`, and `status` still supplies the default label. Statuses: online, offline, busy, away, active, inactive, pending, success, error, warning, info, draft, processing (`processing` is primary and pulses by default).
- `pulse` only affects the dot: it does nothing with `icon="spinner"` or a custom icon node. In `StatusBadge`, `variant` is the pill style (`soft`, `outline`, `plain`); the dot's own fill (`solid`, `hollow`, `dashed`) exists only on `StatusDot`.
- `icon={null}` or `false` removes the indicator on `StatusBadge`; on `StatusDot` any `null` or boolean icon draws the plain dot.
- `children` replace the default label, and `label` is ignored when `children` are present.

## StepIndicator

> Alias of `Steps`.

**Deprecated:** Use `Steps` (this is a plain alias).

- Import: `import { StepIndicator } from "@sutra/ui"` (or from `@sutra/ui/core`)
- Source: `packages/ui/src/primitives/step-indicator` (primitives)
- Also accepts the props of HTMLAttributes

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `current` (required) | `number` |  | Zero-based index of the current step. Use `steps.length` to mark all complete. |
| `steps` (required) | `StepIndicatorStep[]` |  | Steps in order; each has a `title` and optional description. |
| `connector` | `boolean` |  | Draw the line between markers (circles/dots). Default true. |
| `onStepClick` | `(index: number) => void` |  | Makes steps clickable. |
| `orientation` | `"horizontal" \| "vertical"` | `"horizontal"` | Lays the steps out in a row or a column. |
| `restrictToCompleted` | `boolean` |  | Only allow clicking completed steps (and the current one). Default true. |
| `size` | `"sm" \| "md"` |  | Marker size for circles: `md` (32px, default) or `sm` (24px, tighter spacing). |
| `variant` | `"circles" \| "bars" \| "dots"` | `"circles"` | Marker style: numbered `circles`, thin progress `bars` or small `dots`. |

### Notes

**When to use:** Shows progress through a multi-step flow as numbered circles, thin bars or dots, horizontal or vertical. Optional clickable steps, per-step `status`, `description`, `content` and (vertical) `action`.

**Use instead when:**
- `Progress`: a single percentage bar
- `Breadcrumbs`: where the user is in a site hierarchy
- `Tabs`: switching between panels of equal rank
- `StepWizard`: the whole wizard with panels, navigation and validation

#### Keyboard

Not focusable by default: no keyboard interaction. With `onStepClick`, each completed and current step is a native `<button type="button">` and its own tab stop; Enter and Space activate it. Upcoming steps stay plain `div`s (not focusable) unless `restrictToCompleted={false}`. There are no arrow keys, so nothing swaps in RTL.

#### Screen readers

The root is an `<ol>` named "Progress" unless you pass `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`. The current step's `<li>` has `aria-current="step"`; completed steps get an sr-only "(completed)" after the title (English text, not translatable through a prop); upcoming steps carry no extra text. The marker number is real text, so a step reads like "2 Profile", while the check icon and the connector lines are `aria-hidden`. The `bars` variant adds a visible "Step N" line. `data-status` on each `<li>` reflects `complete`, `current` or `upcoming`.

#### Reduced motion

The marker colours, connector fill and bar fill are transitions that end in 1 ms under reduced motion. The check mark that replaces a number on completion pops in with `animate-in zoom-in-50 fade-in-0`, and the reduced-motion net removes the scale and keeps the fade.

#### Server rendering

Server render: same markup as the client. Plain markup with no browser API or measuring, so the server and the client render the same list.

#### Gotchas

- `current` is the zero-based index of the current step; `steps.length` marks every step complete. A step's own `status` overrides what `current` implies, including `aria-current` and the "(completed)" text, which suits checklists finished out of order.
- The step label field is `title`. The `steps` prop description in the generated reference says `label`, but only `title`, `description`, `icon`, `status`, `content`, `action` and `itemProps` exist.
- `content` renders under the step but outside the clickable area, so inputs and links inside it are not nested in the step button; `action` shows only for the vertical `circles` and `dots`. The `bars` variant ignores `icon`, `action`, `size` and `connector`.
- `StepIndicator` is a deprecated plain alias of `Steps` (and `StepIndicatorProps` of `StepsProps`); use `Steps`.

## Steps

> Progress through a multi-step flow.

- Import: `import { Steps } from "@sutra/ui"` (or from `@sutra/ui/core`)
- Source: `packages/ui/src/primitives/step-indicator` (primitives)
- Also accepts the props of HTMLAttributes

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `current` (required) | `number` |  | Zero-based index of the current step. Use `steps.length` to mark all complete. |
| `steps` (required) | `StepIndicatorStep[]` |  | Steps in order; each has a `title` and optional description. |
| `connector` | `boolean` | `true` | Draw the line between markers (circles/dots). Default true. |
| `onStepClick` | `(index: number) => void` |  | Makes steps clickable. |
| `orientation` | `"horizontal" \| "vertical"` | `"horizontal"` | Lays the steps out in a row or a column. |
| `restrictToCompleted` | `boolean` | `true` | Only allow clicking completed steps (and the current one). Default true. |
| `size` | `"sm" \| "md"` | `"md"` | Marker size for circles: `md` (32px, default) or `sm` (24px, tighter spacing). |
| `variant` | `"circles" \| "bars" \| "dots"` | `"circles"` | Marker style: numbered `circles`, thin progress `bars` or small `dots`. |

### Notes

**When to use:** Shows progress through a multi-step flow as numbered circles, thin bars or dots, horizontal or vertical. Optional clickable steps, per-step `status`, `description`, `content` and (vertical) `action`.

**Use instead when:**
- `Progress`: a single percentage bar
- `Breadcrumbs`: where the user is in a site hierarchy
- `Tabs`: switching between panels of equal rank
- `StepWizard`: the whole wizard with panels, navigation and validation

#### Keyboard

Upcoming steps stay plain `div`s (not focusable) unless `restrictToCompleted={false}`. There are no arrow keys, so nothing swaps in RTL.

The current step's `<li>` has `aria-current="step"`; completed steps get an sr-only "(completed)" after the title (English text, not translatable through a prop); upcoming steps carry no extra text. The marker number is real text, so a step reads like "2 Profile", while the check icon and the connector lines are `aria-hidden`. The `bars` variant adds a visible "Step N" line. `data-status` on each `<li>` reflects `complete`, `current` or `upcoming`.

#### Reduced motion

The marker colours, connector fill and bar fill are transitions that end in 1 ms under reduced motion. The check mark that replaces a number on completion pops in with `animate-in zoom-in-50 fade-in-0`, and the reduced-motion net removes the scale and keeps the fade.

#### Server rendering

#### Gotchas

- `current` is the zero-based index of the current step; `steps.length` marks every step complete. A step's own `status` overrides what `current` implies, including `aria-current` and the "(completed)" text, which suits checklists finished out of order.
- The step label field is `title`. The `steps` prop description in the generated reference says `label`, but only `title`, `description`, `icon`, `status`, `content`, `action` and `itemProps` exist.
- `content` renders under the step but outside the clickable area, so inputs and links inside it are not nested in the step button; `action` shows only for the vertical `circles` and `dots`. The `bars` variant ignores `icon`, `action`, `size` and `connector`.
- `StepIndicator` is a deprecated plain alias of `Steps` (and `StepIndicatorProps` of `StepsProps`); use `Steps`.

## Switch

> Toggle switch with a springy thumb and optional thumb icons. Consumes `Field` context.

- Import: `import { Switch } from "@sutra/ui"` (or from `@sutra/ui/forms`)
- Source: `packages/ui/src/primitives/switch` (primitives)
- `data-slot`: `switch`, `switch-thumb`
- Parts: [`SwitchField`](SwitchField.md), [`SwitchGroup`](SwitchGroup.md)
- Also accepts the props of HTMLAttributes, ButtonHTMLAttributes, SwitchProps, PrimitivePropsWithRef

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `checkedIcon` | `React.ReactNode` |  | Icon shown in the thumb while on. |
| `invalid` | `boolean` |  | Marks the switch invalid: error ring and `aria-invalid`. Inherited from a surrounding `Field` when omitted. |
| `size` | `"sm" \| "md" \| "lg"` | `"md"` | Switch size: `sm`, `md` or `lg`. |
| `thumbClassName` | `string` |  | Classes for the thumb (the sliding knob). |
| `uncheckedIcon` | `React.ReactNode` |  | Icon shown in the thumb while off. |

### Variants

- `size`: `sm`, `md`, `lg` (default "md")

### Part props

Props of `SwitchField`, `SwitchGroup`: see [the full page](md/Switch.md).

### Notes

**When to use:** An on or off setting that takes effect at once, drawn as a sliding switch. `SwitchField` adds a label and description for forms, and `SwitchGroup` stacks switch rows in a fieldset with a `value` map.

**Use instead when:**
- `Checkbox`: a yes or no answer submitted with a form, or a choice in a list
- `SettingsRow`: a settings page row (whole-row target, icon, `disabledReason`)
- `ToggleButton`: a button that stays pressed
- `RadioGroup`: exactly one of several options

#### Keyboard

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Moves between switches; every switch is its own tab stop. A disabled switch is skipped |
| Space, Enter | Toggle the focused switch (native button behaviour) |

No arrow keys, so RTL changes nothing except that the thumb slides the other way. Clicking the label of a `SwitchField` toggles the switch.

#### Screen readers

- A `<button role="switch">` with `aria-checked` and `aria-required` from `required`. `invalid` sets `aria-invalid`, and a surrounding `Field` supplies `id`, `aria-describedby`, `disabled`, `required` and `invalid` when you do not pass them.
- `SwitchField` names the switch through `<label htmlFor>` and adds the description to `aria-describedby`; `label` is required. A bare `Switch` has no name: pass `aria-label`, or put it under a `FieldLabel`.
- `SwitchGroup` is a native `<fieldset>` named by its `legend`, described by `description`. Disabling the group disables every switch natively.
- `checkedIcon` and `uncheckedIcon` are shown in the thumb exactly as you pass them, so pass `aria-hidden` icons.

#### Reduced motion

The thumb slides with a 300 ms spring transform, and the track colour and thumb icons fade; the reduced-motion net ends all of them in 1 ms, so the thumb jumps.

#### Server rendering

Server render: same markup as the client. Plain markup: the state comes from `checked` or `defaultChecked`, and the ids come from `useId`, so server and client output match.

#### Slots

- `switch`: the button; `switch-thumb`: the sliding knob
- `switch-field`: the row of switch, label and description
- `switch-group`: the fieldset

#### Gotchas

- `labelPosition="left"` moves the switch to the end visually with CSS `order`; the markup order, and so the tab and reading order, stays switch then label.
- `SwitchGroup` keeps a `Record<string, boolean>` keyed by option `value`, and `onValueChange` receives the whole map. Each generated switch gets `name` equal to its option value, so a form posts the checked ones under their own names.
- Use `checked` with `onCheckedChange` (a boolean) to control a switch; the Radix `value` prop is the string a form posts when it is on.
- `size` is `sm`, `md` or `lg` (28, 36 and 44 px wide); the hit area is padded to at least 24 px.

## TabDropdown

> A tab bar that collapses tabs which don't fit into a "More" dropdown (ResizeObserver-driven).

- Import: `import { TabDropdown } from "@sutra/ui"` (or from `@sutra/ui/core`)
- Source: `packages/ui/src/primitives/tab-dropdown` (primitives)
- `data-slot`: `tab-dropdown-measure`
- Also accepts the props of HTMLAttributes

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `items` (required) | `TabDropdownItem[]` |  | Tabs in order; tabs that do not fit collapse into the overflow menu. |
| `defaultValue` | `string` |  | Initially selected tab value when uncontrolled. |
| `label` | `string` | `"Tabs"` | Accessible name of the tab list. |
| `moreLabel` | `string` | `"More"` | Label of the overflow trigger. Default "More". |
| `onValueChange` | `(value: string) => void` |  | Called with the value of the tab the user picked. |
| `size` | `"sm" \| "md"` | `"md"` | Tab height and text size. |
| `value` | `string` |  | Controlled selected tab value. Use with `onValueChange`. |

### Notes

**When to use:** A tab bar that measures its width and moves the tabs that do not fit into a "More" dropdown. It renders only the tab strip: you render the panel for the selected `value`.

**Use instead when:**
- `Tabs`: the tabs fit and each has a panel
- `TabMenu`: navigation between pages
- `DropdownMenu`: a menu of actions, not a selection that stays visible

#### Keyboard

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab / Shift+Tab | The selected visible tab is the only tab stop (the first enabled one when the selected tab is in the overflow or disabled); then the More button |
| ArrowRight, ArrowLeft | Focus and select the next or previous enabled tab, wrapping around |
| Home, End | Focus and select the first or last enabled tab |
| Enter, Space | Select the focused tab (native button) |
| Enter, Space, ArrowDown | On the More button: open the overflow menu; ArrowUp and ArrowDown then move through it, Escape closes it |

The arrow keys follow the reading direction: in RTL ArrowLeft goes to the next tab and ArrowRight to the previous one (the nearest `dir`, else `<html dir>`). Arrow keys select as they move, there is no manual activation mode.

#### Screen readers

The strip is `role="tablist"` with `aria-orientation="horizontal"` and an accessible name from `label` (default "Tabs"); each tab is a button with `role="tab"` and `aria-selected`. There is no `tabpanel` and no `aria-controls`: give your own panel `role="tabpanel"` and `aria-labelledby` if you want that relationship. The overflow button is named "More tabs" (`moreLabel` plus " tabs"), or "More tabs, current: Billing" when the selected tab is in the overflow, and its menu is a group of `menuitemradio` rows. A hidden measuring copy of all tabs is `aria-hidden` and not focusable.

#### Reduced motion

Static layout: the only motion is colour fades on the tabs, which end in 1 ms under reduced motion. There is no sliding indicator.

#### Server rendering

Server render: part of it fills in after mount. The server renders every tab (`visibleCount` starts at the item count and no More button), and the widths are measured after mount with a layout effect and a `ResizeObserver`. A bar that overflows the container therefore collapses into More at hydration, and it re-measures when the container resizes or `items` changes.

#### Slots

- `tab-dropdown-measure`: the invisible, `aria-hidden` copy of every tab and the More button used to measure widths

#### Gotchas

- It does not render panels or own your content: read `value` (or `onValueChange`) and show the matching panel yourself.
- Overflow rows show text only. A `label` that is not a string needs `textValue`, otherwise the menu and the More button fall back to the item `value`. Icons and badges appear only in the visible tabs.
- Tabs collapse from the end: the items that fit stay in order, the rest go to More, and a selected overflow tab is shown on the More button instead of among the tabs.
- Uncontrolled it starts on `defaultValue`, else the first item. The root needs a width of its own (it is `min-w-0` and measures `offsetWidth`), so put it in a container that can shrink.

## Table

> Data table inside a bordered, scrollable box. The box takes focus while it overflows (so the arrow keys scroll it) and becomes a named `region` when the table has an `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`.

- Import: `import { Table } from "@sutra/ui"` (or from `@sutra/ui/core`)
- Source: `packages/ui/src/primitives/table` (primitives)
- Parts: [`TableBody`](TableBody.md), [`TableCaption`](TableCaption.md), [`TableCell`](TableCell.md), [`TableCheckbox`](TableCheckbox.md), [`TableFooter`](TableFooter.md), [`TableHead`](TableHead.md), [`TableHeader`](TableHeader.md), [`TableRow`](TableRow.md)
- Also accepts the props of HTMLAttributes, TableHTMLAttributes

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `bare` | `boolean` |  | Remove the bordered box around the table. |
| `containerClassName` | `string` |  | Classes for the scroll container that wraps the `<table>` (`className` styles the table itself). |
| `density` | `TableDensity` |  | Row density. Default `normal`; `"comfortable"` is accepted as a legacy alias of `relaxed`. |
| `maxHeight` | `number \| string` |  | Maximum height of the scroll container (px number or CSS length); the body scrolls past it. Pair with `stickyHeader`. |
| `stickyHeader` | `boolean` | `false` | Keeps the header visible while the container scrolls. Pair with `maxHeight`. |
| `striped` | `boolean` | `false` | Zebra-stripe the body rows. |

### Part props

Props of `TableCell`, `TableCheckbox`, `TableHead`: see [the full page](md/Table.md).

### Notes

**When to use:** A native HTML table in a bordered, scrollable box with density, striping and a sticky header, for composing tables by hand. `TableHead` can be a sort button, `TableCheckbox` a selection box.

**Use instead when:**
- `DataTable`: columns and rows from data, with sorting, selection, loading and empty states built in
- `ItemGroup`: a list of rows with media and actions
- `KeyValue`: two-column facts
- `Card`: free-form content

#### Keyboard

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Moves to sort buttons in headers, checkboxes and any control in a cell |
| Enter, Space | On a sortable header, calls its `onSort` (native `<button>`) |
| Space | On a `TableCheckbox`, toggles it (native checkbox with a 24px hit area) |

There is no arrow-key navigation between cells and rows are not focusable; this is a plain table (only the scroll box around it takes focus, and only while the table is wider or taller than it). No key depends on direction, but `align` is logical: `left` and `right` mean start and end, so they flip in RTL.

#### Screen readers

- Real `table`, `thead`, `tbody`, `tfoot`, `tr`, `th` and `td` elements, so row and column navigation comes from the browser. `TableHead` sets `scope="col"` unless you pass another `scope`. `TableCaption` is a real `<caption>` that names the table, even though it is drawn under it.
- A header is sortable when it has `onSort` or `sortDirection`: it then holds a button named by the header text, and `aria-sort` is `ascending`, `descending` or `none` (`sortDirection={false}`). Without either it has no `aria-sort`. The arrow icon is `aria-hidden`.
- `TableCheckbox` is a native checkbox with the `checkbox` role and no label of its own: pass `aria-label` ("Select row Ada"). `indeterminate` sets the DOM mixed state.
- The scroll container around the table has `tabIndex="0"` and a focus ring while the content overflows it (measured after mount and on resize; not on the server), so a keyboard user can scroll it; a table that fits adds no tab stop. It becomes a `role="region"` named like the table when the `Table` has an `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`; otherwise it has no role. `DataTable` takes the same two props.

#### Reduced motion

Row hover, the sort button and the checkbox tick are transitions, which the reduced-motion net in `sutra.css` ends within 1 ms.

#### Server rendering

Server render: same markup as the client. Plain table markup with no browser API, so server and client output match. The `indeterminate` state of a `TableCheckbox` is a DOM property set after mount.

#### Gotchas

- `TableHead` is stateless about sorting: you pass `sortDirection` and flip it in `onSort`. For a sort that manages itself, use `DataTable`.
- `className` styles the `<table>`; `containerClassName` styles the scroll box around it, and `bare` removes that box's border and shadow. `stickyHeader` needs a height limit (`maxHeight`) to have anything to stick against.
- `density` is `compact`, `normal` or `relaxed` (`comfortable` is a legacy alias of `relaxed`). A row shows as selected with `data-state="selected"`.
- `TableCheckbox` stops click propagation, so it does not trigger a click handler on its row, and `checked` and `defaultChecked` follow the controlled and uncontrolled rules (`onCheckedChange` receives a boolean).

## Tabs

> Tabs root. `variant`, `size` and `accent` flow to every list and trigger inside.

- Import: `import { Tabs } from "@sutra/ui"` (or from `@sutra/ui/navigation`)
- Source: `packages/ui/src/primitives/tabs` (primitives)
- Parts: [`TabsContent`](TabsContent.md), [`TabsList`](TabsList.md), [`TabsTrigger`](TabsTrigger.md)
- Also accepts the props of HTMLAttributes, TabsProps, PrimitivePropsWithRef

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `accent` | `Accent` |  | Categorical colour for the active trigger (pill, underline, text) on every trigger. Inactive triggers stay neutral. `TabsTrigger`'s own `accent` overrides it per trigger. |
| `size` | `Size` | `"md"` | Tab height and text size. |
| `variant` | `TabsVariant` | `"pill"` | Tab list style: `pill` (filled active pill), `underline`, `solid` (segmented) or `ghost`. |

### Part props

Props of `TabsList`, `TabsTrigger`: see [the full page](md/Tabs.md).

### Notes

**When to use:** Switches between panels of related content in place, with a sliding active indicator. Four looks (`pill`, `underline`, `solid`, `ghost`), three sizes, horizontal or vertical, optional `accent` colour, trigger `icon` and `badge`.

**Use instead when:**
- `TabDropdown`: too many tabs for the width, the rest go into a More menu
- `TabMenu`: navigation between pages (links with `aria-current`, no panels)
- `SegmentedControl`: a compact switch of a view or a setting
- `Accordion`: stacked sections that can be open together

#### Keyboard

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Enters the tab list on the active tab (the only tab stop), then moves on to the panel |
| ArrowRight, ArrowLeft | Move to the next or previous tab and wrap around; with the default automatic activation the tab is also selected |
| ArrowDown, ArrowUp | The same for `orientation="vertical"`; ignored in a horizontal list |
| Home, End | First or last tab |
| Enter, Space | Select the focused tab (what matters with `activationMode="manual"`) |

In RTL the horizontal keys swap: ArrowLeft goes to the next tab and ArrowRight to the previous one (the direction comes from `<html dir>` or the nearest `DirectionProvider`). Vertical lists do not swap.

#### Screen readers

`TabsList` is `role="tablist"` with `aria-orientation`; each trigger is `role="tab"` with `aria-selected` and `aria-controls`; each panel is `role="tabpanel"` labelled by its trigger and is itself a tab stop (`tabindex="0"`). A `badge` is part of the tab's name ("Inbox 4"). The sliding indicator is `aria-hidden`. An `icon` you pass is not hidden for you, and an icon-only tab needs `aria-label`. Pass `aria-label` to `TabsList` when the page has more than one tab list.

#### Reduced motion

The indicator slides over 300 ms (`motion-reduce:transition-none` makes it jump) and the trigger colour fades are transitions that end in 1 ms. The active panel fades in with `animate-in fade-in-0`; the net removes any movement and the short fade remains.

#### Server rendering

Server render: part of it fills in after mount. The server renders the tabs, the selected panel and a plain filled active tab. The sliding indicator is measured after mount (`data-indicator="ready"` on the list), and until then the active trigger paints its own fill, so the look shifts slightly at hydration. The root `dir` is also read after mount (the server writes `ltr`), so in an RTL document the first server paint has `dir="ltr"`.

#### Gotchas

- Activation is automatic: moving focus with the arrows selects the tab and calls `onValueChange`. For panels that are costly to render or fetch, set `activationMode="manual"` so only Enter or Space selects.
- Inactive `TabsContent` is unmounted (state inside is lost); pass `forceMount` to keep it in the tree, hidden. `value` on `Tabs` and on each trigger and panel must match.
- `accent` on `Tabs` colours every active trigger and the indicator; `TabsTrigger accent` overrides it for one tab and inactive tabs stay neutral. `variant="ghost"` has no sliding indicator.
- `TabsList` scrolls horizontally (`overflow-x-auto`, no scrollbar) when the tabs do not fit; use `TabDropdown` if they should collapse instead. `fullWidth` stretches the triggers.

## TagInput

> Text input that turns entries into removable tag chips, with optional suggestions.

- Import: `import { TagInput } from "@sutra/ui"` (or from `@sutra/ui/forms`)
- Source: `packages/ui/src/primitives/tag-input` (primitives)
- `data-slot`: `tag-input`, `tag-input-tag`, `tag-input-field`, `tag-input-count`, `tag-input-announcer`
- Also accepts the props of HTMLAttributes, InputHTMLAttributes

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `addOnBlur` | `boolean` | `false` | Commit the pending text when the input loses focus. |
| `allowDuplicates` | `boolean` | `false` | Allow the same tag more than once (case-insensitive comparison otherwise). |
| `confirmBackspace` | `boolean` | `false` | Backspace on an empty field first marks the last tag (announced politely: "Press Backspace again to remove …") and a second press removes it. Typing, blur or any other key clears the mark, and a held key never confirms. Default false: Backspace removes the last tag at once. |
| `defaultValue` | `string[]` | `[]` | Initial tags when uncontrolled. |
| `emptyState` | `React.ReactNode` |  | Empty state inside the suggestions dropdown. |
| `emptyText` | `React.ReactNode` |  | **Deprecated.** Use `emptyState`. Legacy name of `emptyState`. |
| `invalid` | `boolean` |  | Marks the field invalid: error border and `aria-invalid`. Inherited from a surrounding `Field` when omitted. |
| `max` | `number` |  | Maximum number of tags. |
| `normalize` | `(text: string) => string` | `defaultNormalize` | Transform text before it becomes a tag. Default trims whitespace. |
| `onReject` | `(tag: string, reason: TagRejectReason) => void` |  | Called when a tag is rejected. |
| `onValueChange` | `(value: string[]) => void` |  | Called with the full tag list after a tag is added or removed. |
| `renderTag` | `(tag: string, state: TagRenderState) => React.ReactNode` |  | Custom content for a tag, in place of its text. The chip frame, remove button and pending mark stay. |
| `restrictToSuggestions` | `boolean` | `false` | Only accept tags from `suggestions`. |
| `separators` | `string[]` | `[","]` | Extra characters (or strings) that commit a tag. Enter and Tab always do; key names like "Enter" are treated as keys, not characters. Default `[","]`. |
| `showCount` | `boolean` | `false` | Show the number of tags (and the limit, with `max`) after the tags. |
| `size` | `Size` | `"md"` | Field height and text size. |
| `suggestions` | `string[]` |  | Options shown in a dropdown, filtered as you type. |
| `tagClassName` | `string` |  | Classes for each tag chip. |
| `validate` | `(tag: string, tags: string[]) => boolean` |  | Return `false` to reject a tag. |
| `value` | `string[]` |  | Controlled list of tags. Use with `onValueChange`. |
| `variant` | `"outline" \| "filled"` |  | `outline` (default) is the bordered box; `filled` is a tinted surface with a hidden border. |
| `wrapperClassName` | `string` |  | Class for the outer container. |

### Notes

**When to use:** A text field that turns what you type into removable tag chips. It takes a `string[]`, with duplicate, `max` and `validate` checks, optional `suggestions` in a dropdown, and paste that splits on separators.

**Use instead when:**
- `Combobox`: the choices come from a fixed list and need labels (`multiple` mode)
- `Input`: a single text value
- `Chip`: a standalone label, not an editor
- `Badge`: a categorical label

#### Keyboard

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| Enter, or a `separators` character (default `,`) | Commit the typed text as a tag. With empty text Enter is left to the browser (a form submits) |
| Tab | With text, commits it and keeps focus; if the tag is rejected, or the text is empty, focus moves on |
| Backspace | In an empty field, remove the last tag. With `confirmBackspace` the first press marks it and the second removes it |
| ArrowDown | With `suggestions`: open the list and highlight the first match; then ArrowUp and ArrowDown move through it, Home and End jump (while an option is highlighted) |
| Enter, Tab | With a highlighted suggestion: add it |
| Escape | Close the suggestions |

The chips are not focusable and their remove buttons are not tab stops (`tabIndex` -1), so the keyboard way to remove a tag is Backspace. Left and Right are not handled, so RTL changes only the layout. While the user is composing text with an IME, none of these keys fire.

#### Screen readers

- A native text input named by a `<label>`, `aria-label` or a surrounding `FieldLabel`; `invalid`, `required`, `disabled` and `aria-describedby` come from a surrounding `Field` unless you pass them. Chips are plain text; each remove button is named "Remove" plus the tag.
- With `suggestions` the input becomes a `combobox` with `aria-expanded`, `aria-controls`, `aria-autocomplete="list"` and `aria-activedescendant`; the popover holds a `listbox` named "Suggestions" whose options mark the highlighted row with `aria-selected`. Focus stays in the input.
- `showCount` renders "3" or "3 / 5" with a screen reader suffix ("tags") and ties it to the input through `aria-describedby`. `confirmBackspace` adds a polite live region that says "Press Backspace again to remove ...".

#### Reduced motion

Each chip fades and zooms in with `animate-in zoom-in-95`, and the dropdown does the same; the reduced-motion net removes the movement and ends the rest in 1 ms. Existing chips animate on mount too.

#### Server rendering

Server render: same markup as the client. The chips, the input and the count render on the server from `value` or `defaultValue`, so server and client match. The suggestions popover is portalled and opens only after focus, so it is never in the server HTML.

#### Slots

- `tag-input`: the outer box; `tag-input-tag`: a chip (`data-pending-remove` while marked)
- `tag-input-field`: the text input; `tag-input-count`: the count
- `tag-input-announcer`: the live region, only with `confirmBackspace`

#### Gotchas

- Duplicates are rejected case-insensitively unless `allowDuplicates`. At `max` the input turns read-only and shrinks away. `onReject(tag, reason)` reports `"duplicate"`, `"invalid"` (from `validate` or `restrictToSuggestions`) and `"max"`.
- Pasting text that contains a separator or a line break splits it into tags (up to `max`); plain text with no separator lands in the field. Typing a separator splits the same way.
- `separators` lists extra characters; Enter and Tab always commit, and the key names `"Enter"` and `"Tab"` in the list are not treated as characters.
- `name` posts one hidden input per tag under the same name. `addOnBlur` commits the pending text on blur, and `normalize` (default trim) runs before every check. `emptyText` is a deprecated alias of `emptyState`.

## Text

> Body text with `size`, `tone` and `weight`; renders a `<p>` unless `as` says otherwise. Extra props are spread to the element.

- Import: `import { Text } from "@sutra/ui"` (or from `@sutra/ui/core`)
- Source: `packages/ui/src/primitives/typography` (primitives)
- Also accepts the props of HTMLAttributes

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `as` | `"p" \| "span" \| "div" \| "small" \| "strong" \| "em"` | `"p"` | Element to render, independent of the visual styles. |
| `asChild` | `boolean` |  | Render as the child element instead of the text tag, keeping the text styles. |
| `size` | `"xs" \| "sm" \| "md" \| "lg" \| "xl"` | `"md"` | Type scale step: `xs`, `sm`, `md` (base), `lg` or `xl`. |
| `tone` | `"default" \| "primary" \| "neutral" \| "success" \| "warning" \| "destructive" \| "info" \| "muted"` | `"default"` | `default` is plain foreground text; the semantic tones follow `Tone` (`muted` is the legacy name of `neutral`). |
| `weight` | `"regular" \| "medium" \| "semibold"` | `"regular"` | Font weight. |

### Variants

- `size`: `xs`, `sm`, `md`, `lg`, `xl` (default "md")
- `tone`: `default`, `primary`, `neutral`, `success`, `warning`, `destructive`, `info`, `muted` (default "default")
- `weight`: `regular`, `medium`, `semibold` (default "regular")

### Notes

**When to use:** Body text with size, tone and weight steps, plus the small typographic pieces: `Eyebrow` (an all-caps label above a heading), `Kbd` (a key hint) and `InlineCode`.

**Use instead when:**
- `Heading`: a heading with the display scale
- `ShortcutKeys`: a whole key combination from a shortcut string
- `CodeBlock`: multi-line code
- `Badge`: a short status label

#### Keyboard

Not focusable: no keyboard interaction. `Kbd` only shows a key; it does not listen for it.

#### Screen readers

- `Text` renders a `p` by default; `as` takes `p`, `span`, `div`, `small`, `strong` or `em`, and `asChild` styles your own element. Use `span` inside a line of text so you do not nest paragraphs.
- `Eyebrow` is a plain `p`, not a heading: it is read as a paragraph in front of the heading it labels.
- `Kbd` renders a native `<kbd>`, which screen readers read as its text. A symbol such as the command key may be read as nothing or as a name, so for combinations that matter use `ShortcutKeys` (it carries spoken text) or add visually hidden words.
- `InlineCode` renders a native `<code>`.

#### Reduced motion

Static: no animation.

#### Server rendering

Server render: same markup as the client. Plain markup with no browser API, so server and client output match.

#### Gotchas

- `tone` is `default` (foreground), `neutral`, `primary`, `success`, `warning`, `destructive` or `info`; `muted` is the old name of `neutral`. `neutral` is the muted grey, so it is quieter than `default`; `warning` uses the darker readable shade.
- `size` is `xs` to `xl` with `md` being `text-base`; `Text` sets no line-height or margin, so spacing comes from the parent (a `Stack`) and line-height from the surrounding styles.
- `Eyebrow` is always `text-primary`, uppercase and tracked; override with `className`. `Kbd` and `InlineCode` take only the HTML props of their element plus `className`; they have no size or tone variants.

## Textarea

> Multi-line text input with optional auto-resize and character counter. Consumes `Field` context.

- Import: `import { Textarea } from "@sutra/ui"` (or from `@sutra/ui/forms`)
- Source: `packages/ui/src/primitives/textarea` (primitives)
- `data-slot`: `textarea`, `textarea-wrapper`
- Also accepts the props of HTMLAttributes, TextareaHTMLAttributes

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `autoResize` | `boolean` | `false` | Grow with the content between `minRows` and `maxRows`. |
| `invalid` | `boolean` |  | Marks the textarea invalid: error border and `aria-invalid`. Inherited from a surrounding `Field` when omitted. |
| `maxRows` | `number` |  | Largest height in text rows when `autoResize` is on; taller content scrolls. Default: unlimited. |
| `minRows` | `number` | `3` | Minimum height in text rows (also the initial height). |
| `showCount` | `boolean` | `false` | Show a character counter (uses `maxLength` as the limit when set). |
| `variant` | `"outline" \| "filled"` |  | `outline` (default) is the bordered box; `filled` is a tinted surface with a hidden border. |
| `wrapperClassName` | `string` |  | Class for the wrapper rendered when `showCount` is on. |

### Notes

**When to use:** The multi-line text field. A native `<textarea>` with the shared input look, optional auto-resize between `minRows` and `maxRows`, and a character counter that uses `maxLength` as its limit.

**Use instead when:**
- `Input`: a single line
- `InputGroupTextarea`: a textarea that needs addons around it inside an `InputGroup`
- `RichTextEditor`: formatted text
- `TagInput`: several short tags

#### Keyboard

Native textarea behaviour: Enter inserts a new line, Tab moves focus on, and the text keys and selection shortcuts work as in any text field. The component adds no key handlers and nothing is direction dependent, so RTL changes nothing.

#### Screen readers

- A native `<textarea>` named by a `<label>`, `aria-label` or a surrounding `FieldLabel`; a textarea with no visible label needs `aria-label`. `invalid` sets `aria-invalid`, and `Field` supplies `id`, `aria-describedby`, `disabled` and `required` unless you pass them.
- The `showCount` counter is plain text ("12/280" with a hidden " characters used", or "12" with " characters" when there is no `maxLength`). It is not a live region and is not added to `aria-describedby`, so a screen reader finds it by reading the page but is not told as the count changes. Native `maxLength` stops typing at the limit.

#### Reduced motion

Static apart from the border, ring and counter colour transitions, which the reduced-motion net ends in 1 ms. The auto-resize height change is applied directly, with no transition.

#### Server rendering

Server render: part of it fills in after mount. The textarea renders on the server with `rows` set to `minRows` and the value or `defaultValue`. With `autoResize` the height is measured in a layout effect after mount, so a long value is `minRows` tall in the server HTML and grows when the page hydrates. Without `autoResize` nothing is measured and the output matches.

#### Slots

- `textarea`: the `<textarea>`
- `textarea-wrapper`: the outer `div`, rendered only with `showCount`

#### Gotchas

- `minRows` defaults to 3 and is both the initial height and, with `autoResize`, the smallest height; `maxRows` defaults to unlimited, and taller content scrolls inside once it is set. A `rows` prop sets the attribute but `autoResize` still sizes from `minRows`.
- `autoResize` turns the manual resize handle off (`resize-none`); otherwise the textarea is `resize-y`. It re-measures when the value changes and when the width changes.
- `className` is always on the `<textarea>`; `wrapperClassName` applies only when `showCount` adds the wrapper.
- The counter turns red when the length reaches `maxLength`, not only when it passes it, and with `showCount` the textarea gets extra bottom padding for it.

## TextLink

> Inline text link with underline styles and optional external indicator. With `onClick` and no `href` (or `as="button"`) it renders a button that reads as part of the sentence. For a standalone action use `Button variant="link"`.

- Import: `import { TextLink } from "@sutra/ui"` (or from `@sutra/ui/core`)
- Source: `packages/ui/src/primitives/text-link` (primitives)
- Also accepts the props of HTMLAttributes, AnchorHTMLAttributes

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `as` | `"a" \| "button"` |  | `button` renders a `<button type="button">` styled as a link, for an inline action inside a sentence. Default: `button` when there is an `onClick` but no `href`, otherwise `a`. |
| `asChild` | `boolean` |  | Render as the child element (e.g. a router Link). |
| `disabled` | `boolean` |  | Disables the button, or in link mode renders an `aria-disabled` link without `href` that ignores clicks. |
| `external` | `boolean` |  | Opens in a new tab with safe `rel` and shows an arrow-up-right icon. |
| `size` | `"inherit" \| "sm" \| "md" \| "lg"` | `"inherit"` | Text size: `inherit` keeps the surrounding size, or `sm`, `md`, `lg`. |
| `underline` | `"always" \| "hover" \| "none"` | `"hover"` | When the underline shows: `always`, on `hover` or `none`. |
| `variant` | `"default" \| "muted" \| "subtle" \| "destructive"` | `"default"` | Colour: `default` (primary), `muted`, `subtle` (text colour) or `destructive`. |

### Variants

- `variant`: `default`, `muted`, `subtle`, `destructive` (default "default")
- `underline`: `always`, `hover`, `none` (default "hover")
- `size`: `inherit`, `sm`, `md`, `lg` (default "inherit")

### Notes

**When to use:** An inline link that reads as part of a sentence, with underline styles, an optional external indicator and a button mode for in-sentence actions. With `onClick` and no `href` it renders a `<button>`.

**Use instead when:**
- `Button`: a standalone action (`variant="link"` gives the look)
- `Breadcrumb`: a navigation trail
- `AppStoreBadge`: a store download badge

#### Keyboard

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Moves focus to and from it. A disabled link or button is skipped |
| Enter | Follows the link, or presses the button |
| Space | Presses the button (not a link) |

No arrow keys are used, so nothing changes in RTL.

#### Screen readers

- Link mode is a native `<a>`; button mode is a `<button type="button">` unless you pass `type`. The name is the text.
- `external` adds target `_blank`, `rel="noopener noreferrer"` and a visually hidden " (opens in a new tab)" after the text; the arrow icon is `aria-hidden`.
- A disabled link has no `href`, `aria-disabled="true"`, `tabindex="-1"` and `role="link"`, so it is still announced as a link, as unavailable. A disabled button is natively disabled.

#### Reduced motion

The colour and underline fades and the nudge of the external arrow on hover are transitions, which the reduced-motion net ends within 1 ms: the effects still happen, without the glide.

#### Server rendering

Server render: same markup as the client. Plain markup with no browser API, so server and client output match.

#### Gotchas

- The element is chosen for you: a `<button>` when there is an `onClick` and no `href`, otherwise an `<a>`. Pass `as="a"` or `as="button"` to force one. `as="a"` without `href` is not focusable. `ref` is typed as an anchor in both cases, and `external` does nothing on a button.
- `underline` defaults to `hover`: inside running text the link shows only its colour until the pointer is over it, so use `underline="always"` there. `size` defaults to `inherit`, which takes the surrounding font size.
- `target="_blank"` on its own gets `rel="noopener noreferrer"` but not the screen reader hint; only `external` adds the hint. An explicit `target` or `rel` always wins over what `external` would set.
- With `asChild`, `external` still sets `target` and `rel` on the child and adds the arrow and the hidden " (opens in a new tab)" text, as the plain link does. A disabled `asChild` link keeps the child's `href`, with `aria-disabled`, `tabindex="-1"` and clicks blocked in the capture phase, so a router link does not navigate.

## TextShimmer

> Text with an animated light sweep, used for "Thinking…" style status lines.

- Import: `import { TextShimmer } from "@sutra/ui"` (or from `@sutra/ui/ai`)
- Source: `packages/ui/src/primitives/text-shimmer` (primitives)
- Also accepts the props of HTMLAttributes

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `as` | `React.ElementType` | `"span"` | Element to render. Defaults to `span`. |
| `duration` | `number` | `2` | Seconds for one sweep of the highlight. |
| `spread` | `number` | `12` | Half-width of the bright band, as a percentage of the text width. |

### Notes

**When to use:** Text with a light sweep moving across it, for "Thinking…" style status lines. It renders a `span` (or the element in `as`), sets the shimmer through CSS variables and keeps the text itself plain.

**Use instead when:**
- `AgentStatusLine`: a live "agent is working" line with verbs and a timer
- `Spinner`: a loading indicator that is not text
- `Typewriter`: text that types itself out
- `Skeleton`: a placeholder shape for content that is loading

#### Keyboard

Not focusable: no keyboard interaction.

#### Screen readers

The text is ordinary text in a `span` (or `as`), read as written. The shimmer is a background gradient clipped to the text, so it adds nothing to the accessibility tree. It is not a live region and has no role: for a status that changes, wrap it in your own `role="status"` or put it inside one.

#### Reduced motion

The component adds `motion-reduce:animate-none` itself, because the global net does not cover the shimmer animation (the motion guard test lists it as self-guarded). Under `prefers-reduced-motion` the text stops on a static gradient: muted text that brightens towards its right edge.

#### Server rendering

Server render: same markup as the client. Plain markup and inline CSS variables, no browser API, so server and client output match. The animation is pure CSS.

#### Gotchas

- `duration` is in seconds (default 2) and `spread` is the half-width of the bright band as a percentage of the gradient, clamped to 1 to 50 (default 12). The gradient is twice as wide as the text, so the band covers about twice that share of the text.
- The text is `color: transparent` with the gradient clipped to it, and the gradient reads `--muted-foreground` and `--foreground`. A `text-<colour>` class in `className` (`text-foreground`, `text-primary`) is dropped by the class merge so the shimmer keeps working; colour the two ends of the sweep with `--muted-foreground` and `--foreground` instead. Size classes such as `text-sm` are kept.
- It is `inline-block`, so it does not wrap with the surrounding line like inline text; give it a block parent for long text. `style` you pass is merged after the shimmer variables, so you can override them.

## TimePicker

> Time field with hour, minute (and optional second / AM-PM) segments. Each segment is a spinbutton: arrows step it, digits type into it, Backspace clears it. Value is a 24-hour `"HH:mm"` string.

- Import: `import { TimePicker } from "@sutra/ui"` (or from `@sutra/ui/forms`)
- Source: `packages/ui/src/primitives/time-picker` (primitives)
- `data-slot`: `time-picker`
- Also accepts the props of HTMLAttributes

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clearable` | `boolean` |  | Show an inline button that clears the time. |
| `defaultValue` | `string` |  | Initial time (`"HH:mm"`) when uncontrolled. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` |  | Disables every segment. |
| `granularity` | `TimeGranularity` | `"minute"` | Show a seconds segment. Default `"minute"`. |
| `hourCycle` | `12 \| 24` |  | Force a 12- or 24-hour clock. Defaults to the locale's convention. |
| `icon` | `boolean` | `true` | Show the leading clock icon. Default true. With `wheel` on it is the button that opens the wheels, so it stays. |
| `invalid` | `boolean` |  | Marks the field invalid: error border and `aria-invalid`. Inherited from a surrounding `Field` when omitted. |
| `labels` | `TimePickerLabels` |  | Override the segment names and the clear button label (i18n). |
| `locale` | `string` |  | BCP 47 locale for the clock convention, segment order and AM/PM labels. |
| `max` | `string` |  | Latest allowed time (`"HH:mm"`). |
| `min` | `string` |  | Earliest allowed time (`"HH:mm"`). Values outside the range are clamped. |
| `name` | `string` |  | Submits the value under this name through a hidden input. |
| `onValueChange` | `(value: string \| undefined) => void` |  | Called with the new time, or `undefined` when it is cleared or no longer complete. |
| `readOnly` | `boolean` |  | Shows the time without letting the user change it. |
| `required` | `boolean` |  | Marks the field required. Inherited from a surrounding `Field` when omitted. |
| `size` | `Size` | `"md"` | Field height and text size. |
| `step` | `number` | `1` | Minutes moved by the minute segment's arrow keys (snaps to multiples). Default 1. |
| `value` | `string` |  | Time as `"HH:mm"` (24-hour), or `"HH:mm:ss"` with `granularity="second"`. `undefined` means empty. |
| `wheel` | `boolean \| "touch"` | `false` | Offer scrolling wheels (hours, minutes, optional seconds and AM/PM, in the locale's order) in a popover, for touch. `true` adds a clock button that opens them on any device; `"touch"` does so only where the primary pointer is coarse, and there a tap on the field opens them and the segments stop raising the on-screen keyboard. The wheels keep `step`, `min`, `max` and `granularity`, change the value as they scroll, and Done closes them. The segments and their keys work as before. |

### Notes

**When to use:** A typed time of day made of hour, minute, optional second and AM/PM segments, each a spinbutton. The value is a 24-hour `"HH:mm"` string (`"HH:mm:ss"` with `granularity="second"`) whatever clock is shown.

**Use instead when:**
- `DateTimePicker`: a day and a time
- `WheelPicker`: a touch-first scrolling picker (`TimePicker wheel` puts those wheels in a popover)
- `Input`: a native `type="time"` field
- `NumberInput`: a plain number

#### Keyboard

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Moves between the segments, then the clear button (with `wheel` on, the clock button comes first) |
| ArrowLeft, ArrowRight | Previous or next segment (unfinished digits are committed first) |
| ArrowUp, ArrowDown | Step the segment by 1, wrapping at the ends without carrying into the next segment; the minute segment moves by `step` and snaps to its multiples; AM/PM toggles |
| Home, End | Set the segment to its lowest or highest value |
| 0 to 9 | Type into the segment; a complete entry moves focus to the next segment |
| A, P | In the AM/PM segment (or from the hour or minute on a 12-hour clock): set AM or PM |
| Backspace, Delete | Clear an hour, minute or second segment (AM/PM stays) |

Focusing a segment selects its text. With `wheel` the clock button opens the wheels: each is a listbox (arrows, Page keys, Home, End, type-ahead), Tab reaches Done, Escape closes and returns focus to the button. Ctrl, Meta and Alt chords are left to the browser. The segments sit in a `dir="ltr"` row in any reading direction, so Left and Right keep their physical meaning and nothing swaps in RTL.

#### Screen readers

- The wrapper is a `role="group"` named by `aria-label`, `aria-labelledby` or a surrounding `FieldLabel`. Each segment is a text input with `role="spinbutton"`, a name ("Hour", "Minute", "Second", "AM/PM"), `aria-valuemin`, `aria-valuemax`, `aria-valuenow` and `aria-valuetext` ("Empty" when unset).
- `labels` replaces the segment names, the clear button ("Clear time") and the spoken empty value, for translation.
- `invalid`, `required` and `readOnly` set `aria-invalid`, `aria-required` and `aria-readonly` on each segment; `disabled` also sets `aria-disabled` on the group. The clock icon and the separators are `aria-hidden`. With `wheel` the clock icon becomes a button named "Choose time" (`aria-haspopup="dialog"`) that opens a dialog of that name with one listbox per wheel (named like the segments) and Done; `labels.wheel` and `labels.done` translate them. On a coarse pointer the segments use `inputmode="none"`, so a tap opens the wheels, not the keyboard.

#### Reduced motion

Without `wheel` nothing moves; only the border and focus colours transition, which the net ends in 1 ms. With it the panel fades in like a popover, and a wheel glides to a row it was sent to (a click, an arrow key), which becomes a jump under reduced motion.

#### Server rendering

Server render: part of it fills in after mount. Without `hourCycle` and `locale` the clock convention and segment order come from the runtime's default locale, so a server and a browser with different locales can render a 24-hour field against a 12-hour one (an extra AM/PM segment) and trigger a hydration warning. Pass `locale` or `hourCycle` to make the first render deterministic.

#### Slots

- `time-picker`: the group element that wraps the segments

#### Gotchas

- `onValueChange` receives `undefined` whenever the time is incomplete, for example after clearing one segment; typing a digit that can still grow ("3" in the minute) waits until focus leaves or another digit completes it. `min` and `max` clamp the value when it is committed rather than blocking keys, and they are `"HH:mm"` strings.
- With `value` and no `onValueChange` the segments show what was typed but nothing is committed upstream. `name` posts the 24-hour value through a hidden input (empty when incomplete). `step` applies to minutes only and is rounded and limited to 1 to 59.
- `wheel` is opt-in: `true` adds the clock button everywhere, `"touch"` only on a coarse primary pointer. The wheels list every hour, minutes in multiples of `step` (a typed minute that is not one stays while it is the value), seconds with `granularity="second"` and AM/PM on a 12-hour clock, in the locale's order but always left to right; rows that `min` and `max` rule out are disabled. `readOnly` and `disabled` turn them off, and `DateTimePicker` does not take `wheel`.
- The wheels report through `onValueChange` as they move, like a typed time; a controlled parent that refuses a time keeps the old one. An empty field starts the wheels at `min` (or midnight) and stays empty until a wheel moves or Done is pressed.

## Toaster

> Sonner toaster styled with Sutra tokens. Follows the `.dark` class on <html> unless `theme` is set.

- Import: `import { Toaster } from "@sutra/ui"` (or from `@sutra/ui/core`)
- Source: `packages/ui/src/primitives/toast` (primitives)
- Also accepts the props of ToasterProps

### Props

No props of its own.

### Notes

**When to use:** Transient notifications through sonner. Mount `Toaster` once, then call `toast()` or `toast.success`, `toast.error`, `toast.promise` from anywhere. `snackbar()` shows the compact dark `Snackbar`; `Snackbar` also works as a plain inline bar.

**Use instead when:**
- `InlineAlert`: a message that stays next to the content it concerns
- `AlertBanner`: a page-level notice that persists
- `ConfirmDialog`: something the user must answer
- `DialogProvider`: ask from code and wait for the answer

#### Keyboard

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| Alt+T | Anywhere on the page: expand the stack and move focus to the notifications region (sonner's default `hotkey`, changeable with `hotkey`) |
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Moves through the focusable toasts and their action, cancel and close buttons once the region is focused |
| Enter, Space | Activate the focused button |
| Escape | While focus is inside the region: collapse the stack (it does not dismiss a toast) |

The region is not in the normal tab order (`tabindex="-1"`), so keyboard users reach it only through the hotkey. Toasts can also be swiped away with a pointer. The hotkey has no arrow keys. Sonner reads the document direction (`dir="auto"`) and mirrors its buttons and icons, but `position` is physical: `bottom-right` stays on the right in RTL.

#### Screen readers

The Toaster renders a `<section aria-label="Notifications alt+T" aria-live="polite" aria-relevant="additions text" aria-atomic="false">` on first render, so new toasts are announced politely without moving focus (`containerAriaLabel` and `customAriaLabel` rename it). Toasts are focusable list items with no role of their own; the close button is named "Close toast" (`closeButtonAriaLabel`). The success, info, warning and error icons are `aria-hidden`. `Snackbar` is `role="status"` with `aria-live="polite"` (pass `role="alert"` for errors), its dismiss button is named "Dismiss" (`closeLabel`), and its `icon` sits in an `aria-hidden` span. A snackbar shown through `snackbar()` sits inside the Toaster's live region and carries its own `status`.

#### Reduced motion

Sonner's own stylesheet turns off the toast transitions and animations under `prefers-reduced-motion`, so toasts appear and leave without sliding or stacking motion. The loading icon is Sutra's `Spinner`. Auto-dismiss timers are not affected.

#### Server rendering

Server render: same markup as the client. The server renders the empty live-region `<section>` only: toasts exist only after `toast()` is called on the client. The colour theme is read from `<html>` in an effect (light first), which cannot show before a toast appears.

#### Gotchas

- `toast()` is sonner's own function (re-exported from this module), callable outside React, and shows nothing until a `Toaster` is mounted. Mount exactly one near the root.
- Toasts last 4 seconds, pause while hovered, focused or expanded, and have no close button unless you pass `closeButton` to `Toaster`. Without it a keyboard user can only wait or press the hotkey; give actionable toasts `duration: Infinity` and a close button.
- `Toaster` follows `.dark` or `data-theme="dark"` on `<html>` unless you set `theme`; it defaults to `position="bottom-right"` and `gap={10}`, shows `visibleToasts` (3) at once, and applies Sutra classes with `unstyled` on. `toastOptions.classNames` are merged with the Sutra ones.
- `snackbar(message, options)` returns the toast id and closes after its action runs; `closable` (default true) shows a dismiss button whose `onClose` fires only for that button, so use sonner's `onDismiss` to catch timeouts and swipes. `Snackbar onClose` is a deprecated alias of `onDismiss`.

## ToggleButton

> A button that stays pressed (`aria-pressed`): bold, mute, pin. Controlled with `pressed`, or uncontrolled with `defaultPressed`.

- Import: `import { ToggleButton } from "@sutra/ui"` (or from `@sutra/ui/core`)
- Source: `packages/ui/src/primitives/toggle-group` (primitives)
- `data-slot`: `toggle-button`
- Also accepts the props of HTMLAttributes, ButtonHTMLAttributes, ToggleProps, PrimitivePropsWithRef

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `size` | `"sm" \| "md" \| "lg"` | `"md"` | Item height and padding. |
| `variant` | `"default" \| "outline" \| "soft"` | `"default"` | Look of the items: `default` (ghost), `outline` or `soft` (tinted when on). |

### Variants

- `variant`: `default`, `outline`, `soft` (default "default")
- `size`: `sm`, `md`, `lg` (default "md")

### Notes

**When to use:** A row of toggle buttons that stay pressed, in `type="single"` (at most one) or `type="multiple"` mode, with roving focus. `ToggleButton` is one standalone pressable button (bold, mute, pin).

**Use instead when:**
- `SegmentedControl`: an exclusive choice that must always have one selected
- `ButtonGroup`: attached action buttons or an attached radio-role choice
- `Checkbox`: a yes or no answer in a form
- `Switch`: a setting that applies at once
- `Tabs`: the choice swaps panels

#### Keyboard

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab / Shift+Tab | One tab stop for the whole group: the first pressed item, else the first item. A standalone `ToggleButton` is its own stop |
| ArrowRight, ArrowLeft | Move focus to the next or previous enabled item, wrapping at the ends (turn off with `loop={false}`) |
| Home, End | Focus the first or last item |
| Enter, Space | Press or unpress the focused item (native button) |

Arrow keys move focus only; they never change the value. Disabled items are skipped. In RTL the horizontal arrows swap: the group reads the direction from its parent (a `DirectionProvider`, a `dir` container or `<html dir>`), and its `dir` prop overrides it. With no `orientation` set the Up and Down arrows also move focus; set `orientation` to restrict the axis.

#### Screen readers

- The group is `role="group"` (not Radix's radiogroup or toolbar) and has no name of its own: pass `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`. Every item is a plain `<button>` with `aria-pressed` in both modes, not a radio.
- An icon-only item or `ToggleButton` needs `aria-label`. Icons are not hidden for you: pass `aria-hidden` icons next to text.
- Pressed state is announced as "pressed" or "not pressed"; the visual tint comes from `data-state="on"`.

#### Reduced motion

Only colour, background and border transitions, which the reduced-motion net ends in 1 ms. Nothing slides; for a sliding thumb use `SegmentedControl`.

#### Server rendering

Server render: same markup as the client. Plain markup: pressed state comes from `value`, `defaultValue` or `defaultPressed`, so server and client output match. The group writes a `dir` attribute that is `ltr` in the server HTML and settles after hydration, which only shows on an RTL page.

#### Slots

- `toggle-group-item`: an item in the group
- `toggle-button`: a standalone `ToggleButton`

#### Gotchas

- In `single` mode, pressing the pressed item clears the value: `onValueChange` receives `""`. If one item must always stay on, use `SegmentedControl`. `multiple` mode gives and takes a `string[]`.
- `variant` (`default`, `outline` or `soft`) and `size` set on the group flow to the items through context; an item's own `variant` or `size` wins.
- `ToggleGroupItem` needs `value`; a `ToggleButton` is controlled with `pressed` and `onPressedChange`, or uncontrolled with `defaultPressed`.
- The group wraps onto several lines (`flex-wrap`) instead of overflowing a narrow container.

## ToggleGroup

> Row of toggle buttons, `type="single"` or `"multiple"`, with roving focus (one tab stop, arrow keys move). Each item is a button with `aria-pressed`; give the group an `aria-label`. For an exclusive choice that reads as a tab-like switch, `SegmentedControl` is the better fit.

- Import: `import { ToggleGroup } from "@sutra/ui"` (or from `@sutra/ui/core`)
- Source: `packages/ui/src/primitives/toggle-group` (primitives)
- `data-slot`: `toggle-group`
- Parts: [`ToggleGroupItem`](ToggleGroupItem.md)
- Also accepts the props of HTMLAttributes

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `defaultValue` | `string \| string[]` |  | Initially pressed item value when uncontrolled. |
| `dir` | `"ltr" \| "rtl"` |  | Reading direction for arrow-key navigation; inherits the surrounding direction by default. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` |  | Disables every item. |
| `loop` | `boolean` |  | Wrap focus from the last item to the first (default true). |
| `onValueChange` | `((value: string) => void) \| ((value: string[]) => void)` |  | Called with the pressed item value, or an empty string when it is toggled off. |
| `orientation` | `"horizontal" \| "vertical"` |  | Restricts the arrow keys to this axis. Unset (the default), all four arrow keys move focus, and the group keeps its row layout either way. |
| `size` | `"sm" \| "md" \| "lg"` | `"md"` | Item height and padding. |
| `type` | `"single" \| "multiple"` |  | At most one item pressed; pressing it again clears the value to `""`. Any number of items pressed. |
| `value` | `string \| string[]` |  | Controlled pressed item value (empty string for none). Use with `onValueChange`. |
| `variant` | `"default" \| "outline" \| "soft"` | `"default"` | Look of the items: `default` (ghost), `outline` or `soft` (tinted when on). |

### Variants

- `variant`: `default`, `outline`, `soft` (default "default")
- `size`: `sm`, `md`, `lg` (default "md")

### Part props

Props of `ToggleGroupItem`: see [the full page](md/ToggleGroup.md).

### Notes

**When to use:** A row of toggle buttons that stay pressed, in `type="single"` (at most one) or `type="multiple"` mode, with roving focus. `ToggleButton` is one standalone pressable button (bold, mute, pin).

**Use instead when:**
- `SegmentedControl`: an exclusive choice that must always have one selected
- `ButtonGroup`: attached action buttons or an attached radio-role choice
- `Checkbox`: a yes or no answer in a form
- `Switch`: a setting that applies at once
- `Tabs`: the choice swaps panels

#### Keyboard

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab / Shift+Tab | One tab stop for the whole group: the first pressed item, else the first item. A standalone `ToggleButton` is its own stop |
| ArrowRight, ArrowLeft | Move focus to the next or previous enabled item, wrapping at the ends (turn off with `loop={false}`) |
| Home, End | Focus the first or last item |
| Enter, Space | Press or unpress the focused item (native button) |

Arrow keys move focus only; they never change the value. Disabled items are skipped. In RTL the horizontal arrows swap: the group reads the direction from its parent (a `DirectionProvider`, a `dir` container or `<html dir>`), and its `dir` prop overrides it. With no `orientation` set the Up and Down arrows also move focus; set `orientation` to restrict the axis.

#### Screen readers

- The group is `role="group"` (not Radix's radiogroup or toolbar) and has no name of its own: pass `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`. Every item is a plain `<button>` with `aria-pressed` in both modes, not a radio.
- An icon-only item or `ToggleButton` needs `aria-label`. Icons are not hidden for you: pass `aria-hidden` icons next to text.
- Pressed state is announced as "pressed" or "not pressed"; the visual tint comes from `data-state="on"`.

#### Reduced motion

Only colour, background and border transitions, which the reduced-motion net ends in 1 ms. Nothing slides; for a sliding thumb use `SegmentedControl`.

#### Server rendering

Server render: same markup as the client. Plain markup: pressed state comes from `value`, `defaultValue` or `defaultPressed`, so server and client output match. The group writes a `dir` attribute that is `ltr` in the server HTML and settles after hydration, which only shows on an RTL page.

#### Slots

- `toggle-group-item`: an item in the group
- `toggle-button`: a standalone `ToggleButton`

#### Gotchas

- In `single` mode, pressing the pressed item clears the value: `onValueChange` receives `""`. If one item must always stay on, use `SegmentedControl`. `multiple` mode gives and takes a `string[]`.
- `variant` (`default`, `outline` or `soft`) and `size` set on the group flow to the items through context; an item's own `variant` or `size` wins.
- `ToggleGroupItem` needs `value`; a `ToggleButton` is controlled with `pressed` and `onPressedChange`, or uncontrolled with `defaultPressed`.
- The group wraps onto several lines (`flex-wrap`) instead of overflowing a narrow container.

## Tooltip

> Tooltip root. Uses the nearest `TooltipProvider` (so skip-delay works across tooltips) and falls back to its own provider when there is none.

- Import: `import { Tooltip } from "@sutra/ui"` (or from `@sutra/ui/overlays`)
- Source: `packages/ui/src/primitives/tooltip` (primitives)
- Parts: [`TooltipContent`](TooltipContent.md), [`TooltipProvider`](TooltipProvider.md), [`TooltipTrigger`](TooltipTrigger.md)
- Also accepts the props of TooltipProps

### Props

No props of its own.

### Part props

Props of `TooltipContent`: see [the full page](md/Tooltip.md).

### Notes

**When to use:** A short text label that appears when an element is hovered or focused, for icon buttons and truncated text. `SimpleTooltip` is the one-line form with an optional keyboard `shortcut` chip.

**Use instead when:**
- `Popover`: interactive or rich content the user can click into
- `HoverCard`: a rich preview on hover
- `InfoTooltip`: a help icon with a title and description
- `Dialog`: anything the user must read or act on

#### Keyboard

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Focusing the trigger opens the tooltip after the delay; moving focus away closes it |
| Escape | Close the tooltip while its trigger has focus |

The tooltip has no focusable content and the trigger keeps its own keyboard behaviour. There are no arrow keys, so RTL changes nothing. In RTL, `side="start"` and `side="end"` swap left and right (read through `useDirection()`: a `DirectionProvider` with a `dir`, else `<html dir>`; a plain `dir` attribute on a container is not seen); the default is `top`, `left` and `right` stay physical, and Radix still flips the bubble on a collision. Pressing the trigger (click, Enter or Space) also closes the tooltip.

#### Screen readers
