The content is `role="tooltip"` and, while open, the trigger gets `aria-describedby` pointing at it, so it is read as the trigger's description, not its name. Give icon-only triggers an `aria-label`: the tooltip alone does not name them. If you pass `aria-label` to `TooltipContent`, Radix hides the visual content from assistive technology and exposes that label in a visually hidden `role="tooltip"` copy. The arrow is decoration. Keep tooltip text short and plain; no links or buttons.

#### Reduced motion

The bubble fades and zooms in from its trigger and slides slightly from its side; the reduced-motion net removes the slide and the scale and keeps only the fade. The open delay is a timer and stays.

#### Server rendering

Server render: same markup as the client. Only the trigger renders on the server; the bubble is portalled after mount and only opens from pointer hover or focus. Nothing differs between server and client.

#### Gotchas

- The default open delay is 200 ms (`TooltipProvider` and a provider-less `Tooltip` both fall back to 200, not Radix's 700), and `skipDelayDuration` is 300 ms. Mount one `TooltipProvider` near the root so moving between tooltips skips the delay; without one each `Tooltip` makes its own provider.
- Touch does not open it: Radix ignores touch pointers and a tap closes it, so never keep essential information only in a tooltip.
- `SimpleTooltip` wraps `children` in `TooltipTrigger asChild`, so the child must accept a ref and forward props to a focusable element. It renders just the children when `disabled`, or when `content` is `null`, `undefined` or `false`.
- `SimpleTooltip shortcut` is display only: a spec like `"mod+k"` renders platform-aware chips, a glyph string or an array renders one `Kbd` per entry. Nothing is bound to the keys.

## UndoAction

> A destructive button that turns into a counted "Undo" for N seconds and only then commits (`onCommit`). The deadline is the wall clock, so a throttled tab still commits on time; the ring and the number follow it. The focus stays on the same button, so Enter or Space undoes. Pair it with a `Toast` through `onArm` and a controlled `armed`. The three labels sit in one grid cell, so the width never jumps. A polite live region announces the countdown, the undo and the commit.

- Import: `import { UndoAction } from "@sutra/ui"` (or from `@sutra/ui/core`)
- Source: `packages/ui/src/primitives/undo-action` (primitives)
- `data-slot`: `undo-action`, `undo-action-ring`
- Also accepts the props of HTMLAttributes, ButtonHTMLAttributes

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `onCommit` (required) | `() => void \| Promise<unknown>` |  | Runs once the countdown ends (not before). A returned promise shows a spinner; a rejection brings the button back. |
| `armed` | `boolean` |  | The countdown is running. Set it from outside (a toast's Undo button sets it to false). |
| `armedVariant` | `ButtonProps["variant"]` | `"secondary"` | Variant while the countdown runs. Default "secondary". |
| `committedLabel` | `React.ReactNode` | `"Deleted"` | Text shown once the action went through (after the window closes). |
| `defaultArmed` | `boolean` | `false` | Initial armed state when uncontrolled. |
| `fullWidth` | `boolean \| null` |  | Stretches the button to the width of its container. |
| `icon` | `React.ReactNode` |  | Icon before the idle label. |
| `label` | `React.ReactNode` | `"Delete"` | Label of the idle button. Default "Delete". |
| `messages` | `{ armed?: (seconds: number) => string; undone?: string; committed?: string }` |  | Screen reader messages (a polite live region). |
| `onArm` | `() => void` |  | Runs when the user presses the button and the countdown starts (start a `Toast` here). |
| `onArmedChange` | `(armed: boolean) => void` |  | Called when the countdown starts or stops (including when undone). |
| `onUndo` | `() => void` |  | Runs when the user presses "Undo". Setting a controlled `armed` to false from outside cancels silently. |
| `pauseOnFocus` | `boolean` | `false` | Hold the countdown while the button has keyboard focus (focus that came from a click does not count). |
| `pauseOnHover` | `boolean` | `false` | Hold the countdown while the pointer is over the button. |
| `seconds` | `number` | `8` | Seconds the user has to undo. Default 8. |
| `size` | `"icon" \| "sm" \| "md" \| "lg" \| "xs" \| "xl" \| "icon-xs" \| "icon-sm" \| "icon-lg" \| "icon-xl" \| null` | `"md"` | Button height and padding; `icon-*` sizes are square. |
| `spinnerProps` | `Partial<SpinnerProps>` |  | Overrides for the loading spinner (variant, size, `label`, colour via `className`); it inherits the button text colour by default. |
| `undoLabel` | `React.ReactNode` | `"Undo"` | Label of the button while the undo window is open. |
| `variant` | `"link" \| "ghost" \| "primary" \| "destructive" \| "soft" \| "outline" \| "inverse" \| "secondary" \| "tertiary" \| "destructive-soft" \| null` | `"primary"` | Visual style: `primary` (filled), `secondary` (bordered), `tertiary` (muted fill), `soft`, `ghost`, `outline`, `destructive`, `destructive-soft`, `inverse` or `link`. |

### Notes

**When to use:** A destructive button that, once pressed, turns into a counted "Undo" for a few seconds and only then commits. The countdown follows the wall clock, shows a ring and a number, and the focus stays on the same button.

**Use instead when:**
- `ConfirmDialog`: the action needs an explicit yes or no first
- `SlideToConfirm`: the action is deliberate and cannot be undone
- `Button`: nothing to undo
- `Toaster`: show the undo as a toast (pair it through `onArm` and a controlled `armed`)

#### Keyboard

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Moves focus to and from the button. A `disabled` button is skipped |
| Enter, Space | Idle: starts the countdown (`onArm`). During it: undoes (`onUndo`). The focus never leaves the button |

It is a single native button, so there are no arrow keys and nothing changes in RTL. Once committed it is `aria-disabled` and presses do nothing, but it stays focusable. `pauseOnFocus` holds the countdown while the button has keyboard focus (focus from a click does not count).

#### Screen readers

- The name is the visible label of the current phase: `label` ("Delete"), then `undoLabel` ("Undo"), then `committedLabel` ("Deleted"). The other two labels are `aria-hidden`, and so are the ring and its number, so the changing digit is not read.
- A sibling visually hidden `role="status"` announces the transitions, nothing on first render: "Undo available for N seconds" when armed, "Undone" after an undo, "Done" after the commit. `messages` replaces any of the three (`armed` is a function of the seconds).
- `aria-busy` is on the button while a promise from `onCommit` runs (it is a `Button` with `loading`).

#### Reduced motion

The label cross-fade and the ring's progress are short transitions, which the reduced-motion net ends within 1 ms, so the ring steps instead of gliding. The countdown is wall-clock time, not an animation, so it runs the same.

#### Server rendering

Server render: same markup as the client. No browser API at render: the deadline starts in a layout effect after mount, and before that the ring shows the full window. A `defaultArmed` button renders armed and begins counting after hydration.

#### Slots

- `undo-action`: the button
- `undo-action-ring`: the ring with the seconds left

#### Gotchas

- Unmounting during the window drops the action: `onCommit` never runs (the test pins it). Keep it mounted until the countdown ends, or commit on unmount yourself.
- After the commit the button stays on `committedLabel` and is inert; it does not reset on its own. Re-arm it from outside with a controlled `armed`, or remount it. A promise from `onCommit` shows a spinner, and a rejection brings the button back to idle.
- With a controlled `armed`, setting it to `false` from outside cancels silently (no `onUndo`), and setting it to `true` starts the countdown. `onArmedChange(false)` fires at the commit too, not only on undo.
- `pauseOnHover` ignores touch pointers. `seconds` is at least 1 (default 8). `variant` is the idle look (default `destructive-soft`) and `armedVariant` the counting one (default `secondary`); `onClick`, `children`, `asChild` and `loading` are not accepted.

## VolumeSlider

> Volume control: a mute toggle (speaker icon by level), a `Slider` and the level ("64%" or "Muted"). Muting keeps the value, so unmuting restores it; moving the slider while muted unmutes.

- Import: `import { VolumeSlider } from "@sutra/ui"` (or from `@sutra/ui/system`)
- Source: `packages/ui/src/primitives/volume-slider` (primitives)
- `data-slot`: `volume-slider`, `volume-slider-level`
- Also accepts the props of HTMLAttributes

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `accent` | `Accent` |  | Categorical colour of the range and thumb. Default primary. |
| `defaultMuted` | `boolean` | `false` | Initial muted state when uncontrolled. |
| `defaultValue` | `number` | `100` | Initial volume from 0 to 100 when uncontrolled. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` |  | Disables the slider and the mute button. |
| `hideMuteButton` | `boolean` | `false` | Hide the mute toggle (the slider alone). Default false. |
| `label` | `string` | `"Volume"` | Accessible name of the slider, e.g. "Music volume". Default "Volume". |
| `levelClassName` | `string` |  | Class for the level label. |
| `muteButtonClassName` | `string` |  | Class for the mute toggle, merged last (e.g. another button style). |
| `muted` | `boolean` |  | Controlled muted state. While muted the slider keeps the stored level (turned neutral grey) unless `zeroWhenMuted` shows it at 0. Use with `onMutedChange`. |
| `muteLabel` | `string` |  | Accessible name of the mute toggle. Default `Mute ${label}`. |
| `muteToggle` | `"pressed" \| "label"` | `"pressed"` | How the toggle exposes its state: `"pressed"` (default) keeps one name with `aria-pressed`; `"label"` swaps its name between `muteLabel` and `unmuteLabel`. |
| `onMutedChange` | `(muted: boolean) => void` |  | Called when the mute button toggles the muted state. |
| `onValueChange` | `(value: number) => void` |  | Called with the new volume (0 to 100) as the slider moves. |
| `orientation` | `"horizontal" \| "vertical"` | `"horizontal"` | Slider direction. Vertical stacks the toggle, slider and level in a column. Default "horizontal". |
| `renderSlider` | `(slider: React.ReactElement) => React.ReactNode` |  | Wrap the slider, e.g. in a reveal-on-hover container or a popover. |
| `restoreOnUnmute` | `number` |  | Value to set when the toggle unmutes a level of 0 (the toggle then reads as "unmute" at 0). Default: none. |
| `showLevel` | `boolean` | `true` | Show the level ("64%", or "Muted") after the slider. Default true. |
| `size` | `Size` | `"md"` | Slider and button size. |
| `sliderClassName` | `string` |  | Class for the slider. |
| `step` | `number` | `1` | Keyboard step. Default 1. |
| `unmuteLabel` | `string` |  | Accessible name of the toggle when it unmutes (`muteToggle="label"`). Default `Unmute ${label}`. |
| `value` | `number` |  | Volume 0–100. |
| `zeroWhenMuted` | `boolean` | `false` | Show the slider at 0 while muted instead of keeping the stored level. Default false. |

### Notes

**When to use:** A volume control made of a mute toggle with a level-aware speaker icon, a `Slider` from 0 to 100 and a level label ("64%" or "Muted"). Muting keeps the level, so unmuting restores it.

**Use instead when:**
- `Slider`: any other numeric range
- `Switch`: an on or off setting
- `ToggleButton`: a pressed state with no level
- `Progress`: playback or loading position the user does not drag

#### Keyboard

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab / Shift+Tab | The mute toggle, then the slider thumb |
| Enter, Space | On the toggle: mute or unmute (native button) |
| ArrowRight, ArrowUp | On the thumb: raise by `step` (default 1); moving while muted also unmutes |
| ArrowLeft, ArrowDown | Lower by `step` |
| Shift+Arrow, PageUp, PageDown | Move ten steps |
| Home, End | 0 or 100 |

The thumb follows `Slider`, so in RTL ArrowLeft raises and ArrowRight lowers; the toggle has no direction dependent keys. With `orientation="vertical"` the toggle, slider and level stack in a column.

#### Screen readers

- The thumb is a `role="slider"` named by `label` (default "Volume") with `aria-valuenow` from 0 to 100 and `aria-valuetext` set to the level text: "64%", or "Muted" while muted (the value stays at the kept level).
- The toggle is a native button. By default it keeps one name, "Mute" plus the label, and reports the state with `aria-pressed`. With `muteToggle="label"` there is no `aria-pressed` and the name swaps to `unmuteLabel` ("Unmute Volume") while it would unmute. Set `muteLabel` and `unmuteLabel` to translate them.
- The visible level text is `aria-hidden` because the thumb already announces it; the speaker icon is `aria-hidden`. `hideMuteButton` removes the toggle.

#### Reduced motion

The toggle colour fades and the slider's thumb ring and press scale use short transitions; the reduced-motion net ends them in 1 ms.

#### Server rendering

Server render: part of it fills in after mount. The toggle, level text and slider track render on the server from `value`, `defaultValue` and `muted`. The slider thumb is `display: none` until Radix mounts and locates it, so it appears after hydration, and the direction settles after hydration on an RTL page.

#### Slots

- `volume-slider`: the root; `data-muted` and `data-orientation` are set on it
- `volume-slider-level`: the level label

#### Gotchas

- Muting does not change the value: the slider stays at the kept level (it turns neutral grey) unless `zeroWhenMuted` shows it at 0. Moving the slider while muted unmutes and sets the value.
- At a level of 0 the icon is muted but `muted` is false. With `restoreOnUnmute={30}` the toggle then reads as "unmute" and sets 30 on press.
- `value` is a number from 0 to 100, rounded and clamped; `onValueChange` receives a number and `onMutedChange` a boolean. `muted` and `value` are controlled independently.
- `renderSlider` wraps the slider element (for a reveal-on-hover container or a popover); `disabled` disables both the toggle and the slider. `dir` is not accepted: the direction comes from the page.

## WheelPicker

> An iOS-style wheel for one list of values (time, duration, amount, day): the rows scroll with the mouse wheel or a finger and snap one at a time (CSS scroll-snap with `scroll-snap-stop: always`, so a fling cannot skip rows), the row in the centre is the value once the scroll stops. It is a `role="listbox"` with the selected row as `aria-activedescendant`: Arrow keys move one row, Page keys five, Home and End jump to the ends, typing selects by prefix, clicking a row selects it. Disabled rows are skipped. Controlled (`value`) or uncontrolled (`defaultValue`); under reduced motion the keys jump instead of gliding. The accessible name comes from `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`.

- Import: `import { WheelPicker } from "@sutra/ui"` (or from `@sutra/ui/forms`)
- Source: `packages/ui/src/primitives/wheel-picker` (primitives)
- `data-slot`: `wheel-picker`, `wheel-picker-band`, `wheel-picker-list`
- Parts: [`WheelPickerGroup`](WheelPickerGroup.md)
- Also accepts the props of HTMLAttributes

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `options` (required) | `readonly (string \| WheelPickerOption)[]` |  | Items on the wheel, as strings or `{ value, label }` objects, in order. |
| `band` | `boolean` | `true` | Draw the highlight band behind the centre row (a `WheelPickerGroup` draws one band across its columns). Default true. |
| `defaultValue` | `string \| null` |  | Initially selected value when uncontrolled. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Disables scrolling and keyboard changes. |
| `emptyState` | `React.ReactNode` | `"No options"` | Shown when there are no options. Default "No options". |
| `itemHeight` | `number` | `36` | Row height in px. Default 36. |
| `listClassName` | `string` |  | Class names for the scrolling listbox. |
| `loading` | `boolean` | `false` | Options are on their way: placeholder rows and `aria-busy`, no listbox. |
| `onValueChange` | `(value: string) => void` |  | Called with the value that is centred when scrolling settles or a key is pressed. |
| `value` | `string \| null` |  | Controlled selected value. Use with `onValueChange`. |
| `visibleCount` | `number` | `5` | Rows in view (odd; an even number is raised by one). Default 5. |

### Part props

Props of `WheelPickerGroup`: see [the full page](md/WheelPicker.md).

### Notes

**When to use:** An iOS-style wheel for one list of values (hour, minute, duration, amount) that you scroll or flick, with one row snapping into the centre band. `WheelPickerGroup` puts several wheels side by side under one band, with one value per column.

**Use instead when:**
- `Select`: a desktop dropdown from a list
- `TimePicker`: a typed time field
- `NumberInput`: an exact number
- `SegmentedControl`: a few visible options
- `DateTimePicker`: a calendar date and time

#### Keyboard

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab / Shift+Tab | The wheel is one tab stop (a group has one per column) |
| ArrowDown, ArrowUp | Move the selection one row, skipping disabled rows, without wrapping |
| PageDown, PageUp | Move five rows |
| Home, End | First or last enabled row |
| A letter or digit | Type-ahead: select the next row whose text starts with what you typed (a 600 ms pause starts a new query; a repeated letter cycles) |

Space and Enter do nothing; moving the selection is the choice. Alt, Ctrl and Meta chords are left alone. With the mouse or a finger, scrolling snaps one row at a time and clicking a row selects it. The wheel is vertical, so RTL swaps no keys.

#### Screen readers

- One wheel is a `role="listbox"` that keeps focus; the selected row is `aria-activedescendant` and `aria-selected` on its `role="option"`, and disabled rows are `aria-disabled`. Name it with `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`: a bare `WheelPicker` has no name.
- `WheelPickerGroup` is a `role="group"` (pass it an `aria-label`) of listboxes named by each column `label`, such as "Hours". Separators and the highlight band are `aria-hidden`.
- With `loading` there is no listbox, only placeholder rows, `aria-busy` and the text "Loading…" for screen readers; with no options the `emptyState` text shows instead.
- The value is reported when scrolling settles, not for every row that passes the centre.

#### Reduced motion

Under `prefers-reduced-motion` a key press jumps to the row; otherwise it glides with a smooth scroll. A parent changing `value` also glides only when motion is allowed, and the row colours fade in a short transition that the net ends in 1 ms.

#### Server rendering

Server render: part of it fills in after mount. The listbox and all rows render on the server, but the scroll position is set after mount, so the server HTML is scrolled to the first row and the centre row's bold, foreground style is applied by script after hydration. The box height is set inline from `visibleCount` and `itemHeight`, so only the scroll position changes on hydration.

#### Slots

- `wheel-picker`: the root; `wheel-picker-list`: the scrolling listbox
- `wheel-picker-band`: the highlight behind the centre row
- `wheel-picker-group`: the group root

#### Gotchas

- `options` take strings or `{ value, label, disabled, textValue }`; `textValue` is what type-ahead matches when `label` is not a string. Values must be unique strings.
- `visibleCount` (default 5) is raised to the next odd number so there is a centre row, and `itemHeight` (default 36) is in pixels.
- `onValueChange` receives a string once the scroll stops. A scroll that stops on a disabled row moves to the nearest enabled one. In a group it receives all values plus `{ columnId, index }`.
- `wheelRange` (exported from the same module) builds padded numeric options such as `00` to `59`.

Domain-neutral compositions in short form; `md/<Name>.md` has the props tables, variants and an example.

- Props: `items`*, `bottomBarProps`, `breakpoint`, `defaultValue`, `label`, `mode`, `onValueChange`, `query`, `renderLink`, `value` (* required)

> Procedural agent avatar drawn as pure SVG from `{ shape, color, face, seed }`.

- Props: `spec`*, `label`, `size` (* required)

> See `AnimatedListInner`: the generic cast keeps `ref` and the item type together.

- Import: `import { AnimatedList } from "@sutra/ui/motion"` ([full page](md/AnimatedList.md))

## AnimatedNumber

> A number whose digits roll to their new values, in tabular figures. Each digit is a column of 0 to 9 slid with a CSS transition, so the first render shows the value without motion and reduced motion shows changes at once. Screen readers get the formatted value once as text (the columns are hidden from them, and from copy and paste); add `aria-live="polite"` to announce changes. Numbers only: format other values yourself.

- Import: `import { AnimatedNumber } from "@sutra/ui/dataviz"` ([full page](md/AnimatedNumber.md))
- Props: `value`*, `animate`, `duration`, `format`, `locale` (* required)

**When to use:** A number whose digits roll to their new values when `value` changes, in tabular figures. Formatting uses `Intl.NumberFormat` (currency, percent, compact), and the first render shows the value without motion.

**Use instead when:**
- `StatValue`: a number inside a StatCard (it has an `animate` option that uses this)
- `Countdown`: a time that counts down
- `Typewriter`: text that types itself out
- `Text`: a number that never changes

#### Keyboard

Not focusable: no keyboard interaction.

#### Screen readers

The formatted value is rendered once as visually hidden text, and the rolling digit columns are `aria-hidden` and `select-none`, so a screen reader reads the number once and copy and paste do not pick up the columns. It is not a live region: pass `aria-live="polite"` (props go on the root `span`) to have changes announced. It has no role or label of its own, so say what the number is in the surrounding text.

#### Reduced motion

The digits roll through a CSS transition on `transform` and a new digit column fades in with `animate-fade-in`. Under `prefers-reduced-motion` the net ends the transition in 1 ms and stops the fade, so a change shows at once.

#### Server rendering

Server render: part of it fills in after mount. The first render is the final value with no motion and no browser API, so the markup is stable. It is formatted with `Intl.NumberFormat`, though: without `locale` the server's runtime locale and the browser's can format the same number differently (`1,234` against `1.234`) and hydration will warn, so pass `locale` where the HTML is rendered on a server.

#### Slots

- `animated-number`: the root `span` (also with `animate={false}`, where it holds plain text)
- `animated-number-digit`: one rolling digit column (`data-digit` is its value)
- `animated-number-text`: a separator, sign, currency symbol or unit

#### Gotchas

- Numbers only: `value` is a `number`. A value that is not finite (`NaN`, `Infinity`) shows as one static piece of text. Format anything else yourself.
- Columns are keyed from the decimal point outward, so a digit stays in its column when one is added (99 to 100 keeps the nines and fades in the new hundreds place). Only added columns fade in, never the first render.
- `animate={false}` renders plain formatted text with no columns, which suits dense tables and lists; `duration` is in milliseconds and defaults to the fill speed token (`--sutra-duration-fill`, 500 ms).
- `locale` also picks the digit glyphs (Arabic-Indic, Devanagari and so on), and a bad `locale` or `format` falls back to the default format instead of throwing. An inline `format` object is fine: it is compared by its contents.

## AreaChart

## BottomTabBar

> Fixed mobile bottom navigation: icon over label, ≥44px targets, badges and safe-area padding.

- Import: `import { BottomTabBar } from "@sutra/ui/mobile"` ([full page](md/BottomTabBar.md))
- Parts: `BottomTabBarItem`
- Props: `defaultValue`, `glass`, `hideAbove`, `items`, `onValueChange`, `position`, `primaryAction`, `renderLink`, `value` (* required)

**When to use:** Mobile bottom navigation: icon over label tabs at least 44 px tall, count and dot badges, an optional raised centre action and safe-area padding. It hides itself from a breakpoint up. `AdaptiveTabs` shows the same items as inline pills on wide screens and as this bar on phones.

**Use instead when:**
- `Tabs`: switch panels inside a page
- `Sidebar`: app navigation on wide screens
- `HeaderNav`: site navigation in a top bar
- `SegmentedControl`: switch between a few views of one thing
- `FloatingActionButton`: one pinned screen action

#### Keyboard

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Each tab (and the centre action) is its own tab stop |
| Enter, Space | Press a button tab. A link tab follows on Enter only |

It is navigation, not a tablist: there is no arrow-key roving, and no key depends on direction, so RTL changes nothing except that the tabs run right to left.

#### Screen readers

- A `nav` named "Primary" (`aria-label`; `AdaptiveTabs` names its two navigations "Sections" and "Sections tab bar") holding a list. The selected tab has `aria-current="page"`; there is no `aria-selected` or `tab` role.
- A badge is `aria-hidden`; a hidden "(3 new)" or "(new)" follows the label instead, so the tab reads "Inbox (3 new)". The icon is not hidden for you: pass `aria-hidden` icons.
- The centre action is a plain button named by `primaryAction.label`. A disabled link loses its `href` and gets `aria-disabled`.
- With `AdaptiveTabs` both navigations are in the page and CSS (`display: none`) hides one, so only one is exposed at a time.

#### Reduced motion

The active pill grows in over 200 ms, a tap scales the centre action, and a changing badge pops (`animate-pop`). The global net ends the transitions in 1 ms and stops the pop.

#### Server rendering

Server render: same markup as the client. Plain markup from props; showing or hiding by breakpoint is CSS (`md:hidden`), so the server and client HTML match.

#### Slots

- `bottom-tab-bar`: the `nav`
- `primary-action`: the raised centre button
- `indicator`: the active pill behind the icon
- `badge-count`, `badge-dot`: the badges
- `adaptive-tabs-inline`: the inline navigation of `AdaptiveTabs`

#### Gotchas

- `position="fixed"` (default) pins the bar to the viewport bottom and hides it from `md` up (`hideAbove`, `"never"` keeps it): give the page bottom padding, and use `static` or `sticky` for previews and frames. The safe-area padding needs `viewport-fit=cover`.
- A click selects the tab at once, even for links. In a router app control `value` from the current route (and `onValueChange` for the rest), or the highlight and the page can disagree after back and forward.
- A tab is a `<button>`, an `<a>` when it has `href` (through `renderLink` for a router link, which receives `className`, `aria-current`, `onClick` and `data-state`), or your element with `asChild`. Pass `items` or `BottomTabBarItem` children, and `label` is required text.
- `primaryAction` is inserted in the middle of the tabs (after the first half), so use an even number of items. `badge` is a number (shown as `99+` above 99) or `true` for a dot; `0` and `false` hide it.

## CalendarHeatmap

> GitHub-style contribution calendar: week columns, month/weekday labels, totals, month mode.

- Import: `import { CalendarHeatmap } from "@sutra/ui/ops"` ([full page](md/CalendarHeatmap.md))
- Props: `data`*, `cellSize`, `colorStops`, `defaultMonth`, `endDate`, `formatTooltip`, `formatValue`, `gap`, `label`, `legend`, `locale`, `max`, `min`, `mode`, `month`, `onCellClick`, `onMonthChange`, `scale`, `showDayNumbers`, `showMonthLabels`, `showTotal`, `showWeekdayLabels`, `steps`, `unit`, `weekStartsOn` (* required)

**When to use:** A GitHub-style activity calendar: one cell per day, in week columns over the last year (`mode="year"`) or in a single month with previous and next buttons (`mode="month"`), with a total and a "Less to More" legend.

**Use instead when:**
- `HeatmapGrid`: a plain grid of values that are not days
- `DatePicker`: choose a date rather than read activity
- `BarChart`: daily values read off an axis
- `StatCard`: one total with a trend

#### Keyboard

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab / Shift+Tab | One day cell holds the tab stop; the month buttons are separate stops |
| ArrowLeft, ArrowRight | The same weekday in the previous or next week |
| ArrowUp, ArrowDown | The previous or next day in the week column |
| Home, End | The same weekday in the first or last week shown |
| Ctrl+Home, Ctrl+End (Cmd on Mac) | The first or last day shown |
| Enter, Space | On a day: calls `onCellClick(date, value)` when it is set. On "Previous month" or "Next month" (month mode): changes the month |
| Escape | Hides the tooltip |

The whole calendar is a forced `dir="ltr"` island: time runs left to right and the arrows never swap in RTL; the month buttons keep previous on the left.

#### Screen readers

- A `grid` named by `label` (default "Activity in the last year" or "Activity in October 2026") with seven `row`s, one per weekday. Each row header holds the long weekday name as hidden text; the visible short names are `aria-hidden` (every other row in year mode).
- A day is named "15 sessions on Oct 3 (Saturday, October 3, 2026)"; days with no data read as 0. `formatTooltip` changes the first part. Month labels, day numbers and the tooltip are `aria-hidden`.
- In month mode the title ("October 2026") is `aria-live="polite"`, so navigating announces the new month. The total line ("19 sessions in the last year") and the legend are plain text.

#### Reduced motion

Cell colour fades over 300 ms with a transition that the global net ends within 1 ms. Nothing else moves.

#### Server rendering

Server render: part of it fills in after mount. Without `endDate` (year) or `defaultMonth` (month) the range starts from `new Date()`, and day keys, month names and numbers use the local time zone and the runtime locale, so the server HTML can differ from the browser's. Pass `endDate` or `defaultMonth` and a `locale` to make both sides agree.

#### Gotchas

- Year mode shows exactly the 53 week columns that end on `endDate` (default today) and is fixed width (cell size plus gap, 14 px per week by default), so in a narrow box it scrolls sideways from the oldest week; it does not scroll to the newest.
- Several entries on the same day are summed, and entries outside the range are ignored (and left out of the total). `max` defaults to the largest day (at least 1), so one huge day washes out the rest: set `max`.
- `date` strings are local calendar days (`YYYY-MM-DD`); a datetime string or a `Date` is bucketed by its local date.
- `month` (any date in the month) makes month mode controlled and needs `onMonthChange`; use `defaultMonth` for uncontrolled. `weekStartsOn` is 0 (Sunday, default) or 1 (Monday).

## CameraCapture

> Camera photo and video capture with a mirrored preview, countdown, timed prompts, review, and permission states.

- Import: `import { CameraCapture } from "@sutra/ui/media"` ([full page](md/CameraCapture.md))
- Props: `onCapture`*, `audio`, `constraints`, `countdown`, `deviceId`, `facingMode`, `hint`, `loading`, `maxDuration`, `mirror`, `mode`, `onError`, `photoQuality`, `photoType`, `promptInterval`, `prompts`, `review`, `stopAfterPrompts`, `videoBitsPerSecond`, `videoTypes`, `viewportClassName` (* required)

## Carousel

> A snap carousel: native CSS scroll-snap strip (swipe, trackpad and wheel just work), previous and next buttons, dots, Arrow / Home / End keys on the strip, and the slide in view as `value` (found with an IntersectionObserver, so a free scroll updates it). It follows the ARIA carousel pattern: `aria-roledescription="carousel"` and "slide" with "n of N" names, and a status line that announces the slide unless it is rotating. `autoplay` pauses while the pointer or focus is inside, has a visible pause button (WCAG 2.2.2) and stays off under reduced motion until the user starts it. Controlled or uncontrolled.

- Import: `import { Carousel } from "@sutra/ui/navigation"` ([full page](md/Carousel.md))
- Props: `align`, `arrows`, `autoplay`, `children`, `defaultValue`, `dots`, `emptyState`, `label`, `labels`, `loading`, `loop`, `onValueChange`, `progress`, `slideClassName`, `trackClassName`, `value` (* required)

**When to use:** A scroll-snap strip of slides with previous and next buttons, dots, arrow and Home and End keys, and optional autoplay. Swiping, trackpad and wheel are native scrolling; the slide in view is `value`.

**Use instead when:**
- `Tabs`: switch between named views
- `StepWizard`: ordered steps with validation
- `SwipeDeck`: decide on cards one by one
- `WheelPicker`: pick a value by scrolling a wheel
- `ScrollArea`: plain scrolling content with no slide state

#### Keyboard

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Strip (it is focusable), then play or pause, previous, each dot, next. Slides that are fully off-screen are `inert`, so their links and buttons are skipped (a slide showing even a sliver stays interactive) |
| ArrowRight, ArrowLeft | On the strip or on any control: next or previous slide. Stops at the ends unless `loop` |
| Home, End | First or last slide |
| Enter, Space | Press the focused button or dot |

Keys with Alt, Ctrl or Meta are ignored, and so are keys pressed inside a slide, so an input in a slide keeps its arrows. In RTL the keys follow reading order: ArrowLeft is next and ArrowRight previous (the test pins it). The arrow glyphs are mirrored, the strip is scrolled by on-screen distance, and the `progress` bar fills from the right.

#### Screen readers

- The root is a `<section aria-roledescription="carousel">` named by `label`. Pass `label`: a section with a name is a `region` landmark, without one it has none.
- The strip is a focusable `group` named "Slides". Each slide is a `group` with `aria-roledescription="slide"` named "n of N".
- Dots are buttons named "Go to slide n", the current one has `aria-current="true"`. Previous and next are disabled at the ends unless `loop`. `labels` replaces the English strings (the strip, previous, next, play, pause, dot and slide names).
- A polite `role="status"` says "n of N" after a button, dot, key press or a free scroll. A slide that autoplay changes by itself is not announced.
- `loading` sets `aria-busy` and renders a skeleton with hidden "Loading…" text, which `labels` does not cover.

#### Reduced motion

Under `prefers-reduced-motion` the strip jumps to a slide instead of scrolling smoothly, the `progress` bar is not drawn, and autoplay stays off until the user presses play. The dot size and colour changes are transitions that the net ends in 1 ms. The snap itself is the browser's scrolling.

#### Server rendering

Server render: part of it fills in after mount. The server renders every slide, the strip and the controls. A starting slide other than the first is scrolled into view after mount, the slide in view is read from an `IntersectionObserver` in an effect, and the preference for autoplay is read in the browser: the server markup of an `autoplay` carousel shows "Pause slide show" and flips to "Start slide show" after hydration for a reduced-motion user.

#### Slots

- `carousel`: the root section
- `carousel-track`: the scrolling strip that holds the slides
- `carousel-controls`: the row with play or pause, arrows and dots

#### Gotchas

- Slides that do not intersect the strip at all are `inert` (set from the same observer that tracks the slide in view, so they are not inert on the server or before the first report): Tab and the accessibility tree skip their content, and a keyboard user reaches them with the arrows, Home, End or the dots. If nothing reports as showing, no slide is made inert.
- `value` follows the strip as well as the buttons, because the slide with the largest visible share wins, so `onValueChange` also fires on a free swipe. Controlled, the parent decides: a press only reports the index.
- `autoplay` is `true` for 5 s or a number of ms (at least 1000). It pauses while the pointer or focus is inside and restarts its interval afterwards. Without `loop` it stops on the last slide. A play or pause button shows only with more than one slide.
- Each child is one slide (the children of a fragment count one by one), `basis-full` wide unless `slideClassName` says otherwise (`basis-4/5` lets the next one peek). One slide shows no controls.

## ChartContainer

> Responsive chart frame: measures its width, exposes `role="img"` and a screen-reader data table.

- Import: `import { ChartContainer } from "@sutra/ui/dataviz"` ([full page](md/ChartContainer.md))
- Props: `children`*, `label`*, `defaultWidth`, `height`, `table` (* required)

**When to use:** The frame every Sutra chart is built on, and the parts to build a chart of your own. `ChartContainer` measures its width, gives the drawing an accessible name and a hidden data table; `ChartTooltip` and `ChartLegend` are the readout card and the series toggle.

**Use instead when:**
- `LineChart`: a standard line, area or bar chart (they already use this frame)
- `DonutChart`: parts of a whole
- `Sparkline`: a tiny trend without axes

#### Keyboard

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| Enter, Space | On an interactive `ChartLegend` entry: hide or show that series |
| Alt+Enter, Alt+Space | On a legend entry: show only that series, or restore all if it is already the only one |
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Moves between legend entries |

`ChartContainer` handles no keys itself: pass `tabIndex` and `onKeyDown` to step through points (the cartesian charts do exactly that). The frame has `dir="ltr"`, so keys you map to arrows keep their physical meaning on an RTL page. `ChartLegend` is outside the island and follows the page direction. `ChartTooltip` is not focusable.

#### Screen readers

- The frame is `role="img"` named by the required `label`; everything drawn inside is inside an image, so put data in the `table` prop: a visually hidden `<table>` after the frame (caption is the label, first column becomes row headers).
- Mark the SVG you draw `aria-hidden`, as the built-in charts do.
- An interactive legend is a `group` named "Toggle series" of buttons with `aria-pressed`; without `onHiddenChange` it is a `list` named "Legend" of `listitem`s. Swatches are `aria-hidden`.
- `ChartTooltip` has no role and is not announced; add your own live region for keyboard use.

#### Reduced motion

No motion of its own. The legend colours fade with a transition that the global net ends in 1 ms. Motion in your own marks is your choice (use `motion-safe:`).

#### Server rendering

Server render: part of it fills in after mount. The first render, on the server and before hydration, passes `defaultWidth` (600) to a `children` function; the real width is measured after mount with a layout effect and `ResizeObserver` and the children re-render. A plain node as `children` is unaffected. The sr-only table and the legend render on the server.

#### Slots

- `chart`: the frame (`role="img"`, `dir="ltr"`, `relative`, full width)
- `chart-tooltip`: the floating readout card
- `chart-legend`: the legend row

#### Gotchas

- Props are spread after the defaults, so a `dir`, `role` or `aria-label` you pass replaces the island's `dir="ltr"`, `role="img"` or the label: do not pass `dir` unless the chart really should mirror.
- `ChartTooltip` is absolutely positioned inside the nearest positioned ancestor and does not use a portal; you place it with `style`. It is `pointer-events-none`, so it cannot be hovered or clicked.
- `ChartLegend` is controlled: keep the `hidden` keys in state and update them in `onHiddenChange`. Its `marker` is `square`, `line` or `dot`.
- `height` sizes the frame (default 240), not the legend; a `table` row's first cell is rendered as a `th scope="row"`.

## CheckBurst

> A tiny celebratory pop for completing a task or reaching a streak: a ring of particles flies out of the centre and fades (Web Animations on `translate`, `scale` and `opacity`, no keyframes in the stylesheet), and the content swells. Pure decoration: the layer is `aria-hidden` and never carries information, so say the result in text (a live region, the checked state). Under `prefers-reduced-motion` nothing plays. It draws past its own box, so keep it out of an `overflow-hidden` ancestor. Drive it with `active`, `burstKey` or `apiRef.burst()`.

- Import: `import { CheckBurst } from "@sutra/ui/motion"` ([full page](md/CheckBurst.md))
- Props: `active`, `apiRef`, `burstKey`, `children`, `count`, `duration`, `onBurst`, `onBurstEnd`, `particleSize`, `pop`, `radius`, `shape`, `tone` (* required)

## Checklist

> Subtask checklist with add / edit / delete / reorder, an "n/m" count with a thin progress bar and a hide-completed toggle.

- Import: `import { Checklist } from "@sutra/ui/social"` ([full page](md/Checklist.md))
- Props: `addPlaceholder`, `createId`, `defaultHideCompleted`, `defaultItems`, `editable`, `hideCompleted`, `items`, `label`, `moveButtons`, `onHideCompletedChange`, `onItemsChange`, `reorderable` (* required)

**When to use:** A subtask list with checkboxes, inline editing, add and delete, drag or keyboard reordering, an "n/m" count with a thin progress bar and a hide-completed toggle. It is the ready-made use of `ReorderableList`.

**Use instead when:**
- `ReorderableList`: your own rows with a manual order
- `OnboardingChecklist`: guided setup steps with status and actions
- `Steps`: ordered stages with a current one
- `CheckboxGroup`: a few options for a form
- `Progress`: only the bar

#### Keyboard

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Through each row: drag handle, checkbox, the item text (a button), delete button; then the hide toggle and the add field |
| Space | On a checkbox: toggle done |
| Enter, Space | On the item text: edit it in place. On a handle: pick the row up (then arrows move it, Space or Enter drops, Escape cancels) |
| Enter | In the edit field: save (empty text deletes the item). In the add field: add the item |
| Escape | In the edit field: discard the change. While a row is picked up: cancel |

Leaving the edit field saves it. Up and down are the only arrows, so RTL changes nothing.

#### Screen readers

- A `group` named by `label` (default "Checklist") with the "2/5" count next to it. The bar is a `progressbar` named "2 of 5 done".
- Each checkbox is named by the item text; the text button is "Edit <text>", the delete button "Delete <text>", the editing input "Edit <text>"; the add field is named by `addPlaceholder` ("Add an item"). Reordering is announced by the `ReorderableList` live region ("Picked up Pack. Position 3 of 5...").
- "Hide completed" is a toggle button with `aria-pressed`; it becomes "Show completed (3)". With everything hidden, "All done." is plain text.

#### Reduced motion

Rows glide when reordered (`flip`) and hover fades are transitions; under `prefers-reduced-motion` the glide is off and the global net ends the rest in 1 ms.

#### Server rendering

Server render: same markup as the client. Plain markup from `items` or `defaultItems`. New ids come from `createId` only when an item is added, so rendering is deterministic.

#### Gotchas

- Each entry is `{ id, text, done }`. Control it with `items` and `onItemsChange`, which receives the whole new list after an add, edit, toggle, delete or reorder; ids for new entries come from `createId` (time based by default).
- The delete button is hidden until the row is hovered or focused, so on a touch screen it is invisible (it still works when tapped). Set `editable={false}` to drop add, edit and delete; `reorderable={false}` drops the handles and renders a plain list.
- With "hide completed" on, reordering only rearranges the unfinished slots: completed items keep their positions.
- `hideCompleted` can be controlled with `onHideCompletedChange` (or start hidden with `defaultHideCompleted`); the toggle only appears once at least one item is done.

## CoachmarkTour

> Dependency-free guided tour: spotlight cutout, anchored step card, keyboard and completion callbacks.

- Import: `import { CoachmarkTour } from "@sutra/ui/workspace"` ([full page](md/CoachmarkTour.md))
- Props: `steps`*, `className`, `closeOnOverlayClick`, `defaultOpen`, `defaultStep`, `labels`, `onComplete`, `onFinish`, `onOpenChange`, `onSkip`, `onStepChange`, `open`, `padding`, `radius`, `step` (* required)

## CodeBlock

> Syntax-highlighted code with filename, copy, line numbers and highlights.

- Import: `import { CodeBlock } from "@sutra/ui"` ([full page](md/CodeBlock.md))
- Parts: `CodeBlockTabs`
- Props: `actions`, `children`, `code`, `copyable`, `defaultWrap`, `filename`, `hideHeader`, `highlightLines`, `language`, `maxHeight`, `onWrapChange`, `showLineNumbers`, `showWrapToggle`, `startLine`, `theme`, `wrap` (* required)

**When to use:** Syntax-highlighted code with an optional header (file name or language, wrap toggle, copy button), line numbers and highlighted lines. `CodeBlockTabs` switches between snippets (npm, pnpm, yarn, or several files); `InlineCopy` is a one-line command with a copy button.

**Use instead when:**
- `CopyField`: any single value with a copy button that is not a command
- `Markdown`: prose that contains code fences
- `InlineCode`: a short code span inside a sentence
- `CodeEditor`: code the user edits
- `DiffViewer`: changes between two versions

#### Keyboard

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab / Shift+Tab | The wrap toggle and copy button in the header, then the code area, which is a tab stop because it scrolls |
| Arrows, PageUp, PageDown, Home, End | Scroll the focused code area (native) |
| Enter, Space | On the copy button: copy. On the wrap toggle: switch wrapping |
| ArrowLeft, ArrowRight, Home, End | `CodeBlockTabs`: move between tabs and show that snippet at once; wraps from the last to the first |

The whole block is a `dir="ltr"` island, so the tab arrows do not swap in RTL.

#### Screen readers

- The code is a `<pre tabindex="0"><code>` (focusable so it can scroll) with no role or label. Line numbers are `aria-hidden` and not selectable, so neither screen readers nor copy-paste see them.
- `highlightLines` is a colour and a bar only; it is not announced. The language and file name are plain header text.
- The copy button is named "Copy code" (`InlineCopy`: "Copy command") and a polite live region announces "Copied to clipboard"; the wrap toggle is "Toggle line wrap" with `aria-pressed`. The `$` prompt of `InlineCopy` is hidden from assistive technology and is not copied.
- `CodeBlockTabs` is a Radix `tablist` of `tab`s and a `tabpanel` per snippet.

#### Reduced motion

The copy icon swaps with a 200 ms transition, the tab underline slides in over 200 ms and the header buttons fade, all transitions that the global net ends within 1 ms. Nothing else moves.

#### Server rendering

Server render: same markup as the client. Highlighting is a pure function of `code` and `language`, so the server renders the full tokenized markup with no browser API. The clipboard is touched only on click.

#### Gotchas

- Highlighting is a small built-in tokenizer for `ts`/`js`/`tsx`/`jsx`, `json`, `css`/`scss`, `html`/`xml`/`svg`, and `bash`/`sh`/`shell`. Other languages (python, go, rust) render as plain text, so use another highlighter inside your own `pre` for them.
- `theme="dark"` (default) is an always-dark surface from the `--code-*` tokens, also in a light app; `"light"` follows the app theme. `InlineCopy` defaults to `"light"`.
- With no header (no `filename`, `language`, `actions` or `showWrapToggle`, or `hideHeader`), the copy button floats in the corner and is visible only on hover or keyboard focus, so touch users never see it: give the block a `language` or `filename`.
- `code` wins over `children`; a trailing newline is removed. `wrap` is controllable only on `CodeBlock` (`wrap`, `defaultWrap`, `onWrapChange`, toggle with `showWrapToggle`); `CodeBlockTabs` takes a plain `wrap` and `highlightLines` per tab.

## Command

> Command palette root (cmdk). Handles filtering and keyboard navigation.

- Import: `import { Command } from "@sutra/ui/overlays"` ([full page](md/Command.md))
- Parts: `CommandDialog`, `CommandEmpty`, `CommandFooter`, `CommandGroup`, `CommandInput`, `CommandItem`, `CommandList`, `CommandLoading`, `CommandPaletteFromRegistry`, `CommandSeparator`, `CommandShortcut`

## CommentComposer

## Countdown

> Countdown to a date with d/h/m/s segments or a compact "2h 14m" form; fires `onComplete` once.

- Import: `import { Countdown } from "@sutra/ui/social"` ([full page](md/Countdown.md))
- Props: `target`*, `completeContent`, `flip`, `format`, `hideSeconds`, `onComplete`, `size`, `urgentBelow` (* required)

**When to use:** Time left until a moment, as days, hours, minutes and seconds boxes or a compact "2h 14m" line. It fires `onComplete` once at the deadline and can switch to a warning tone for the last stretch. Use it for sales, expiring codes and session timeouts.

**Use instead when:**
- `Stopwatch`: time counting up with laps
- `Progress`: completion of a task
- `AnimatedNumber`: a changing number without a clock
- `useCountdown`: the remaining time as data for your own layout

#### Keyboard

Not focusable: no keyboard interaction.

#### Screen readers

- The root is `role="timer"` with an `aria-label` such as "Time remaining: 2 hours 14 minutes" (up to three units, seconds shown only under a day), or "Time is up" once finished. The digits, colons and unit captions are `aria-hidden`, so the label is all that is read.
- A timer is not a live region by default, so nothing is announced while it ticks; the label is current when someone reads it. Add `aria-live` only if you want announcements, and expect chatter once a second.
- `data-urgent` and the warning colour are visual: put an explicit message next to the countdown if the last stretch matters.

#### Reduced motion

The optional `flip` entrance (`animate-in` with a small slide) is skipped when the reduced-motion preference is on (read live). Without `flip` the digits change in place, so the component never moves.

#### Server rendering

Server render: part of it fills in after mount. The remaining time is computed from `Date.now()` during the first render, so the server's snapshot differs from the browser's first render by the time between them (seconds in the label and digits change on the first tick after mount). Pass a deadline far enough ahead, or hide the countdown until mounted, if a mismatch warning matters.

#### Gotchas

- `target` is a `Date` or epoch milliseconds. The display recomputes from the wall clock on every tick, so it does not drift when the tab was in the background.
- `onComplete` fires once per `target`, also when the target is already past on mount. When finished, the zeros stay unless you pass `completeContent`, which replaces the digits (the root still has role `timer` and "Time is up").
- `format="compact"` shows the two largest units ("2h 14m", "45s"); `segments` hides the days box when there are no whole days and `hideSeconds` drops the seconds box (and ticks once a second instead of four times).
- `urgentBelow` (milliseconds) only sets the warning tone and `data-urgent` during the last stretch while time remains; it does not change the label.

## DonutChart

> Donut (ring) chart with segments, center label, toggleable legend and tooltip.

- Import: `import { DonutChart } from "@sutra/ui/dataviz"` ([full page](md/DonutChart.md))
- Props: `data`*, `index`*, `animate`, `centerLabel`, `centerValue`, `colorFor`, `colors`, `defaultHiddenSeries`, `emptyState`, `hiddenSeries`, `iconFor`, `label`, `legend`, `legendInteractive`, `legendValues`, `loading`, `onHiddenSeriesChange`, `padAngle`, `size`, `thickness`, `tooltip`, `valueFormatter`, `valueKey` (* required)

**When to use:** A ring split into segments for the parts of a whole, with the total (or a value you choose) in the centre, a legend that hides and shows segments, and a tooltip with name, value and share.

**Use instead when:**
- `StackedMeter`: the same parts as one horizontal bar
- `BreakdownList`: only the legend rows, no ring
- `Gauge`: one value against a range
- `BarChart`: compare many categories or values that are not parts of a whole
- `Treemap`: parts with a hierarchy or many tiles

#### Keyboard

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab | Focuses the ring; leaving it clears the active segment |
| ArrowRight, ArrowDown | Next visible segment, clockwise; wraps from the last to the first |
| ArrowLeft, ArrowUp | Previous visible segment; wraps from the first to the last |
| Escape | Clears the active segment and its tooltip |
| Enter, Space | On a legend entry: hide or show that segment. With Alt: show only that one, or restore all |

There is no Home or End. The ring is a `dir="ltr"` island, so the arrows never swap in RTL. The legend is outside it and follows the page direction, so `legend="right"` puts it at the inline end (visually left in RTL).

#### Screen readers

- The ring is a focusable `role="img"` named by `label`, by default "Donut chart: alice 40, bob 35" listing every segment, hidden ones included. The SVG and the centre text are not read separately.
- A visually hidden table follows it: columns are the `index` key, the `valueKey` and "Share"; a hidden segment shows "hidden" as its share. Shares are of the visible total.
- Stepping with the keyboard writes "alice: 40 (40%)" into a polite live region. Hovering shows the tooltip but does not announce.
- The chip legend is a `group` named "Toggle series" of `aria-pressed` buttons; with `legendValues` or `iconFor` it becomes a `list` named "Legend" whose rows are the same toggle buttons. With `loading`, the root has `aria-busy` and one hidden "Loading donut chart…".

#### Reduced motion

Segments carry `motion-safe:transition-all duration-500` (`animate`, default true), which eases the hover dimming and colour changes; the arc shape is a `d` attribute, so it changes at once when data or the hidden set changes, and under `prefers-reduced-motion` nothing eases. The loading ring pulses with `animate-pulse` and carries `motion-reduce:animate-none`. There is no entrance animation on mount.

#### Server rendering

Server render: same markup as the client. The ring is drawn from `size` alone, so the server HTML already contains the segments, centre text and legend; nothing waits for mount. The one thing that can differ is number text: values and shares go through `Intl` with the runtime default locale, so pass `valueFormatter` when the server and the browser locale differ.

#### Slots

- `chart-segment`: one ring segment (hidden segments are not rendered)
- `chart-center-value`: the centre number
- `chart-center-label`: the caption under it
- `chart-skeleton`: the loading ring
- `chart-empty`: the empty placeholder

#### Gotchas

- Values below 0 or that are not finite numbers count as 0. When the visible total is 0 the ring is one muted track and the centre shows 0.
- The centre defaults to the formatted total of visible segments, so it changes when you hide one; `centerValue={null}` removes it, `centerLabel` alone still shows.
- Segment keys are the `index` text; a repeated name gets `#1`, `#2` suffixes, which is what `hiddenSeries` and `onHiddenSeriesChange` contain for the repeats.
- `legend={false}` removes the only toggle control (segments then cannot be hidden by keyboard or pointer unless you control `hiddenSeries`). `legendInteractive={false}` keeps the legend as a plain list.

While the dialog is open the card is hidden (it comes back as the panel lands on it). The card is a native button with `aria-haspopup="dialog"`; its content may use blocks. Controlled with `open` / `defaultOpen` / `onOpenChange`.

- Import: `import { ExpandCard } from "@sutra/ui/motion"` ([full page](md/ExpandCard.md))
- Props: `children`*, `detail`*, `title`*, `defaultOpen`, `description`, `onMorphEnd`, `onOpenChange`, `open`, `panelClassName`, `repeatFace`, `showClose`, `size`, `variant` (* required)

## FileUpload

> Compound file uploader root: owns file state, validation and the hidden input.

- Import: `import { FileUpload } from "@sutra/ui/forms"` ([full page](md/FileUpload.md))
- Parts: `FileUploadDropzone`, `FileUploadItem`, `FileUploadList`, `FileUploadTrigger`
- Props: `accept`, `defaultFiles`, `disabled`, `files`, `maxFiles`, `maxSize`, `multiple`, `name`, `onFilesAdded`, `onFilesChange`, `onFilesRejected`, `showErrors` (* required)

**When to use:** A compound file uploader. `FileUpload` owns the file list, the type, size and count checks and a hidden input; `FileUploadDropzone` and `FileUploadTrigger` (files or a folder) add files, `FileUploadList` and `FileUploadItem` show them with progress, status and remove. It manages the list: you do the upload.

**Use instead when:**
- `Dropzone`: just a drop area with no list or state
- `CopyButton`: copy rather than upload
- `ChatAttachment`: one attachment tile in a conversation
- `FileViewer`: preview a file
- `Progress`: just a bar

#### Keyboard

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab / Shift+Tab | The dropzone, each trigger and each row's remove button are tab stops |
| Enter, Space | On the dropzone or a trigger: open the file (or folder) picker. On a remove button: remove the file |

Dragging has no keyboard form, so the dropzone and the triggers are the keyboard route. There are no arrow keys, so RTL changes nothing.

#### Screen readers

- `FileUploadDropzone` is a `role="button"` named by its text ("Click to upload or drag and drop") and described by its hint (types, size and count limits); it has `aria-disabled` when disabled and `aria-busy` while a dropped folder is read. The real file input is a hidden sibling (`aria-hidden`, not focusable).
- Rejected files show in a `role="alert"` list, one message per file (the first problem only, such as "n.txt isn't a supported file type."), until the next add.
- The list is a `ul` named "Files". Each row shows the name (the folder path for folder files) and size, a "Complete" or error text with an icon labelled "Uploaded" or "Failed", and a `progressbar` named "Uploading <name>" (indeterminate when `progress` is undefined). The remove button is "Remove <name>".
- Where the browser cannot pick folders, `FileUploadTrigger directory` is `aria-disabled` and described by "This browser can't choose folders. Choose files instead."

#### Reduced motion

Drag feedback (border, tint, icon lift) and the progress fill use transitions that the global net ends in 1 ms. The tick pops with `animate-pop` when a file finishes, which the net stops.

#### Server rendering

Server render: part of it fills in after mount. Without `directory` the markup is the same on both sides. The folder trigger and folder dropzone ask the browser for `webkitdirectory` support with `useSyncExternalStore`: the server and hydration render the "unsupported" state, and the real answer appears after hydration.

#### Gotchas

- Nothing is uploaded for you. `onFilesAdded` gives the new `UploadFile`s (`status: "idle"`): start your request there and feed `progress` and `status` back through controlled `files` (or `onFilesChange`). `status` also takes `pending`, `running`, `succeeded`, `failed` and `canceled`.
- `accept`, `maxSize` (bytes) and `maxFiles` (in total, counting files already listed) are checked on every add; rejections go to `onFilesRejected` and the alert. `multiple={false}` makes each new file replace the previous one.
- With `name` the hidden input carries the whole file list (picked, dropped and `defaultFiles`; removing a file removes it) through `DataTransfer`, so a native form post sends the files. Without `name`, or in a browser that cannot set `input.files`, the input is emptied after each pick: read the files from the list or `onFilesAdded`. Picking a file that is already on the input again may fire no change event.
- `FileUploadList` renders nothing for an empty list; `FileUploadItem` outside a `FileUpload` needs its own `onRemove`. Read the state anywhere inside with the `useFileUpload` hook.

## FileViewer

> Previews a file by type (image, PDF, video, audio, text/code/markdown/JSON) in a modal or inline. Apps can add their own renderers, browse several `files`, put actions in the header and show a side panel.

- Import: `import { FileViewer } from "@sutra/ui/mobile"` ([full page](md/FileViewer.md))
- Props: `actions`, `className`, `defaultIndex`, `defaultOpen`, `defaultPanelOpen`, `download`, `emptyState`, `file`, `files`, `index`, `inline`, `kind`, `loading`, `loadText`, `loop`, `onClose`, `onDownload`, `onIndexChange`, `onOpenChange`, `onPanelOpenChange`, `open`, `openInNewTab`, `panel`, `panelLabel`, `panelOpen`, `renderers`, `subtitle`, `text`, `thumbnails`, `title` (* required)

## FilterBar

> Toolbar row for lists and tables: search, filter chips and actions.

- Import: `import { FilterBar } from "@sutra/ui"` ([full page](md/FilterBar.md))
- Parts: `FilterBarActive`, `FilterBarChip`, `FilterBarClear`, `FilterBarSearch`, `FilterBarToken`

**When to use:** The toolbar above a list or table: a search field, dashed "+ Filter" chips that open a multi-select checklist, a row of removable tokens for the applied filters, and a "Clear all" button. The parts hold no shared state, so you wire them to your own filter state.

**Use instead when:**
- `Combobox`: pick one or more values for a form field
- `Select`: one value from a short list
- `SegmentedControl`: switch between a few views
- `CommandDialog`: a global search and command palette
- `SearchTrigger`: a field-shaped button that opens it

#### Keyboard

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Each control is its own tab stop: the search field, its clear button, each chip, each token's remove button, "Clear all" |
| Escape | In the search field with text: clears it (not during IME composition). In an open chip popover: closes it |
| Enter, Space | On a chip: opens the checklist. On an option: toggles it (the list stays open) |
| ArrowDown | In the chip's search input: moves to the first option. In the list: next option, wrapping to the first |
| ArrowUp | Previous option, wrapping to the last |
| Home, End | First or last option |

The chip checklist opens with the first option focused, or the search input when `searchable` (default above 7 options). The checklist is vertical, so RTL changes nothing; icons and padding use logical sides.

#### Screen readers

- `FilterBar` is `role="toolbar"` with no label of its own: pass `aria-label`. It does not implement roving arrow keys, so it is a plain row of tab stops.
- A chip is a button named by its label plus the selected values as text ("Status Active Paused", or "Status 3 selected" past `maxDisplay`). It opens a popover with a `listbox` named by the label and `aria-multiselectable`; each option has `aria-selected`; the check box is `aria-hidden`. The search input is named "Search <label>". "No results" is plain text, not a live region.
- `FilterBarSearch` is an `<input type="search">` (role `searchbox`) with a "Clear search" button once it has text; give it an `aria-label`, since the placeholder ("Search…") is its only other name.
- `FilterBarActive` is a `group` named "Active filters"; each token reads "Status: Active" followed by its remove button.

#### Reduced motion

The chip popover fades and zooms in with `animate-in` and the check mark scales in over 150 ms; new tokens fade in. The global net removes the movement and ends the transitions within 1 ms.

#### Server rendering

Server render: same markup as the client. Plain markup from props (`useId` for the list id). The chip popover is portalled and closed on first render, so nothing is missing on either side.

#### Gotchas

- All filter state is yours: `FilterBarChip` takes `value` (string array) with `onValueChange`, `FilterBarSearch` takes `value` with `onValueChange`. Chips do not create tokens: map your state to `FilterBarActive filters`, or render `FilterBarToken`s yourself.
- Every token built from `filters` has the remove button name "Remove filter" unless you name them: `removeLabel` on `FilterBarActive` (a string, or a function of the filter such as `(f) => "Remove " + f.id`) or `removeLabel` on a single filter (which wins); `FilterBarToken` children take `removeLabel` too. Setting `onRemove` is what shows the button.
- Chip options are strings or `{ value, label, icon, count, textValue }`. Search and the summary use `textValue`, else the label when it is a string or number, else the raw `value`: set `textValue` when `label` is a node.
- `FilterPill` is a deprecated alias of `FilterBarChip`. Chip `align` sets the popover alignment (default `start`); `disabled` on the chip prevents opening.

- Props: `label`*, `options`*, `align`, `defaultValue`, `icon`, `maxDisplay`, `onValueChange`, `searchable`, `value` (* required)

## Gauge

> Radial arc gauge with threshold coloring (role="meter").

- Import: `import { Gauge } from "@sutra/ui/dataviz"` ([full page](md/Gauge.md))
- Props: `value`*, `accent`, `ariaValueText`, `children`, `color`, `colorStops`, `endAngle`, `glow`, `label`, `loading`, `max`, `min`, `size`, `startAngle`, `thickness`, `thresholds`, `tone`, `unit`, `valueFormatter` (* required)

**When to use:** A radial arc showing one reading inside a range (temperature, load, score), coloured by thresholds, with the value in the middle. `RingMeter` is the compact ring for inline use, such as a context window.

**Use instead when:**
- `Meter`: a level against a limit as a bar
- `ProgressCircle`: completion of a task (role progressbar)
- `DonutChart`: several parts of a whole
- `QuotaRing`: a plan limit with a pace
- `Sparkline`: history rather than the current value

#### Keyboard

Not focusable: no keyboard interaction. The reading is exposed to screen readers as a meter, with no controls.

#### Screen readers

- The root is `role="meter"` with `aria-valuenow` (clamped into `min` and `max`), `aria-valuemin` and `aria-valuemax`. `aria-valuetext` is the formatted value plus `unit` ("62 °C"), "No data" for `value={null}`, "Loading" while `loading` has no value, or whatever you pass as `ariaValueText`.
- The name is `label` (referenced with `aria-labelledby`, and kept as hidden text when `children` replaces the visible caption); without `label` it is "Gauge", so pass one when several are on a page.
- `data-level` (`ok`, `warn`, `danger`) is a styling hook, not announced: the warn and danger colour is visual only, so put the state in `ariaValueText` when it matters.
- `RingMeter` is a `role="meter"` span named by `label` (default "Usage"), always on a 0 to 100 scale, with value text like "92%". Its percentage is shown only from `showValueAbove` (50) upwards, but the value text is always there.

#### Reduced motion

The arc animates `stroke-dasharray` and colour over 500 ms with `motion-reduce:transition-none`, so under `prefers-reduced-motion` it jumps to the new value. The loading placeholder uses the `Skeleton` pulse, which the global net stops.

#### Server rendering

Server render: same markup as the client. A static SVG computed from the props (arc path, `pathLength` dash), so the server and client markup match. The arc fills clockwise in both directions: nothing mirrors in RTL.

#### Slots

- `gauge-fill`: the coloured value arc (absent when empty or at 0)
- `gauge-value`: the number and unit in the middle
- `ring-value`: the percentage beside a `RingMeter`

#### Gotchas

- Thresholds are percentages of `min` to `max` and higher is worse (warn at 75, danger at 90). For readings where high is good, pass `thresholds={false}`, or use `colorStops`, which use absolute values, win over thresholds and leave `data-level` at `ok`.
- Arc colour order: `colorStops`, then the warn and danger colours, then `tone`, then `accent`, then primary. `color` is a deprecated alias of `tone`, and `tone="neutral"` draws the arc in the foreground colour.
- `value={null}` draws an empty track and "—". With `loading`, the placeholder replaces the number only when the value is null; with a value the gauge keeps showing it and just sets `aria-busy`.
- The number in the middle is the unclamped `value` through `valueFormatter` (rounded to one decimal by default), while `aria-valuenow` and the arc are clamped to the range.

- Props: `border`, `containerSize`, `innerClassName`, `sticky` (* required)

## HeatmapGrid

> Generic value → color cell grid (per-core CPU, per-GPU load, matrices) with keyboard navigation.

- Import: `import { HeatmapGrid } from "@sutra/ui/ops"` ([full page](md/HeatmapGrid.md))
- Props: `data`*, `cellHeight`, `cellLabel`, `cellSize`, `colorStops`, `columns`, `formatValue`, `gap`, `label`, `legend`, `legendLabels`, `max`, `min`, `onCellClick`, `scale`, `shape`, `showIndices`, `steps`, `thresholds`, `tooltip` (* required)

**When to use:** A grid of cells coloured by value, in square tiles or vertical fill bars (per-core CPU, per-GPU load, matrices), with a tooltip and keyboard navigation. `HeatmapLegend` is the "Less to More" key that the grid shows with `legend`.

**Use instead when:**
- `CalendarHeatmap`: one cell per day over a year or month
- `Treemap`: cells sized by value
- `BarChart`: values on an axis with exact heights
- `StatCard`: a single number

#### Keyboard

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab / Shift+Tab | One cell holds the tab stop (the last focused); Tab then leaves the grid |
| ArrowLeft, ArrowRight | Previous or next cell in the row |
| ArrowUp, ArrowDown | The cell above or below; a missing cell is skipped, and at an edge nothing moves |
| Home, End | First or last cell of the row |
| Ctrl+Home, Ctrl+End (Cmd on Mac) | First or last cell of the grid |
| Enter, Space | Calls `onCellClick` (Space never scrolls the page) |
| Escape | Hides the tooltip |

The grid is a forced `dir="ltr"` island: columns run left to right and ArrowRight is always the next column, also in RTL.

#### Screen readers

- A `grid` named by `label` (default "Heatmap") with `row`s and `gridcell`s. Each cell is named "Core 3: 15%": its label, a colon, then the formatted value, or "no data" for `null`.
- The default cell label is "Cell 0" (index from 0), so pass `cellLabel` or a `label` per cell. Colour carries the level visually only; the value is in the name.
- The tooltip appears on hover and focus and is `aria-hidden`; the legend is plain text with `aria-hidden` swatches. Cells also expose `data-level` (-1 no data, 0 empty, 1 to `steps`).

#### Reduced motion

Cell colour and the focus ring fade over 300 ms and bar fills grow over 500 ms with transitions, which the global net ends within 1 ms.

#### Server rendering

Server render: same markup as the client. Everything is computed from `data` and the props, and the default value text uses `toFixed` rather than `Intl`, so server and client markup are the same. The tooltip only exists after hover or focus.

#### Gotchas

- The defaults assume percentages: `min` 0, `max` 100 and a `formatValue` that appends "%". For other units set `min`, `max` and `formatValue`.
- `null` is "no data" (transparent, a dashed outline on squares); a value at or below `min` is the muted "empty" step, a different thing.
- `scale` defaults to `primary` for squares and `thresholds` for `shape="bar"` (warn at 75 and danger at 90 percent of the range, or `thresholds`); `colorStops` (absolute values) override both. `steps` is the number of intensity steps above empty.
- `onCellClick` adds a pointer cursor and the Enter and Space handling, but cells stay `gridcell`s, not buttons. Pass `dir` only if you want to leave the LTR island: props are spread after it.

## HeatmapLegend

> "Less ▢▢▢▢ More" scale legend, or labeled swatches for custom stops.

- Props: `colors`*, `highLabel`, `lowLabel`, `stops`, `swatchSize` (* required)

## ImageCropper

> Image crop box: drag to move, eight handles to resize, aspect presets, quarter-turn rotation and optional zoom.

- Props: `src`*, `alt`, `applyLabel`, `aspect`, `aspectOptions`, `crop`, `cropperRef`, `crossOrigin`, `defaultAspect`, `defaultCrop`, `defaultRotation`, `defaultZoom`, `errorState`, `keyboardStep`, `loading`, `maxZoom`, `minHeight`, `minWidth`, `minZoom`, `onAspectChange`, `onComplete`, `onCropChange`, `onCropEnd`, `onImageError`, `onImageLoad`, `onRotationChange`, `onZoomChange`, `output`, `rotatable`, `rotation`, `stageClassName`, `toolbar`, `zoom`, `zoomable` (* required)

## ImageWithFallback

> Image that reserves its aspect ratio, shimmers while loading and shows "Image unavailable" on error.

- Import: `import { ImageWithFallback } from "@sutra/ui/mobile"` ([full page](md/ImageWithFallback.md))
- Props: `alt`*, `fallback`, `fetcher`, `fit`, `height`, `imgClassName`, `onError`, `onLoad`, `ratio`, `src`, `width` (* required)

**When to use:** An image that reserves its space, shimmers until it loads, fades in, and shows an "Image unavailable" state when it fails or has no `src`. It can load through your own fetch (for authenticated images).

**Use instead when:**
- `Avatar`: a person's picture with initials as the fallback
- `Lightbox`: open images full screen
- `FileViewer`: previews for non-image files
- `Skeleton`: a placeholder you control yourself

#### Keyboard

Not focusable: no keyboard interaction.

#### Screen readers

- The image keeps its `alt` (an empty string for a decorative image). On failure the area becomes a `role="img"` named "<alt> (image unavailable)", or "Image unavailable" with no alt; the visible "Image unavailable" text is `aria-hidden` so it is not read twice.
- The shimmer skeleton is `aria-hidden`. There is no live announcement when the image finishes loading or fails.

#### Reduced motion

The shimmer has `motion-reduce:animate-none`, and the fade-in is a 300 ms opacity transition that the global net ends in 1 ms.

#### Server rendering

Server render: part of it fills in after mount. With a `src` the server renders the `<img>` at opacity 0 over the shimmer skeleton; it becomes visible only after hydration, when the load (or an already complete image) is detected, so the picture is invisible until the script runs. Reserve the space with `ratio` or `width` and `height` to avoid a layout jump. With no `src` the error state renders on both sides.

#### Slots

- `image`: the wrapper (`data-status` is `loading`, `loaded` or `error`)
- `image-skeleton`: the loading shimmer

#### Gotchas

- Pass `width` and `height` (or `ratio`, which wins) so the box has its aspect ratio before the image arrives; without either, it holds a minimum height of 6rem while loading.
- `className` goes on the wrapper and `imgClassName` on the `<img>`. `fit` is `cover` by default, `contain` shows the whole image. `loading` defaults to `lazy`.
- `fetcher(src)` returns a `Blob` that is shown through an object URL, revoked on unmount; a rejection shows the fallback. Use `fallback` to replace the default icon and text, `onLoad` and `onError` to react.
