## Lightbox

> Fullscreen media viewer: arrows/swipe, zoom + pan, counter, thumbnails, Escape to close, focus trap.

- Import: `import { Lightbox } from "@sutra/ui/mobile"` ([full page](md/Lightbox.md))
- Parts: `LightboxTrigger`
- Props: `items`*, `children`, `className`, `defaultIndex`, `defaultOpen`, `download`, `index`, `label`, `loop`, `maxZoom`, `onIndexChange`, `onOpenChange`, `open`, `thumbnails` (* required)

**When to use:** A full-screen viewer for a set of images or videos: previous and next, a counter, a thumbnail strip, zoom and pan, swipe, optional download. Put `LightboxTrigger`s (your thumbnails) inside it, or open it from code with `useLightbox`.

**Use instead when:**
- `Dialog`: any other content in a modal
- `Carousel`: browse in place without a full-screen viewer
- `FileViewer`: previews for pdf, text and other file types
- `ImageWithFallback`: one image that handles loading and errors
- `Drawer`: a touch-first bottom sheet

#### Keyboard

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| ArrowLeft, ArrowRight | Previous or next item (stops at the ends unless `loop`). Ignored while a video is focused |
| Home, End | First or last item |
| + or =, -, 0 | Zoom in or out by 1.5 times, or reset to 100% |
| Escape | Close |
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Cycles through the toolbar buttons, the previous and next buttons, and the thumbnails (focus is trapped while open) |
| Enter, Space | Press the focused button, including a thumbnail |

In RTL the arrows follow reading order: ArrowLeft goes to the next item and ArrowRight to the previous, and a swipe towards the inline start brings the next item. Closing sends focus back to the element that had it when the viewer opened (the `LightboxTrigger`, or a button that called `openAt`), even though the viewer has no Radix trigger; if that element is gone, focus ends on the page body. Pointer extras: double-click toggles 200%, a drag pans a zoomed image, Ctrl or Cmd with the wheel or a trackpad pinch zooms.

#### Screen readers

- Radix gives the panel `role="dialog"` named by `label` (default "Image viewer") and hides the page. The counter ("2 / 5") is a polite live region, so it announces each change of item.
- The current image has its `alt` (a failed one reads "<alt> (image unavailable)"); videos get `aria-label` from `alt` and native controls. Captions are plain text.
- Buttons are named "Zoom out", "Zoom in", "Download", "Close viewer", "Previous" and "Next". Thumbnails are a `group` named "Thumbnails" of buttons "View 2 of 5: <alt>" with `aria-current` on the shown one.
- `LightboxTrigger` has `aria-haspopup="dialog"` and defaults to the name "Open <alt>" of its item; give it an `aria-label` when it holds more than an image.

#### Reduced motion

The backdrop and panel fade and scale in with `animate-in` (movement stripped under reduced motion), and zoom changes use a 150 ms transform transition that the global net ends in 1 ms, so zoom is immediate. The thumbnail fade is a transition too.

#### Server rendering

Server render: same markup as the client. A closed viewer renders only its children (the triggers) on both sides; the panel is portalled. A viewer that is `open` on first render appears after hydration.

#### Slots

- `lightbox`: the panel
- `lightbox-counter`: the "2 / 5" text
- `lightbox-stage`: the area that holds the media, the swipe and pan surface

#### Gotchas

- Control it with `open`, `index` and their `onOpenChange` and `onIndexChange`, or take `useLightbox()` and spread `{...lb.props}`. Opening through a `LightboxTrigger` sets the index first. `index` is clamped to the items.
- The previous and next buttons are hidden below the `sm` breakpoint (swipe and the arrow keys remain); there is no wrap unless `loop`, and the buttons disable at the ends.
- Zoom resets whenever the item changes or the viewer opens or closes, and a swipe to the next item is ignored while zoomed in (it pans instead). `maxZoom` defaults to 4.
- `download` adds a plain link with the `download` attribute (so it is subject to the browser's cross-origin rule) and `downloadName` names the file. The two neighbouring images are preloaded.

## LineChart

> Multi-series line chart with optional dots and reference (threshold) lines.

- Import: `import { LineChart } from "@sutra/ui/dataviz"` ([full page](md/LineChart.md))
- Props: `data`*, `index`*, `series`*, `animate`, `connectNulls`, `curve`, `defaultHiddenSeries`, `dots`, `emptyState`, `grid`, `height`, `hiddenSeries`, `label`, `legend`, `legendInteractive`, `loading`, `onActiveIndexChange`, `onHiddenSeriesChange`, `referenceLines`, `strokeWidth`, `tooltip`, `valueFormatter`, `xAxis`, `yAxis` (* required)

**When to use:** Cartesian charts over rows of data. `LineChart` draws lines, `AreaChart` filled (optionally stacked) areas, `BarChart` grouped, stacked or horizontal bars; all three take `data`, `index` and `series`, and share axes, legend, tooltip, time axis and reference lines.

**Use instead when:**
- `Sparkline`: a tiny trend inside a row or card, no axes
- `DonutChart`: parts of a whole
- `StatCard`: one number with a small trend
- `BarList`: a ranked list with proportional bars
- `ChartContainer`: build a chart type that does not exist yet

#### Keyboard

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab | Focuses the chart frame; leaving it clears the active point |
| ArrowRight, ArrowDown | Next point (the first one when none is active); stops at the last |
| ArrowLeft, ArrowUp | Previous point (the last one when none is active); stops at the first |
| Home, End | First or last point |
| Escape | Clears the active point and its tooltip |
| Enter, Space | On a legend button: hide or show the series. With Alt: show only that series, or restore all |

The frame is a forced `dir="ltr"` island, so ArrowRight always goes toward later points, also on an RTL page; nothing swaps. The legend sits outside the island and follows the page direction.

#### Screen readers

- The frame is `role="img"` (focusable) named by `label`, by default "Line chart of Revenue, Cost by day" (also "Area chart", "Stacked area chart", "Bar chart", "Horizontal bar chart"). The SVG is `aria-hidden`; pass your own `label` for a useful name.
- The data is a visually hidden `<table>` after the chart: caption is the label, one row per datum, the index as row header, a missing value as "–". Hidden series drop out of the table and the tooltip.
- Stepping with the keyboard writes "Fri: Prompt 160, Completion 50" into a polite live region. Hover shows the tooltip but does not announce.
- The legend is a `group` named "Toggle series" of buttons with `aria-pressed` (a plain `list` when `legendInteractive={false}`). With `loading`, the root has `aria-busy` and one hidden "Loading line chart…" text.

#### Reduced motion

Lines, areas, bars and dots animate data changes with `motion-safe:transition-all duration-500` (the `animate` prop, default true), so with `prefers-reduced-motion` no transition class applies and the chart updates in place. Bar dimming uses `transition-opacity`, which the global net ends in 1 ms. `animate={false}` turns the transitions off for everyone.

#### Server rendering

Server render: part of it fills in after mount. The full SVG renders on the server, but at the fixed fallback width of 600 px: the real width is measured after mount (layout effect plus `ResizeObserver`) and the plot is redrawn then. Tick labels and tooltip text use `Intl` with the runtime locale (and time zone on a time axis), so a server with another locale can differ from the browser: pass `valueFormatter`, `yAxis.formatter` or `xAxis.formatter` to pin them.

#### Slots

- `chart-line`: the stroke path of a series (`LineChart` and `AreaChart`)
- `chart-area`: the filled area of a series
- `chart-bar`: one bar
- `chart-dot`: a point marker (`LineChart dots`)
- `chart-active-dot`: the marker on the hovered or focused point
- `chart-crosshair`: the vertical guide on line and area charts
- `chart-hit`: the transparent rectangle that receives pointer and touch events
- `chart-reference-line`: a `referenceLines` entry
- `chart-empty`: the empty placeholder
- `chart-skeleton`: the loading placeholder

#### Gotchas

- `loading` shows the placeholder only while `data` is empty; with rows it keeps the chart and just sets `aria-busy`. `emptyState` (default "No data") is never shown while loading.
- `connectNulls` and `xAxis.type="time" | "linear"` have no effect on `BarChart` (bars are always categories), and `connectNulls` is ignored on stacked areas, where a null counts as 0. `referenceLines` with `axis: "x"` need a time or linear axis.
- The legend shows by default only for two or more series. The value axis includes 0 unless you pass `yAxis.min="auto"`.
- Series without a `color` take `var(--chart-N, hex)` in order, so a theme can recolour them; a token name or any CSS colour also works.

## Magnetic

> Makes its child drift toward the mouse when the pointer comes within `radius` of it (the `magnetic` utility). The wrapper stays put and measures; an inner box moves, so the hit area and the layout do not shift. Clicks, hover and focus work as without it. Wrap a button, a link or an icon; not a text field. Touch and reduced motion: still.

- Import: `import { Magnetic } from "@sutra/ui/motion"` ([full page](md/Magnetic.md))
- Props: `radius`, `strength` (* required)

## Markdown

> Token-styled markdown renderer (GFM), memoized per block so streaming only re-renders the tail.

- Import: `import { Markdown } from "@sutra/ui/ai"` ([full page](md/Markdown.md))
- Props: `children`*, `citeCount`, `components`, `math`, `onCite`, `rehypePlugins`, `remarkPlugins`, `sources` (* required)

**When to use:** Renders a markdown string with GitHub-flavoured extras (tables, task lists, strikethrough) in the design tokens: headings, lists, quotes, links, images, inline and fenced code with a copy button, optional KaTeX math and citation pills. It is memoized per block, so streamed text only re-renders the tail.

**Use instead when:**
- `CodeBlock`: one snippet with highlighting, a file name and line numbers
- `RichTextEditor`: text the user edits
- `ChatMessageContent`: a chat message that wraps this
- `Text`: a few styled lines rather than a document
- `InlineCode`: a code span inside your own text

#### Keyboard

There is no keyboard handling of its own. Links are normal tab stops, and so are each code block and each table wrapper while it overflows (scroll boxes, so the arrow keys scroll them), each code block's "Copy code" button and, with `onCite`, each citation pill (a button; Enter and Space activate it).

#### Screen readers

- The output is plain semantic HTML: `h1` to `h6`, `p`, `ul`, `ol`, `blockquote`, `table` with `thead` and `th`, `img`. Heading levels are written as in the source and are not shifted. An image without alt text gets `alt=""`.
- A fenced block is a header with the language (or "text") and a button named "Copy code", which becomes "Copied" after a copy, then a `pre`. The code is not highlighted. The `pre` and the wrapper around a table are scroll boxes that get `tabindex="0"` while they overflow (arrow keys scroll them), and always have a name through `role="group"`: "ts code" (the language, or "Code") and "Table".
- Citation pills: a `button` named "Source 2: Title" with `onCite`, a link with a hover card when the source has `href`, else a plain `sup`.
- Task-list items are native checkboxes rendered by GFM.

#### Reduced motion

Nothing moves except the copy-check icon, which zooms in with `animate-in` (the global net removes the movement) and link colour fades (ended in 1 ms).

#### Server rendering

Server render: same markup as the client. react-markdown and KaTeX produce their HTML synchronously, so the server renders the whole document. The block split and block keys derive from `useId`, which matches on both sides.

#### Gotchas

- Raw HTML in the source is shown as text, not rendered (no `rehype-raw`), and link and image URLs go through react-markdown's default filter that drops schemes such as `javascript:`. Add `rehypePlugins` for HTML, and sanitize it yourself.
- Keep `components`, `remarkPlugins` and `rehypePlugins` stable (module scope or `useMemo`): each block is memoized on those references, so a new array on every render re-renders every block while streaming. `components` is merged over the defaults.
- `math` needs the KaTeX stylesheet loaded once by the app (`import "katex/dist/katex.min.css"`); without `math` dollar signs stay as text. Invalid TeX shows rather than throwing.
- `[1]` and `[2, 3]` in prose turn into citation pills only up to `citeCount` (default `sources.length`), and never inside code or links. External `http(s)` links get `target="_blank"` with `rel="noopener noreferrer"`. Fenced code does not use `CodeBlock`: override `pre` in `components` to get highlighting.

## MorphDialog

> A dialog (or bottom sheet) that grows out of the rectangle of the thing that opened it and shrinks back into it. The panel is clipped to the origin's box and its radius and slides onto its final place (Web Animations on the spring token, nothing is scaled, so text never stretches); the scrim, the shadow and the parts marked `data-morph-fade` appear late and go early. It is a Radix Dialog underneath: focus is trapped and handed back on close (to the `trigger`, or to whatever had it), Escape, the close button and a press on the scrim close it, and the panel stays mounted until the closing flight ends. Reduced motion (or no `animate`) means no flight at all. Pass `origin` (an element, a ref or a rect), or use `ExpandCard` for a card that is its own origin. Start the panel's content with the same face as the origin and the flight reads as one object.

- Import: `import { MorphDialog } from "@sutra/ui/motion"` ([full page](md/MorphDialog.md))
- Props: `title`*, `children`, `className`, `defaultOpen`, `description`, `onCloseAutoFocus`, `onMorphEnd`, `onOpenAutoFocus`, `onOpenChange`, `open`, `origin`, `overlayClassName`, `showClose`, `showTitle`, `size`, `trigger`, `variant` (* required)

## MorphPill

> One surface that changes size between states (idle, a picker, a running timer, a sync status): its width and height follow the measured content on a spring token, and the new content fades in as the old one goes. Under reduced motion the size and the content swap at once (the shared net). Controlled (`state`) or uncontrolled (`defaultState`); pass a function as a state's content to switch states from inside. It is an inline surface: put it in a container with room (`max-w-full` keeps it inside a narrow one, and its content is clipped, not overflowing).

- Import: `import { MorphPill } from "@sutra/ui/motion"` ([full page](md/MorphPill.md))
- Props: `states`*, `announcement`, `defaultState`, `label`, `onStateChange`, `ref`, `spring`, `state` (* required)

## PanSurface

> An inertial canvas for boards and big images: drag it and it keeps gliding with time-based friction (`usePan`), stops at its edges with a springy bounce, and moves with the wheel and the arrow keys (Shift for bigger steps, Page Up and Down, Home to recenter). With `zoom` the existing `useZoomPan` handles the scale (wheel with Ctrl or Command, buttons, `+`, `-`, `0`); the offset stays in `usePan`'s CSS variables, so a drag never re-renders. A recenter button appears once the canvas has moved. It is a labelled, focusable group whose content stays in the DOM order for screen readers. A drag on a button inside the canvas still pans and the click after a drag is swallowed; put `data-pan-ignore` on parts that need their own pointer handling. The surface takes touch from the page (`touch-action: none` on its axis), so leave room to scroll around it.

- Import: `import { PanSurface } from "@sutra/ui/mobile"` ([full page](md/PanSurface.md))
- Props: `children`*, `apiRef`, `axis`, `bounds`, `contentClassName`, `contentSize`, `controls`, `defaultScale`, `disabled`, `friction`, `home`, `label`, `maxScale`, `minScale`, `onPan`, `recenterLabel`, `spring`, `step`, `wheel`, `zoom` (* required)

## ReorderableList

> Accessible reorderable list: drag handle with placeholder, Space-to-lift keyboard moves, optional arrow buttons, live announcements. A generic plain function (React 19 `ref` prop) rather than `forwardRef`, which would erase the item type `T`.

- Import: `import { ReorderableList } from "@sutra/ui/social"` ([full page](md/ReorderableList.md))
- Props: `getKey`*, `items`*, `onReorder`*, `renderItem`*, `disabled`, `flip`, `getLabel`, `handle`, `itemClassName`, `label`, `moveButtons`, `ref` (* required)

**When to use:** A list whose rows the user can reorder by dragging a handle, by picking a row up with the keyboard, or with optional up and down buttons, with live announcements. You render each row; the list reports the new order after every move. `Checklist` builds a subtask list on it.

**Use instead when:**
- `AnimatedList`: items that appear and disappear but are not reordered by the user
- `Table`: sortable columns rather than a manual order
- `KanbanBoard`: reorder across columns
- `useReorder`: the move helpers without the list UI

#### Keyboard

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Each row's handle is a tab stop (the handle is a button) |
| Space, Enter | On a handle: pick the row up. While it is picked up: drop it where it is |
| ArrowUp, ArrowDown | While picked up: move the row one place; it stops at the ends |
| Escape | While picked up: cancel and put the row back |
| Enter, Space | On a move button ("Move X up" or "down", with `moveButtons`): move one place at once |

Leaving the handle (blur) while a row is picked up drops it where it is. The arrows are vertical, so nothing changes in RTL. Move buttons are disabled at the ends, while another row is picked up, and with `disabled`.

#### Screen readers

- The list is a `ul` named by `label` (default "Reorderable list"). Each handle is a button named "Reorder <label of the item>" with `aria-pressed` while picked up and `aria-describedby` pointing at hidden instructions ("Press Space to pick up. Use the up and down arrow keys to move, Space to drop, Escape to cancel.").
- An assertive `role="status"` region announces each step: "Picked up Bravo. Position 2 of 5. ...", "Moved Bravo to position 3 of 5.", "Dropped Bravo at position 3 of 5." or "Reorder canceled. Bravo returned to position 2 of 5." Buttons announce their move too.
- The names come from `getLabel`; the default `String(item)` reads "[object Object]" for objects, so pass `getLabel`. The floating copy shown while dragging with a pointer is `aria-hidden`.

#### Reduced motion

With `flip` (default true) rows glide to their new place when the order changes and a dropped row settles from where it was released; under `prefers-reduced-motion` that is off and rows jump. The drag copy fades in with a short `animate-in` that the global net strips of movement.

#### Server rendering

Server render: same markup as the client. The list renders from `items` with plain markup (no browser API at render), so the server HTML is the full list. Drag and keyboard state only exist after interaction.

#### Gotchas

- `items` is the source of truth: `onReorder(next, { from, to })` is called once, on drop (or per button press), and only if the position changed. Keep `items` in your state and set it from `next`. While a row is picked up the list shows its own working order.
- `getKey` must return a stable unique string per item. It is the React key and what the focus and the announcements follow.
- `handle={false}` removes the only drag and keyboard control, so combine it with `moveButtons`. `moveButtons` is off by default.
- It is a generic function component: `ref` is a plain prop (it reaches the `ul`), not a `forwardRef`. `reorderArray`, `reorderBy` and `useReorder` are exported from the same module for the data side.

## RingMeter

> Compact ring showing a fill level against thresholds (role="meter"), e.g. an AI context window. It draws the same ring as `ProgressCircle` (`ProgressRingSvg`); use `ProgressCircle` for task completion (role="progressbar").

- Import: `import { RingMeter } from "@sutra/ui/dataviz"` ([full page](md/RingMeter.md))
- Props: `value`*, `accent`, `children`, `color`, `label`, `loading`, `max`, `showValueAbove`, `size`, `thickness`, `thresholds`, `tone` (* required)

## RotatingNoticeBar

> Global notice strip that rotates through notices with a dot pager, pausing on hover or focus. Renders an `AlertBanner`.

- Import: `import { RotatingNoticeBar } from "@sutra/ui/workspace"` ([full page](md/RotatingNoticeBar.md))
- Props: `notices`*, `autoRotate`, `interval`, `label`, `onDismiss`, `onIndexChange`, `sticky` (* required)

## ScatterChart

> Scatter (and bubble) chart: nearest-point hover, keyboard stepping in x order, toggleable series and reference lines.

- Import: `import { ScatterChart } from "@sutra/ui/dataviz"` ([full page](md/ScatterChart.md))
- Props: `data`*, `index`*, `series`*, `animate`, `bubbleSize`, `defaultHiddenSeries`, `emptyState`, `grid`, `height`, `hiddenSeries`, `label`, `legend`, `legendInteractive`, `loading`, `onActivePointChange`, `onHiddenSeriesChange`, `pointSize`, `referenceLines`, `sizeFormatter`, `tooltip`, `valueFormatter`, `xAxis`, `yAxis` (* required)

## SchemaForm

> Form generated from a JSON-Schema-like object: nested sections, arrays, validation, section nav + search, and debounced autosave.

- Import: `import { SchemaForm } from "@sutra/ui/agent-admin"` ([full page](md/SchemaForm.md))
- Props: `schema`*, `autosave`, `autosaveDelay`, `defaultValue`, `disabled`, `disabledFields`, `navThreshold`, `onChange`, `onSave`, `onSubmit`, `onValueChange`, `submitLabel`, `validateOnMount`, `value` (* required)

**When to use:** A settings form generated from a JSON-Schema-like object: typed controls, nested sections, array fields with add and remove, validation, section navigation with search, and either an explicit Save button or debounced autosave with per-field status. `NestedValueEditor` edits one schema value on its own.

**Use instead when:**
- `Field`: hand-built forms with your own controls and layout
- `Input`: a single text field
- `InlineEditText`: edit one value in place
- `JsonViewer`: read-only structured data
- `McpServerForm`: a ready-made form for one known shape

#### Keyboard

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Through the controls in document order: the search field and section buttons first (when shown), then each field, array buttons, Save |
| Enter | In a text field: submits the form when `onSubmit` is set (native form behaviour) |
| Space | Toggles a switch; the other controls keep their own keys (arrows on a segmented control, the select list keys) |

There are no custom keys, and the layout uses logical sides, so RTL changes nothing.

#### Screen readers

- Each field has a real `<label>`; a required one adds a hidden-from-AT asterisk and `aria-required`. Descriptions and errors are linked with `aria-describedby`, and an invalid field has `aria-invalid`. Error text and the "Saving…", "Saved" and "Not saved" marks are plain text, not live regions.
- Objects are `fieldset`s with a `legend`, arrays are `group`s named by the label (with a count) whose items have "Remove Tag 1" buttons, and top-level sections are `section`s named by an `h3`. The navigation is a `nav` named "Sections", with `aria-current` on the chosen button and a hidden " errors" count after submit.
- After a failed submit a `role="alert"` says "Fix 2 fields to continue". A field with `x-disabled-reason` or `disabledFields` is disabled and shows the reason as text with a lock icon.

#### Reduced motion

Only the "Saved" tick pops (`animate-pop`), which the global net stops, and the controls carry their own transitions (ended in 1 ms).

#### Server rendering

Server render: same markup as the client. The form renders in full from the schema and value, with ids from `useSafeId`; nothing depends on the browser until you type. Autosave timers start on the first edit.

#### Slots

- `schema-form`: the `<form>` element

#### Gotchas

- Control type follows the schema: boolean is a switch; an `enum` of three or fewer is a segmented control, more is a select; `number` and `integer` use a number input; `format: "password"` or `x-secret` masks; `format: "textarea"` is a textarea; `email` and `uri` set the input type. An emptied field removes its key from the value.
- Errors show for a field only after it was blurred, edited under autosave, or after the first submit (or all at once with `validateOnMount`). Empty values skip every rule except `required`, which is a list on the parent object. `uri` accepts only `http(s)` URLs, and an invalid `pattern` never fails.
- Autosave (`autosave`, `onSave(value, changedKeys)`) waits `autosaveDelay` (800 ms) after the last edit and saves only the changed top-level keys that are valid; invalid ones are skipped. Throwing from `onSave` marks them "Not saved". Status shows beside top-level fields and arrays, not on a nested object section.
- `onSubmit` runs only when the value is valid, and the button shows a spinner while its promise is pending. Without `onSubmit` (or with `autosave`) there is no Save button. Navigation and search appear above `navThreshold` (8) top-level fields or with more than two sections (`x-category`, or an object's title, else "General"). `onChange` is a deprecated alias of `onValueChange`.

## ScrollProgressBar

> A thin bar that fills as the scroller scrolls (the `scroll-progress-bar` utility plus the script fallback). Decorative (`aria-hidden`); place it `sticky top-0` inside a scroll area or `fixed inset-x-0 top-0` for the page. Empty where no timeline or script can drive it, and under reduced motion.

- Import: `import { ScrollProgressBar } from "@sutra/ui/motion"` ([full page](md/ScrollProgressBar.md))
- Props: `forceFallback`, `scroller` (* required)

## ScrollReveal

> Fades and moves its content in as it scrolls into view, scrubbed by the scroll position (it reverses when you scroll back). It is the `scroll-reveal` utility plus the script fallback: browsers with `animation-timeline` run it as a CSS animation with no JavaScript; others get `--sutra-progress` from `useScrollProgress`, and with neither the content is simply there. Reduced motion shows the end state at once. Not for dense tables, live data or anything above the fold that must be readable on load. It replaces the element's own `translate` and `scale`, so wrap, do not stack. Keep it out of `overflow-hidden` wrappers (a native timeline binds to the nearest clipping ancestor, which never scrolls): use `overflow-clip` there.

- Import: `import { ScrollReveal } from "@sutra/ui/motion"` ([full page](md/ScrollReveal.md))
- Props: `as`, `distance`, `forceFallback`, `from`, `scroller` (* required)

## ScrollStage

> A sticky stage over a scroll runway: the stage stays in view while you scroll through the runway, and `--sutra-progress` (0 at the start, 1 at the end) is set on the stage root so its children can follow it in CSS (`opacity-(--p)` with `--p: clamp(0, (var(--sutra-progress, 1) - .3) / .4, 1)`). Scrolling stays native: no hijacking, no snapping, keyboard and touch work as usual, and the content can be focused and read at any progress. Without script, or under reduced motion, the variable is unset (children read it with a default of 1, their end state) and the stage is an ordinary block with no runway.

- Import: `import { ScrollStage } from "@sutra/ui/motion"` ([full page](md/ScrollStage.md))
- Props: `onScrollProgress`, `runway`, `scroller`, `stageHeight` (* required)

## SearchTrigger

> A button that looks like a search field and opens a command palette: placeholder text plus the shortcut as `Kbd` chips. With `hotkey` it also listens for the shortcut (through the shortcut registry when a `ShortcutProvider` is present).

- Import: `import { SearchTrigger } from "@sutra/ui/navigation"` ([full page](md/SearchTrigger.md))
- Props: `collapseBelow`, `hotkey`, `label`, `onTrigger`, `placeholder`, `shortcut`, `size` (* required)

**When to use:** A button that looks like a search field, with placeholder text and the shortcut as key chips ("Ctrl K", or the command key on macOS). Clicking it, or pressing the shortcut when `hotkey` is on, calls `onTrigger`, where you open your command palette.

**Use instead when:**
- `SearchInput`: a real text field you type into
- `CommandDialog`: the palette this opens
- `FilterBarSearch`: a search field that filters a list in place
- `Button`: any other action
- `Combobox`: pick a value from a searchable list

#### Keyboard

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Focuses the button |
| Enter, Space | Press it: calls `onClick`, then `onTrigger` (not if `onClick` calls `preventDefault`) |
| The `shortcut` (default Ctrl or Cmd+K) | With `hotkey`, calls `onTrigger` from anywhere on the page and stops the browser's own handling |

A `mod+` chord also fires while typing in an input, a textarea or an editable element; a plain key such as `/` is ignored there and fires elsewhere. On macOS `mod` is the command key and Ctrl is ignored. Nothing depends on arrow keys, so RTL changes nothing.

#### Screen readers

- It is a native `button` named by `label`, else by the placeholder text ("Search…"). The search icon and the key chips are `aria-hidden`, so the shortcut does not become part of the name.
- The shortcut is exposed as a description ("Shortcut: Control K", from a single combination, not for key sequences) and through `aria-keyshortcuts` ("Meta+K Control+K").
- With `collapseBelow`, an icon-only button named `label` or "Search" replaces the field below that breakpoint; both exist in the page and CSS hides one.

#### Reduced motion

Only a colour and border transition on hover, which the global net ends within 1 ms. Static otherwise.

#### Server rendering

Server render: part of it fills in after mount. The shortcut chips depend on the platform: the server and the hydrating client render the non-Mac labels ("Ctrl") and a Mac browser switches to the command key right after hydration, before paint, so the markup matches. Inside a `ShortcutProvider` with a `platform` prop that platform is used from the first render on both sides. The hotkey listener is attached in an effect.

#### Slots

- `search-trigger`: the field-shaped button

#### Gotchas

- It opens nothing itself: `onTrigger` (also called by the hotkey) is where you set your palette's `open`. Pair it with `CommandDialog` by setting its `open` in `onTrigger`.
- `hotkey` defaults to off, so the chips are only a hint until you turn it on. Inside a `ShortcutProvider` it registers as "Search" in the shortcut registry; otherwise it listens on `document`.
- `shortcut` is a keys spec (`"mod+k"`, `"/"`, `"g t"`); the same value draws the chips and sets the hotkey.
- The field has `max-w-72` and takes the full width up to it; `size` is `sm` 32 px, `md` 36 px (default) or `lg` 40 px, and `className` is merged last.

## SectionHeader

> Section heading with eyebrow, title, description, actions and an optional tabs slot.

- Import: `import { SectionHeader } from "@sutra/ui/navigation"` ([full page](md/SectionHeader.md))
- Props: `title`*, `actions`, `align`, `as`, `description`, `divider`, `eyebrow`, `leading`, `size`, `tabs` (* required)

## SectionRail

> Section navigation that highlights the section in view ("On this page", a sticky sub-nav). The links are real anchors (`aria-current="location"` on the active one); a click scrolls the section to the top of its scroller, respecting reduced motion. Tracking is `useScrollSections`; pass `value` to drive the highlight yourself.

- Import: `import { SectionRail } from "@sutra/ui/navigation"` ([full page](md/SectionRail.md))
- Props: `sections`*, `defaultValue`, `emptyState`, `getHref`, `label`, `loading`, `offset`, `onValueChange`, `orientation`, `root`, `rootMargin`, `smoothScroll`, `title`, `value` (* required)

**When to use:** A table of contents that highlights the section in view, as an "On this page" column or a scrolling row of tabs for a sticky sub-navigation. The links are real anchors; a click scrolls the section to the top. `useScrollSections` is the tracking behind it.

**Use instead when:**
- `Tabs`: switch panels, nothing scrolls
- `Breadcrumb`: where you are in a site hierarchy
- `Steps`: progress through ordered stages
- `Sidebar`: app navigation between pages
- `TreeView`: a nested hierarchy you expand and select

#### Keyboard

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Each link is a tab stop (there is no roving focus) |
| Enter | Follows the link: scrolls the section to the top, marks it current and updates the address bar |

Space does nothing on a link, and there are no arrow keys, so RTL changes nothing for the keyboard. A click does not move focus to the section: it stays on the link.

#### Screen readers

- A `nav` named by `label` (default "Table of contents") with a list of links. The current one has `aria-current="location"`. The "On this page" title is plain text, not a heading.
- With `loading` the nav is `aria-busy` with one hidden "Loading…" and `aria-hidden` placeholder rows: no links exist until the sections are known.
- The active mark is the only state; nothing is announced when it moves as you scroll.

#### Reduced motion

Clicks scroll smoothly (`smoothScroll`, default true) but jump under `prefers-reduced-motion`, read when you click. The horizontal rail also re-centres the active tab with an instant scroll then. Link colour changes are transitions that the global net ends in 1 ms.

#### Server rendering

Server render: same markup as the client. The first render is the same on the server and client: the active section is `value`, `defaultValue` or the first id. Tracking starts in an effect after mount.

#### Slots

- `section-rail`: the `nav` (`data-orientation`; `data-state="empty"` on the empty-state wrapper)

#### Gotchas

- Each section needs an element with the matching `id` that is already in the page when the rail mounts or when the ids change; missing ones are skipped. Add `scroll-margin-top` to the targets when a fixed header covers them, and pass `root` when the sections scroll inside a container rather than the page.
- Tracking marks the first listed section that is in the top third of the scroller (`offset` shifts it down by a header's height, `rootMargin` replaces the rule) and keeps the last one while none is. `value` makes it controlled and turns tracking off, yet a click still scrolls and calls `onValueChange`.
- A plain click scrolls with `scrollIntoView` and writes the link to the address bar with `replaceState`, so Back does not undo it; use `getHref` to give router URLs where `#id` is taken. Modified clicks (Ctrl, Cmd, Shift, Alt, middle button) and `smoothScroll={false}` leave the browser's own anchor jump.
- `level` (2 to 4) indents deeper entries relative to the shallowest one, in the vertical rail only. With no sections it renders nothing unless you give `emptyState`.

## SelectionArea

- Import: `import { SelectionArea } from "@sutra/ui"` ([full page](md/SelectionArea.md))

## SparkBar

> Tiny inline column chart. A left-to-right island like `Sparkline`: the first bar is always on the physical left.

- Import: `import { SparkBar } from "@sutra/ui/dataviz"` ([full page](md/SparkBar.md))
- Props: `data`*, `accent`, `color`, `gap`, `height`, `highlightLast`, `label`, `max`, `min`, `mutedColor`, `radius`, `responsive`, `tone`, `width`, `wrapperClassName` (* required)

## Sparkline

> Tiny inline trend chart. It is a left-to-right island: the series always runs from the physical left, also on a right-to-left page.

- Import: `import { Sparkline } from "@sutra/ui/dataviz"` ([full page](md/Sparkline.md))
- Props: `data`*, `accent`, `color`, `gradient`, `height`, `highlightLast`, `label`, `max`, `min`, `responsive`, `smooth`, `strokeWidth`, `tone`, `trend`, `type`, `width`, `wrapperClassName` (* required)

**When to use:** A tiny inline trend with no axes, as a line, a filled area or bars, for a table cell, a stat tile or a list row. `SparkBar` is the bar form on its own; `type="bar"` hands over to it.

**Use instead when:**
- `LineChart`: a chart with axes, tooltip and a data table
- `StatCard`: a number with a built-in trend
- `Meter`: a level against a limit rather than a history
- `Progress`: completion of a task

#### Keyboard

Not focusable: no keyboard interaction. There is no tooltip or point selection.

#### Screen readers

- The SVG is `role="img"` with an `aria-label`: `label` when given, otherwise "Trend from 3 to 9" (first and last value; "No data" for an empty array). `SparkBar` defaults to "5 values, latest 9".
- That is all a screen reader gets: there is no data table. Pass a `label` that says what the numbers are ("Requests per minute, last hour") and show the current value as real text beside it.
- The `highlightLast` dot is `aria-hidden` decoration.

#### Reduced motion

Line and area charts do not animate. `SparkBar` bars change height and position with a 300 ms transition when data changes, which the reduced-motion net ends within 1 ms.

#### Server rendering

Server render: same markup as the client. Pure SVG computed from `data`, `width` and `height`, with an id from `useId` for the area gradient; the server and client markup are the same.

#### Gotchas

- A line or area scales to the range of its data (`min` and `max` override), so a flat series fills the box and a tiny change looks large. `type="bar"` always includes 0 on its scale, so the same data looks different; set `min` and `max` on both to compare them.
- Colour precedence is `tone`, then `color`, then `accent`; `trend` (green when the last value is at least the first, red otherwise) only applies when none of the three is set. A token name such as `"success"` works in `color`.
- With `responsive` the SVG stretches to the container width (`preserveAspectRatio="none"`, strokes keep their width) and `width` only sets the viewBox; without it the box is `width` by `height` (default 120 by 32). Both charts are left-to-right islands (`dir="ltr"` on the wrapper, like the other charts): the series starts at the physical left and the `highlightLast` dot sits on the last point, also on an RTL page.
- `type="bar"` ignores `smooth`, `strokeWidth` and `gradient`; `mutedColor`, `gap` and `radius` are props of `SparkBar` only, so render it directly to set them. `highlightLast` is the dot on a line and the full-colour bar on bars.

## SplitPane

> Two resizable panes with an accessible draggable divider, persistence and a narrow-width fallback.

- Import: `import { SplitPane } from "@sutra/ui/mobile"` ([full page](md/SplitPane.md))
- Parts: `SplitPaneHandle`, `SplitPanePanel`
- Props: `collapseBelow`, `collapseMode`, `collapsible`, `defaultSize`, `max`, `min`, `onSizeChange`, `orientation`, `size`, `step`, `storageKey` (* required)

**When to use:** Two resizable panes with a draggable, keyboard-operable divider, an optional saved size, and a narrow-width fallback that stacks the panes or shows one at a time. Use it for editor and preview, list and detail, or a sidebar next to content.

**Use instead when:**
- `TilingLayout`: more than two panes, nested splits and tab groups
- `Sheet`: a panel that overlays the page
- `Sidebar`: app navigation that collapses
- `Tabs`: switch between views rather than see both

#### Keyboard

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Focuses the divider (the only tab stop in the component) |
| ArrowLeft, ArrowRight | Horizontal split: move the divider left or right by `step` percent (Shift doubles it) |
| ArrowUp, ArrowDown | Vertical split: move the divider up or down |
| Home, End | Shrink the first panel to `min`, or grow it to `max` |
| Enter | Collapse the first panel, or restore it (unless `collapsible={false}`) |
| Double-click | Reset to `defaultSize` (pointer only) |

The divider follows the arrow you press in both directions: in RTL the first panel sits on the right and the two horizontal arrows swap their effect on its size. Dragging with a pointer also measures from the right edge in RTL.

#### Screen readers

- The divider is a focusable `role="separator"` (the window-splitter pattern) with `aria-orientation` (`vertical` for side-by-side panes), `aria-valuenow` as the first panel's percent (0 when collapsed), `aria-valuemin`, `aria-valuemax`, and `aria-controls` pointing at the first panel. Its name is "Resize panels"; pass `aria-label` on `SplitPaneHandle` to say which panes ("Resize editor").
- A collapsed first panel gets `hidden`, so it leaves the accessibility tree. In `collapseMode="primary"` a group "Show panel" of `aria-pressed` buttons (named by each panel's `label`) switches panels; when stacked the divider is not rendered.
- The panels are plain `div`s with no role: add landmarks or labels yourself.

#### Reduced motion

Nothing moves except a colour fade on the divider, which the global net ends in 1 ms. Resizing follows the pointer or key presses directly with no animation.

#### Server rendering

Server render: part of it fills in after mount. The panes render on the server and on the hydrating client render at `defaultSize` (or `size`), so the markup matches. With `storageKey` the saved size is read right after hydration, before paint, and applied without calling `onSizeChange`; `collapseBelow` is judged from a measured width, so stacking only happens after mount.

#### Slots

- `split-pane`: the root (`data-orientation`, `data-stacked`, `data-dragging`)
- `split-pane-panel`: one panel (`data-panel` index, `data-collapsed`)
- `split-pane-handle`: the divider (`data-collapsed`)

#### Gotchas

- It is built for two panels: the first is sized (`size` percent, clamped to `min` 15 and `max` 85) and the second fills the rest. If you render no `SplitPaneHandle`, one is inserted before the second panel.
- Give the pane a height (for example `className="h-96"`): sizes are percentages of the container, the root clips overflow and each panel scrolls itself.
- `defaultSize` is the starting size and the double-click reset value. Controlled use is `size` with `onSizeChange`, which is called on every move, as is the write to `localStorage` when `storageKey` is set (a saved value beats `defaultSize` on mount; a blocked storage is ignored).
- `collapseBelow` is a container width in px: below it the divider is removed and the panes stack (`collapseMode="stack"`) or show one at a time (`"primary"`). Any resize, even from the keyboard, restores a collapsed first panel.

## SplitText

> Text that reveals itself character by character or word by word (`animate-fade-up` plus the `stagger` delay on `--i`). Accessible by construction: the real text sits once in a visually hidden span, and the pieces are `aria-hidden`, so a screen reader never hears letters, and copying and find-in-page still see words (a word stays unbroken at line ends). Under `prefers-reduced-motion`, or with `animate={false}`, it renders the plain text.

- Import: `import { SplitText } from "@sutra/ui/motion"` ([full page](md/SplitText.md))
- Props: `text`*, `animate`, `as`, `by`, `effect`, `step` (* required)

## SpotlightCard

> A `Card` with a soft glow that follows the mouse (the `spotlight` utility on `usePointerVars`). It also glows at the centre while something inside has keyboard focus. Touch, reduced motion and no hover leave it plain. Decoration only.

- Import: `import { SpotlightCard } from "@sutra/ui/motion"` ([full page](md/SpotlightCard.md))
- Props: `as`, `glowSize`, `padded`, `size` (* required)

## StatCard

> KPI tile: label, big value, delta, hint and optional sparkline. With `href`/`onClick` the label becomes a link/button stretched over the card; keep other interactive content out of a linked card (or lift it with `relative z-10`).

- Import: `import { StatCard } from "@sutra/ui/dataviz"` ([full page](md/StatCard.md))
- Props: `label`*, `accent`, `animate`, `caption`, `chevron`, `children`, `delta`, `deltaIntent`, `deltaLabel`, `deltaSuffix`, `hint`, `href`, `icon`, `iconPlacement`, `labelTone`, `loading`, `onClick`, `progress`, `progressMax`, `size`, `stats`, `status`, `tone`, `trend`, `trendColor`, `trendMax`, `trendMin`, `trendPlacement`, `trendType`, `unit`, `value`, `valueFont`, `valueFormat`, `valueLocale` (* required)

**When to use:** A metric tile: label, big value with unit, optional delta, hint, sparkline, progress bar, stat row and body. With `href` or `onClick` the whole card is one link or button. `StatGroup` lays tiles out in a row, `TopItemCard` is the preset for "the biggest item right now", `StatValue` is just the number.

**Use instead when:**
- `MetricHero`: the page-header metric with a live chart
- `Meter`: a value against a limit
- `Gauge`: one reading on an arc
- `AnimatedNumber`: only a rolling number
- `BarList`: a ranked list
- `Sparkline`: just the trend
- `Card`: a plain container

#### Keyboard

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Without `href` or `onClick` the card is not focusable. With either, the label is the one tab stop and the focus ring is drawn around the whole card |
| Enter | Follows the link or presses the button |
| Space | Presses the button (a link does not react to Space) |

Nothing depends on the arrow keys, so RTL changes only the chevron, which mirrors.

#### Screen readers

- The card is a plain `div` with no role. The label, value, unit and delta are read as text in order; a delta adds hidden "Increased", "Decreased" or "Unchanged" before it.
- With `href` or `onClick` the label is an `<a>` or a `<button>` stretched over the card, and `aria-describedby` points at the value block (caption, value, delta), so the link is announced with its value.
- `trend` is an image named "<label> trend" ("Trend" when the label is not a string) with no values: show the number as text too. `progress` is a `progressbar` named by the label.
- With `loading` the root has `aria-busy`, there is one hidden "Loading CPU…", and the label, caption and stat labels stay visible.

#### Reduced motion

Hover only tints the card and nudges the chevron, both transitions the global net ends in 1 ms. The digit roll of `animate` (opt-in, numbers only) is a transition too, so under `prefers-reduced-motion` the value changes at once. The sparkline does not animate, except bars (`trendType="bar"`).

#### Server rendering

Server render: same markup as the client. Plain markup from props with a `useId` id; the same on server and client. `animate` and the default number text use the runtime locale: pass `valueLocale` and `valueFormat` when the server and the browser may differ.

#### Slots

- `stat-card`: the root; `stat-body`: caption, value row and delta; `stat-value`: the number
- `stat-delta`: the change (`data-direction`, `data-quality`); `stat-status`: the right-aligned `status`
- `stat-link`: the label link or button; `stat-chevron`: its arrow
- `stat-stats`, `stat-content`, `stat-trend`: the stat row, the `children` body and the footer trend
- `stat-skeleton` and the `*-skeleton` parts: loading placeholders
- `stat-group`: the `StatGroup` grid; `top-item`: the `TopItemCard` item

#### Gotchas

- `loading` always shows placeholders for the value, hint, delta, stat values, progress, trend and `children`, even when a value is present (there is no refresh state); pass it only until the first value arrives.
- Delta direction comes from the sign of a number or a leading `+`, `-` or `−` in a string; colour comes from `deltaIntent` (default `positive-is-good`: up is green; `negative-is-good` flips it, `neutral` greys it). `deltaSuffix` ("%") is added to numbers only.
- A linked card covers its content with the stretched link: other buttons inside (in `children` or `status`) need `relative z-10` to stay clickable.
- `tone` tints the value only for `warning` and `destructive`; the trend follows the delta quality unless `accent` or `trendColor` is set. In a `StatGroup variant="divided"` the cards lose their own border and shadow.

- Import: `import { StatementHero } from "@sutra/ui"` ([full page](md/StatementHero.md))
- Props: `title`*, `action`, `align`, `animated`, `as`, `description`, `float`, `hint`, `media`, `size` (* required)

- Props: `columns`, `variant` (* required)

## StatusCycle

## StatValue

> The big number of a metric with its unit, shared by StatCard and MetricHero.

## StepWizard

> A multi-step flow in one place: the steps slide in the direction you are going, the area grows or shrinks to the height of the current step, and a progress bar or `Steps` shows where you are. `canAdvance` validates before moving forward (it may be async), Back is free, focus moves to the new step's panel so a screen reader announces it, and Enter in a text field presses Next. Controlled with `value` or uncontrolled. Under reduced motion the steps swap with no slide and the height jumps.

- Import: `import { StepWizard } from "@sutra/ui/navigation"` ([full page](md/StepWizard.md))
- Props: `steps`*, `canAdvance`, `defaultValue`, `footer`, `indicator`, `keepMounted`, `labels`, `onBlocked`, `onComplete`, `onError`, `onValueChange`, `stepsProps`, `value` (* required)

**When to use:** A multi-step flow in one place (onboarding, checkout, setup): a progress bar or step indicator, the current step's content that slides in the direction of travel, validation before moving forward, and Back, Next and Finish buttons.

**Use instead when:**
- `Steps`: only the progress indicator, with you owning the content
- `Tabs`: sections the user may open in any order
- `Progress`: a bar without steps
- `Dialog`: a single focused task without stages

#### Keyboard

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Through the completed-step buttons of the indicator, the step content, then Back and Next |
| Enter | In a text input inside a step: presses Next, or Finish on the last step. Not in a textarea or a button-type input, and not while an IME is composing |
| Enter, Space | On Back, Next or Finish, and on a completed step in the indicator: activates it |

Back is disabled on the first step, and both buttons wait while a check or `onComplete` is pending (Next shows its spinner). Upcoming steps in the indicator are not buttons, so you cannot jump ahead. Nothing uses the arrow keys; in RTL the Back and Next arrows mirror and the slide-in comes from the other side.

#### Screen readers

- Every step panel is a `group` named "Step 2 of 4" (`labels.step` changes it). When the step changes, focus moves to the new panel (not on first render), so it is announced. With `keepMounted`, the other panels are `hidden` and `inert`.
- The indicator is an ordered list named "Progress" with `aria-current="step"` on the current item and hidden "(completed)" text on finished ones. The progress bar is a `progressbar` named by the same "Step n of m" text, next to the step title.
- With `indicator="auto"` both exist, and the container width (28rem) hides one with `display: none`, so only one is exposed. The root is `aria-busy` while a check or completion is pending.
- Showing the error is yours: `onBlocked` and `onError` tell you where, and the wizard does not render a message.

#### Reduced motion

A step change slides and fades in (`animate-in`, from the end side going forward and the start side going back) and the area animates its height. Under `prefers-reduced-motion` no slide class is added and the height transition ends in 1 ms. The preference is read when a step changes, not live.

#### Server rendering

Server render: part of it fills in after mount. The first step renders in full on the server (the first render has no entrance animation). The viewport height is measured after mount and then set as an inline style, and the choice between the step indicator and the bar is a container query in CSS, so the markup does not mismatch.

#### Slots

- `step-wizard`: the root (`data-direction` after a move)
- `step-wizard-steps`, `step-wizard-progress`: the indicator and the bar
- `step-wizard-viewport`: the clipped, height-animated area; `step-wizard-panel`: one step (`data-state` current or hidden)
- `step-wizard-footer`: the Back and Next row

#### Gotchas

- `canAdvance(step, index)` runs before leaving a step forward (Next, Finish) and may be async; return `false` to stay, and `onBlocked` fires. Going back is never checked, and `onValueChange` and `onComplete` run only after the check passes.
- Only the current step is rendered, so local state of other steps is lost on the way back. Pass `keepMounted` to keep every step in the tree.
- `value` is the step id and a missing id shows the first step. A custom `footer` (or `footer={false}`) removes the built-in buttons: drive the wizard with a controlled `value`, which `canAdvance` does not guard (only the buttons, the indicator and Enter go through it).
- `onComplete` only reports Finish (and may return a promise: the button shows loading until it settles); it does not navigate. A throw or rejection from `canAdvance` or `onComplete` goes to `onError` and keeps the step.

- Import: `import { Stopwatch } from "@sutra/ui/social"` ([full page](md/Stopwatch.md))
- Props: `autoStart`, `onLap`, `showLaps` (* required)

- Import: `import { StorageMap } from "@sutra/ui/dataviz"` ([full page](md/StorageMap.md))
- Props: `items`*, `breadcrumb`, `capacity`, `categories`, `defaultPath`, `defaultWidth`, `depth`, `emptyState`, `formatBytes`, `free`, `gap`, `height`, `label`, `legend`, `loading`, `minLabelSize`, `onPathChange`, `onSelect`, `path`, `tooltip`, `used` (* required)

> AI proposal review: word diff of a suggestion with Accept / Discard and per-change accept / reject.

- Import: `import { SuggestionDiff } from "@sutra/ui/editor"` ([full page](md/SuggestionDiff.md))

## SwipeDeck

> Triage cards one at a time: drag the top card and it flies away (past 90 px or on a flick) or springs back, with a tilt of 0.05 degrees per px and the cards behind stepping up the stack as it goes. The same choices are Skip and Keep buttons, the arrow keys and Enter on the focused deck, and Ctrl or Command + Z or the Undo button takes the last swipe back (the card flies in again). `start` and `end` follow the reading direction, `onSwipe(side, item, index)` reports each choice, `onEmpty` fires after the last card, `index` / `defaultIndex` / `onIndexChange` control the position. Screen readers get a labelled group, the top card as "Card 2 of 8" and a polite announcement per swipe; the cards behind are `inert`. Built on `useDrag`, so a drag writes CSS variables and never re-renders; reduced motion drops the flight (a swipe just changes the card).

- Import: `import { SwipeDeck } from "@sutra/ui/mobile"` ([full page](md/SwipeDeck.md))
- Props: `getKey`*, `items`*, `renderCard`*, `actions`, `apiRef`, `cardClassName`, `defaultIndex`, `disabled`, `distance`, `emptyState`, `endIcon`, `endLabel`, `getLabel`, `index`, `label`, `loading`, `onEmpty`, `onIndexChange`, `onSwipe`, `onUndo`, `stack`, `startIcon`, `startLabel` (* required)

**When to use:** Triage cards one at a time. Drag the top card to either side (or press Skip and Keep, the arrow keys or Enter) and it flies away, with the cards behind stepping up and Undo bringing the last one back.

**Use instead when:**
- `Carousel`: browse slides with no decision per card
- `SwipeRow`: swipe actions on a list row
- `ReorderableList`: reorder items by dragging
- `StepWizard`: ordered steps

#### Keyboard

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Focuses the deck, then the Skip, Undo and Keep buttons below it |
| ArrowRight | On the deck: swipes the top card to the right, which is the `end` side in LTR and the `start` side in RTL |
| ArrowLeft | Swipes it to the left: `start` in LTR, `end` in RTL |
| Enter | Always the `end` side (Keep) |
| Ctrl+Z, Cmd+Z | Takes the last swipe back (not with Shift) |

The arrows are physical (the card flies the way the arrow points) while `start` and `end` follow the reading direction, so in RTL ArrowLeft is the `end` side (the test pins it). Keys only count when the deck itself has focus, not when focus is on an input or button inside a card, and are ignored while `disabled` or `loading`.

#### Screen readers

- The focusable stage is a `group` with `aria-roledescription="card deck"`, named "Card deck" (`label`) and described by a hidden hint that lists the keys. The top card is a `group` with `aria-roledescription="card"` named "Card n of N".
- Cards behind and flying cards are `aria-hidden` and `inert`. The Skip and Keep stamps on a card are `aria-hidden`.
- A polite live region announces each swipe, for example "Keep: Invoice 12. 2 left" or "No cards left", and "Undid Skip" for an undo. `getLabel` supplies the item name; without it only the side and the count are said.
- Skip, Undo and Keep are real buttons (`startLabel` and `endLabel` rename them and the announcements). `loading` sets `aria-busy`, hides the controls and adds hidden "Loading cards…" text. The hint, "Undo" and the empty text are English and not in a prop.

#### Reduced motion

The tilt, the stamps and the follow-the-finger offset are written while you drag, with no animation. The flight of a dismissed card and the fly-in of an undone one are springs that `useDrag` skips under `prefers-reduced-motion`: the card is simply replaced. The cards behind move up through a transition that the reduced-motion net ends in 1 ms.

#### Server rendering

Server render: same markup as the client. The server renders the top card and the cards behind it (at most `stack` + 1), the controls and the hint, with no browser API at render. Direction, measuring and the drag are all read in handlers and effects.

#### Slots

- `swipe-deck`: the root
- `swipe-deck-stage`: the focusable group that holds the cards
- `swipe-deck-card`: one card, with `data-position` of `top`, `behind` or `leaving`
- `swipe-deck-stamp`: the Skip or Keep stamp on a card (`data-side`)
- `swipe-deck-empty`: what shows when no cards are left
- `swipe-deck-actions`: the row with the Skip, Undo and Keep buttons

#### Gotchas

- `getKey` must return a stable id per item: cards, their flights and Undo are tracked by it. Undo only takes back the latest swipe, and only while that card is still directly before the current index and still the same item.
- `renderCard` also runs for the cards behind the top one (the deepest is hidden), so keep it cheap. The deck draws the card surface; give it a height through `cardClassName`.
- `onSwipe(side, item, index)` reports the side by reading direction (`start` is left in LTR). `index` is the top card, `items.length` means none left; controlled, a swipe asks for the new index through `onIndexChange`.
- `actions={false}` removes the buttons, leaving drag and keys only, so keep them unless you provide another path. Only the top card can be dragged, and a drag commits past `distance` (default 90 px) or on a flick.

## SwipeRow

> A list row that follows the finger: drag it to reveal buttons at its start or end, or swipe all the way to run the outermost one. It builds on `useDrag` (the offset lives in `--sutra-drag-x`, no render per move), rubber-bands past the end, releases with a spring and opens at 40% of the actions' width. The actions are real buttons: Tab reaches them (a focused button opens its side), Arrow keys on the row open and close it, Escape closes it, and `onAction` runs for buttons and swipes alike. Use `Item` rows as the content; inside an `ItemGroup` the row itself is the list item.

- Import: `import { SwipeRow } from "@sutra/ui/mobile"` ([full page](md/SwipeRow.md))
- Props: `actionsLabel`, `actionWidth`, `commit`, `contentClassName`, `defaultValue`, `disabled`, `endActions`, `onAction`, `onValueChange`, `startActions`, `value` (* required)

**When to use:** A list row you drag sideways to reveal action buttons at its start or end, or swipe all the way to run the outermost one. The actions are real buttons that Tab reaches, with arrow and Escape keys on the row as a keyboard path.

**Use instead when:**
- `DropdownMenu`: the actions fit a menu button on every device
- `ReorderableList`: rows the user reorders by dragging
- `Item`: the row content you put inside it (inside an `ItemGroup` the SwipeRow becomes the list item)

#### Keyboard

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab / Shift+Tab | The action buttons are always in the tab order: focusing one opens its side, and leaving the group closes it |
| ArrowRight | On the row in left-to-right text: opens the `startActions` and moves focus to their first enabled button |
| ArrowLeft | In left-to-right text: opens the `endActions` the same way |
| The arrow of the other side | While a side is open: closes it and returns focus to where it was |
| Escape | Closes an open row and returns focus to where it was |
| Enter, Space | Press the focused action button |

The row itself is not focusable, so the arrows work from a control inside it (a link or button in the content) or from an action. They are ignored in text fields and with Alt, Ctrl or Meta held. In RTL the arrows swap with the drag direction, so ArrowLeft opens the `startActions` and ArrowRight the `endActions`; this follows from the source (`direction.test.tsx` does not cover SwipeRow).

#### Screen readers

- Each side is a `role="group"` named "Actions" (`actionsLabel`), with plain `<button>`s named by their `label`; icons are `aria-hidden`. The actions are in the accessibility tree even while the row is closed, and both sides share one name when both are given.
- Inside an `ItemGroup` the row has `role="listitem"`, and the `Item` inside it is not a second list item. Outside one the row has no role.
- There is no live announcement when the row opens or an action runs: put the result in your own live region or a toast.

#### Reduced motion

The drag follows the finger with no animation. The settle after a release (open, close, or the fly-out of a full swipe) is a spring that `useDrag` skips under `prefers-reduced-motion`: the row jumps to its place and a committed swipe does not visibly fly out. The button colour fade ends in 1 ms.

#### Server rendering

Server render: part of it fills in after mount. The server renders the row and both action groups at rest with a left-to-right direction. The widths are measured and the position is applied after mount, so `defaultValue` or `value` set to a side starts open only after hydration, and in RTL the signs settle after mount.

#### Slots

- `swipe-row`: the root
- `swipe-row-content`: the sliding layer that holds your content
- `swipe-row-actions`: one side's group of buttons (`data-side` is `start` or `end`)

#### Gotchas

- `commit` defaults to true: a swipe past half the row (or a fast flick) runs the outermost action, which is the one marked `commit: true` or the one at the row's edge. Pass `commit={false}` for destructive actions you only want revealed, otherwise one long swipe deletes.
- `startActions` and `endActions` are logical: `startActions` are revealed by dragging toward the inline end (right in LTR, left in RTL). `onAction` runs for a button, a key and a swipe alike, after the action's own `onSelect`, and never for a `disabled` action.
- The content layer must stay opaque (`bg-background` by default) or the buttons show through; set `contentClassName` when the row sits on another surface. Taps on an open row close it instead of activating the content, and so does a press outside.
- `actionWidth` (default 72) fixes the reveal distance without measuring: wider labels truncate rather than widen. Drags that start on inputs, textareas, selects, sliders or `data-swipe-no-drag` elements are ignored.

- Props: `items`*, `bordered`, `defaultValue`, `onValueChange`, `renderLink`, `size`, `value` (* required)

## TallyCounter

> Big tally number with −/+ (press and hold to repeat), step, goal ring and an entry log with undo.

> An action that reads as part of a sentence: inline text, underlined on hover. A link with `href`, a button otherwise.

## ThemeToggle

> Light / dark / system switch: an animated icon button or a segmented control.

- Import: `import { ThemeToggle } from "@sutra/ui/identity"` ([full page](md/ThemeToggle.md))
- Props: `applyToDocument`, `defaultValue`, `modes`, `onValueChange`, `showLabels`, `size`, `storageKey`, `value`, `variant` (* required)

**When to use:** A light, dark and system theme switch, as one icon button that cycles through the modes or as a segmented control showing them all. It toggles the `dark` class and `color-scheme` on `<html>` and remembers the choice in `localStorage`.

**Use instead when:**
- `SegmentedControl`: any choice between a few options
- `Switch`: a plain on or off setting
- `Select`: a long list of options (such as a palette)
- `SearchTrigger`: another header control, a search field button
- `DropdownMenu`: theme and other preferences in one menu

#### Keyboard

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Focuses the button (`icon`), or the selected segment (`segmented`, one tab stop) |
| Enter, Space | `icon`: switch to the next mode. `segmented`: select the focused segment |
| Arrow keys, Home, End | `segmented` only: move focus between the segments (Radix roving focus) |

The `segmented` variant is a `SegmentedControl`, so in RTL its horizontal arrows swap the same way. The icon button has no direction-dependent keys.

#### Screen readers

- `icon` is one button named "Theme: Light. Switch to Dark" (the current mode and the next one), which changes after each press. There is no live region, so a screen reader may not announce the new name until focus returns to it. The three icons are `aria-hidden` and `title` shows the current mode.
- `segmented` is a `radiogroup` named "Theme" with a `radio` per mode ("Light", "Dark", "System"). With `showLabels={false}` each radio keeps its name through `aria-label`.

#### Reduced motion

The sun, moon and computer icons turn and fade into each other over 500 ms; `motion-reduce:transition-none` makes them switch at once under `prefers-reduced-motion`. The segmented thumb follows `SegmentedControl` (jumps).

#### Server rendering

Server render: part of it fills in after mount. The server and the hydrating client render `defaultValue` or "system" (or "light" when `modes` has no system), so the markup matches. Right after hydration, before paint, an uncontrolled toggle reads the saved mode from `localStorage` (or a dark `<html>` when `modes` has no system and there is no `defaultValue`) and switches to it: that restore does not call `onValueChange`, and nothing is written to storage or `<html>` until it is done. The `dark` class on `<html>` is set in an effect after mount, so the first paint shows the page's own theme: set the class early with a small inline script that reads the same key.

#### Gotchas

- Uncontrolled, it stores the mode under `storageKey` (default `"sutra-theme"`; `null` turns it off) and a saved value that is in `modes` wins over `defaultValue`. Controlled with `value` and `onValueChange`, it stores nothing: you persist.
- `applyToDocument` (default true) toggles `dark` on `<html>` and sets `color-scheme`; set it to false when the app applies the theme itself. Two instances do not sync with each other.
- `modes` is the cycle order (default `light`, `dark`, `system`); `["light", "dark"]` makes a two-state toggle. With no saved or default value the start is `system` when offered, else whatever `<html>` shows.
- `system` follows the operating system live and resolves to light or dark (exposed as `data-resolved` on the icon button); its icon is always the computer, not the resolved sun or moon.

## TilingLayout

> IDE-style tiling workspace: nested resizable splits of tab groups with drag-and-drop, zoom and keep-alive panes.

- Import: `import { TilingLayout } from "@sutra/ui/workspace"` ([full page](md/TilingLayout.md))
- Props: `renderPane`*, `createPane`, `defaultLayout`, `defaultMaximizedGroup`, `floating`, `keepAlive`, `label`, `layout`, `maximizedGroup`, `minSize`, `onFloatingChange`, `onLayoutChange`, `onMaximizedGroupChange`, `onPaneClose`, `paneClosable`, `paneIcon`, `paneLabel`, `paneTitle`, `renderEmptyGroup`, `shortcuts`, `step` (* required)

## TiltCard

> A `Card` that tilts toward the mouse in 3D. The pointer is read on a still wrapper (`data-slot="tilt-card-field"`) and the card inside tilts, so it never moves out from under the pointer. Props and the ref go to the card. Touch, reduced motion and no hover leave it flat. Use it for hero, plan and entity cards, not for dense or live content.

- Import: `import { TiltCard } from "@sutra/ui/motion"` ([full page](md/TiltCard.md))
- Props: `as`, `max`, `padded`, `size`, `spotlight` (* required)

## TransferItem
